Nano-Optical Switching of Photochromic Material through Ultraviolet and Visible Plasmon Nanofocusing
works.abstract: Abstract Optical control of photochromic properties is essential for optoelectronic devices. The manipulation of such properties has been limited to the microscale because of the wave nature of light; however, scaling down the volume is highly demanded for the future nanosized devices. Herein, we demonstrate optical switching at the nanoscale in an organic photochromic material. Photochromic materials such as diarylethene derivatives exhibit two different states with distinct optical and electronic properties under ultraviolet (UV) and visible light irradiation. We employed plasmon nanofocusing for optical switching of photochromic materials, which allowed the creation of a nanolight source at the apex of a tapered aluminum structure over a broad frequency range. We achieved in situ wavelength control between visible and UV light at the nanoscale for photochromic reactions. Using this technique, we demonstrated nanoscale optical switching between the two states of diarylethene. The switching performance was confirmed for at least nine cycles without degradation. This demonstration would constitute a significant step toward next-generation optoelectronic devices and benefit diverse scientific fields owing to the broad wavelength tunability of plasmon nanofocusing.

works.title: Competing Surface Dynamics of Copper Catalyst Particles during Electrochemical Carbon Dioxide Reduction
works.abstract: Abstract Copper is a powerful catalyst for the electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO2RR), but it faces challenges with selectivity and stability dependent on its structural characteristics. We developed a platform that combines graphitized carbon nanofibers with identical-location transmission electron microscopy (IL-TEM) to study individual copper nanoparticles at the atomic scale under various reaction conditions. Notably, we observed that competing phenomena such as Ostwald ripening, coalescence, selective etching, and Coulomb-explosion-like fragmentation coexist in the same reaction area, with the latter being qualitatively consistent with a charge-driven fission pathway in larger nanoparticles (>10 nm). By tracking uniquely identifiable nanoparticles both individually and in groups, our findings focus on the range of surface-confined restructuring pathways during CO2RR. This contrasts with solution-mediated phenomena, such as dissolution–precipitation, which dominate under open-circuit potential (OCP) and significantly destabilize the catalyst prior to the reaction, highlighting the importance of eliminating this effect. Under CO2RR conditions, Cu nanoparticles are highly sensitive to subtle variations in the support’s nanotexture, defects, and electronic structure, leading to the coexistence of counteracting mechanisms we observed. These observations provide a structural framework for understanding the dynamic behavior of copper-on-carbon catalysts under CO2RR conditions, guiding the development of strategies to improve catalyst stability and performance.

works.title: Electrically Reconfigurable Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic Cavities on Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
works.abstract: Abstract Interfacing integrated photonics with solid-state spin defects holds great promise for future quantum networks, but the scaling of spin-photon architectures is hindered by frequency mismatches arising from fabrication-induced variations in photonic cavity resonances and inhomogeneous optical transition frequencies of individual spins. These challenges call for a photonic platform with deterministic and wide-range tunability. Here, we demonstrate a hybrid nanophotonic platform based on direct bonding of silicon carbide photonic crystal nanocavity arrays onto a thin-film lithium niobate-on-insulator, enabling deterministic electrical tuning of multiple SiC nanocavities into mutual spectral resonance. By exploiting the strong electro-optic response of lithium niobate, we achieve continuous and wide-range cavity tuning of 380 GHz (∼1.1 nm), sufficient to compensate both cavity disorder and spin spectral inhomogeneity. The nanocavities balance strong optical confinement with electrical tunability, exhibiting a theoretical Purcell factor of approximately 400. This hybrid platform enables electrically reconfigurable spin-photon interfaces for large-scale integrated quantum photonics.

works.title: 5DSTEM of Liquid-Phase Nanocrystal Growth Bridges Ensemble Kinetics and Nanoscale Dynamics
works.abstract: Abstract Resolving how ensemble growth kinetics emerge from particle- and grain-level dynamics is essential for predictive control of nanocrystal synthesis. Here, time-resolved four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM), extended into five dimensions (5DSTEM) through continuous acquisition, is used to simultaneously resolve morphology, crystallographic orientation, and lattice strain during Au nanocrystal growth in aqueous HAuCl4. Although ensemble growth follows surface-reaction-limited kinetics, individual nanoparticles exhibit distinct pathways, including continuous growth and discrete coalescence through oriented attachment. These pathways display characteristic orientation dynamics, with stable or gradually selected orientations during continuous growth and abrupt reconfiguration followed by alignment during coalescence. At the ensemble level, the out-of-plane orientation distribution is established early and remains stable, whereas in-plane orientations remain broadly distributed without global alignment. Tensile strain develops progressively from particle surfaces and interfaces, directly linking lattice distortion with evolving morphology and crystallographic structure. By connecting ensemble kinetics with particle- and grain-resolved structural evolution, 5DSTEM provides a general framework for uncovering heterogeneous growth mechanisms and for relating synthesis pathways to structure-dependent properties in functional nanomaterials.

works.title: Direct Observation of Chirality-Dependent Berry Curvature Dipole via Cross-Axial Nonlinear Hall Effect in Trigonal Te
works.abstract: Abstract Quantum geometric quantities, such as Berry curvature (BC) and quantum metric, are known to govern the physical and topological properties of materials, making access to these quantities critically important for the comprehensive understanding of the materials. Chiral crystals offer a natural platform in which structural handedness can control quantum geometry and nonlinear transport, but direct experimental access to the quantum geometric quantities has remained elusive. Here, we show that trigonal tellurium (Te) hosts an enantiomer-dependent Berry curvature dipole (BCD) that can be accessed through the measurement of the cross-axial nonlinear Hall effect (NHE), unlike in previously studied in-plane configurations, where the BCD contribution vanishes. Angle-resolved measurements on left- and right-handed Te devices reveal a second-order transverse response whose sign reverses with crystal chirality. The extracted cross-axial nonlinear susceptibility, χyxz, exceeds the in-plane susceptibility, χxxx, by more than two-fold, indicating a strong BCD-driven contribution. First-principles calculations attribute this behavior to a topologically nontrivial hedgehog-like BC texture near the H points and predict a BCD that reverses sign between opposite enantiomers, consistent with experiment. These results establish cross-axial nonlinear Hall transport as a symmetry-selective probe of chirality-controlled quantum geometry in tellurium and related chiral materials.

works.title: Hybridization State Engineering of Coal Pitch-Based Carbon Materials Enabling Ultrastable Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries with 150,000 Cycles
works.abstract: Abstract Carbon materials with superior porosity and conductivity are widely adopted in aqueous zinc–iodine batteries to host iodine, but suffer from the polyiodide shuttle and cycling stability challenges. Traditional strategies mainly focus on pore structure engineering or heteroatom doping of carbon hosts to confine iodine, but fail to address the sluggish iodine conversion kinetics. Herein, we initially reveal the significant yet overlooked role of hybridization state in reforming the carbon intrinsic activity toward high-efficiency iodine conversion chemistry. With pitch-derived porous carbon as an example, we controllably regulate the C(sp2)/C(sp3) ratio (from 1.23 to 2.21) while maintaining high surface area. These properties lower the activation energy of iodine conversion and effectively suppress the polyiodide shuttle. The zinc–iodine battery exhibits ultrahigh cycling stability after 150,000 cycles and a low self-discharging rate with only 12.5% capacity loss after 20 days. Ah-level pouch cell with 66.6 mgiodine cm–2 achieves a cumulative discharging capacity of 103.51 Ah. The hybridization engineering was successfully extended to commercial porous carbon (YP-50F), prolonging the lifespan from 7425 to 27,000 cycles. This work presents a hybridization state engineering strategy to reform the intrinsic activity of the carbon host to favor the iodine conversion chemistry and beyond.

works.title: Polarization-Controlled Dual-Mode Switching in van der Waals α-In2Se3 Memristors for Multitime-Scale Reservoir Computing
works.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical-metallization (ECM) memristors can implement both nonvolatile memory switching and volatile threshold switching, making them attractive for neuromorphic and reservoir computing; however, the stochastic formation of metallic filaments causes variability in the threshold voltage and switching instability. Here, we report a van der Waals α-In2Se3-based ferroelectric-semiconductor ECM (FeS-ECM) memristor in which a bidirectionally polarized α-In2Se3 layer is inserted between the inert electrode and the switching layer. The out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization, programmed through a decoupled in-plane poling terminal, deterministically selects within the low-compliance operating regime between nonvolatile bipolar memory switching and volatile unipolar threshold switching within a single device, with a coefficient of variation in the set voltage of 4.7% and stable operation over more than 9000 cycles. Exploiting these two modes, a single α-In2Se3 platform exhibits both the volatile reservoir dynamics and the nonvolatile conductance modulation required for the readout weights of a physical reservoir-computing system, in which the pulse width electrically programs multiple relaxation time constants. This pulse-width multitime scale reconfigurability enables efficient temporal information processing, demonstrated through MNIST classification and chaotic time-series prediction.

works.title: Engineered Living Materials: A Therapeutic Paradigm beyond Conventional Biomaterials
works.abstract: Abstract Development of biomaterials in the past two decades has profoundly advanced modern medicine. However, the relatively simple and insufficiently biological functions and lack of self-renewal capability limit their ability to dynamically adapt to complex physiological environments. Engineered living materials (eLMs) use living organisms as core functional units and provide a therapeutic approach for addressing these limitations. Thus, this review systematically summarizes the recent advancements in eLMs, beginning with an overview of the primary biological chassis, including bacteria, microalgae, fungi, and mammalian cells. eLMs hold the valuable capabilities of long-term self-sustainment and self-proliferation within complex biological environments, which are endowed with intelligent regulation. For instance, they can sense environmental signals and execute programmed functional outputs, including therapeutic protein secretion or targeted migration. Moreover, they achieve precise control over therapeutic actions, encompassing spatial localization at the disease site, temporal dynamics of the intervention, and quantitative regulation of outputs. Furthermore, we highlight the broad therapeutic applications of these dynamic systems in addressing complex diseases. Finally, we discuss the current translational challenges and future directions of the field, emphasizing the potential of integrating artificial intelligence with synthetic biology and nanomaterial engineering to develop next-generation programmable eLMs and expand their utility across diverse sectors.

works.title: Ultrasound-Responsive Electroactive Polyetheretherketone Scaffold Promotes Bioenergetic Bone Regeneration by Regulating Mitochondrial Permeability Transition Pores
works.abstract: Abstract Mitochondrial dysfunction and energy metabolic imbalance in senescent bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are critical pathological foundations for senile bone regeneration. Existing therapeutic strategies suffer from a lack of active mitochondrial bioenergetic driving forces, failing to effectively reverse energy metabolic suppression of senescent BMSCs. Here, an ultrasound-activated electroactive scaffold was constructed by anchoring barium titanate-transition metal carbide (MXene@BaTiO3) heterojunctions on the surface of polyetheretherketone (PEEK) to reactivate mitochondrial energy metabolism and promote bone regeneration under senescence-associated bone loss conditions. These heterojunctions adhere to BMSC membranes and generate electrical stimulation upon ultrasound stimulation, which significantly inhibits abnormal opening of mitochondrial permeability transition pores (mPTP), reduces leakage of mtDNA and Cyt c, and maintains membrane potential stability. Mechanistic investigations reveal that electrical stimulation activates the PI3K/Akt/MDM2 signaling axis to promote the degradation of accumulated p53, which relieves the competitive binding of p53 to TRAP1, thereby restoring TRAP1-CypD-mediated mPTP gating and mitochondrial homeostasis. Consequently, this ultrasound-activated electroactive scaffold drives mitochondrial energy metabolism and osteogenic differentiation of senescence-like BMSCs in vitro, which is further confirmed in a rat model. These results demonstrate the potential of this electroactive scaffold as a regulator of mitochondrial energy metabolism for senescence-associated bone regeneration.

works.title: Switching of Exciton-Polaritons in Covalent Organic Framework-Based Optical Resonators through Interaction with the Molecular Environment
works.abstract: Abstract We report a demonstration of a covalent organic framework (COF) integrated into an optical cavity for the realization of exciton–polaritons and their reversible switching through changes in the surrounding molecular environment. Films of COF nanoplates were integrated into Fabry–Pérot resonators engineered to achieve spectral matching between cavity modes and COF excitonic transitions, yielding strong light–matter coupling with a Rabi splitting above 300 meV. The cavity architecture preserves accessibility of the porous framework, enabling interaction with guest molecules. The potential of this interplay is shown by exposing the resonators to water vapor, which induces both a redshift and a pronounced reduction of the COF optical absorption. The observed hypochromic effect drives a reversible shift from strong to weak coupling, effectively switching exciton–polaritons on and off, as guest molecules are desorbed from or adsorbed in the reticular material host. The process is reversible upon desorption, with preservation of structural and optical integrity. These results establish COFs as a versatile platform for chemically tunable polaritonic systems, opening avenues for responsive photonic devices, sensing, and control of light–matter interactions in nanostructured materials.

works.title: Chronic Stress-Triggerable Nanoprodrugs Ameliorate Metabolic Abnormalities Driven by Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal Axis Dysregulation in Early Alzheimer’s Disease
works.abstract: Abstract Chronic stress-induced dysregulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis is a crucial early risk factor that triggers brain energy metabolism disorders to accelerate the onset and progression of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Herein, an amphiphilic precursor conjugate of ginsenoside Rc (Rc) covalently linked with a reactive oxygen species-sensitive thioketo bond is constructed to form stimuli-responsive prodrug assemblies, which are further modified with the TGN-Tet1 dual-ligand fusion peptide TPL to obtain a chronic stress-triggerable programmed nanoprodrug (TLRN). Following TPL-mediated blood-brain barrier penetration and neuronal preferential targeting, nanoprodrugs specifically disintegrate to selectively release active Rc in the chronic stress-induced excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) microenvironment. Benefiting from the restoration of HPA axis homeostasis by normalizing glucocorticoid receptor nuclear translocation, TLRN treatment exhibits multifaceted rectification of cerebral metabolic abnormalities, including enhancing glucose uptake, promoting oxidative phosphorylation, and mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction. In young amyloid precursor protein/presenilin 1 (APP/PS1) transgenic mouse models exposed to chronic stress, this intervention can alleviate brain energy deprivation and amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation, ultimately rescuing depressive-like behaviors and cognitive deficits, offering a promising approach for early prevention and flexible management of AD at high risk of chronic stress.

works.title: Accelerating the Discovery of Synthesizable 2D Hybrid Double Perovskites through Human–LLM Collaborative Descriptor Engineering
works.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional hybrid perovskites offer exceptional structural diversity and multifunctional properties, yet their synthesis remains a major bottleneck due to low hit rates and strong reliance on empirical intuition. Here we introduce AL-SynAgent, a human-in-the-loop, ML-guided screening workflow that integrates literature-derived synthetic priors, expert-refined chemical descriptors, and active learning to assess the synthesis feasibility of two dimensional (2D) hybrid organic–inorganic rare-earth double perovskites (HORDPs). By converting LLM-assisted literature knowledge and expert chemical reasoning into system-specific computable descriptors, AL-SynAgent reduces dependence on large experimental data sets while retaining chemically interpretable decision rules. With experimental feedback from only 4.8% of candidate space, the model converged and achieved successful target-phase formation for 11 of the 14 candidates in the prospectively selected experimental set, corresponding to a hit rate of 78.6%. Screening of an enumerated virtual library of 280,000 candidates further prioritized 64,482 compositions with high predicted synthesis feasibility. Notably, three newly obtained compounds also exhibit both excellent ferroelectricity and photoluminescence, including (4-F-321)4RbEu(NO3)8, which displays an exceptionally high Curie temperature of 388 K and strong emission at 592 nm. This work establishes a practical, human-in-the-loop strategy for data-efficient prioritization of candidate compositions within chemically constrained 2D HORDP space under a standardized laboratory synthesis protocol.

works.title: Micro-LED-Activated Formaldehyde Sensing via Au Loading-Regulated Interfacial Engineering in Anatase TiO2 Nanofibers
works.abstract: Abstract Photoactivated metal-oxide gas sensors reduce the energy demand associated with continuous heating, yet selective detection of volatile organic compounds remains constrained by weak electrical transduction and complex surface oxidation pathways. Here, Au-functionalized anatase TiO2 nanofibers (Au/aTiO2 NFs) were integrated with a 395 nm microlight-emitting diode (LED) for low-power formaldehyde (HCHO) sensing. One-pot electrospinning followed by calcination enabled systematic control of Au loading while preserving the anatase nanofiber architecture. Au loading regulated TiO2 crystallite growth, defect states, dispersion, interfacial Au chemical states, and photoexcited carrier relaxation. At 0.15 wt % Au, finely dispersed Au nanoparticles produced a distinct Au/TiO2 interfacial environment and carrier-relaxation behavior, whereas higher loadings induced nanoparticle aggregation and additional nonradiative energy-loss pathways. Under UV micro-LED illumination at 2.63 mW, the optimized sensor exhibited a response of 1093 toward 1 ppm of HCHO, an estimated detection limit of 4.9 ppb, and stable operation over 40 consecutive cycles. Density functional theory calculations further supported the loading-dependent selectivity, showing that changes in the local Au environment selectively modify HCHO adsorption and bond reconstruction. These results identify local Au-site density as a key design parameter governing interfacial reactivity and molecular selectivity in low-power photoactivated gas sensing.

works.title: Fluorinated Copper(I) Iodine Cluster Scintillators Enable High-Temperature X-ray Imaging
works.abstract: Abstract The development of scintillators that maintain excellent performance under high temperatures is a critical challenge. Here, by simply replacing the triphenylphosphine ligand with its fluorinated analogue, we successfully switched the emission pathway of Cu2I2 clusters from pure phosphorescence to a hybrid phosphorescence/thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) mechanism, enabling adaptive high-temperature X-ray imaging. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that the fluorination strategy reduces the singlet–triplet energy gap to an exceptionally small value of 35 meV, thereby promoting efficient reverse intersystem crossing. The TADF contribution reaches 95.7% at room temperature. This temperature-responsive characteristic endows the fluorinated cluster with adaptive X-ray imaging capability across a broad temperature window from 293 to 413 K, overcoming the thermal quenching phenomenon in traditional phosphorescence-only scintillators. This work establishes a molecular design approach for smart scintillators capable of reliable operation in demanding thermal environments.

works.title: Frozen 2D Adatom Gas at the Surface of Gold–Copper Alloys
works.abstract: Abstract Isolated, undercoordinated metal atoms exhibit enhanced reactivity central to catalysis, yet their stabilization on surfaces remains challenging. In heterogeneous single-atom catalysis, activity derives from interactions between individual atoms and a host matrix, but the absence of stabilizing ligands often leads to diffusion, aggregation, and sintering, obscuring structure–activity relationships. On metal surfaces, reactivity is typically limited to sparse, dynamic, undercoordinated sites lining step edges or lattice defects. Here we report a defect-engineering strategy to stabilize isolated adatoms on dilute metal alloy substrates. Scanning tunneling microscopy reveals a high density of uniformly distributed adatoms on Au–Cu(111) terraces that persist under thermal cycling. Combined experiments and modeling attribute this stability to alloy-induced subsurface dislocation networks that trap adatoms and suppress diffusion, forming a two-dimensional frozen gas. These adatoms act as a reactive reservoir, enabling on-surface coordination chemistry inaccessible on pure metals, and providing insights into atomic-scale processes on the surfaces of defect-engineered alloys with implications for heterogeneous catalysis.

works.title: Silencing MSR1 in Macrophages Attenuates the Cochlear Foreign Body Response and Preserves Electrode–Neural Interface
works.abstract: Abstract Cochlear implantation (CI) provides effective auditory rehabilitation for patients with severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss. Implantation can nevertheless induce local foreign body response (FBR) and cochlear fibrosis, motivating strategies to reduce tissue reactions and preserve cochlear integrity. Macrophages play a key role in FBR, but their functions are multiple and stage-dependent, and indiscriminate intervention may aggravate cochlear injury. Therefore, more precise strategies are needed to modulate macrophage-mediated FBR after CI. Here, through transcriptomic profiling of cochlear tissues from rats 30 days after cochlear implantation, we identified macrophage scavenger receptor 1 (MSR1) as a prominent signature after CI. In vitro assays further verified the role of MSR1 in reshaping macrophage phenotype and inflammatory activation. To achieve targeted MSR1 regulation in the cochlea, we engineered iRGD-modified extracellular vesicles to deliver siMSR1 (iRGD-EV/siMSR1). iRGD modification enhanced macrophage uptake of EV and enabled efficient siRNA delivery. In a rat CI model, local administration of iRGD-EV/siMSR1 reduced cochlear fibrotic tissue formation and decreased fibrosis-related protein expression. Moreover, iRGD-EV/siMSR1 preserved spiral ganglion neurons and myelin structures, contributing to residual hearing protection after implantation. Early stage analysis at 7 days after implantation showed that iRGD-EV/siMSR1 suppressed macrophage inflammatory activation, reduced TGF-β1-related profibrotic signaling, regulated matrix remodeling, and limited early apoptosis. These findings identify MSR1 as a promising molecular target for cochlear implant-induced FBR and support iRGD-EV/siMSR1 as a potentially translatable strategy for attenuating cochlear fibrosis and preserving the cochlear neural interface, also highlighting the importance of considering neural health when modulating macrophage-mediated responses to cochlear implants.

works.title: Shield-and-Amplify Nanoparticle Vaccines Retune Immunodominance for Broad Protection against SARS-CoV-2
works.abstract: Abstract Antigenic variation severely constrains the durability and breadth of vaccine-induced protection against rapidly evolving viruses. Although conserved epitopes can support cross-variant immunity, antibody responses to viral glycoproteins are often biased toward exposed, mutable immunodominant epitopes, leaving conserved protective sites subdominant. We previously identified a cryptic, conserved class 5 epitope (the 6D6/7D6 epitope) on the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain (RBD) capable of eliciting broad cross-neutralization. Here, we present a modular “shield-and-amplify” nanoparticle vaccination strategy to redirect immunodominance toward this subdominant epitope. We engineered site-specific N-linked glycans─alongside the native N343 glycan to mask variable immunodominant regions while preserving accessibility to the class 5 epitope. The resulting glycan-masked RBD antigen (RGM) was displayed on p239 nanoparticles via nanobody-mediated assembly, yielding multivalent RGM@p239 immunogens. Antigenic profiling revealed that glycan shielding preserved recognition by 6D6 and 7D6 antibodies while reducing binding of representative class 1–4 antibodies by at least 80%. In immunized animals, RGM@p239 enriched 7D6-competitive serum antibodies blocking approximately 70–80% of serum binding to RGM and broadened cross-variant neutralization against 8 representative variant strains, including detectable activity against Omicron lineages. Furthermore, RGM@p239 reduced disease severity after Omicron EG.1 challenge in a hamster model. These results support a model in which glycan shielding and nanoparticle multivalency act as complementary immune-focusing modules: shielding attenuates competing responses, while multivalency amplifies responses to conserved subdominant epitopes. This study establishes a nanovaccine design strategy to address antigenic variation by focusing immunity on conserved viral vulnerabilities.

works.title: Exciton Transport in Disordered Perovskite Nanocrystal Solids
works.abstract: Abstract Solution-processed thin films of colloidal lead halide perovskite (LHP) nanocrystals (NCs) show great potential for next-generation optoelectronic devices. However, these NC solids exhibit non-negligible size and shape polydispersity, which introduces both structural and energetic disorder. Here we resolve the exciton dynamics in space, time, and energy to elucidate the impact of disorder on exciton transport. We show that the disorder depends sensitively on the alkylamine ligand used in the synthesis. While shorter alkyl chain lengths lead to high polydispersity, longer alkyl chains lead to a narrower size distribution and smaller particles where quantum confinement becomes more pronounced, consequently leading to increased energetic disorder. Strikingly, we find that exciton transport is less efficient in NC solids with long alkyl chains, despite the fact that they have significantly more narrowly size-distributed ensembles. This demonstrates that energetic disorder rather than structural disorder is the dominant factor for predicting exciton transport within these disordered systems.

works.title: Endogenous Fe Single-Atom-Induced Short-Range Graphitization Enables Integrated Electromagnetic Wave Absorption and Thermal Management in PTFE Composites
works.abstract: Abstract Modern electronics require polymer composites that integrate electromagnetic wave absorption (EWA) and thermal dissipation, yet these functions impose competing structural requirements. Herein, we construct Fe single-atom@short-range graphitized porous carbon (Fe1@SGC) that integrates electromagnetic attenuation and thermal conduction within a single material. Distinct from conventional exogenous metal-introduction routes, egg white serves as both the carbon source and coordination medium, enabling Fe single-atom anchoring without metal salts or organic ligands. Fe single atoms induce charge redistribution, polarization centers, and local ordering of carbon domains, synergistically regulating dielectric loss, thermal transport, and impedance matching. The multiscale carbon network further promotes electromagnetic wave penetration and multiple reflections/scattering. After incorporation into polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), the Fe1@SGC/PTFE composite achieves a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 7.92 GHz and improved thermal conductivity. This work establishes endogenous single-atom-induced local graphitization as a ligand-free and structurally precise strategy for designing single-component fillers toward integrated EWA and thermal management.

works.title: Hierarchical Ionic Programming of Stretchable Organic Electrochemical Transistors for Dual-Mode Sensing and Computing
works.abstract: Abstract Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) are promising building blocks for flexible in-sensor computing, yet the conflicting ionic dynamic demands of high-fidelity sensing and nonvolatile memory remain challenging to reconcile within a unified hardware platform. Here, we report a hierarchical compositional programming strategy that addresses this trade-off across a standardized stretchable OECT architecture. Regulating 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl (TEMPO)-oxidized cellulose nanofiber content in poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) tunes channel capacitance and mechanical compliance, while tailoring the supramolecular network in a deep eutectic solvent gel electrolyte dictates ion retention kinetics. This strategy establishes distinct operational regimes via tailored formulations: a rapidly reversible, low-hysteresis state for sensing and a persistent ion trapping state for neuromorphic computing. The sensing OECT enables real-time electrocardiogram acquisition with a 35.6 dB signal-to-noise ratio and 98.9% biometric identification accuracy across 15 subjects. The computing state supports temporal Morse code demodulation and Pavlovian associative learning, demonstrating application-adaptive stretchable bioelectronics.

works.title: Resolving the Quantum Origin of Anisotropic Raman Response in Quasi-1D Ta2Ni3Te5
works.abstract: Abstract Probing anisotropic electron–phonon interactions (EPIs) is fundamental to understanding low-dimensional quantum materials, yet isolating their intrinsic signatures remains a challenge due to the confounding influence of extrinsic effects. Here, we resolve this ambiguity in quasi-one-dimensional Ta2Ni3Te5 through a combination of angle-resolved polarized Raman spectroscopy and density functional perturbation theory (DFPT). Anomalous four-lobe angular dependences were observed in Ag phonon modes, which deviate from the real-valued Raman tensor prediction. Further, we explicitly highlight that, despite their distinct physical origins, light absorption and birefringence yield mathematically identical angular dependencies in Ta2Ni3Te5, rendering phenomenological fitting alone insufficient to identify the true physical mechanism. By employing a full quantum treatment incorporating detailed interaction mechanisms, we capture the qualitative characteristics and mode-to-mode diversity of the anomalous angular responses observed experimentally. The DFPT calculations further reveal mode-specific and momentum-resolved EPIs, providing microscopic support for anisotropic EPIs as the mechanism of anomalous Raman responses.

works.title: Sequential Monomer Addition Regulates Hydration in Branched Poly(aryl piperidinium) Membranes for Water Electrolysis
works.abstract: Abstract The conductivity-swelling trade-off limits anion exchange membranes (AEMs) for water electrolysis. Here, we investigated how the timing of tetraphenylmethane (TPM) incorporation influences precursor assembly and membrane hydration in poly(aryl piperidinium) AEMs. Introducing TPM before backbone extension alters precursor formation and favors a more uniform distribution of hydrophilic domains in the resulting membranes. Spectroscopic and NMR analyses further associate this route with enhanced hydrogen-bond organization and increased local mobility within the hydrated membranes. The optimized P-TPM5 membrane reaches an OH– conductivity of 229.4 ± 6 mS cm–1 at 80 °C while maintaining a swelling ratio of approximately 15%. In an AEM water electrolyzer containing a NiFe-LDH anode and Pt/C cathode, the membrane delivers 5.74 A cm–2 at 2.0 V and operates for more than 1100 h in a staged-current test. These results identify the timing of branching-unit incorporation as a synthesis variable for tailoring hydration environments and improving the conductivity-swelling balance of AEMs.

Plasmonic-Enhanced MoS2 Photodetectors for Polarization-Sensitive Edge Vision
works.abstract: Abstract Polarization-sensitive photodetectors have important application value in fields such as polarization imaging, target recognition and edge visual sensing. However, conventional polarization detection schemes suffer from high fabrication costs and the limitation of crystal structures on the polarization response of intrinsic materials, making it difficult to achieve effective polarization detection. In this paper, we propose a MoS2 photodetector enhanced by the Au/polymer nano-elliptical pillar array (AP-NEPA). Experimental results show that AP-NEPA can comprehensively improve the optoelectronic performance of the device in the visible wavelength band. The AP-NEPA-enhanced device achieves a maximum responsivity of 14.4 mA/W and a maximum specific detectivity of 2.16 × 109 Jones. At 640 nm, it achieves a minimum noise-equivalent power of 15 pW/Hz1/2, corresponding to 30.2-, 41-, and 11.3-fold enhancements in photocurrent, responsivity, and detectivity, respectively. The induced anisotropic plasmonic coupling further enables polarization-dependent photoresponse with a polarization ratio of 1.4 at 520 nm. As a proof of concept, the measured polarization-dependent photocurrents are used as convolution weights for offline edge-feature extraction from blurred and noisy images, demonstrating the potential of the device for polarization-assisted image preprocessing.

works.title: Nanostructured Display of the Conserved Neuraminidase HCA2 Epitope by Nanocomplexes and Virus-Like Particles for Influenza Vaccine Development
works.abstract: Abstract Influenza neuraminidase (NA) has emerged as a promising target for universal influenza vaccine development because it undergoes less antigenic drift than hemagglutinin. Among the diverse NA subtypes of influenza A and B viruses, a highly conserved sequence adjacent to the enzymatic active site, termed highly conserved area 2 (HCA2), has been identified as an exceptionally conserved antigenic region. Here, we developed and evaluated two nanostructured vaccine platformsself-assembling protein nanocomplexes (NCXs) and virus-like particles (VLPs)displaying conserved HCA2 epitopes from influenza A and B NAs to enhance HCA2 immunogenicity. Intranasal immunization with HCA2 NCXs elicited anti-HCA2 IgG antibodies, predominantly of the IgG1 subclass, but induced low or undetectable T-cell responses in the spleen. In contrast, intranasal immunization with HCA2 VLPs elicited not only anti-HCA2 IgG antibodies but also anti-N1, anti-N2, and anti-BN IgG antibodies in sera, as well as detectable anti-N1 and anti-BN IgA antibodies in bronchoalveolar lavage fluids. HCA2 VLPs also induced substantially stronger CD4+ helper and CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell responses, particularly including both their central and effector memory subsets. Notably, only HCA2 VLP immunization, but not HCA2 NCX immunization, conferred protection against a lethal H1N1 virus challenge. These findings demonstrate that the architecture of HCA2 antigen presentation influences the quality and magnitude of the immune response. HCA2 VLPs elicited robust humoral and cellular immune responses and were associated with protection against a lethal influenza virus challenge. These results highlight the importance of nanostructure platforms in the development of conserved-epitope vaccines and support HCA2-displaying VLPs as a promising platform for next-generation influenza vaccine development.

works.title: Defect-Tolerant Frenkel Exciton Delocalization in Supramolecular Nanotubes
works.abstract: Abstract Preserving exciton delocalization in the presence of structural and environmental disorder is a central challenge for nanoscale photonic and optoelectronic materials. Here we show that Frenkel excitons in two-dimensional supramolecular nanostructures retain extensive delocalization even in the presence of intentionally incorporated deep-energy traps. Fluorescent trap molecules introduced during the self-assembly of double-walled molecular nanotubes provide a controlled model system in which strong local energetic perturbations are created without significant distortion of the host structure. Increasing the trap concentration shortens the host-exciton PL lifetime from ∼190 ps to ∼15 ps, while polarization-resolved microscopy of individual nanotubes shows that the collective excitonic polarization remains essentially unchanged. Frenkel-exciton calculations based on experimentally established molecular structures reproduce this robustness and reveal that delocalization decreases only weakly because the excitonic wave functions redistribute around the trap sites while remaining extended over large molecular domains. These results demonstrate an intrinsic defect tolerance of delocalized Frenkel excitons in a two-dimensional supramolecular architecture and identify dimensionality as an important design principle for preserving collective excitonic states in structurally imperfect nanomaterials.

works.title: Tunable Gaussian Random Number Generator from a Nanoscopic Domain-Wall-Based Spintronic Device
works.abstract: Abstract Existing hardware implementations of Gaussian random number generators (RNGs) rely on large arrays of binary devices, resulting in substantial hardware footprints or sampling-time overheads. Here, we present a racetrack memory-based random number generator (RTM-RNG) that directly generates analog Gaussian random number streams from a single domain-wall-based nanoscale racetrack. A geometrically engineered racetrack tip creates a localized current-density gradient, enabling field-free stochastic domain-wall nucleation driven by nanosecond current pulses. The domain-wall nucleation probability is continuously tunable via an electrically generated Oersted field or an external magnetic field, providing direct control over the mean of the output distribution. We demonstrate more than 256 distinguishable states from a single nanoscopic RTM-RNG device, thus making a Gaussian RNG with more than 8-bit resolution possible. Compared with conventional binary random bitstreams, the RTM-RNG achieves high-quality Gaussian distributions up to 83 times faster.

works.title: Deciphering Charge Delocalization across Mercaptobenzonitrile Ligand Terminals and Inner Hydrides in Atomically Precise Cu14H10 Nanoclusters for Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction
works.abstract: Abstract Cu hydride nanoclusters with atomic precision in composition and structure offer exciting catalytic activities and opportunities for rigorous structure–function correlations. Determination of their atomic structures, especially the hydride locations, hinges on the availability of high-quality single crystals and neutron beams, while their relatively weak UV–visible absorption and electrochemical instability challenge the analysis of their electronic properties. Herein, we synthesize a Cu14H10 nanocluster coordinated by three 4-mercaptobenzonitrile (MBN) and eight triphenylphosphine ligands. Two-dimensional NMR analyses combined with single crystal X-ray diffraction reveal unequivocally the locations of the ten hydrides in four groups (stoichiometry ratio of 1:3:3:3) with drastically different environments (chemical shifts 11–3 ppm): one H at the inversion center and three triangular layers along the C3 axial bridging together the Cu core. MBN serves two additional purposes besides stabilizing ligands: its electron-withdrawing nature and a highly sensitive vibrational reporter of its local charge density. The first property gives rise to a low-lying Cu-core-to-MBN metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) excited state, and the second property enables direct spectroscopic probing of both the charge transfer nature and dynamics of the MLCT excited state through the dynamic spectral shift of the MBN CN stretching mode. Through combined transient IR absorption spectroscopy and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations, we obtained the complete atomic and electronic structure, revealing core-to-ligand charge transfers in these nanoclusters. Computed under identical conditions using an iso-structure with a mildly electron-donating ligand, the Cu14H10 featuring charge delocalization toward the electron-withdrawing MBN has a smaller HOMO–LUMO gap, which is deemed favorable for electrocatalytic CO2 reduction. The preferential formation of complex multielectron-hydrogenation products (8–12 e–, C1 hydrocarbons, and C2+ products) over two-electron pathways such as CO formation or the competing hydrogen evolution reaction highlights their promise as atomically precise catalysts for deep CO2 reduction.

works.title: Receptor-Modular Nanocaptors for Programmable Cytokine Sequestration
works.abstract: Abstract Pathological cytokine networks underlie inflammatory injury and tumor-associated immunosuppression, yet most cytokine-targeted therapies rely on molecularly fixed, pathway-specific antagonists. We present a receptor-modular nanomaterial strategy for constructing modular cytokine nanocaptors (MCNs) whose sequestration profiles can be reconfigured by exchanging receptor modules. Cytokine receptor ectodomains are engineered as independently producible serum albumin fusion proteins and coassembled with poly(L-lactic acid) (PLLA) into compositionally defined nanoparticles. This architecture decouples cytokine-binding specificity from nanoparticle structure, enabling high-density codisplay of multiple receptor modules on single particles. Representative MCNs simultaneously sequester IL-6, TNF-α, and IFN-γ and suppress cytokine-driven inflammatory signaling more effectively than matched soluble receptor mixtures. By altering module composition while preserving the same assembly framework, MCNs can be redirected from sequestering pro-inflammatory cytokines in sepsis, acute lung injury, and fulminant hepatitis to depleting immunosuppressive mediators in tumors. These results establish receptor-modular nanocaptors as programmable materials for disease-tailored cytokine sequestration and immune-microenvironment reconfiguration.

works.title: Janus Biofuel Cells for Electrosynergistic Enhancement of Microenvironment-Adaptive Cascade Catalysis in Infected Diabetic Wound Healing
works.abstract: Abstract The treatment of infectious diabetic wound is greatly hampered by hyperglycemia, inflammation, and microcirculatory dysfunction. Bioelectric stimulation and nanozyme catalysis provide a potential strategy for chronic wound repair but suffer from limitations including external electric power, low activity, and competitive multienzyme reactions. Given this, we developed microenvironment-responsive Janus GOx-Au@PCH–Pt nanoparticles (NPs) as biofuel cells, integrating cascade enzymatic catalysis and self-powered electrical stimulation. The biofuel cell features hydroxylated polyaniline (PCH) NPs as conductive bridges, Pt nanoclusters as the cathode, and glucose oxidase (GOx)-grafted Au (GOx-Au) as the anode. Under infection (acidic pH), conductive PCH shuttles electrons to generate microcurrent that accelerates enzyme catalysis on both the Au anode (GOx) and Pt cathode (peroxidase, POD). The enhanced GOx-POD cascade strengthens ·OH generation, and the self-powered electric field enhances ·OH diffusion across phospholipid bilayers, achieving significant bacterial killing and biofilm dispersion. During tissue repair, neutral/alkaline conditions switch Pt nanozyme from POD to catalase (CAT) and transform PCH into a benzoquinone structure as the electron acceptor. Reversed electron flow boosts the GOx-CAT cascade catalysis on the electrodes, accelerating glucose consumption, suppressing advanced glycation end product formation, and alleviating oxidative stress, while electrical stimulation reduces hypoxia-inducible factor-1α expressions. This synergistic effect promotes collagen deposition and orderly arrangement and normalizes microenvironment with oxygen-generating, hypoglycemic, anti-inflammatory, and macrophage phenotype-shifted features, thereby accelerating wound healing. This designed nanoscale biofuel cells realize adaptive microcurrent modulation and spatiotemporal cascade catalysis, offering a minimally invasive paradigm for infected diabetic wound therapy.

works.title: Engineered Peptide Nanoparticle Targeting Both Bacterial Load Reduction and Bone Repair for the Treatment of Bone Infections
works.abstract: Bone infection is a common and serious complication in orthopedic surgery. Conventional antibiotic strategies frequently induce antibiotic resistance, leading to the persistence of bone infections. In this study, an engineered peptide nanoparticle named C8-IK21 was designed based on the coiled-coil motif. Specifically, C8-IK21 effectively targeted bacterial cell membranes, further exacerbating bacterial death through lipid peroxidation. At safe doses, local administration of C8-IK21 demonstrated high efficacy in treating S. aureus-infected cortical bone defects in mice. No detectable resistance emerged under the tested experimental conditions. Additionally, C8-IK21 exhibited anti-inflammatory activity. Furthermore, C8-IK21 could enter cells by binding to ADAM9, activating the ERK signaling pathway to regulate osteoblast differentiation. Meanwhile, C8-IK21 reduced the expression of ITGB1 via ADAM9, thereby inhibiting osteoclast differentiation and function. Moreover, the pro-osteogenic effect of C8-IK21 was validated in organoids. In conclusion, C8-IK21 represents a promising therapeutic approach for the treatment of refractory bacterial infections and bone homeostasis disorders.

works.title: Full-Length Protein Classification through Sequence Reading by Solid-State Subnanopores
works.abstract: Abstract Nanopore sequencing for full-length proteins is daunting due to inaccuracy of fingerprinting amino acids with ionic current and lack of theoretical models. Here, we demonstrate that nanopores drilled in 5 nm-thick membranes with constriction diameter <1 nm, i.e., subnanopores, can site-specifically read the primary structure of amyloid-β (Aβ) isoforms after 50-fold coverage. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that charged side chains near the constriction swing and modulate the volume exclusion of neighboring residues, resulting in a sequence context-dependent signal altered between translocation orientations. Orientation of individual label-free molecules is inferred by clustering, which yields high-fidelity empirical consensus that strongly correlates with computational trajectories (PCC = 0.78 ± 0.03). A homemade self-supervised learning method categorizes Aβ42 and Aβ40 at the single-molecule level (AUC = 0.88 ± 0.02) and predicts the mole fraction in agreement with actual ratios. Solid-state subnanopores offer a straightforward strategy for proteoform single-molecule classification and sequence extraction in mixtures.

works.title: Ferroelectric-Empowered van der Waals Spectrometer with Record-High Sensitivity and Ultralow Noise
works.abstract: Abstract Miniaturized spectrometers are essential for portable and consumer-oriented applications, yet their reduced physical footprint inherently limits the detector’s active area, leading to compromised sensitivity. Conventional strategies to enhance sensitivity, such as cryogenic cooling or photomultiplier tubes, are incompatible with miniaturization due to their bulk, cost, and power demands. Here, we present a miniaturized spectrometer based on a van der Waals heterojunction integrated on a ferroelectric thin film. Spectral discrimination is enabled by engineering both interlayer and intralayer photoresponses within the heterojunction, which can be dynamically tuned solely via the source-drain bias, eliminating the need for a gate electrode and enabling a two-terminal architecture. This design is inherently compatible with simple two-pad readout integrated circuits, facilitating scalable array integration for compact spectroscopic systems. Critically, the built-in electric field generated by the ferroelectric polarization promotes efficient dissociation of interlayer excitons, yielding an ultralow noise floor of below 5 × 10–16 A Hz–1/2, more than 2 orders of magnitude lower than existing miniaturized spectrometers and surpassing the performance of most benchtop instruments. This work in sensitivity without sacrificing size or complexity present a strategy for deploying high-performance spectroscopy in real-world applications.

works.title: Cucurbit[ n ]uril-Programmed Chlorogenic Acid Release for Collagen Mineralization and Pulp–Dentin Repair in Near-Pulp Bonding
works.abstract: Abstract Long-term failure of resin–dentin bonding arises from persistent hydration and enzymatic degradation of exposed collagen in the deep hybrid layer, whereas diffusion of bioactive components through dentinal tubules toward the pulp may cause pulpal irritation. An ideal pretreatment should therefore promote collagen remineralization and interfacial stabilization while reducing pulp-adjacent cellular irritation and supporting pulp–dentin repair. Herein, supramolecular complexes of chlorogenic acid (CGA) and cucurbit[n]uril (Q[n], n = 6, 7, and 8), denoted CGA@Q[n], were constructed to regulate CGA loading, release, and interfacial exposure. CGA@Q[6] showed limited loading, release, and mineralization capacity. CGA@Q[7] exhibited faster early release and achieved complete collagen mineralization within 24 h, whereas CGA@Q[8] showed the highest encapsulation efficiency, sustained CGA supply, complete mineralization at 36 h, and a continuous, dense, integrated intrafibrillar mineral phase. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that CGA released from Q[8] reanchored to collagen and recruited Ca2+, promoting mineral formation within confined intrafibrillar spaces. These advantages extended to three-dimensional collagen networks and demineralized dentin, yielding higher HAp content, enhanced mineral–collagen integration, tubule occlusion, mechanical recovery, and MMP-9 inhibition. As a bonding pretreatment, CGA@Q[8] reduced nanoleakage, endogenous gelatinolytic activity, and aging-induced bond-strength loss. It also improved cytocompatibility relative to free CGA and promoted mineralization and odontogenic differentiation of human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs). In vivo, CGA@Q[8] promoted dentin remineralization, maintained near-pulp interfacial stability, alleviated pulpal irritation, and enhanced odontogenic repair. Together, these findings identify CGA@Q[8] as the most effective formulation and show that homologue selection can tune CGA exposure kinetics for coordinated dentin interface repair.

works.title: ZnO–Te Anti-Ambipolar Switch Integration with Complementary Field-Effect Transistors Enabling a Pull-Middle Architecture for Standard Ternary Inverters
works.abstract: Abstract We demonstrate a pull-middle architecture for standard ternary inverters (STIs) operating at 77 K, enabled by the cointegration of a ZnO–Te antiambipolar switch (AAS) and vertically stacked ZnO/Te complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) using a BEOL-compatible low-temperature process (≤150 °C). Operation at 77 K not only isolates the intrinsic pull-middle switching mechanism by suppressing thermally activated off-currents but also establishes the architecture’s immediate viability for extreme-environment computing, such as radiation-hardened space data centers and cryogenic aerospace systems. In this architecture, the ZnO–Te AAS acts as an independent pull-middle device connected to an explicit Vdd/2 node, while the ZnO and Te FETs in the CFET serve as the pull-down and pull-up devices, respectively. Unlike conventional ternary logic schemes governed by precise pull-up/pull-down current matching, by explicitly clamping the intermediate state, this architecture structurally prevents variation-induced voltage shifts and suppresses static power dissipation. Consequently, the proposed STI exhibits a narrow middle-state voltage distribution across 25 cells and achieves an I/O swing ratio of 1, with cascaded operation without level-restoring circuitry supported by measurement-calibrated circuit simulations. Ultimately, this vertically integrated ZnO/Te STI offers a compact and variation-tolerant platform for cryogenic logic, while presenting a material-optimization pathway toward room-temperature multivalued systems.

works.title: MXene-PS-Based Soft Actuator with Deformation Reversal Capability through Time-Sequence Difference of Asymmetric Water Absorption Kinetics
works.abstract: Abstract Many soft actuators have been developed to achieve bending deformation under external stimuli through asymmetric structures or nonuniform material distributions. However, most existing actuators can only produce bending in a single direction, and developing soft actuators with deformation reversal capability remains a challenge. To address this issue, this study proposes an MXene-PS/MXene bilayer soft actuator, which is fabricated by sequential vacuum-assisted filtration, resulting in a loose MXene-PS top layer and a dense MXene bottom layer. The MXene-PS layer features a high water absorption/desorption rate but low capacity, while the MXene layer exhibits a low rate but high capacity. This complementary kinetic-capacity coupling mechanism, termed the time-sequence difference of asymmetric water absorption kinetics, enables the actuator to achieve reversible deformation reversal under NIR light and humidity stimuli. Furthermore, simply by changing the placement orientation of the actuator, two distinct self-sustained oscillation behaviors can be obtained in a humidity gradient environment, namely, periodic motion toward or away from the water surface. Leveraging this deformation reversal capability, we demonstrate two proof-of-concept applications: a biomimetic flower and a self-sustained motion sailboat. This work introduces a deformation mode and actuation principle for MXene-based soft actuators and further broadens their application prospects in biomimetic devices and soft robotics.

works.title: Nontrivial Edge Superconductivity in Dirac Superconductor PdTe2
works.abstract: Abstract Superconducting topological materials with coexisted superconductivities and topological boundary states are promising platforms for realizing intrinsic topological superconductivity. In this work, the superconducting type-II Dirac semimetal PdTe2 is shown to exhibit clear periodic critical current oscillations in perpendicular magnetic fields due to the fluxoid quantization, indicating the existence of edge superconductivity in PdTe2. Furthermore, a comparative study of the different superconducting properties of the bulk and edge of PdTe2 provides direct evidence for this edge superconductivity. More importantly, by a careful analysis of the flux penetration area, the nontrivial character of the edge superconductivity is revealed, i.e., the edge superconductivity appears not only at the physical boundary of the flake, but also at the interior interface between superconducting and normal regions of PdTe2. The emergence of nontrivial edge superconductivity, indicative of the putative bulk topological superconductivity, not only reveals the great potential of PdTe2 but also provides an experimental avenue for exploring intrinsic topological superconductivity by leveraging bulk-boundary correspondence.

works.title: Decoupling Conductivity and Interfacial State in Pristine-Like Carbon Nanotube Coatings Reveals Their Distinct Contributions to Neuronal Function
works.abstract: Abstract Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) combine high electrical conductivity, mechanical robustness, and nanoscale architecture, making them promising materials for neural interfaces. However, the strong coupling between CNT morphology, electrical transport, and surface chemistry has limited identification of the material properties that directly regulate neuronal function. Here, we establish an experimental strategy to disentangle morphology-dependent network transport from interfacial wettability using pristine-like CNT coatings. Multiwalled CNTs with comparable diameters but distinct lengths were reversibly functionalized, spray-coated, and thermally defunctionalized to produce homogeneous conductive networks while recovering pristine-like electrical transport and surface chemistry. Subsequent conditioning in phosphate-buffered saline substantially reduced surface hydrophobicity without detectable alteration of the graphitic CNT framework, generating coatings with comparable interfacial wettability but distinct network morphologies. Primary spinal cord neuron-glia cultures grown on these substrates were characterized by immunocytochemistry, electrophysiology, and calcium imaging. All CNT coatings supported comparable neuroglial density and network formation, whereas PBS-conditioned coatings, characterized by a more wettable interface, consistently exhibited enhanced spontaneous bursting and calcium activity compared with their untreated coatings. Across all conditions, neuronal network activity was more consistently associated with the initial interfacial state of CNT coatings, as experimentally reflected by their wetting behavior, than with CNT length or morphology-dependent electrical transport. These findings identify the initial CNT interfacial state, with wettability serving as an experimentally accessible descriptor, as a key design parameter for CNT-based neural interfaces. Furthermore, they suggest that the initial interfacial state may influence the subsequent evolution of the biomolecular layer at the cell-facing interface, thereby contributing to the modulation of neuronal function.

works.title: Measurement of Parity-Dependent Energy-Phase Relations in a Potential Artificial Kitaev Chain Utilizing a Transmon Qubit
works.abstract: Abstract Artificial Kitaev chains have emerged as a promising platform for realizing topological quantum computing. Once the chains are formed and Majorana zero modes are braided/fused, reading out the parity of the chains is essential for verifying the non-Abelian property of Majorana zero modes. Here, we demonstrate a transmon-based microwave probe for a four-site quantum dot–superconductor chain based on a Ge/Si nanowire. One end of the chain is incorporated into a superconducting transmon circuit, enabling spectroscopic identification of the chain’s singlet/doublet ground state and thereby inference of its total Fermion parity. We also demonstrate that, for multiple-dot chains, there are two types of 0−π transitions between different charging states: the parity-flip 0−π transition and the parity-preserved 0−π transition. Furthermore, we demonstrate electrostatic tunability of the interdot coupling. This phase-sensitive microwave platform provides a tool for studying complex hybrid superconducting quantum dot systems and for future extended artificial Kitaev chains.

works.title: Layer-Number-Controlled Symmetry Breaking and Surface-State Transport in Rhombohedral Graphene Multilayers
works.abstract: Abstract Rhombohedral multilayer graphene hosts layer-polarized flat bands, providing an intriguing platform for correlated and topological states; however, how layer number governs symmetry breaking and surface screening remains elusive. Here, we prepare rhombohedral graphene multilayers and systematically conduct electrical transport measurements. We uncover an unconventional layer dependence of phase transitions: the critical displacement field Dc for the layer-antiferromagnetic-to-semimetal transitions remains nearly constant across tetralayer to hexalayer graphene, whereas Dc for the semimetal-to-layer-polarized-insulator transition increases with layer number, defying unscreened Coulomb interaction models. In hexalayer graphene, surface-state-dominated transport emerges with Landau levels and resistive peaks predominantly controlled by adjacent gates, revealing strong interlayer screening. High magnetic fields further reveal valley-layer-locked Landau levels and dissipative states associated with interlayer backscattering, highlighting the presence of decoupled surface states. Our findings establish the layer number as a key tuning knob for engineering correlated and topological phases in rhombohedral graphene multilayers.

works.title: Revealing Polar Walls in CsPbBr3: Herringbone Structure and Formation Pathway
works.abstract: Abstract Domain walls in ferroic materials can host nanoscale functionalities absent from the periodic crystal, offering new opportunities to control electronic transport and polarization in semiconductor devices. Metal halide perovskites demonstrate important photophysical properties; however, their ferroic properties remain unclear. Here we discover a hierarchical herringbone network of polar walls within the nonpolar halide perovskite CsPbBr3 comprising ferroelastic twin walls and antiphase walls. Atomic-scale imaging reveals that both wall types comprise nanoscale regions whose inversion-symmetry is broken compared to the surrounding bulk lattice. In-situ heating experiments show that these interfaces form sequentially during symmetry-lowering phase transitions, revealing a different formation pathway compared with ‘conventional’ oxide perovskites. These polar nanowalls, together with their enclosed topology, may impact carrier transport. This reveals a previously unrecognized structural motif in CsPbBr3, providing new insights into their photophysical and optoelectronic behavior.

works.title: Ultralow Electron Temperature Plasma for Damage-Reduced Processing of High-k/Metal Gate Films toward Vertically Stacked Nanosheet Devices
works.abstract: Abstract In vertically stacked nanosheet devices, repeated plasma-processing steps are required to realize multiple threshold voltages (Vth), but such repeated exposure can accumulate plasma-induced damage (PID) in ultrathin high-k/metal gate (HKMG) stacks. Here, we demonstrate that ultralow electron temperature (ULET, Te < 1 eV) plasma generated using a DC-biased grid suppresses PID by controlling the electron temperature and ion energy distribution function (IEDF). Compared with conventional inductively coupled plasma processing at the same substrate bias (−100 V), ULET plasma reduces the mean ion energy from 131 to 101 eV and reduces the IEDF standard deviation by 44% (from 37.4 to 20.9 eV). Consequently, surface roughness decreases by up to 58%, fluorine incorporation decreases by up to 58%, and HfO2 Raman-band intensities are 1.32–1.81 times those under conventional ICP processing. These results establish electron-temperature control as a key parameter for minimizing PID in HKMG films relevant to vertically stacked nanosheet devices.

works.title: Magnetic Exciton-Based On-Chip Optical Attenuators Using CrSBr
works.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors, in which excitonic resonances are coupled directly to the underlying spin order, offer a fundamentally distinct route to active photonic functionality unattainable in conventional dielectrics. The van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr exemplifies this class: its sharp excitons exhibit large oscillator strengths and energies that are continuously and reversibly tunable through the magnetic state of the material, producing dramatic field-induced changes in the permittivity. Here, we exploit this magneto-excitonic response to realize compact, magnetically tunable optical attenuators in standard silicon nitride waveguides. We demonstrate up to 2.5 dB/μm continuous attenuation from CrSBr flakes under in-plane magnetic fields below 1 T. We further show that the device response depends nontrivially on the CrSBr thickness through coupled-mode physics with the polarity of the field response inverting between the perturbative and strongly coupled regimes. This work highlights two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors as a promising materials platform for compact, continuously reconfigurable control of guided light.

works.title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead
Self‐Healing Electrothermal Anti‐Icing/De‐Icing Composites With Excellent Superhydrophobicity
works.abstract: This study addresses the high energy consumption, susceptibility to superhydrophobic performance degradation, and insufficient durability of electrothermal anti-icing/de-icing composites by developing a self-healing superhydrophobic/electrothermal composite structure (SS-EC) consisting of a porous polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) thermal insulation layer, a graphene electrothermal layer, and a fluorinated boron nitride/self-healing polyurethane (F-BN/PUU) superhydrophobic layer. The SS-EC exhibits excellent wettability, self-healing capability, electrothermal conversion performance, and anti-icing/de-icing performance, with a water contact angle of 155° and a sliding angle of 6.4°, surface scratches can be repaired within 2 h of electrical heating, while the contact angle remains above 145.2° after five healing cycles; under -5 and -15°C conditions, the icing delay times reach 1415 and 1012 s, respectively, while the corresponding de-icing times are only 44 and 54 s. The structure achieves synergistic optimization of multiple functionalities, providing a new strategy for the design of long-life, low-energy-consumption anti-icing/de-icing materials.

works.title: Bioactive metal-phenolic network and prebiotic hydrogel synergize with mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles for microenvironment-modulating therapy of inflammatory bowel disease
works.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MVs) hold great promise for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) therapy. However, oral delivery of MVs therapeutic efficacy is severely compromised by the harsh gastrointestinal environment and the hostile inflammatory milieu, characterized by excessive oxidative stress and dysbiosis. To surmount these biological barriers, we engineered Inu@MPN@MV, a multifunctional oral delivery platform that integrates MVs with a caffeic acid-Fe³⁺ metal-phenolic network (MPN) coating and an inulin-based hydrogel matrix. In this synergistic system, the inulin hydrogel provides gastric protection and enables colon-specific release, while simultaneously functioning as a prebiotic to foster a beneficial microbial niche. Concurrently, the MPN coating endows the vesicles with potent ROS-scavenging capabilities, shielding them from oxidative damage and promoting their accumulation at inflamed sites. In a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis model, oral administration of Inu@MPN@MV yielded superior therapeutic outcomes compared to controls, effectively ameliorating clinical symptoms, restoring epithelial barrier integrity, and mitigating oxidative injury. Mechanistically, the formulation orchestrates a synergistic interplay between the immunoregulatory cargo of MVs and the microenvironment-modulating properties of the carrier. This combination reprograms macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype, remodels gut microbiota composition, and restores metabolic homeostasis. Collectively, this study presents a rationally designed bioactive oral system where carrier components actively potentiate the intrinsic therapeutic effects of MVs, offering a robust strategy for IBD management. Graphic abstract illustrating the multi-functional synergistic regulatory mechanism of Inu@MPN@MV in the treatment of IBD. Inu@MPN@MV is designed to protect MV during gastrointestinal transit, enable colonic release and retention, scavenge reactive oxygen species, modulate gut microbiota, regulate macrophage polarization, and promote epithelial barrier repair in DSS-induced colitis

works.title: Nanobodies in precision oncology from target recognition to tumor-state-matched therapy
works.abstract: Nanobodies, the variable domains of camelid heavy-chain-only antibodies, are increasingly viewed as more than compact affinity reagents and are being developed as versatile components of precision oncology. Their small size, high stability, convex paratopes and ease of genetic or chemical engineering create a pharmacological design space that differs from that of conventional monoclonal antibodies. These properties can support rapid lesion access, rapid systemic clearance, modular multivalency, fusion to proteins or incorporation into cell-based recognition systems, and conjugation to radionuclides, cytotoxins, photosensitizers and nanocarriers. In this review, we propose that nanobody development in oncology is shifting from a target-centric approach toward tumor-state-matched pharmacology. We organize the field around six linked domains: molecular imaging and patient stratification, payload delivery and targeted therapy, immune engineering and checkpoint modulation, tumor microenvironment targeting, target blockade and degradation, and translational evidence standards for clinical implementation. Across these areas, precision is not defined by target positivity alone. It depends on alignment among target accessibility, VHH format, pharmacokinetics, payload mechanism, the tumor microenvironment and longitudinal biomarker readouts. We also outline the evidence needed to advance nanobody platforms from well-characterized preclinical constructs toward clinical use. These requirements include lesion-level imaging, format-specific pharmacology, mechanistic validation, safety and CMC assessment, and clinical trial designs in which VHH-derived readouts are linked to treatment decisions. This framework may help distinguish settings in which VHHs offer a practical advantage from those better served by other modalities. Nanobodies in precision oncology: from target recognition to tumor-state-matched therapy. This schematic summarizes the proposed tumor-state-matched framework for VHH-based oncology. VHH modules can support molecular imaging and patient stratification, payload delivery, immune engineering, tumor-microenvironment targeting, target blockade, cell-state control and degradation, and translational evidence generation. Together, these functions form a conceptual, hypothesis-generating adaptive loop linking lesion-level information with format selection, therapeutic intervention, monitoring and clinical decision-making. VHH, variable domain of a camelid heavy-chain-only antibody; TME, tumor microenvironment; CAFs, cancer-associated fibroblasts; CAR-NK, chimeric antigen receptor natural killer cell; CAR-T, chimeric antigen receptor T cell; ECM, extracellular matrix; NDC, nanobody-drug conjugate; NK, natural killer cell; PET, positron emission tomography; SPECT, single-photon emission computed tomography.

works.title: Correction: Injectable hydrogels with ROS-triggered drug release enable the co-delivery of antibacterial agent and anti-inflammatory nanoparticle for periodontitis treatment
Functionally modular hydrogel enables dynamic sensing and adaptive regulation for wound regeneration
works.abstract: Impaired wound healing, typified by diabetic ulcers, is driven by sustained inflammation, compromised angiogenesis, and a susceptibility to infection, which collectively disrupt tissue repair and functional regeneration. To address this challenge, therapeutic systems capable of dynamically sensing and actively modulating the wound milieu are urgently needed. Here, we present a functionally compartmentalized theranostic hydrogel platform that integrates real‑time infection monitoring with coordinated immunomodulatory and pro-angiogenic regulation. The system comprises a sensing base layer with high-sensitivity resistive temperature response via ion-doping, enabling real-time detection of local temperature elevation associated with infection, and a therapeutic layer containing engineered microspheres loaded with anti-inflammatory diclofenac sodium and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), enabling temperature-triggered anti-inflammatory modulation alongside sustained pro-angiogenic support. In a diabetic full-thickness wound model, the hydrogel platform demonstrated real‑time monitoring capability and multifunctional therapeutic activity: it effectively suppressed excessive inflammation, enhanced vascular network formation, accelerated wound closure by approximately 80%, improved collagen organization, and promoted functional skin regeneration. By integrating dynamic sensing with on‑demand drug release, this sense-and-respond strategy offers a modular and adaptive platform for precision management of chronic, hard‑to‑heal wounds. The functionally compartmentalized theranostic hydrogel platform enables real-time monitoring of diabetic wounds while promoting tissue regeneration through inflammation regulation, macrophage polarization, and enhanced angiogenesis.

works.title: Lactobacillus reuteri extracellular vesicles alleviate septic liver injury via cGAS-STING-dependent macrophage reprogramming
works.abstract: Sepsis-associated liver injury (SALI) is highly lethal and primarily driven by dysregulated macrophage responses, yet safe and targeted interventions remain limited. Probiotic-derived bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) offer a promising naturally-derived, cell-free nanotherapeutic alternative, but their precise immunomodulatory mechanisms and intracellular targets remain undefined. Here, we demonstrate that Lactobacillus reuteri-derived BEVs (BEV L. reuteri ) effectively mitigate SALI by reprogramming hepatic macrophages from a pro-inflammatory M1 toward a reparative M2 state. Mechanistically, internalized BEV L. reuteri preserve mitochondrial structural integrity and prevent the cytosolic leakage of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA). This upstream protection significantly restricts the activation of the mtDNA-cGAS-STING-NF-κB inflammatory cascade, serving as a crucial blockade that drives the macrophages’ anti-inflammatory phenotypic switch. Furthermore, utilizing systemically administered myeloid-specific STING conditional knockout mice, we confirm that the hepatoprotective and systemic therapeutic effects of BEV L. reuteri strictly depend on the suppression of macrophage STING signaling. BEV L. reuteri fundamentally intercept the pathogenic mitochondria-STING crosstalk to resolve macrophage-driven systemic inflammation. These findings highlight the potential of utilizing specific Gram-positive bacterial nanovesicles as a biologically safe, highly biocompatible, and targeted nanotherapeutic strategy for sepsis and related severe acute inflammatory disorders. BEV L. reuteri protects against sepsis-induced liver injury by targeting the cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Internalized BEV L. reuteri prevent mitochondrial DNA leakage, thereby silencing the STING/NF-κB inflammatory cascade and restoring hepatic homeostasis

works.title: Core-shell nanocarriers for brain delivery of dopamine and dopaminergic therapeutics: integrating materials design, electrochemical validation, and multiscale computational modelling
works.abstract: Dopaminergic dysfunction is a central feature of neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders, most prominently Parkinson’s disease (PD), with additional relevance for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and major depressive disorder (MDD). Direct therapeutic delivery of dopamine remains difficult because dopamine is chemically labile, rapidly metabolized in the periphery, and does not use an established endogenous transporter to cross the intact blood–brain barrier (BBB). L-DOPA presents a distinct delivery problem: it crosses the BBB through the large neutral amino acid transporter LAT1 but is susceptible to peripheral decarboxylation and catechol-O-methylation. These payload-specific differences preclude direct extrapolation between dopamine- and L-DOPA-loaded delivery systems. This review critically evaluates core–shell and related structured nanocarriers investigated for dopamine, L-DOPA, and selected dopaminergic therapeutics. The analysis covers mesoporous silica, biodegradable polymers, lipid-based systems, metal–silica constructs, metal–organic frameworks, and hybrid organic–inorganic interfaces. Particular emphasis is placed on how core and shell composition affect loading, chemical stability, release, nano–bio interactions, and experimentally measured transport endpoints. Evidence is classified as physicochemical, cellular, BBB-model-based, animal-based, or clinical, and endothelial association, model-barrier transport, brain-associated signal, pharmacodynamic benefit, and intact-carrier transcytosis are treated as distinct outcomes. Current evidence is strongest for formulation-dependent control of loading and release and, in selected systems, reduced dopamine oxidation. BBB-related evidence is more limited and heterogeneous: some polymeric and lipid formulations have been examined in endothelial models, and a smaller number of systems have produced brain-associated or pharmacodynamic effects in rodents. However, these findings do not generally establish delivery of an intact carrier to brain parenchyma, and no dopamine- or L-DOPA-loaded nanocarrier has yet demonstrated clinical efficacy.
