Electrochemical methods provide sensitive tools for studying dopamine redox chemistry and release, but evidence from endogenous dopamine sensing should not be interpreted as direct validation of a therapeutic nanocarrier. Similarly, computational approaches can generate testable hypotheses concerning interfacial binding, shell transport, release, and systemic disposition, but currently require formulation-specific experimental calibration. By integrating an evidence-based classification of the literature with payload-specific materials analysis, electrochemical validation, and multiscale modelling, this review identifies where experimental support is robust, where conclusions remain formulation- or model-dependent, and which validation steps are required before dopaminergic core–shell nanocarriers can be considered clinically competitive.

works.title: Phage@CeO₂ nanozyme nanoplatform: concurrent bactericidal and detoxifying therapy for sepsis
works.abstract: Sepsis caused by drug-resistant bacteria remains a global health crisis. Under such circumstances, phage therapy represents a promising option. However, phage-mediated bacterial lysis process can release a large amount of lipopolysaccharide (LPS), which in turn triggers inflammatory storms. Herein, we equipped phage with LPS-degrading CeO₂ nanozymes (X03@CeO₂). In vitro, X03@CeO₂ achieved 99.99% bactericidal efficiency against Pseudomonas aeruginosa ( P. aeruginosa ), 63.76% biofilm clearance, and reduced lysis-released LPS to 49.60%. It protected cells from LPS-induced inflammation, as evidenced by the prevention of cell death, normalization of interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α levels, inhibition of reactive oxygen species production, and blockade of Toll-like receptor 4 activation. In a P. aeruginosa -induced sepsis mouse model, X03@CeO₂ boosted 24-h survival to 87.50%, reduced blood bacterial load and LPS content, and reversed hematological abnormalities and multi-organ damage. X03@CeO₂ not only eradicates pathogens but also degrades leaked virulence factors, thereby mitigating the excessive host immune response. This multimodal strategy presents a promising therapeutic approach for drug-resistant bacterial sepsis.

works.title: Sphinganine (d17:0)-enriched outer membrane vesicles from Parabacteroides goldsteinii alleviate obesity via modulating mitochondrial dynamics
works.abstract: Obesity, a global crisis linking metabolic syndrome and inflammation, remains inadequately addressed. In this study, we found that outer membrane vesicles derived from Parabacteroides goldsteinii (PGOMV) were more effective than live or pasteurized bacteria in alleviating high‑fat diet (HFD)‑induced obesity. Multi-omics analysis indicates that PGOMV regulates metabolic homeostasis by modulating the levels of key metabolites such as 3-hydroxybutyric acid and by modulating the gut microbiota. Its key bioactive component, sphinganine (d17:0, SA), directly binds to the mitochondrial fission proteins DRP1 and MFF, inhibiting excessive fission, thereby alleviating oxidative stress and inflammation, and disrupting the lipid–inflammation–oxidative damage vicious cycle. Based on this, we engineered an orally deliverable SA‑enriched system, PGOMV@SA. In models of HFD-induced obesity and obesity-comorbid psoriasis, PGOMV@SA simultaneously ameliorated metabolic disorders and inflammatory skin lesions. This study demonstrates that SA delivered via bacterial vesicles exhibits dual metabolic and immunomodulatory functions, providing a novel nanotherapeutic strategy for obesity‑associated inflammatory diseases. Parabacteroides goldsteinii -derived outer membrane vesicles (PGOMVs) are enriched with active components such as sphinganine (d17:0, SA), effectively alleviating obesity and metabolic inflammation. To further enhance its therapeutic efficacy, we engineered PGOMV@SA, a nanotherapeutic targeting the gut–liver axis. Its cargo, SA, directly binds to DRP1 and MFF, thereby blocking pathological mitochondrial fission and mitigating metabolic inflammation, providing a novel microbiome-inspired intervention strategy for obesity and related inflammatory diseases.

works.title: Correction: Docetaxel-loaded M1 macrophage-derived exosomes for a safe and efficient chemoimmunotherapy of breast cancer
Engineered Milk‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles Integrate PCSK9 Silencing and Inflammation Modulation for Hyperlipidemia Therapy
works.abstract: Hyperlipidemia is a systemic metabolic disorder closely associated with chronic inflammation. Effective management requires integrated strategies that simultaneously lower lipid level and attenuate inflammation. Nucleic acid therapeutics, such as proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) siRNA, represent a breakthrough in lipid-lowering therapy. However, they either lack direct anti-inflammatory effects (GalNAc-siRNA) or are prone to triggering unintended inflammatory responses themselves such as lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). Milk-derived extracellular vesicles (MDEs) emerge as naturally anti-inflammatory nanocarriers that suppress key pro-inflammatory cytokines by 30.0%-96.5% in vitro. However, MDEs predominantly undergo endocytic trafficking with substantial endosomal/lysosomal sequestration, which can limit productive cytosolic siRNA delivery. To address this, we developed engineered MDEs by incorporating 30.0% (w/w) probiotic-derived glycolipids into their membranes to facilitate early endosomal escape. When loaded with PCSK9 siRNA, the engineered MDEs achieved a remarkable silencing efficiency of 90.2 ± 0.2%, significantly outperforming both unmodified MDEs and conventional LNPs. In hyperlipidemic mice, systemic administration of engineered MDEs improved serum lipid profiles, reduced lipid accumulation and systemic inflammation, and showed a favorable safety profile under the conditions examined. Collectively, this work provides a promising nucleic acid delivery platform based on engineered MDEs for enhanced hyperlipidemia therapy through simultaneous lipid-lowering and anti-inflammatory effects.

works.title: Establishment of a Responsive Tooth‐on‐a‐Chip Platform for the Assessment of Regenerative Factors in Dental Tissue Regeneration
works.abstract: Tooth formation relies on reciprocal signaling between embryological dental epithelial (DE) and mesenchymal (DM) cells, orchestrating the formation of enamel, dentin, and vascularized pulp. Current regenerative strategies aim to recreate DE-DM signaling, yet responsive in vitro platforms that faithfully reconstruct this interface and enable benchmarking of candidate cues are unavailable. Herein, a tooth-on-a-chip with a reconstructed DE-DM interface was tested for cue-specific tissue maturation in vitro. The platform comprises a polydimethylsiloxane microfluidic device integrating a fibrin-based mesenchymal compartment with an overlying epithelial layer. The system was exposed to two developmental inducers, sequential fibroblast growth factor 10 (FGF10) and bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP4), and BMP2, as well as the clinically used enamel matrix derivative Emdogain, to emulate distinct inductive environments. The platform robustly supported interface formation and revealed cue-specific maturation trajectories with high experimental reproducibility. Notably, Emdogain induced enamel organ-like structural maturation, revealing a previously unrecognized pro-enamel (amelogenic) activity of a biomaterial that has been used clinically for over three decades. Together, these findings validated the tooth-on-a-chip system as a biologically relevant in vitro test platform, providing a translational framework for benchmarking regenerative cues and guiding the development of dental regenerative therapies.

works.title: A Novel 3D Model Co‐Culturing Breast Cancer Cells in Direct Contact with Patient‐Derived Mature Adipocytes Demonstrates Cell‐Type Specific Alterations in Phenotype and Chemosensitivity
works.abstract: Mature adipocytes within the breast tumour microenvironment contribute a significant role in malignant progression. At the invasive front of breast tumours, mature adipocytes undergo morphological and phenotypic changes and may provide metabolic support to fuel tumour growth and spread. However, investigations into mature adipocyte-breast cancer interactions have been limited by the lack of suitable in vitro models. Here, we developed an innovative 3D in vitro co-culture system allowing direct contact between patient-derived mature breast adipocytes and breast cancer cell lines, to systematically examine cell-cell interactions over 21 days. In co-culture with triple negative breast cancer cells (MDA-MB-231), mature adipocytes exhibited loss of Perilipin 1 (PLIN1) expression and were associated with reduced chemotherapy responsiveness and increased Major Vault Protein (MVP) abundance. In contrast, Luminal A (MCF7) breast cancer cells displayed increased expression of mesenchymal markers (N-cadherin and Vimentin), consistent with a partial epithelial to mesenchymal transition. The direct 3D co-culture model developed by this work provides a novel platform to study breast cancer subtype-specific interactions between mature adipocytes and cancer cells, revealing interactions associated with chemotherapy responsiveness and malignant progression.

works.title: Adaptive MSC@ECM/PRP Matrix Sustains Transplanted Stem Cells and Restores Endometrial Regeneration
works.abstract: Stem cell-based therapy holds promise for endometrial regeneration but suffers from rapid cell loss in the oxidative and cytokine-deficient uterine niche. We developed a biomimetic decellularized extracellular matrix integrated with platelet-rich plasma (ECM/PRP) that serves as a bioactive cytokine reservoir designed to construct a supportive local microenvironment capable of retaining cytokines and maintaining transplanted cell viability. The ECM binds PRP-derived cytokines, stabilizing their bioactivity and converting burst release into sustained signaling. Adhered human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (HUC-MSCs) respond to these anchored cues, with changes in mitochondrial electron transport activity correlating with enhanced cellular antioxidant capacity. This ECM/PRP composite improves HUC-MSC survival, alleviating intracellular ROS, sustain their paracrine secretion under the IUA pathological microenvironment, and elevate the number of surviving transplanted HUC-MSCs in vivo. In a murine intrauterine adhesion (IUA) model, MSC@ECM/PRP enhanced endometrial proliferation and microvessel density while reducing collagen deposition. These coordinated changes facilitate reconstruction of physiological endometrial structure and produce a marked improvement in fertility relative to the untreated IUA group. Collectively, the adaptive MSC@ECM/PRP scaffold protects transplanted HUC-MSCs against oxidative stress in the IUA microenvironment, facilitates endometrial structural repair and angiogenesis, suppresses excessive fibrosis, and achieves satisfactory therapeutic and fertility-restoring effects in IUA.

works.title: Sequential Modeling of Fibrotic and Mineralizing Osteoarthritis‐Like Remodeling in hDPSC‐Derived Cartilage Microtissues
works.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) involves alterations in cartilage mechanics, matrix composition, and mineralization, yet in vitro models that resolve remodeling transitions remain limited. Scaffold-free cartilage microtissues derived from human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs) are subjected to sequential dynamic rocking culture and triiodothyronine (T3) treatment. Dynamic rocking produces superficial Col I-positive fibrotic and matrix-degrading changes, whereas T3 induces proteoglycan loss, increased Col I and MMP13, irregular mineral deposition, and altered nanomechanical properties, defining a mixed terminal catabolic and mineralizing OA-like state. Transcriptomic profiling shows stage-associated reorganization rather than uniform pathway activation. In T3-treated microtissues, ATF6-associated ER-stress abnormalities include ER cisternal dilation and increased ATF6 signal. Targeted ATF6 knockdown reduces ATF6 signal, ER dilation, extracellular-matrix disorganization, and ER-stress/proteostasis and inflammatory/catabolic transcriptional module scores, supporting ATF6-associated signaling as a functionally relevant component of this degenerative state. In mouse temporomandibular joint and knee OA models, intra-articular Ad-shATF6 is associated with partial cartilage preservation and subchondral-bone indices shifted toward control ranges.

works.title: Dynamically Repairable Hydration‐Lubricating Microspheres for Osteoarthritis Therapy
works.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) progression is closely associated with the deterioration of joint lubrication. Although surface-grafted lubrication coatings can reduce friction, they are susceptible to mechanical damage under repetitive shear stress, resulting in rapid lubrication failure. Therefore, constructing a dynamically reconfigurable lubrication interface capable of continuous restoration under friction is critical for long-term joint protection. Herein, a dynamically self-repairing hydration lubrication microsphere system (HMs-CD@Ad-PMPC) is developed based on host-guest interactions. β-Cyclodextrin (β-CD)-functionalized silk fibroin microspheres dynamically recruit adamantane (Ad)-terminated poly(2-methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine) (PMPC) brushes through supramolecular host-guest recognition, thereby establishing a robust yet reversible hydration lubrication interface. Under shear stress during joint motion, partial dissociation of Ad-PMPC chains induces transient lubrication attenuation, while spontaneous molecular reassembly rapidly restores the lubrication interface upon stress release, thereby enabling dynamic self-repairing lubrication. In vitro, HMs-CD@Ad-PMPC maintains a stable low coefficient of friction (COF, 0.03-0.04) under cyclic shear conditions, exhibiting excellent wear resistance and long-term lubrication stability. In vivo, the system effectively reduces joint wear, preserves cartilage integrity, and significantly delays OA progression. This work establishes a dynamic lubrication strategy capable of restoring interfacial functionality under mechanical stress, providing a promising platform for long-term joint lubrication and OA therapy.

works.title: Directional and Tunable Evaporation of Liquid Marbles via an Asymmetric and Reconfigurable Architecture Synergizing Permeable‐Impermeable Domains
works.abstract: Particle-armored liquid droplets (liquid marbles) have emerged as a multifunctional microfluidic system for sensing, active-material delivery, biosynthesis, and analysis, owing to their ease of fabrication, versatility, nonstickiness, and gas permeability. While the porous characteristic of the liquid marbles is essential for mediating interactions with the surrounding environment, it inevitably leads to evaporation-driven mass loss, limiting their lifetime, stability, and effective utilization. Furthermore, evaporation dynamics and structural integrity of the marbles are subject to substrate-dependent effects that modulate thermal and vapor transport through the particulate shell. We address these challenges by introducing a hybrid interfacial design: a dual-faced liquid marble comprising permeable (particulate) and impermeable domains, namely, a hybrid Janus liquid marble (hJLM), with a tunable structural profile. The asymmetric structure of the hJLMs enables tunability and substrate-independent directional control over the evaporation of encapsulated liquid. The hJLMs exhibit greater resistance to operational conditions, including substrate type (solid or liquid), temperature, and external compression pressure, thereby enhancing their lifespan and mechanical integrity. We demonstrate the versatility and reusability of the hJLMs by reconfiguring them with different liquid-particle combinations. We believe that the unique structure and enhanced functionality of the hJLMs could improve the sustainability and efficiency of droplet-based platforms.

works.title: C-Doped SnO2-Integrated MoSe2/MoS2 Heterostructure as a High-Performance Bifunctional Electrocatalyst for Overall Water Splitting
works.abstract: Abstract Overall water splitting powered by low-cost and efficient electrocatalysts offers a promising pathway for the sustainable production of H2 energy. Here, we have successfully designed and prepared a C-SnO2-MoSe2/MoS2 composite material comprising carbon-doped SnO2 and layered 2D materials (MoSe2 and MoS2) for overall water splitting. The composite exhibited attractive electrocatalytic activities for both HER and OER, possessing very low overpotentials and Tafel slopes, along with high faradaic efficiencies. Notably, the prepared composite material demonstrated bifunctional electrocatalytic activity for efficient overall water splitting, achieving a low cell potential of 1.72 V at 10 mA cm−2. Along with this high electrocatalytic efficiency, the composite presented long-term operational stability up to 90 h in overall water splitting.

works.title: Bridging Atom Engineering of Naphthalene Diimide-Based Semiconducting Polymer Dots for NIR-II Imaging-Guided Tumor Photodynamic and Photothermal Therapy
works.abstract: Abstract Near-infrared second-window fluorescence imaging (NIR-II FI)-guided synergistic photothermal therapy (PTT) and type-I photodynamic therapy (PDT) hold great promise for noninvasive tumor treatment. However, it is remains highly challenging to develop phototheranostic agents with desired performances, and the systematic exploration of naphthalene diimide (NDI)-based conjugated polymers in this field is still limited. Herein, three NDI-based semiconducting polymers (Si-NDI, C-NDI, and N-NDI)-derived Pdots with various bridge atoms (C, N, and Si) in the cyclopentadithiophene donor units are rationally constructed by nanoprecipitation. These Pdots exhibit uniform spherical morphologies with hydrodynamic diameters of ∼30−40 nm, excellent colloidal stability, and efficient passive tumor targeting via the enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect. Among them, C-NDI Pdots exhibit the most superior performance, including robust NIR-II fluorescence, efficient type I reactive oxygen species (O2•−/•OH) generation, and high photothermal conversion efficiency (58.8%). The as-prepared C-NDI Pdots are further applied for efficient tumor cell ablation in vitro and achieve NIR-II imaging-guided synergistic PTT/PDT tumor ablation in 4T1 tumor-bearing nude mouse with satisfactory results. We believe that this work not only provides outstanding NDI Pdots-based phototheranostic nanoagents for non-invasive tumor treatment but also offers a bridge atom tuning strategy for the design of high-performance multimodality phototheranostic nanoagents.

works.title: Co-Doped [Ni(1-ipIM)3·B6O7(OH)6]·[H3BO3]·2.5H2O via In-Situ Pyrolysis Achieving CoNi Alloy Nanocrystals for High-Performance Zinc−Air Batteries
works.abstract: Abstract A series of CoNi bimetallic borates [NixCo1−x(1-ipIM)3·B6O7(OH)6]·[H3BO3]·3.5H2O (x = 0.9, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3) have been synthesized, in which the oxoboron clusters in the structure contain abundant hydrogen-bonding sites, which are prone to form an open framework and a supramolecular porous structure, providing sufficient free space for catalytic reactions. The borates were converted into CoNi alloy nanocrystals loaded on amorphous carbon via in-situ pyrolysis. Notably, these are the first CoNi alloy nanocrystal oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalysts derived from borate precursors that exhibited excellent ORR activity in alkaline media with a half-wave potential as high as 0.881 V, which is slightly better than commercial Pt/C. When applied in zinc−air batteries (ZABs), they exhibited outstanding electrochemical performance, especially a cycling stability of up to 800 h. The superior catalytic performance is attributed to the synergistic effect between Co and Ni, which provides ideas for the development of efficient borate-based ORR catalysts through multi-metallic synergy and promotes their application in high-performance ZABs.

works.title: Ion-Conductive Hydrogels with Adhesion and Self-Healing Properties for Flexible Wearable Sensors
works.abstract: Abstract The application of flexible sensors in long-term wearable activity and micro-expression monitoring is limited by signal drift due to interface delamination, material damage, and insufficient sensitivity. To address this challenge, an ionically conductive hydrogel (PAMTC-Zr) integrating self-adhesion, self-healing, and high sensitivity enabled by its nanoscale features was developed in this study using digital light processing (DLP) three-dimensional (3D) printing. This hydrogel was developed based on a copolymer network of acrylamide and core−shell nanostructured tannic acid-coated cellulose nanocrystals (TA@CNC) that provide abundant nanoscale interactions. The hydrogel-based sensors accurately detected intense movements of joints, such as fingers and wrists, while precisely distinguishing subtle movements, such as smiling and cheek bulging. The integration of this hydrogel with DLP 3D printing for the fabrication of customized curved surfaces, holds promise for the developing conformable, real-time, multimodal skin patches. This study provides a practical nanoscale design strategy for developing next-generation flexible health monitoring sensors that can simultaneously monitor macroscopic movements and microscopic facial expressions.

works.title: Covalently Linked Porphyrin-g-C3N4 Nanosheet with Intrinsically Integrated Catalytic Sites Promoting Efficient Photocatalytic H2 Evolution
works.abstract: Abstract Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4 and g-CN) is a promising metal-free semiconductor for photocatalytic solar energy conversion, yet its practical application is hindered by high charge recombination rates, limited visible light absorption, and lack of catalytic centers. Molecular doping offers an effective strategy to address these limitations by incorporating functional molecular fragments within the CN nanosheet, enhancing charge separation and electronic properties without the interfacial losses typical of heterojunctions. In this work, we report the rational design of an integrated porphyrin-CN covalent hybrid catalyst via a molecular doping approach. A meso-tetrakis(4-cyanophenyl)porphyrin derivative is functionalized to form polymerizable 2,4-diamino-1,3,5-triazine (DAT) domains, enabling copolymerization with melamine. The resulting porphyrin-doped CN hybrids with intrinsic catalytic centers exhibited extended light absorption and suppressed radiative recombination. Post-synthetic metalation at intrinsically integrated catalytic sites with Ni2+ or Co2+ ions yields efficient solar-driven H2 Evolution. This strategy demonstrates a versatile platform for constructing multifunctional molecular CN hybrids tailored for solar-energy applications. Under photocatalytic conditions using visible light, the Ni- and Co-based porphyrin-modified CN hybrids show a hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) rate of 640 μmol·g−1 h−1 and 720 μmol·g−1 h−1, respectively, in the presence of ascorbic acid as a sacrificial agent.

works.title: Biomimetic Nanozyme-Decoys Reprogram Immune Niches to Intercept Colitis-Carcinoma Transition
works.abstract: Abstract Colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC) arises from chronic inflammatory niches characterized by persistent oxidative stress and dysregulated immune cell recruitment. Current anti-inflammatory therapies provide only transient symptom relief and fail to prevent malignant progression due to their inability to simultaneously mitigate oxidative injury and immune chemotaxis. Our analysis of clinical samples revealed markedly elevated C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CXCL2) in intestinal tissues from patients with inflammatory bowel disease and CAC, implicating the CXCL2-CXCR2 (C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 2) axis in driving excessive neutrophil and macrophage infiltration and fostering tumorigenesis. Herein, we report a biomimetic nanozyme (PB@ECM) that reprograms inflammatory immune niches to intercept CAC progression. PB@ECM integrates a Prussian blue nanozyme core with genetically engineered macrophage membranes, enabling concurrent scavenging of reactive oxygen species through superoxide dismutase- and catalase-like activities and sequestration of CXCL2 via membrane-displayed CXCR2 receptors. In murine models of colitis and CAC, PB@ECM significantly alleviated intestinal inflammation, suppressed neutrophil and macrophage infiltration, and effectively inhibited colitis-carcinoma transition. Notably, treatment with PB@ECM significantly prolonged survival compared with other groups. By disrupting the pathological crosstalk between oxidative stress and immune chemotaxis, this work establishes a biomimetic nanozyme strategy for preventing inflammation-driven carcinogenesis.

works.title: Bright Alkyl Quantum Defects Govern Early Carbon Nanotube Pharmacokinetics in Mice
works.abstract: Abstract Fluorescent quantum defects in single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) are a major advance in nanocarbon research, owing to their bright, single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths and versatile conjugation chemistries for biomedical sensing and disease targeting. Here, we introduce an efficient, oxygen-free sonochemical route that generates long-chain alkyl defects, simultaneously shortening nanotubes and producing a bright, homogeneously emissive (6,5) SWCNT ensemble. Among 15 screened reactants, the branched-chain NiaproofⓇ 4, which molecular dynamics simulations show packs more densely and uniformly than linear surfactants, yields a 3.4-fold brightness enhancement and a sharp emission peak near 1108 nm. Single-particle spectroscopy reveals J-aggregate emission redshifts at high defect densities, and fibrinogen titration shows defect chemistry governs protein-driven coating displacement. Using a home-built short-wave infrared imaging system (25 mW cm–2, 989 nm excitation, 1150 nm long-pass collection), we show that these sparse defects (∼9–16 μm–1) drive different pharmacokinetics between NiaproofⓇ 4– and lipid-PEG–functionalized (6,5) at early time points, converging as protein-corona formation masks the underlying chemistry. Histology localizes the nanotubes within macrophages of mononuclear phagocyte system–associated organs. Intravenous administration (∼41 μg kg–1) causes no acute toxicity and a short ∼2-day retention. The NiaproofⓇ 4 group exhibits a reduced circulating myeloid-cell fraction following corona formation, which may reflect organ recruitment and sequestration, while the accompanying increase in CD3+ T cells may partly reflect a proportional shift in leukocyte composition.

works.title: Charge-Induced Formation and Field-Driven Directional Motion of Vacancies in a Two-Dimensional Halide
works.abstract: Abstract Controlling defect evolution in two-dimensional (2D) materials is essential for reliable nanoelectronic functionalities, yet selectively inducing defect formation and externally driven migration remains a key challenge. Here, we demonstrate two distinct mechanisms governing halogen vacancy formation and migration in a PbBr2 monolayer on highly ordered pyrolytic graphite using low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy combined with density functional theory calculations. We show that halogen vacancies reshape the local density of states and electrostatic potential beyond the immediate defect site. Crucially, electric fields and charge injection mediate distinct atomic-scale responses: tip-induced electric fields drive directional vacancy migration and coalescence, whereas charge injection from the tunneling current induces vacancy formation, with enhanced efficiency when coupling to shallow defect states. These results demonstrate that direct electrical stimuli can drive both vacancy motion and creation in a two-dimensional, predominantly ionic material system. Our findings establish a framework linking defect-induced electronic structure, local electrostatics, and externally driven atomic rearrangement under conditions relevant to device operation.

works.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Data-Driven Atomic Interplay Modulation Enables Dual-Functional High-Entropy Alloy Mediator for Li–S Batteries
works.abstract: Abstract High-entropy alloys (HEAs) have emerged as appealing candidates to achieve performance regulation in Li–S batteries. Nevertheless, the design principles and working mechanisms of HEAs for dual electrodes remain elusive because of their structural disorder and chemical complexity. Herein, we propose a data-driven maneuver to enable rapid and precise screening of a customized HEA nanocatalyst (FeCoNiCuVMn, 6E-HEAs) via a performance-oriented theoretical criterion in the realm of Li–S electrochemistry. The delicate modulation of atomic interplay in 6E-HEAs simultaneously accelerates sulfur redox kinetics and stabilizes lithium metal deposition. Consequently, Li–S batteries sustain favorable cycling performance at 1.0 C over 1000 cycles while affording a capacity decay rate of merely 0.067% per cycle. The pouch cell harvests a specific capacity of 884.8 mAh g–1 at 0.5 C with steady cyclic operation. Our study elucidates crucial roles of effective compositional gain in boosting bidirectional Li–S electrocatalysis, offering atomic-level insights into HEA design for electrocatalytic reactions.

works.title: Attempts to Understand and Manipulate the Orientation and Retention of Peptides Inside Nanopores Expand the Toolbox for Nanopore-Based Proteomics
works.abstract: Abstract Nanopore techniques have emerged as promising tools for deciphering complex proteomics from the single-molecule level by profiling individual peptides. The entry orientation of a peptide and its subsequent retention inside the nanopore are crucial for the analytical results but remain challenging to be properly defined, which limits the sensing capability of nanopore-based proteomics technology. Here, we propose that electrically driving peptide entry into α-hemolysin nanopores against opposing electroosmotic flows is a promising platform to guide the polypeptide with a preferential orientation. α-Hemolysin mutants with opposite ion selectivity have been engineered and employed to measure peptides at pH 3.8 and at alkaline pH exceeding 10.0. The impact of peptide charge distribution on the orientation has been investigated by simulating the peptide dipole moment and electrophysiology measurements. In addition, the retention position of the peptide has been altered by introducing tryptophan residues at position 125 within the β-barrel region of α-hemolysin, which increases the sensitivity for specific peptide region and enables the detection of initially inaccessible monomethylation modifications. Thus, we present a rational framework to investigate and manipulate the orientation and dwelling position of peptides inside the α-hemolysin nanopore, which can enhance our capability to profile polypeptides by using nanopore techniques.

works.title: Addressable Control of Hybrid Spin Qubit in Single-Atom Copper-Modified Fullerene
works.abstract: Developing high-dimensional solid-state quantum technologies requires overcoming the trade-off between spin dimensionality and quantum coherence. Hybrid spin architectures offer a promising solution to expand the quantum state space bottom-up by combining rapid electronic manipulation with robust nuclear phase memory. However, solid-state hybrid spin materials capable of simultaneously supporting both electron and nuclear spin manipulations remain exceedingly rare. Here, we report a Cu2+ (S = 1/2, I = 3/2) hybrid spin system dispersed in a magnetically silent C60 matrix, in which we not only demonstrate comprehensive coherent control over both electron and nuclear spin degrees of freedom but also strike a balance between spin dimensionality and coherence time. The pristine carbon environment suppresses surrounding magnetic noise, acting in tandem with dynamical decoupling to prolong the electron spin coherence time to 16.16 μs. Simultaneously, the nuclear quadrupole interaction of Cu2+ breaks the degeneracy of the nuclear spin manifold, enabling precise addressability of an eight-dimensional Hilbert space. Furthermore, strong electron-nuclear hyperfine coupling acts as a powerful lever, accelerating the nuclear spin Rabi frequency by a factor of 17. By achieving the coexistence of a large manifold of addressable levels and long-lived quantum coherence, Cu/C60 provides a high-dimensional hybrid spin node and a compelling bottom-up approach to expanding the quantum state space.

works.title: An Optoelectronic SnP2S6 Memristive Neuron for Biologically Inspired Multimodal Neuromorphic Information Processing
works.abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic systems capable of integrating multiple sensory modalities offer a promising route toward energy-efficient information processing that more closely emulates biological neural networks. Here, we demonstrate a multifunctional ITO/SnP2S6/Ti memristive neuron that combines reproducible volatile resistive switching and integrate-and-fire dynamics under electrical-pulse stimulation with wavelength-selective photoresponses and short-term optoelectronic synaptic plasticity. Leveraging these experimentally measured device characteristics, we construct a multimodal neuromorphic recognition framework that integrates volatile memristive neurons with programmable memristive synapses. Inspired by the parallel processing of visual features in the primate visual system, structural and color information are independently encoded and processed through separate electrical and optical pathways before being integrated for classification. Importantly, inference is implemented using experimentally measured neuronal firing statistics and programmed synaptic conductance states, rather than idealized device models, thereby establishing a direct link between device characteristics and system-level functionality. As a proof-of-concept, the framework is evaluated on a fruit-recognition task using a subset of the Fruits-360 image data set, achieving a classification accuracy of 94.9% through multimodal fusion and substantially outperforming recognition based on either modality alone. These results establish SnP2S6 memristive devices as a versatile platform for integrating electrical and optical neuronal functionalities and highlight their potential for hardware-realistic multimodal in-sensor neuromorphic computing.

works.title: Breaking the Capacity–Stability Trade-Off in High-Voltage LiCoO2 via Opposite Co/O Redox Activity
works.abstract: Abstract LiCoO2 (LCO) suffers from daunting capacity–stability trade-off due to deeper Co oxidation and ensuing O oxidation (O2– → Co4+ electron transfer) at high-voltage (≥4.5 V). Aggressive Co4+ and O2/On– (0 < n < 2) species result in pronounced mechanical/chemical failure and fast capacity decay. Most of the state-of-the-art solutions partially resolve these problems yet sacrificing capacity. Herein, facilitated Co3+/4+ redox and effectively restrained O redox are simultaneously achieved by amplifying Co t2g electron density of states (DOS) near the Fermi level while reducing O 2p electron DOS. Consequently, the engineered cathode harvests a remarkable initial capacity of 212.1 mAh g–1 at 4.6 V (vs 212.9 mAh g–1 of bare LCO). Moreover, advanced multiscale X-ray/electron spectroscopy and imaging techniques reveal that mitigated O redox prevents irreversible phase transitions, lattice O loss, and undesirable surface parasitic reactions. As a result, the cathode has reinforced electrochemical (capacity retention of 88.4% within 330 cycles at 5C) and thermal stability thanks to fatigue-free (de)lithiation channels, less new-generated Co3O4 layer, and inorganic-rich cathode/electrolyte interphase (CEI) film. This work provides a valuable inspiration for the electronic structure engineer of robust LCO cathode toward high operation voltages.

works.title: Ultrafast Imaging of Dynamic Disorder in Superionic Chalcocite
works.abstract: Abstract The optimal functionalities of matter often appear at emergent structural orders involving entangled changes in the lattice structures and the underlying atomic degree of freedom. Here, we report laser-induced, thermally driven dynamic structural orders evolving in the low- to high-chalcocite transition of copper(I) sulfide using time-resolved electron diffractometry in ultrafast electron microscopy. We filmed the complete phase trajectory of the transient atomic motions and the hierarchical decoupling of structural orders that unfold over time. Moreover, a transient, disordered state is unveiled. The disordered state emerges during the superionic diffusion of copper ions along a few-nanometer-thick lattice channels. Temporal gating of the various combinations of structure could expand the range of accessible functional states in matter.

works.title: Truly Asynchronous and One-Hot Constraint Probabilistic Potts Computing with Floating-Body Metal–Oxide–Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors
works.abstract: Abstract This work presents a truly asynchronous physical Potts node (TAPPN) using floating-body metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistors (FB-MOSFETs) to overcome the scalability and encoding overhead limitations of binary Ising-based probabilistic computing. The TAPPN enables native multistate representation without external random-number generators (RNGs) or complex digital arbitration by the intrinsic stochastic single-transistor latch (STL) effect and a drain-sharing configuration. The stochastic source and the one-hot constraint are realized by three transistors, and the node requires 25 transistors and 220 nW including the readout, compared with 2160 transistors and 52 μW for a self-contained digital node evaluated at the same boundary. Its truly asynchronous operation allows efficient exploration of the problem space in large-scale graph-coloring benchmarks. In simulations of the update rule, the Potts-based system achieves a higher success probability than simulated annealing (SA) and parallel tempering (PT) on graph-coloring benchmarks. For an integrated array assumed to operate at 5 MHz, the architecture is projected to reach a time-to-solution (TTS) of 3.4 μs and an energy-to-solution (ETS) of 504 nJ. This platform establishes a complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible pathway toward large-scale, multistate combinatorial optimization.

works.title: Ultrafast High-Photogain UV–Vis-NIR Broadband Photodetection in Parallelly Overlapped Stacking Type-I GaSe/MoTe2 Heterostructure
works.abstract: Abstract Broadband photodetectors are important for next-generation optoelectronic applications, ranging from fundamental science, environmental monitoring, industrial detection to artificial-intelligence-enabled Internet of Things systems, where both high responsivity and fast response are critically demanded. Typically, a trade-off exists between the two in the photogating effect, making it challenging to achieve both simultaneously. This study reports a parallelly overlapped stacking GaSe/MoTe2 heterostructure with type-I band alignment (PSH-GM), which simultaneously realizes an ultrafast photoresponse of 523 ns and a high responsivity of 8.95 × 103 A·W–1, together with a noise equivalent power of ∼0.38 × 10–14 W·Hz–1/2 and a specific detectivity of 8.01 × 1011 Jones. Furthermore, PSH-GM exhibits a responsivity of up to 103 A·W–1 over a broad spectral range of 355–1100 nm, covering the ultraviolet (UV), visible (Vis), and near-infrared (NIR) regions. The underlying photodetection mechanism of the parallelly overlapped stacking type-I heterostructure is clarified using photocurrent mapping, and the origin of the dark current shift at different operation frequencies is elucidated, both of which offer insights into the design principles of two-dimensional heterostructures optimized to simultaneously achieve high responsivity and high response bandwidth. Imaging demonstrations are conducted at 355, 520, and 850 nm, and free-space optical communication is demonstrated at 115.2 kbit·s–1, which highlights the potential of PSH-GM for broadband UV–Vis–NIR photodetection, ultrafast data communication, high-speed imaging, and integration into advanced optoelectronic systems.

works.title: Self-Assembly of Two-Dimensional Open Structures with Adjustable Square Voids
works.abstract: Abstract Self-assembly of anisotropic particles offers a powerful route to design materials with tailored microstructures. Here we investigate two-dimensional systems of patchy hard rectangles using Monte Carlo simulations and free volume theory, mapping their phase diagram across packing fractions and interaction strengths. Low attraction recovers excluded-volume phase behavior (isotropic–tetratic–smectic), while intermediate attraction strengths feature a broad isotropic–smectic coexistence region. For high interaction strengths our theory predicts, and simulations confirm, a highly ordered “weaver” phase characterized by a four-rectangle unit cell that forms a regular grid of square voids. Although the pure weaver phase forms only in a narrow window of packing fractions, it coexists with either the isotropic gas or smectic solid over a wide range of packing fractions. Patchy rectangles demonstrate how shape together with tunable interactions can be utilized to self-assemble porous materials with precisely adjustable void sizes and geometries and could be realized using DNA origami structures.

works.title: Issue Publication Information
Overcoming Oral Environmental Barriers: Nanoengineering Strategies for Antimicrobial Peptides in Biofilm-Associated Oral Diseases
works.abstract: Abstract Biofilm-associated oral diseases impose a substantial global health burden and are closely linked to systemic inflammation. Although antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) offer a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics, their therapeutic efficacy in the oral cavity is limited by barriers in the oral environment. Free AMPs are rapidly removed by salivary flow, destabilized by local proteases, and impeded by substantial diffusion barriers within mature biofilms. Nanoengineering provides a systematic approach to address these limitations. In this review, we present a barrier-oriented framework for AMP delivery and examine how nanomaterial design addresses the specific constraints of the oral environment. Interfacial engineering prolongs local retention, spatial protection preserves AMP stability, and microenvironment-responsive systems provide on-demand activation for effective biofilm disruption. Alongside these approaches, multifunctional nanosystems combining antimicrobial, immunomodulatory, and regenerative activities are discussed. Finally, key translational challenges, including biosafety, microbiome homeostasis, manufacturing, and regulatory barriers, are critically examined. This review traces the development of AMP nanoengineering from passive delivery vehicles toward precision therapeutic platforms that respond dynamically to the oral microenvironment.

works.title: A Scalable Nonsuperconducting Tunnel Junction Technology
works.abstract: Tunnel junctions are essential for various technologies ranging from classical microelectronics to quantum information and cryogenic electronics. Aluminum and its oxide (AlOx) have long dominated cryogenic and quantum tunnel junction applications for their excellent material quality and superconductivity. However, some applications require junctions to remain normal conducting, either as standalone components or integrated with superconducting circuitry. Magnetic fields, impurity doping, or proximity effects can suppress superconductivity, but often pose challenges for scalability and integration. Here, we present a CMOS-compatible normal conducting tunnel junction platform using TiW alloy electrodes and AlOx tunnel barriers, achieving high yield and uniformity through wafer-scale fabrication. As a cryogenic use-case, the wafers incorporate junction arrays designed for Coulomb blockade thermometry, confirming reliable normal conducting state performance down to 20 mK. These results demonstrate a scalable and integrable normal conducting junction technology, supporting its use in cryogenic, quantum, and nanoelectronic systems, including hybrid superconducting-normal metal circuits.

works.title: Direct Visualization of Na,K-ATPase Clustering by 3D DNA-PAINT MINFLUX Nanoscopy
works.abstract: Abstract The sodium–potassium pump (Na,K-ATPase) is an essential plasma-membrane transporter that consumes 20%–30% of cellular energy, and up to approximately 50% in the kidneys. Whether it assembles into defined oligomers in its native membrane has been debated for decades. Resolving this question demands imaging precision at molecular length scales. Here, we combine 3D MINFLUX nanoscopy with DNA-PAINT to map EGFP-tagged Na,K-ATPase α1 and β1 subunits in mammalian cells with 3–5 nm localization precision. We introduce two point-cloud analysis tools: a data-driven algorithm that assigns localizations to the apical or basal membrane, removing trans-membrane artifacts, and a sequential nearest-neighbor analysis that estimates oligomer stoichiometry without structural priors. Both subunits show preferential nearest-neighbor distances of approximately 7 nm, direct evidence of dimerization, and are further organized into nanoclusters of approximately 7 to 12 molecules. These results provide direct structural evidence of Na,K-ATPase self-assembly and a framework for quantifying membrane-protein clustering at single-molecule resolution.

works.title: Machine-Learning-Accelerated Metallene Stabilization from High-Throughput Sandwich Modeling
works.abstract: Abstract Metallenes have appealing properties, but stabilizing them in a monolayer phase poses synthesis challenges. A recent experiment showed that the van der Waals squeezing method can stabilize certain metallenes in a MoS2 sandwich. This pioneering work motivates systematic studies, but such studies are experimentally impractical, while first-principles modeling remains prohibitive. Here, using universal machine-learning interatomic potentials, we constructed 1620 metallene sandwich heterostructures containing 6 different sandwich layers and 45 metals. We performed phonon calculations, which revealed 1208 dynamically stable structures and narrowed them to 331 after structural filtering. We found that Se-based transition-metal dichalcogenides stabilize metallenes effectively. Specifically, hexagonal and buckled hexagonal crystal lattices exhibit the greatest stability. We further evaluated the thermal stability of selected heterostructures with density-functional-theory molecular dynamics simulations at room temperature. By uncovering the physical and chemical factors that govern metallenes stabilization, our results provide systematic insights to guide and accelerate synthesis for future applications.

works.title: Quasi-One-Dimensional Topological Band Structure and Van Hove Singularities in Monolayer TaIrTe4 from Laser μ-ARPES
works.abstract: Abstract Recent transport experiments reported a quantum spin Hall insulator phase in monolayer 1T-TaIrTe4 gated away from charge neutrality. This phase is not predicted by band structure calculations and has been attributed to an electronic instability induced by strong correlations at a putative Van Hove singularity. Here, we investigate the electronic structure of exfoliated monolayer 1T-TaIrTe4 using microfocus laser angle resolved photoemission. We find a strongly anisotropic band structure susceptible to density wave instabilities. Our data further reveal a saddle point singularity in the density of states. However, we find that the saddle point lies at a density for which linear transport experiments found no anomalies. Moreover, the quasiparticle line widths suggest weak electron correlations only. This points to a secondary role of Van Hove singularities and electron correlations in the transport phase diagram of monolayer 1T-TaIrTe4.

works.title: Gold Nanoclusters with Wavelike Chiral Lattices Interact with Outer Membrane Protein BamA to Kill Gram-Negative Bacteria through the Screw-in Effect
works.abstract: Abstract Resistance threatens to render antibiotics ineffective, which is posing a threat to global public health. Innovative strategies against drug-resistant bacteria are urgent. The outer membrane protein BamA, a hollow barrel with a pore of 2–4 nm, is a unique and essential structure in Gram-negative bacteria. We prepared chiral 3 nm gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) targeting BamA, exhibiting enantiomer-dependent antibacterial activity against drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The AuNCs with right-handed wavelike lattices (D-AuNCs) preferentially interacted with BamA through the screw-in effect, creating pores in the cell wall and resulting in bacterial death. P. aeruginosa was still susceptible to D-AuNCs due to their excellent antibiofilm activity even after 20 successive passages. D-AuNCs were applied to P. aeruginosa-infected skin wounds in mice, achieving superior wound healing compared to levofloxacin. Our work documented that chiral nanoclusters targeting BamA can efficiently kill P. aeruginosa through the screw-in effect, providing an innovative strategy to combat Gram-negative bacteria.

works.title: Highly Reliable Sub-2-nm Hafnia Ferroelectric Tunnel Junction via All-Atomic Layer Deposition Growth
works.abstract: Abstract Hafnia-based ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for post-Moore memories, offering fast, low-power polarization switching and compatibility with the technological maturity of the hafnia platform. Yet nanometer-scale barrier thinning, while desirable for higher speed and energy efficiency, introduces a critical reliability bottleneck. Here, we develop an all-atomic layer deposition (ALD) process for reliable sub-2 nm hafnia FTJs through precise growth and low-roughness interface formation. The resulting devices combine sub-2-V operation with a high breakdown field of ∼12.1 MV/cm, while maintaining stable ferroelectric switching through 1010 cycles without breakdown. Further interface optimization extends the resistance-state endurance toward 1010 cycles, reconciling aggressive barrier scaling with reliable device operation. We further exploit 4-bit nonvolatile multilevel operation to demonstrate an in-memory computing simulation with 95.78% accuracy. By combining the advantages of scaling with high reliability, this work advances hafnia-based FTJs toward high-speed, energy-efficient, and robust memory applications.

works.title: Tungsten–Carbon Nanohelix Arrays by Helium-Ion Direct Writing: Geometry-Dependent Circular-Polarization Response in the Visible
works.abstract: Abstract 3D nanohelices provide a direct route to control light–matter interactions with circular polarization at the nanoscale. Here, we report periodic arrays of W–C nanohelices fabricated by He+ focused-ion-beam-induced deposition (FIBID), combining direct-write 3D growth with high spatial resolution and W-rich deposits (∼65 at. % W). Two arrays with the same lateral geometry were fabricated while varying only the vertical pitch, corresponding to helical ratios HR ≈ 1 and HR ≈ 2. Transmittance measurements under circularly polarized light reveal a clear geometry-dependent response. The compact nanohelices (HR ≈ 1) show a larger circular-polarization-dependent transmission contrast (g ≈ 0.17, θ ≈ 2.35°), moderate transmittance (∼30–50%), and a sign inversion near 600 nm. The larger-pitch helices (HR ≈ 2) show higher transmittance (∼35–100%) with a weaker but stable response (g ≈ 0.13, θ ≈ 1.60°). Qualitative simulations reproduce the main spectral trends and support distinct optical responses of the two pitch geometries.

works.title: Single-Twinned Seed-Mediated Synthesis of Au Right Bipyramids for Uniform Near-Field Focusing
works.abstract: Abstract Noble metal nanoparticles with sharp edges and corners, such as triangles, tetrahedrons, bipyramids, etc., support superior plasmonic field enhancement for enhanced spectroscopy. However, high-yield synthesis of gold right bipyramids (Au RBPs) with sharp tips has remained limited because they have a single-twinned (ST) crystal structure whose growth pathway is hard to control. Here, we report the seed-mediated growth of Au RBPs using ST seeds, achieving a yield exceeding 70% by moderately increasing the size of these seeds. Au RBPs with sizes from 34 to 94 nm and controlled corner sharpness are achieved through the regulation of seed and bromide amounts. Uniform and strong near-field enhancement is generated in the Au RBPs-on-mirror configuration, which outperforms the well-established nanocube-on-mirror configuration in Raman enhancement. This work highlights the merits of ST seed-mediated growth for anisotropic nanocrystals and their potentials in plasmonic near-field focusing.

works.title: Optical Resonance Tuning of Single Polystyrene Microspheres Using the Phase-Change Material In3SbTe2 as a Switchable Mirror
works.abstract: Abstract Dielectric nanoparticles and microparticles show rich optical responses due to their electric and magnetic multipolar Mie modes and low losses. These optical resonances can be modified via the particle size, shape, and dielectric environment. Here we tune the infrared multipolar Mie resonances of dielectric polystyrene microspheres using the plasmonic phase-change material In3SbTe2 (IST). IST exhibits a phase change between a dielectric amorphous phase and a crystalline phase that is metallic in the infrared. We show that a reversibly switchable particle-on-mirror geometry can be created by locally switching the IST under the polystyrene microspheres. Measuring the light-scattering spectra of single polystyrene microspheres before and after crystallization and reamorphization, we observe huge shifts of the resonance wavelength, e.g., from 5.2 to 8.9 μm and back for 6 μm diameter spheres. Our work is a first step toward a controlled tuning of multipolar Mie modes of various particles using reprogrammable IST mirror structures.

works.title: Correction to “Physical- and Chemical-Dually ROS-Responsive Nano-in-Gel Platforms with Sequential Release of OX40 Agonist and PD-1 Inhibitor for Augmented Combination Immunotherapy”
Intrinsically Moiré-Patterned Two-Dimensional Polymorphic Networks for Modulated Charge Order and Proximity Superconductivity
works.abstract: Abstract Moiré superlattices provide a versatile route to engineering correlated electronic and topological states in van der Waals heterostructures, yet their use to organize structural polymorphism and phase-selective charge, magnetic, and superconducting states within a single two-dimensional material remains elusive. Here, we report modulated charge order and proximity superconductivity in an intrinsically moiré-patterned 1T/1T′ polymorphic network of monolayer VTe2 grown epitaxially on superconducting NbSe2. Scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy and first-principles calculations show that in situ annealing of twist-moiré VTe2/NbSe2 creates alternating 1T and 1T′ domains. The origin of the selective 1T-to-1T′ conversion is due to the moiré-induced anisotropic strain. This moiré-registered network hosts phase-specific short-range charge orders: 4 × 4 in 1T and 3 × 3 in 1T′. In the proximity-superconducting regime, spatially modulated in-gap bound states and suppressed coherence peaks reveal phase-dependent magnetic pair breaking. This work establishes intrinsically moiré-patterned polymorphism as a route to programmable two-dimensional quantum materials.

works.title: A Gradient‐Structured Nanofiber Sensor Integrating Moisture‐Induced Voltage Generation and Resistive Humidity Sensing for Plant Transpiration Monitoring
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Recently, plant species decline, reduced crop productivity, and declining efficacy of Chinese herbs have raised growing concern, largely due to environmental change and biotic stress. Intelligent plant health monitoring systems enabling early detection and dynamic tracking are therefore essential. Although flexible wearable sensors offer good biocompatibility, the requirement for external power remains an important challenge for long‐term field deployment. Here, we developed a plant‐transpiration‐responsive sensor based on gradient‐structured cellulose acetate (CA) nanofiber membranes and MXene nanosheets. An asymmetric gradient was constructed by tuning the doping ratio of poly(4‐styrenesulfonic acid) (PSSA) through electrospinning, enabling moisture‐induced voltage generation under a humidity gradient. This structure promotes directional moisture transport and ionic migration, allowing a single device (1.5 × 1.5 cm 2 ) to produce an open‐circuit voltage of ∼1187 mV at 75% relative humidity (RH). Owing to the high conductivity and humidity sensitivity of MXene, the same device integrates moisture‐induced voltage generation with resistive humidity sensing for real‐time transpiration monitoring. This study offers a sustainable, non‐invasive strategy for plant health monitoring and early stress warning and supports the integration of smart agriculture and green energy.

works.title: Compression‐Driven Self‐Assembly of Fusion Peptides Into Fibrous Networks Revealed by In Situ Grazing‐Incidence X‐Ray Diffraction
works.abstract: Fusion peptides (FPs) have emerged as versatile building blocks for nanoscale architectures with potential applications in nanolithography, surface templating, and bioinspired materials. However, most studies of FP self-assembly at fluid interfaces rely on ex situ characterization after transfer to solid substrates, making it difficult to determine whether the observed structures form at the interface or during transfer and drying. Here, we employ grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXD), combined with X-ray reflectivity (XRR), to directly probe in situ the structural evolution of FP monolayers at the air-water interface during uniaxial compression. The results reveal that compression drives the development of lateral molecular order and fibrillar assemblies at the fluid interface. For FP1, increasing surface pressure promotes β-sheet ordering and fibril coherence, with maximum in-plane correlation at an intermediate pressure, whereas further compression partially disrupts this organization. In contrast, FP4 exhibits only short-range order with limited response to compression. These findings identify surface pressure as a physical parameter for controlling peptide organization at fluid interfaces and provide a basis for compression-directed fabrication of tunable peptide nanostructures.

works.title: Engineered probiotic-nanozyme bio-hybrid remodels host-microbiome homeostasis for multi-targeted metabolic syndrome amelioration
Interplay of stiffness and conductivity in modulating host immune reactions to conductive hydrogels
works.abstract: Electrically conductive hydrogels (ECHs) that combine mechanical softness with electrical conductivity are emerging as promising materials for implantable electronics and tissue engineering. However, the individual and combined influences of their mechanical and electrical properties on the host immune system remain poorly understood. In this study, we independently controlled stiffness and conductivity in graphene oxide–polyacrylamide (GO/PAAm) hydrogels by varying crosslinker concentration and chemical reduction and examined their effects on macrophage polarization and tissue responses in vitro and in vivo. Four hydrogels with independently tunable stiffness and conductivity were fabricated: low-conductivity soft (LS), low-conductivity rigid (LR), high-conductivity soft (HS), and high-conductivity rigid (HR). Rigid ECHs consistently induced pro-inflammatory macrophage activation and promoted fibrotic collagen deposition. In contrast, conductivity attenuated inflammation in the early stages, regardless of stiffness. Notably, conductivity amplified stiffness-dependent immune responses: high-conductivity soft ECHs suppressed fibrosis, while high-conductivity rigid ECHs exhibited the most severe fibrotic responses. Our studies reveal a previously unrecognized interplay between stiffness and conductivity in shaping early-stage immune reactions to ECHs, providing vital insights for the rational design of immune-compatible ECHs for implantable biomedical devices.

works.title: ROS-responsive NIR-II-trackable tea polyphenol-based LYTAC nanotheranostics for precision protein degradation and endometrial receptivity improvement in PCOS
works.abstract: Endometrial dysfunction in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is associated with persistent activation of the androgen receptor (AR)-DPP4-reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mitochondrial stress axis in endometrial stromal cells. However, current therapeutic approaches are limited by insufficient cellular selectivity and an inability to coordinately disrupt the pathological axis. We developed ITP-LYTACs@Gel, an intrauterine nanotherapeutic platform. Its mesoporous tea polyphenol core incorporated an ICG-thioketal-spironolactone module, enabling ROS-responsive near-infrared-II fluorescence imaging and on-demand spironolactone release to suppress AR signaling. Aberrantly accumulated membrane DPP4 was captured by a DPP4 antibody and internalized through an SDC2-recognition peptide for lysosomal degradation. Meanwhile, the polyphenol core scavenged intracellular ROS, alleviated mitochondrial oxidative stress, and promoted mitochondrial recovery. Incorporation into gelatin hydrogel prolonged uterine retention and enhanced stromal distribution. In PCOS rats, intrauterine ITP-LYTACs@Gel reduced hormonal dysregulation and local inflammation, improved extracellular matrix remodeling, increased decidualization- and receptivity-related markers, and improved reproductive outcomes. Thus, the feedback-regulated system integrates AR inhibition, lysosomal DPP4 degradation, ROS scavenging, and mitochondrial repair, offering a promising strategy to improve endometrial receptivity and improve pregnancy outcomes in PCOS.

works.title: Mutual Waxing and Waning—A Novel Nano‐Biocomposite Harnesses the Lactate Gradient to Enhance Cuproptosis and Anti‐Tumor Immunity
works.abstract: Modifying the lactate gradient in tumors can induce acidosis and improve the immunosuppressive microenvironment. However, the therapeutic benefit is offset by compensatory metabolic adaptations and the inability of small-molecule drugs to regulate the gradient throughout the tumor tissue. This study developed a novel nano-biocomposite (LOB@CDSH) that combines cuproptosis to damage mitochondria and cut off energy supply, thereby improving the therapeutic outcome of acidosis induction. Simultaneously, it utilizes the invasive and tumor-colonizing capabilities of engineered bacteria to efficiently reduce lactate levels within tumor tissues. The MCT4 inhibitor syrosingopine (Syro) was loaded into a reactive oxygen species-responsive copper-based metal-organic framework (Cu-DTA) and coated with hyaluronic acid (HA) to form Cu-DTA@Syro@HA (CDSH). Syro inhibits lactate efflux, leading to intracellular lactate accumulation and acidosis. This promotes mitochondrial metabolism and induces lactylation modification of methyltransferase-like 16 (METTL16), thereby upregulating the expression of ferredoxin 1 (FDX1) to enhance cuproptosis. Lactate oxidase (LOX)-engineered Escherichia coli BL21 (LOB) serves as a carrier to deliver CDSH to the tumor site, where it proliferates, disseminates, and continuously expresses LOX to deplete lactate in the tumor microenvironment, thereby alleviating lactate-mediated immunosuppression. The aforementioned nano-biocomposite provides a reciprocally modulating strategy for lactate metabolism, offering a novel approach for tumor immunotherapy.

works.title: A 3D‐Printed Model of Human Lactation
works.abstract: Engineering physiologically relevant breast in vitro models remains challenging due to the gland's complex three-dimensional microanatomy, together with the need for epithelial polarity and hormone responsiveness. To overcome these challenges, fabrication methods are needed that rapidly create alveoli-scale structures with efficient diffusion and sustained hormonal stimulation. Here, Filamented Light (FLight) biofabrication is leveraged to print highly porous, ECM-based hydrogel scaffolds directly within standard Transwell inserts with separate apical and basal access. FLight's speckle-patterned laser generates multiscale scaffold architectures that integrate FLight channels (∼15 µm) to promote diffusion with alveoli-inspired cylindrical microwell arrays (Ø100, Ø150, and Ø200 µm) that impose geometric constraints to guide epithelial organization. Each insert is printed in <10 s and incorporates slow-release prolactin microcrystals to provide lactogenic stimulation in situ. Primary human milk-derived mammary epithelial cells (milk MECs) were seeded onto the constructs. There, milk MECs line the printed microwells, establish zona occludens-1-positive tight junctions, and express lactation-associated markers (prolactin receptor and β-casein), alongside milk fat globules and intracellular lipid droplets. Collectively, this rapidly reconfigurable FLight platform enables high-throughput generation of hormone-responsive human mammary microtissues for lactation-focused studies and is adaptable to other lumen-forming epithelia.

works.title: Influence of Microsphere‐to‐Hydrogel Matrix Composition on Long‐Term Volume Retention and Host Tissue Remodeling of Injectable Composite Collagen Hydrogels
works.abstract: The most commonly used materials for soft tissue augmentation, including autologous fat and hyaluronic acid, remain limited by inconsistent graft survival or repeated application to maintain volume. Composite collagen hydrogels (CCH) containing high-density crosslinked collagen microspheres embedded within a low-density collagen hydrogel, have demonstrated significantly enhanced vascularization, enabling simultaneous skin grafting and neodermis formation in one surgical step in preclinical models. Herein we evaluated an injectable form of the CCH (iCCH) to determine its long-term volume retention, host tissue integration, and remodeling following subcutaneous implantation. One percent collagen microspheres were mixed with 0.3% collagen hydrogel at microsphere-to-hydrogel ratios of 70:30 (MS70), 50:50 (MS50), and 30:70 (MS30). A microsphere-only formulation (MS-Only; 70:30 microsphere:PBS) and a 1% hyaluronic acid (HA) vehicle were included as controls. Each wild-type mouse received two 0.5 mL dorsal subcutaneous administrations of the assigned material. The iCCH formulations demonstrated cellular infiltration, neovascularization, and progressive inter-microsphere tissue remodeling, while MS70 showed near-complete construct volume retention at 12 months. Across the iCCH formulations, a mild and transient inflammatory response without evidence of an adverse foreign body reaction was observed. Overall, these findings support the potential of iCCH as a durable collagen scaffold for soft tissue augmentation.

works.title: Route‐Gated Lymphatic Delivery of Antigen‐Only Gliadin Nanoparticles for Celiac Disease‐Oriented Immune Modulation
works.abstract: Celiac disease (CeD) lacks approved pharmacologic therapy. Targeted delivery of antigens to immune inductive sites may provide a means to modulate pathogenic immune responses, yet practical delivery remains challenging. We show that minimal, adjuvant-free, self-assembled gliadin nanoparticles (L@GNP) attenuated antibody boosting after exploratory intravenous (i.v.) pre-exposure. Both soluble gliadin and L@GNP attenuated subsequent anti-gliadin antibody boosting under the tested i.v. conditions, with L@GNP providing a particulate antigen format with a controlled surface antigen positive rate. Rather than i.v. dosing, subcutaneous (s.c.) administration of L@GNP preferentially accessed draining lymphoid tissues and exhibited temporally coordinated uptake by multiple antigen-presenting cell (APC) populations, characterized by early CD11b+ myeloid-cell capture, transient B220+ cell involvement, and sustained enrichment in CD11c+ APCs at later time points. In a short-term CeD-like mouse model, L@GNP preserved villus architecture as indicated by higher V/C and reduced intestinal inflammation by lowering Transglutaminase 2 (TGM2) and key cytokines, rebalanced Th1/Th2, and increased Foxp3 expression, whereas a rapamycin-loaded counterpart (R/L@GNP) did not confer additional benefit at matched antigen doses. These data highlight route-gated lymphatic access and antigen-only simplicity as materials design principles for immunomodulatory nanomedicines.

works.title: Functional Construction Strategies and Multidimensional Applications of Kidney Organoids
works.abstract: Kidney diseases represent a major global health burden, highlighting the need for advanced human-relevant models to investigate disease mechanisms and develop therapeutic strategies. Stem cell-derived kidney organoids have emerged as powerful human-relevant platforms that recapitulate key aspects of kidney development and enable the modeling of renal diseases. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in kidney organoid construction and characterization and highlights key bioengineering strategies for improving their structural and functional properties. These strategies include decellularized extracellular matrix scaffolds, 3D bioprinting, genetic engineering, vascularization, and organoid-on-a-chip technologies. Their broad biomedical applications in disease modeling, drug screening, toxicity assessment, and regenerative medicine are further discussed. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives are addressed, with emphasis on improving reproducibility, maturation, and functional relevance to advance the translational potential of kidney organoids.

works.title: Hydrothermally grown ZnO nanoarrays on phase-change core-shell fibers for solar heat-load reduction and thermal buffering
works.abstract: Abstract Integrating a phase-change core with hydrothermally grown optical nanostructures remains challenging because water-sensitive phase-change components may be lost or structurally damaged during aqueous mineralization. Inspired by the hierarchical leaf architecture of the Silversword, a dual scale core-shell fiber membrane was fabricated by combining coaxial electrospinning with in situ hydrothermal growth of ZnO nanorods. A PVDF-modified PEG/PAN core-shell architecture enabled the formation of a ZnO-nanorod scattering exterior while retaining the phase-transition behavior of the PEG-containing core after hydrothermal processing. This spatially separated architecture assigns distinct thermal-management roles to the two domains: the ZnO exterior reduces solar heat loading, whereas the PEG-containing core buffers transient temperature variation through reversible latent-heat storage and release.The resulting phase-change radiative fiber membrane (PRFM) exhibited a solar reflectivity of 91%, an atmospheric-window emissivity of 85%, and a melting enthalpy of 59.6 J/g. Under repeated simulated solar irradiation at approximately 1000 W/m², PRFM showed suppression of temperature rise. During the third irradiation cycle, its temperature was more than 6 °C lower than that of the control. In the outdoor device test, PRFM achieved a maximum temperature reduction of 5.3 °C relative to PAN during the high irradiance period. After 500 twisting-spreading cycles, the membrane retained 86.4% of its initial latent heat. When attached directly to the arm in the outdoor wearable test, it maintained an average temperature 4.6 °C lower than that of commercial cotton. This work provides a structural strategy for integrating optical heat-load regulation and latent-heat buffering within a single fibrous platform.

works.title: Uniform Radial Compression Enabling Densification of High‐Curvature Fiber Electrodes for High‐Rate Ah‐Level Energy Textiles
works.abstract: Fiber lithium-ion batteries (FLIBs), which can be woven into flexible energy textiles, are promising power sources for wearable electronics. However, increasing their cell-level energy density requires high-loading fiber electrodes that are limited by the porous, loosely packed structures formed during dip-coating, since conventional calendering cannot be applied to highly curved fibers without fracturing the coating. Here, we address this limitation by applying uniform radial compression around fiber electrodes through a flexible-roller calendering approach that uses an elastomer-wrapped steel roller, enabling efficient densification with substantially reduced structural disruption. X-ray computed tomography (CT) shows that calendering reduces porosity to 27.36% and removes large voids, along with improved particle packing and coating-collector contact. These microstructural optimizations effectively enhance transport kinetics, enabling calendered FLIBs to deliver a 72.70% increase in 4C capacity and improved cycling stability (300 cycles with retention over 87.41%). Their strengthened structural integrity affords reliable operation upon repeated deformations like bending and knotting, supports integration into Ah-level energy textiles, and allows conformal mounting on drone arms for high-power use. This work presents an effective, damage-free densification route for high-curvature fiber electrodes and provides a scalable microstructure-engineering approach for advancing wearable energy textiles and other deformable energy systems.

works.title: Pre‐Strain‐Activated Strain‐Sensing Ink for Facile Printing of Highly Sensitive and Stable Electronic Textiles
works.abstract: Printable strain-sensing electronic textiles (e-textiles) are promising for wearable health monitoring and human-machine interfaces, yet achieving simultaneous high sensitivity, mechanical stability, and comfort remains challenging due to unstable conductive networks and weak interfacial integration with textile substrates. Here, we report a printable strain-sensing ink based on a styrene-isoprene-styrene elastomer integrated with carbon nanotubes and graphene oxide. Guided by percolation theory and interfacial interaction engineering, we introduce a pre-strain-activated conductive-network strategy to reconstruct and regulate conductive pathways within the printed sensing layer, enabling efficient strain-to-resistance conversion while maintaining structural robustness under repeated deformation. The resulting e-textile exhibits a low strain detection limit of 0.05%, a high gauge factor of 160.5, a fast response time of 45.4 ms, a sensing range of 36.7%, and durability over 1000 cycles at 15% strain. Thanks to strong interfacial adhesion between the infiltrated sensing layer and porous textile scaffold, the device maintains stable electromechanical performance under complex deformations while preserving intrinsic softness and breathability. It further enables reliable real-time monitoring of respiration and human motion. This work provides a simple and scalable conductive-network engineering strategy for high-performance strain-sensing e-textiles, offering a generalizable route toward next-generation wearable electronics.

works.title: Spatially Convergent Encoding of Linked Data Through Assembled DNA Nanostructures
works.abstract: DNA-based storage is a promising candidate for next-generation data media, providing a powerful strategy for preserving digital information in molecular formats. As information complexity increases, multiple DNA molecules are often used to encode related data elements, but their independent distribution can compromise information linkage during amplification-based readout. Although microdroplet PCR reduces amplification bias through spatial compartmentalization, stochastic partitioning of individual DNA molecules may hinder the recovery of associated information. Here, we present a Y-shaped DNA nanostructure system that integrates multiple related DNA sequences into a single molecular scaffold, enabling physical co-localization of linked information before compartmentalization. The Y-shaped architecture serves as a unified input unit for microdroplet PCR, allowing coordinated amplification and accurate recovery of associated data within individual droplets. By maintaining molecular linkage during processing, this strategy improves the uniformity of DNA-encoded linked information recovery. Overall, this system provides a programmable framework for DNA data organization and droplet-based retrieval of linked information.

works.title: Modulated Laser‐Assisted Nanopore Fabrication With Ammonium Sulfate for Single‐Molecule Sensing
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanopore sensing provides a label‐free platform for single‐molecule analysis. To achieve reliable solid‐state nanopore sensing, however, it is essential to optimize appropriate nanopore fabrication methods, as variations in pore diameter, geometry, surface state, and fabrication residues can affect molecular discrimination capability. Here, we report a temporally modulated CW laser‐assisted dielectric breakdown method for facilitating in‐situ fabrication of nanopores in silicon nitride membranes, coupled with ammonium sulfate electrolytes to improve sensing performance. Systematic characterization revealed that temporally modulated CW laser minimizes contamination/debris formation during pore fabrication and yields improved nanopore sensing. Streaming‐potential measurements and interfacial ion‐transport simulations suggest that ammonium‐containing electrolytes modify the SiN nanopore interface by promoting NH 4 + adsorption on the inner pore surface as well as SO 4 2− ions, thereby enhancing DNA–pore interactions. This effect slowed a subset of DNA translocation events, enabling longer dwell‐time observations and differentiation between poly(dA) and poly(dC) blockade populations. Furthermore, aptamer‐assisted detection enabled detection of Scp1‐bound aptamer complexes under conditions where the protein alone tended to clog the pore. The Scp1–aptamer complex showed prolonged dwell times compared with those of free aptamers, even under 0.14 M KCl. Together, these results demonstrate that integrating our approach provides an improved approach for high‐performance single‐molecule nanopore detection.

works.title: Rigid Bis‐Amidinium Anchoring Engineering Enables Synergistic Defect Suppression and Ion Stabilization for High‐Performance Flexible Perovskite X‐Ray Detectors and TFT‐Array Imaging
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible direct‐conversion X‐ray detectors based on halide perovskites hold great promise for mechanically compliant and array‐integrated imaging, yet their performance is limited by grain‐boundary defects and electrical instability in polycrystalline thick films. Here, we introduce 1,4‐benzenedicarboximidamide dihydrochloride (p‐BDAm) as an additive for regulating polycrystalline methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI 3 ) detector layers. Spectroscopic measurements and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support multisite interactions between the bis‐amidinium framework and Pb–I‐containing species as a plausible contribution to the p‐BDAm‐mediated regulation of the local grain‐boundary environment and crystallization behavior.
