Overall, p‐BDAm incorporation suppresses nonradiative recombination, increases the resistivity and mobility–lifetime product, raises the apparent activation energy extracted from temperature‐dependent conductivity from 0.17 to 0.49 eV, and substantially improves dark‐current stability. The optimized flexible perovskite composite membrane detector achieves a sensitivity of 2165.5 µC Gy air −1 cm −2 at 10 V and an estimated detection limit of 15.0 nGy air s −1 . Moreover, the p‐BDAm‐regulated MAPbI 3 layer is compatible with thin‐film transistor (TFT)‐array integration, enabling parallel X‐ray imaging. A representative TFT image was obtained at an X‐ray dose rate of 12.3 µGy air s −1 with an exposure time of 0.5 s. These results demonstrate a transferable molecular‐regulation strategy for stabilizing polycrystalline perovskite X‐ray detectors across flexible and array‐integrated architectures.

works.title: Crystallographic Design of Electrodeposited Copper for Ultra‐Low‐Temperature Cu‐Cu Direct Bonding
works.abstract: Low-temperature Cu-Cu direct bonding (<150°C) for 3D integration faces a severe bottleneck from interfacial voids caused by limited atomic diffusion. While nanocrystalline Cu (NC-Cu) has emerged as a promising bonding material owing to its high stored energy, the thermodynamic influence of initial crystallographic orientation remains unclear. Here, we systematically investigate the orientation-dependent bonding thermodynamics of NC-Cu thin films with (100), (111), and (101) orientations. Despite high internal energy, (100) and (111) Cu consume significant energy for internal defect curing (dislocation glide and twin annihilation), inducing void aggregation. Conversely, (101) Cu, despite not possessing the largest absolute total driving force, directs the largest fraction of its available positive driving force toward macroscopic grain-boundary migration, thereby achieving extensive interfacial-crossing growth and enhanced overall mechanical reliability. We demonstrate that reliable bonding requires targeted allocation of grain boundary energy, establishing a novel crystallographic design principle for advanced heterogeneous integration and solid-state joining technologies.

works.title: A Simplified Front-Contact Layer for Reduced Recombination and Improved Performance of (Ag,Cu)(In,Ga)Se2 Solar Cells
works.abstract: Abstract Transparent conductive oxide (TCO) layers play a critical role in determining optical transmission, carrier collection, and interfacial recombination in thin-film solar cells. In Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) devices, the widely used ZnO/AZO front contact often introduces parasitic optical absorption due to its relatively large thickness. Here, we introduce a front-contact layer (FCL) structure to replace the conventional thick ZnO/AZO stack. Structural and interfacial analyses reveal that the FCLs form a dense, conformal contact, significantly reducing the interface trap density and suppressing recombination losses. The optimized front-contact structure reduces parasitic optical losses and improves device performance from 16.25% to 17.30%, with the most notable gains in VOC and FF, consistent with reduced interfacial recombination. Electrical characterization and optical simulations further indicate reduced saturation current density and improved diode behavior, consistent with enhanced junction quality. Importantly, the reduced thickness and high transparency of the FCLs make this architecture highly suitable for tandem photovoltaic applications, where efficient light management and minimal optical loss are essential.

works.title: Location-Controlled Ge Grain Growth via Nanoscale Cooling-Hole-Assi-sted Laser Crystallization for Low-Thermal-Budget Monolithic 3D Integration
works.abstract: Abstract Monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) integration requires high-performance channel materials processed under strict thermal budgets (<400 °C). While germanium (Ge) is a promising candidate, the stochastic nature of grain boundaries (GBs) in conventionally crystallized films severely degrades carrier transport and device uniformity. In this work, we demonstrate a deterministic location-controlled grain (LCG) growth technique for Ge thin films utilizing a nanoscale “cooling hole” architecture combined with green nanosecond laser crystallization (GNSLC). Transient thermal simulations and microstructural analyses reveal that the nanoscale cooling holes act as localized thermal sinks, inducing lateral crystallization while maintaining the underlying substrate temperature below 240 °C. Furthermore, the incorporation of a silicon nitride (SiNx) capping layer modulates thermal dissipation and exerts stress-mediated growth, yielding highly ordered, single-crystal-like Ge domains up to 1.2 μm with GBs precisely confined between the nanoscale cooling holes. Back-end-of-line (BEOL)-compatible FinFETs fabricated within these deterministic grains exhibit superior electrical characteristics and significantly tightened performance distributions. Notably, the standard deviation of the subthreshold swing (SS) is reduced by more than 50% compared to conventional polycrystalline devices. By effectively eliminating random GB scattering from the active channel, this LCG platform significantly suppresses device-to-device variability. Ultimately, it provides a robust nanoscale material engineering solution for advanced heterogeneous M3D integration.

works.title: Dynamic electrical control of on-chip second-harmonic generation with ferroelectric NbOBr2
works.abstract: Abstract Niobium oxide dihalides such as NbOCl2, featured by vanishing interlayer electronic coupling, present thickness-scalable strong second-harmonic generation (SHG), which has demonstrated their compelling performance of free-space nonlinear optics (NLO). However, practical on-chip photonic applications demand not only high NLO efficiency but also robust electrical tunability, a critical capability that has remained elusive until now. Our work reports the first realization of an in-situ electrically tunable NLO response within a NbOBr2-photonic integrated circuit (PIC). This material uniquely combines two critical features: exceptional tunability enabled by in-plane ferroelectricity and a strong second-order susceptibility resulting from its intrinsic broken-inversion symmetry. In this on-chip photonic circuitry scenario, NbOBr2 showcases larger SHG efficiency than NbOCl2 because of its low index contrast and completely outperforms NbOCl2 in the modulation capability thanks to much stronger in-plane ferroelectricity of NbOBr2. We achieve dynamic, non-volatile SHG intensity modulation exceeding 53%, with polarization states retained even after removing the external electric field. This work establishes the integration of 2D ferroelectric NbOBr2 into PICs as a transformative approach for developing scalable and reconfigurable ultracompact NLO devices, opening new avenues for versatile applications in tunable light sources, optical information processing, and quantum photonics.

works.title: Layer-Dependent Variation in Raman Modes of MoS2
works.abstract: Abstract Raman spectroscopy is used widely to probe phonon properties and layer thickness in two-dimensional MoS2. However, relative peak heights of the out-of-plane (A1g) and in-plane (E2g1) Raman modes can vary with layer numbers. The explanation for origin of this variation has remained elusive. In this work, we show through statistical analysis of hundreds of Raman spectra on hundreds of samples that the A1g/E2g1 peak height ratio is ∼1.4 for monolayer and <1.0 for bilayer MoS2. However, in tri- and four layered MoS2, the A1g/E2g1 ratio can be both above or below 1.0, and gradually rises with thickness – approaching a saturation value of ∼1.3. We find – based on measurements on different dielectrics and at multiple temperatures down to 8 K – that the peak height ratio is modulated by the A1g line width, which depends on both substrate-dependent electronic effects and thermally activated contributions associated with interlayer-related phonon scattering. In monolayer MoS2, the anomalous area ratio originates from suppression of the E2g1 peak area and depends on excitation energy, suggesting the influence of its distinct electronic structure. Our results show that the variation of the A1g/E2g1 peak height ratio arises from the coupling of line width and monolayer-specific Raman response.

works.title: A Flexible Complementary Memristive Synapse for Convolutional Neural Network Applications
works.abstract: Abstract The memristive artificial synapse, which typically operates on the basis of various filamentary conductance-update mechanisms, has been extensively utilized to implement hardware neural networks for brain-inspired computing. However, the stochastic conductance-switching characteristics that arise from uncontrollable filamentary evolution within the two-terminal device have long hindered hardware neural networks from achieving training and recognition performance comparable to their software neural network. Here, we propose a flexible complementary memristive synapse that achieves highly linear conductance-update behavior while preserving a large dynamic range. This synapse consists of a homogeneous bilayer of two amorphous indium–gallium-tin oxide (a-IGTO) films deposited under different oxygen partial pressures: an oxygen-deficient, VO-rich layer formed without O2 supply and an oxygen-supplied, VO-poor layer formed with O2 supply, exhibiting incremental and decremental conductance-update behaviors, respectively. The distinct oxygen-vacancy-related states and filament-evolution characteristics of the two layers suggest vacancy-mediated layer-to-layer redistribution, which can mutually compensate the nonideal conductive filament evolution of the two different layers, thereby facilitating more gradual modulation of the net conductance. The proposed flexible synapse exhibits robust mechanical stability and durability after 12,000 bending–release cycles, as confirmed by electrical characterization while maintained in the bent state at a bending radius of 2 mm. Finally, the applicability of the proposed flexible synapses to HW-NNs is evaluated through a VGG-8-based CIFAR-10 image recognition simulation using experimentally measured synaptic characteristics for weight updates in the two fully connected layers.

works.title: Recombinant Humanized Collagen V-Engineered Implant Interfaces Drive in situ Low-Thrombogenic Vascular Repair via Selective Bioadhesion
works.abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular implants (e.g., vascular stents, occluders) face persistent challenges of thrombosis, immune activation, and delayed endothelial healing. Moreover, functional surfaces that can synergistically balance the demands of antithrombosis and pro-endothelialization remain suboptimal. Here, we develop a genetically engineered, recombinant humanized collagen V (rhCol V) that promotes vascular endothelial cell proliferation via the αvβ3-FAK pathway and induces smooth muscle contractile transition. Proteomics indicates reduced platelet adhesion via αIIbβ3 inhibition, thereby reducing thrombogenicity. In rabbit models, rhCol V-coated stents outperformed drug-eluting stents in long-term endothelial repair and remodeling, while suppressing acute thrombosis and immune activation. This engineered biomaterial has the potential to enhance the safety and efficacy of cardiovascular implantable devices.

works.title: Bacteria-Derived Micro/Nanoparticles for Vaccine Design
works.abstract: Abstract Vaccines have profoundly reduced the global burden of infectious diseases and are increasingly being explored for cancer immunotherapy. However, developing vaccine platforms capable of simultaneously achieving efficient antigen delivery, precise immune modulation, and durable protective immunity remains a major challenge. Bacteria-derived micro/nanoparticles (BPs) have recently emerged as promising vaccine platforms that integrate the structural advantages of nanomaterials with the intrinsic immunostimulatory properties of bacterial components. Their micro-to-nanoscale dimension, pathogen-mimicking architecture, and capacity for multivalent antigen presentation facilitate efficient lymphatic trafficking, antigen-presenting cell targeting, and coordinated activation of both innate and adaptive immunity. Moreover, the endogenous pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) within BPs serve as built-in adjuvants, potentiating antigen cross-presentation, inducing trained immunity, and eliciting robust T-cell and B-cell responses. These unique structure–function relationships have accelerated the clinical translation of BP-based vaccines, with several candidates now in clinical trials or already commercialized. In this review, we discuss the fundamental mechanisms, engineering strategies, and clinical research progress of BPs in vaccine development, while critically emphasizing the current challenges in safety, mechanistic elucidation, and scalable manufacturing. We further outline future opportunities for harnessing BPs as precision-tailored platforms for next-generation immunization paradigms.

works.title: Toward Generalized Dynamic Metasurface Holography with Learned Real-Momentum-Locked Evolution
works.abstract: Abstract Dynamic holography is pivotal for next-generation displays with critical applications in augmented reality, virtual reality, and beyond. While metasurfaces have emerged as powerful approaches for dynamic holography, existing works remain largely confined to intensity-only modulation, restricting the available channels for display and information storage. Herein, we realize a generalized platform applicable to major types of dynamic holography (monochromatic, color, 3D, and vectorial) by introducing a learned metasurface and aperture synthesis framework (LMAS). This paradigm extends Fourier duality from the intrinsic static real-momentum mapping relationship into the dynamical regime and establishes a learned mapping between real-space aperture displacement and momentum-space holographic evolution via gradient optimization. Crucially, the aperture’s inherent field-agnostic nature provides a universal physical interface that unifies diverse optical degrees of freedom, allowing us to demonstrate four distinct types of dynamic meta-holography. The LMAS approach establishes metasurfaces as a generalized, compact, and scalable architecture for holographic evolution within a minimalist system configuration, offering broad potential in advanced displays, optical storage, and information multiplexing.

works.title: Resolving Overlapping Signals in Quantum Relaxometry Enabled by Spectral Hole Burning
works.abstract: Abstract Quantum relaxometry based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is an easy-to-use technique that detects magnetic noise by measuring the longitudinal relaxation of NV centers. It is favored in chemical and biological applications due to the robustness against imperfect spin control. By tuning the energy level, NV relaxometry can detect magnetic noise generated by other spins and obtain magnetic resonance spectra through cross relaxation. However, the spectral resolution is greatly limited by the inhomogeneous broadening of NV centers, especially for nanodiamond-based relaxometry. Here we demonstrate a hole-burning technique to remove the inhomogeneous broadening. We utilize a weak pump field to deplete specific NV centers during the relaxation measurement, which contribute a reverse signal in the cross-relaxation spectra with a much narrower line width. Our method retains the convenience and sensitivity of NV relaxometry, opening up new avenues for high-resolution magnetic resonance spectroscopy in complex scenarios.

works.title: Correction to “A Dual-Cascade Activatable Near-Infrared Fluorescent Probe for Precise Intraoperative Imaging of Tumor”
Single-Reactor-Run Architecture of Cleaving Homoepitaxial GaN with Aperture-Driven Disordered BN Interlayers
works.abstract: Abstract High-quality freestanding GaN membranes are fabricated using a single-reactor-run metal–organic chemical vapor deposition. The procedure begins with the growth of a single-crystalline GaN template, followed by the formation of a 20 nm-thick full-coverage disordered BN layer on GaN, which remains stable under high-temperature GaN growth conditions. We introduce a heat-treatment step to generate numerous nanoscale apertures in the BN layer, enabling aperture-mediated homoepitaxial regrowth. Meanwhile, the BN layer suppresses strong epitaxial bonding, where the regrown GaN is mechanically detachable from the GaN template. In addition, multiple disordered BN interlayer formations are established, enabling epitaxial lateral overgrowth (ELOG). Moreover, GaN Schottky diodes are fabricated to demonstrate minimal material degradation through the aperture-mediated lift-off process, enhanced device performance with BN-assisted ELOG, and the feasibility of ultralight wearable UV detectors. This approach eliminates the need for ex situ transfer or substrate-specific lift-off processes, providing a simple and thermally robust platform for manufacturing freestanding wide-bandgap semiconductor membranes.

works.title: Atomically Precise Au14V1 Clusters Selectively Block the Neutrophil Elastase-NETosis Axis
works.abstract: Abstract Neutrophil elastase (NE) is a key driver of neutrophil-mediated inflammation and tissue injury across diverse diseases. However, current NE inhibitors often lack sufficient target selectivity, limiting their therapeutic efficacy in suppressing inflammation and promoting organ repair. Here, we report that single-atom V doping programs atomically precise Au15 clusters into a relatively selective and potent NE inhibitor. The ultrasmall size of Au14V1 enables selective accommodation within the NE binding pocket. Multiscale mechanistic analyses demonstrated that Au14V1 inhibits NE through a reversible mixed inhibition mechanism with an inhibition rate of 87.6%, while exhibiting minimal activity toward closely related proteases, highlighting its preferential inhibition toward NE. In LPS- and CLP-induced systemic inflammatory injury models, Au14V1 reduced NE activity and NET formation, alleviated oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, mitigated tissue injury, and improved survival. These findings establish a single-atom engineering strategy for developing selective enzyme modulators and precise therapy targeting the NE-NETosis axis.

works.title: The Answer Lies within the Puzzle Piece: PET-Derived Defect-rich MOFs Boosting Ethylene Glycol Oxidation for Total-Product PET Upcycling
works.abstract: Abstract Chemical recycling of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) is limited by harsh depolymerization conditions and the low-value utilization of terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG). Herein, we report a “one-stone-three-birds” strategy that couples PET depolymerization, TPA utilization, and EG upgrading for total-product upcycling. Waste PET serves as an in situ slow-release terephthalate precursor, whose gradual, incomplete hydrolysis dynamically perturbs metal–ligand stoichiometry, generating missing-linker defects and oxygen-deficient, coordinatively unsaturated environments in a bimetallic MOF (NiCo-PET). Relative to NiCo-MOF prepared from commercial TPA, NiCo-PET exhibits 67% higher spin concentration and enhanced EG oxidation, requiring only 1.29 V vs RHE at 50 mA cm–2 while achieving 93.6% formate Faradaic efficiency and stable operation for 24 h at 2 A cm–2. Operando analysis confirms favorable reconstruction into high-valence oxyhydroxides. This work valorizes both PET-derived products without additional purification or isolation, offering a sustainable route to total-product plastic upcycling.

works.title: Scintillation as an Extreme Exciton Density Regime in Colloidal Nanocrystals
works.abstract: Abstract Colloidal semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs) have emerged as versatile light emitters for a broad range of applications, where they are typically operated in the dilute- or single-exciton regime. Scintillation under ionizing radiation, however, represents a fundamentally different mode of operation. A single absorbed X-ray photon can generate a large number of electron–hole pairs within a nanoscale interaction volume, driving individual NCs into extreme exciton occupancies. In this Perspective, we argue that scintillation in NCs should be viewed as an extreme exciton-density problem and show how simple occupancy considerations impose fundamental limits on achievable scintillation light yield. We further outline two complementary strategies to overcome these limitations: (i) engineering NCs for enhanced multiexciton radiative yields and (ii) designing NC composites that redistribute deposited energy across larger NC populations. We anticipate that exciton-density engineering will provide a unifying framework for designing the next generation of NC scintillators.

works.title: Theoretical Foundations of Goldene Plasmonics
works.abstract: Abstract The recent experimental realization of goldene, an atomically thin form of gold, provides a unique platform to investigate collective electronic excitations in the ultimate two-dimensional (2D) limit of a noble metal. Here we reveal that goldene is a plasmonic material whose collective response is strongly shaped by its reduced dimensionality and underlying electronic structure. Using first-principles many-body calculations, we show that monolayer goldene supports intrinsic acoustic and optical plasmons arising from the interplay between the low-energy metallic response and dispersive s and more localized d states. As the number of layers increases, interlayer coupling and enhanced screening progressively quench this directional anisotropy, driving the system toward the isotropic response of bulk gold. In finite nanostructures, the plasmonic resonance follows the size scaling characteristic of confined 2D metallic systems. Our results establish the foundations of goldene plasmonics, with technological implications for nanophotonic sensing, photocatalysis, and atomically thin optoelectronic devices.

works.title: Operando Imaging of Battery Interfaces through Combined Analysis of Broadband Optical Backgrounds and Raman Features
works.abstract: Abstract Solid-state batteries promise improved safety and energy density, but their performance is governed by buried interfaces where ion transport, chemical reactions, and stress evolution are strongly coupled. Resolving these processes during operation remains challenging. Here, we present an operando spectroscopic strategy that jointly analyzes broadband optical backgrounds and characteristic electrolyte Raman features within a single measurement. Asymmetric least-squares baseline (ALS) estimation extracts broadband optical contrast associated with lithium distribution, while Raman band intensities and peak positions provide complementary information on interfacial chemistry and local stress estimates. This capability provides a unified optical framework for visualizing structural, chemical, and mechanical evolution at battery interfaces and offers a broadly applicable route to interrogate buried interphases in diverse electrochemical systems. More generally, by enabling real-time, multimodal insight into interfacial dynamics, this method advances efforts toward safer, longer-lasting, and more predictable energy-storage technologies.

works.title: Reversible Electric-Field-Induced Changes in the Thermal Resistance of Hexagonal Boron Nitride
works.abstract: Abstract Understanding the behavior of ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) materials under high electric fields is essential for advancing next-generation power electronics. While electrical degradation processes have been widely studied, the influence of high electric fields on thermal transport remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the first experimental measurements of changing thermal resistance under an applied electric field in a UWBG material, using single-crystalline hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) as a model system. We observe substantial, and sometimes reversible, changes in thermal resistance during prolonged exposure to a strong DC electric field. These results reveal a previously unrecognized sensitivity of phonon transport to high-field electrical stressing and show that thermal resistance can serve as a sensitive probe of electric-field-induced material evolution that remains undetected by conventional electrical characterization. More broadly, this work establishes thermal transport measurements as a powerful tool for investigating high-field phenomena in UWBG materials.

works.title: Enzyme‐Functionalized Microparticles to Open the Vitreoretinal Interface
authors: María I. Real de Asúa Pérez-Serrano
works.abstract: The transport of therapeutics to their site of action is often hindered by biological barriers, such as cell layers and basement membranes. Among these, the inner limiting membrane (ILM) represents a major barrier within the eye, separating the vitreous body from the retina and restricting the penetration of intravitreally administered materials. Due to its dense, cross-linked composition, only the smallest nanoparticles can pass through the ILM. Here, we demonstrate that active microcolloids decorated with enzymes can locally open the ILM and thereby facilitate the diffusion of passive carriers into retinal tissue. We utilize an ex-vivo porcine eye model to determine the membrane permeability threshold using fluorescent nanoprobes. We further show that collagenase-decorated silica microparticles can facilitate the transport of nanoparticles, while exhibiting excellent biocompatibility with no adverse morphological or functional retinal effects over a six-week in vivo evaluation in a porcine model. Overall, our findings introduce a biocompatible and minimally invasive strategy to facilitate the targeted nanoparticle transport across biological barriers with promising implications for gene therapy.

works.title: Laser‐Enabled Solid–Solid Interface Engineering for Electrochemical Energy Storage: Nonequilibrium Evolution and Cross‐System Strategies
works.abstract: Solid-solid interfaces (SSIs) govern contact continuity, ion/electron transport, and long-term stability in electrochemical energy-storage devices. Laser processing delivers localized, transient, programmable energy to regulate these interfaces. It can generate nanoscale nonequilibrium structural-chemical states while tuning microscale contact geometry and stress. This review frames laser-enabled SSI engineering as the control of nonequilibrium interfacial evolution. It first examines how laser-matter interactions regulate defects, phases, morphology, chemical states, and stress. It then compares four major strategies, including laser texturing (LT), laser-induced modification (LIM), laser sintering (LS), and pulsed laser deposition (PLD) across solid-state batteries (SSBs), conventional rechargeable batteries (CRBs), and supercapacitors (SCs). LT reshapes contact topography, LIM modifies defects and surface chemistry, LS joins and densifies solids, and PLD constructs controlled films or interlayers. Their functions overlap; final performance depends on whether the induced interfacial state relieves the dominant constraint. The resulting Constraint-Physics-Evolution-Strategy (CPES) framework provides a cross-system basis for linking dominant interfacial constraints to their physical origins, required evolution, and compatible laser strategies. Building on this framework, future work should establish measurable descriptors, dynamic characterization, multiscale modeling, and closed-loop optimization to develop transferable parameter-evolution-performance relationships.

works.title: Renatured Organohydrogel Coating for Anti‐Icing
works.abstract: Ice accumulation poses severe threats to industrial operations and public safety. While integrating antifreeze agents into organohydrogels is a thermodynamically proven anti-icing concept, translating these bulk materials into practical, large-area coatings remains challenging. Current adhesion strategies rely either on intricate surface grafting, which lacks scalability and repairability, or on direct physical attachment, which suffers from weak interfacial bonding. Here, we develop a gel-renaturation strategy for constructing scalable and regenerable organohydrogel anti-icing coatings. This approach decouples polymer-network formation from coating assembly and solvent loading. This coating is fabricated by anchoring poly(acrylic acid-co-N,N-dimethylacrylamide) xerogel particles onto various substrates via an adhesive layer, followed by renaturation with an ethylene glycol aqueous solution. Renaturation-induced dissociation and reconstruction of supramolecular interactions promote interparticle chain entanglement, enabling the fusion of discrete xerogel particles into a continuous coating. The coating exhibits excellent freeze resistance, and achieves an ultra-low ice adhesion strength of below 1 kPa. Moreover, the xerogel-based fabrication enables meter-scale coating on diverse substrates without specialized equipment, while re-renaturation provides a simple route for restoring anti-icing performance after coating degradation. This work establishes a xerogel-mediated gel-renaturation route for translating organohydrogel anti-icing materials into scalable and regenerable coating formats.

works.title: Microfluidics Lab‐on‐a‐Chip Approaches to Decipher Atherosclerosis Pathogenesis
works.abstract: Atherosclerosis is a complex, multifactorial disease driven by intricate cellular and molecular interactions within the vascular microenvironment. While conventional experimental models have provided important insights into disease progression, they often fail to recapitulate the coupled mechanical and biochemical stimuli that govern vascular pathology in vivo. Lab-on-a-chip technologies offer a powerful platform for reconstructing key cellular and tissue-level features of atherosclerosis within controlled microscale environments, enabling the study of processes such as endothelial dysfunction, inflammatory signaling, cell-matrix interactions, and vascular remodeling. The integration of microfluidics further enhances these models by enabling precise control of flow-derived mechanical cues, including shear stress, vascular geometry, and pulsatile pressure. This review highlights recent advances in microfluidic lab-on-a-chip models for atherosclerosis research, with a focus on their ability to replicate human-relevant pathophysiological conditions. We discuss pioneering studies that have employed these paltforms to investigate endothelial barrier dysfunction, monocyte recruitment, foam cell formation, vascular remodeling, and plaque instability across different stages of disease progression. Collectively, these microfluidic systems provide powerful, physiologically relevant tools for dissecting the mechanisms underlying atherosclerosis and evaluating therapeutic strategies under controlled, biomimetic vascular conditions.

works.title: Alleviating Passivating Molecule Self‐Aggregation and Interfacial Non‐Radiative Recombination for High‐Performance Two‐Dimensional Metal Halide Solar Cells
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional metal halides paired with organic active layers form p/n interdigitated heterojunctions that offer broad potential owing to their high stability and extended spectral response. However, inherent defect states at p‐type interface frequently cause severe charge accumulation and require efficient passivation. PDAI 2 enables passivation via its strong electrostatic potential and dipole moment, yet inevitably induces severe self‐aggregation. Thus, we develop a synergistic molecular passivation strategy by introducing CyPAI with a rigid cyclopropyl group into PDAI 2 system. Owing to its weaker electrostatic potential and steric hindrance, CyPAI disrupts the hydrogen‐bond network of PDAI 2 , enabling compact and high‐coverage passivation. This strategy suppresses interfacial non‐radiative recombination, while the reconstructed interfacial dipole moment markedly accelerates the cross‐interface extraction kinetics of photogenerated carriers. Meanwhile, the ordered interdigitated p/n heterojunction constructed via nanoimprinting further enhances light trapping and interfacial contact. The optimized devices achieve a champion PCE of 24.34% and a remarkable FF of 85.36%, which is the record value for two‐dimensional metal halide solar cells so far. Notably, unencapsulated devices retain over 92% of their initial efficiency after 2,000 h of MPP tracking under 1‐sun illumination, demonstrating that this synergistic strategy effectively boosts both the high efficiency and excellent operational stability of p/n heterojunction devices.

works.title: A Scale‐up DNA Network‐Driven Autophagy Trap Gated by Cascade Logic Circuits to Program Cancer Cell Death
works.abstract: The autophagy-lysosome system is an intrinsic pathway to degrade intracellular targets, but is limited by the payload size. Those large-scale targets can overload this system, thereby resulting in autophagic cell death. Taking advantage of this feature, here we smartly engineer a scale-up DNA network-driven autophagic overload trap gated by a computing circuit that controls a well-designed DNA nanorobot (GA-AP) to recognize cascade extra/intracellular microenvironments and then execute the downstream tasks in a spatiotemporal sequence. This design allows the in situ construction of scale-up DNA networks inside the targeted cancer cells, overwhelming the autophagy-lysosome system with LC3-II accumulation comparable to that induced by RAPA, but at a ∼30-fold lower effective molar concentration, and thereby selectively killing cancer cells via autophagic overload. This autophagic overload trap thus establishes a conceptually new paradigm for programming cancer cell death with cascade microenvironment-gated DNA nanorobots, providing an in vitro proof-of-concept.

works.title: An Integrated Hydrogen Cascade Reactor for Formic Acid Dehydrogenation, Membrane Purification, and On‐Demand Hydrogenation
works.abstract: ABSTRACT We report an integrated hydrogen cascade reactor that couples formic acid dehydrogenation, selective H 2 separation, and downstream hydrogenation within a single system. A redox‐active bimetallic PdNi‐chloranilate (PdNiCA) metal–organic framework (MOF) catalyst enabled H 2 generation from formic acid under mild conditions, while a mixed‐conducting graphene oxide membrane selectively transported hydrogen and effectively suppressed CO 2 permeation. The separated H 2 was directly supplied to a downstream reaction chamber without intermediate storage or external purification and used for nitroarene hydrogenation under ambient conditions. Representative nitroarenes were converted to the corresponding anilines with conversions of up to 99%, demonstrating that the membrane‐delivered hydrogen was sufficiently reactive for downstream chemical transformation. By integrating H 2 production, purification, and utilization within a single architecture, this system offers a low‐temperature strategy for on‐demand hydrogen utilization and highlights the potential of membrane‐integrated reactors for sustainable hydrogen‐driven synthesis.

works.title: Molecular Engineering of Membrane Electrode Assemblies With Superior Humidity Robustness for Fuel Cells
works.abstract: ABSTRACT It remains a substantial challenge to achieve stable performance of polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) under fluctuating ambient humidity, largely owing to the difficulty of sustaining oxygen diffusion across the full humidity range. Here, we incorporate a spirobifluorene‐containing microporous ionomer (QTPSp) into the cathode catalyst layer to regulate local oxygen transport in PEMFC electrodes. The rigid, contorted spirobifluorene moieties restrict backbone conformational freedom and frustrate chain packing, generating persistent sub‐nanometer free volume and a hierarchical porous architecture with bicontinuous domains and abundant voids. Quantitative analysis reveals a 54% reduction in local oxygen transport resistance, demonstrating that the microporous ionomer architecture effectively alleviates local oxygen‐transport limitations while maintaining sufficient ion transport. The fuel cell achieves a peak power density of 1.04 W cm −2 under fully dry H 2 /Air. The humidity robustness parameter increases 2.5‐fold, showing that the QTPSp‐4%‐based MEA maintains high power density and low sensitivity to humidity.

works.title: Reconfigurable Bulk Photovoltaics via Strain‐Gradient‐Induced Polar Reconstruction in a van der Waals Antiferroelectric
works.abstract: Strain gradients can induce flexoelectric polarization and activate bulk photovoltaic signals, but the response is usually locked to the localized flexoelectric polarization or intrinsic symmetry, limiting its reconfigurability. Van der Waals antiferroelectrics provide a distinct route: strain gradients can reconstruct inversion symmetry and polar evolution via interlayer sliding, converting a centrosymmetric parent crystal into a polar platform with a writable order parameter. Here, we demonstrate strain-gradient-induced interlayer sliding and polar reconstruction in flexural GeSe, and its direct transduction into reconfigurable bulk photovoltaic output. Correlative Raman/second-harmonic generation mapping and vector piezoresponse force microscopy reveal strain-gradient-induced symmetry breaking and an armchair-aligned polarization with asymmetric, direction-selective switching under lateral poling. Photocurrent mapping and polarization-resolved measurements identify a symmetry-allowed bulk photovoltaic current along the polar axis, whose magnitude is spatially programmable, increasing by over two orders of magnitude after polar reconstruction induced within the coupling of effective flexoelectric bias and ferroic order parameter. These results establish a general symmetry-on-demand strategy to program nonlinear photovoltaics in centrosymmetric van der Waals antiferroelectrics.

works.title: Femtosecond Laser Achieving High‐Entropy Alloys Composited Multiscale Structures Toward Efficient Crude Oil Transport
works.abstract: Crude oil becomes highly viscous and may solidify at low temperatures, reducing pipeline throughput and increasing transport energy demand. Conventional heating systems require complex infrastructure and substantial energy input, limiting their use in low-energy, high-performance oil transport. Here, we report a flash femtosecond laser route that creates an in situ photothermal superhydrophobic high-entropy alloy nanoparticle (HEA-NPs)/aluminum surface for solar-assisted crude oil transport. The transient heating and quenching generated by the laser produce FeCoNiCrMnLa HEA-NPs and distribute them uniformly across the hierarchical aluminum substrate (HEAs/PA). After vacuum annealing of HEAs/PA, the resulting multiscale structures (HEAs/MS) surface contains a microscale pyramid array structure, nanoscale porous coral reef structure, and HEA-NPs, providing strong photothermal conversion and superhydrophobicity. It exhibits an average absorptance of ∼96.6% across the visible and near-infrared regions and reaches ∼71.9°C under 1 sun, while its water contact angle (WCA) is ∼155.4° and remains stable after multiple durability tests. As a transport pipe, HEAs/MS reduces crude oil viscosity and delivers a flow rate up to 4 times that of pristine aluminum under 1 sun. This work offers a convenient method for synthesizing metal-based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles and also provides a low-energy strategy for crude oil transport.

works.title: Successive High‐Output Synthesis of Cu Nanowire Ink for 3D Sonication Printing of Large‐Size Transparent Flexible Touch Screen Sheet
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible transparent conductive film is essential in modern optoelectronic applications. However, how to obtain high‐output and high‐quality transparent conductive electrode (TCE) materials at low cost still remains challenging. This study demonstrates a successive synthesis system based on cyclic repeated‐batch operation to achieve low‐cost, high‐output production of high‐quality Cu nanowires (NWs), with an optional Ni‐shell coating step incorporated into the workflow for oxidation protection. The combination of precursor supplying controller and product collector enables the cyclic synthesis of Cu/Cu@Ni NWs. A 3D sonication printer is designed for non‐contact and uniform printing of a conductive film on arbitrary target substrates. The fabricated flexible Cu NW TCEs exhibit excellent optoelectronic performance (34.46 Ω sq −1 @ 85.92% transmittance at 550 nm, with a haze of 1.40%), outstanding large‐area uniformity (20 × 20 cm 2 ) and good mechanical stability, while Ni‐shell coating effectively enhances the oxidation resistance of the Cu NWs. Flexible transparent touch screens based on Cu NW TCEs are further demonstrated with resistive and self‐capacitive sensing structures. Complex motion control and pen writing can be achieved fluently in both flat and curved states. This work shows great potential in future touch displays, for example, the new‐generation smartphones with transparent, rollable, and extendable touch screens.

works.title: Potassium Regulation at Na1 Sites for Enhanced Redox Utilization and Structural Reversibility in Multimetal NASICON Cathodes
works.abstract: ABSTRACT NASICON polyanionic cathodes are widely studied because they combine structural stability, low cost, and superior rate capability for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, local lattice strain and sluggish multielectron redox kinetics during deep (de)sodiation limit the energy density and lifespan of NASICON cathodes. Here, we regulate Na1 sites with potassium in the multimetal NASICON cathode Na 3 K 0.6 V 1.4 Mn 0.3 Fe 0.3 (PO 4 ) 3 (NKVMFP). Calculations and experiments indicate that K occupation at Na1 sites regulates the alkali ion environment, which in turn modifies the MnO 6 crystal field, improves Mn/V redox utilization, and suppresses Na + /vacancy ordering. NKVMFP delivers an energy density of 381 Wh kg −1 , sustains 12,000 cycles at 4 A g −1 , and shows a volume variation of 4.13%; its stable operation in a 320 mAh pouch cell further supports its practical potential. These results show that Na1 site alkali ion regulation can improve redox utilization and structural reversibility in multimetal NASICON cathodes.

works.title: Oxajulolidinyl‐Induced Molecular Twisting in Aza‐BODIPY Nanoplatform for NIR‐Triggered Synergistic Phototherapy of Glioblastoma
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Glioblastoma (GBM) remains a formidable challenge in oncology due to its infiltrative nature and the blood‐brain barrier that impedes drug delivery. Herein, we report three novel oxajulolidinyl ( OJLD )‐functionalized aza‐BODIPY photosensitizers ( Ph‐OJLD , OMe‐OJLD , and CF 3 ‐OJLD ) designed for NIR‐triggered synergistic photodynamic and photothermal therapy. The OJLD moiety induces significant molecular distortion, as confirmed by single‐crystal X‐ray diffraction, which promotes reactive oxygen species generation and photothermal conversion. Ph‐OJLD self‐assembles into uniformly dispersed nanoplatforms (233 nm, polydispersity index = 0.11) with a negative surface charge (−46.1 mV). In vitro, laser‐activated Ph‐OJLD nanoparticles (NPs) suppress U251 cell proliferation and migration, induce mitochondrial damage, and trigger apoptosis. In an orthotopic GL261 glioma model, stereotactic injection of Ph‐OJLD NPs followed by NIR laser irradiation significantly reduces tumor size and enhances apoptosis without observable toxicity. This work establishes oxajulolidinyl modification as a promising strategy for designing multifunctional photosensitizers for GBM.

works.title: Hollow Nanostructure and Electronic Structure Synergistic Modulation of Metal Sulfide Anodes for Sodium–Ion Batteries: Recent Progress and Perspectives
works.abstract: Sodium-ion batteries are promising alternatives to lithium-ion batteries for large-scale energy storage, benefiting from abundant, low-cost sodium resources. Metal sulfides are attractive anode candidates due to diverse compositions, ultrahigh theoretical capacity and favorable electrochemical properties. However, their poor intrinsic conductivity, sluggish reaction kinetics and severe cycling-induced volume expansion greatly restrict practical development. Constructing hierarchical hollow architectures and regulating electronic structures are effective solutions. Hierarchical hollow structures offer large specific surface areas and shortened charge transport paths to mitigate volume variation and stabilize cycling. Electronic modulation improves conductivity, accelerates ion/electron transport and creates more active sites. The synergistic regulation of hierarchical hollow nanostructure and electronic structure is critical to boost overall electrochemical performance, yet its underlying mechanism lacks systematic understanding. This article reviews the latest advances in the design and synthesis of various hierarchical hollow structures and electronic structure-regulated metal sulfide-based anode materials, and focuses on analyzing the influence laws of the coordinated engineering of hierarchical structures and electronic structures on the sodium storage performance. It is expected to provide ideas for the innovative research and development of new battery electrode materials.

works.title: Loop‐Mediated Isothermal Amplification‐Assisted Rapid, Accurate, and Sensitive Photoelectrochemical Biosensing With CdIn 2 S 4 /SnS Heterojunction Quenched by Methylene Blue
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid, sensitive, and accurate detection of human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV‐16) is highly significant for early cervical cancer intervention. Herein, a novel loop‐mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP)‐assisted photoelectrochemical (PEC) biosensor is rationally constructed with type II heterojunction CdIn 2 S 4 /SnS (CIS/SS) quenched by methylene blue (MB). With the superior charge separation of CIS/SS, an intense initial photocurrent is obtained. After intercalating into double‐stranded DNA products of efficient LAMP, residual free MB is rapidly and directly immobilized on CIS/SS via electrostatic and chemical adsorption (15 min), causing remarkable photocurrent quenching. This finding not only circumvents tedious and time‐consuming quenching probe modification, but also shortens the mutual distance with significantly improved quenching efficiency over traditional ones. More importantly, mechanistic investigations innovatively reveal that photogenerated electrons preferentially transfer from CIS to MB over SS, triggering MB reduction. Meanwhile, adsorbed MB exerts a light‐shielding effect to reduce incident light reaching CIS/SS, collectively causing remarkable photocurrent quenching for enhanced sensitivity with a wide linear range from 1 fM to 1 nM and a detection limit of 0.70 fM. Besides constructing a reliable PEC sensing platform for rapid HPV‐16 detection, this work profoundly clarifies the synergistic quenching mechanism of MB, offering theoretical support for various high‐performance PEC quenching biosensors.

works.title: Synergistic Copper and Carbon Nanotube Coatings Enable High‐Performance Na 2+2x Fe 2‐x (SO 4 ) 3 Cathode Material for Sodium‐Ion Batteries
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium iron sulfate (Na 2+2x Fe 2‐x (SO 4 ) 3 , NFS) is a promising cathode material for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) for large‐scale energy storage systems due to its low cost and long life. However, NFS acts as a near‐insulator and cannot reversibly store sodium ions effectively. To address this issue, this work develops a straightforward solid‐state process to realize a simultaneous copper and carbon co‐coating on Na 2.5 Fe 1.75 (SO 4 ) 3 (NFS) cathode material, NFS@C@Cu, via one‐step calcination under the synergistic influence of CuSO 4 and Carbon Nanotubes. Among all samples, NFS@C@Cu‐0.07, containing 0.89 wt.% Cu, delivers the highest discharge capacity of 103.1 mA h g −1 at 0.05 C, approaching its theoretical capacity and representing a significant improvement over solo carbon‐coated NFS (94.8 mA h g −1 ). Furthermore, it exhibits excellent stability, retaining 87.2% of initial capacity after 10 000 cycles at 50 C, along with commendable rate performance. This study demonstrates that in addition to carbon coating, constructing copper coating on NFS particles can significantly enhance the electronic conductivity and reduce internal cell resistance, thereby improving overall electrochemical performance. This work provides a promising avenue for the design of high‐performance polyanion‐type cathode materials for sodium‐ion batteries.

works.title: A Quaternary Copper–Hexacarboxylate Framework With High Porosity for High‐Capacity MTO Product Separation
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The construction of multinary metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) incorporating multiple distinct metal clusters within a single framework remains a significant challenge, particularly in copper‐carboxylate systems where binary assemblies predominate. Herein, we report a quaternary copper–carboxylate framework, ZJNU‐175, assembled from a low‐symmetry hexacarboxylate ligand and three distinct copper‐based secondary building units. The material features high porosity (BET surface area of 2321 m 2 g −1 ) and abundant supramolecular recognition sites. It achieves a C 3 H 6 uptake of 8.57 mmol g −1 , an equimolar IAST selectivity of 8.1, and a polymer‐grade C 2 H 4 productivity of 5.28 mmol g −1 , placing it as one of the leading MOF adsorbents for C 3 H 6 /C 2 H 4 separation. This work highlights ligand symmetry engineering as a promising strategy for constructing multinary MOFs for energy‐efficient hydrocarbon separations.

works.title: Modulating Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking and Spin‐Dependent Transport in Supramolecular Assemblies of Achiral Porphyrins
works.abstract: Spin-selective electron transport, mediated by the chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect, has traditionally been associated with systems that either possess inherently chiral molecular frameworks or incorporate chiral species. In this study, we explore the occurrence of spin-dependent electron transport in mesoscale helical supramolecular assemblies formed entirely from an achiral porphyrin derivative. The supramolecular chirality in these assemblies is induced by a macroscopic chiral factor, specifically through vortex motion, resulting in distinct spin selectivity. Additionally, the generation of spin-polarized currents further substantiates the role of the CISS mechanism in directing electron spin, even in the absence of traditional chiral centres. To deepen our understanding of the interplay between supramolecular helicity and spin transport, we performed comparative studies by introducing chiral species into the system. This allowed us to evaluate the extent to which extrinsic chirality influences or enhances spin-selective behavior in achiral porphyrin assemblies. To further corroborate the spin-dependent process, we developed a prototype device with a spin-valve configuration. Notably, the results obtained from this device align well with the findings from all spin-dependent measurements. Overall, the results reveal nuanced insights into how chirality at different hierarchical levels can affect spin polarization, offering insightful implications for the design of self-assembled organic spintronic materials.

works.title: Directional f‐d Orbital Coupling as a Key Electronic Factor for Enhanced Oxygen Reduction Reaction in Pt‐based Core‐Shell Catalysts
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The intensity and spatial ordering of f‐d orbital coupling in platinum‐rare earth (Pt‐RE) intermetallic compounds represent an important factor for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Using a Pt 5 Ce@Pt core‐shell model, we engineer two distinct structures: ordered s‐Pt 5 Ce@Pt with expected strong directional f‐d coupling, and disordered w‐Pt 5 Ce@Pt with weak localized coupling. Despite similar Pt shell thicknesses, the ordered core confines Ce uniformly within the interior, whereas the disordered counterpart exhibits uneven Ce distribution and partial diffusion into the shell. The periodic ordered lattice enables maximized Ce 4 f ‐Pt 5 d orbital overlap, which drives efficient electron transfer, modulating the Pt d ‐band‐center position toward a more favorable range, strengthening Pt‐Ce bonds, and effectively suppressing Pt dissolution and Ostwald ripening. Consequently, s‐Pt 5 Ce@Pt delivers a mass activity of 0.8 A mg Pt −1 and achieves a 13% increase after 30k cycles in acidic media. Post‐cycling characterizations reveal partial selective dissolution of subsurface Ce atoms, which is expected to sustain the near‐surface compressive‐strain field and contribute to catalyst durability. This work reveals a qualitative correlation between atomic‐ordering‐mediated Pt‐Ce electronic interaction and ORR performance for high‐performance Pt‐RE catalysts and offers new insights into the structural evolution of intermetallic compounds under harsh electrochemical conditions.

works.title: Electronic Modulation via Dual‐Phase Coupling of CoNi Alloy and NiCo 2 S 4 on N, S‐Co‐Doped Porous Carbon Spheres for High‐Performance Rechargeable Zn‐Air Batteries
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of efficient bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts for rechargeable Zn‐air batteries remains constrained by the trade‐off between activity and durability. Here, we break this bottleneck by rationally constructing a CoNi alloy/NiCo 2 S 4 dual‐phase heterostructure embedded in N, S‐codoped porous carbon spheres (CoNi/NiCo 2 S 4 @NSPCs) via controlled partial sulfidation. Crucially, this mild process partially converts CoNi nanoparticles into NiCo 2 S 4 , preserving the highly conductive alloy phase while creating intimately coupled metal/sulfide heterointerfaces. The resulting architecture synergistically combines alloy conductivity, abundant sulfide active sites, and efficient mass transport through the porous carbon framework. Density functional theory(DFT) calculations reveal that interfacial electronic redistribution optimizes oxygen‐intermediate adsorption, thereby accelerating both oxygen reduction reaction(ORR) and oxygen evolution reaction(OER) kinetics. Consequently, the catalyst achieves outstanding bifunctional performance with a low overpotential gap and remarkable operational stability. When employed as an air‐cathode catalyst, CoNi/NiCo 2 S 4 @NSPCs enables a flexible Zn‐air battery (FZAB) with an open‐circuit voltage of 1.44 V and a high specific capacity of 656.77 mAh g Zn −1 , while maintaining stable charge–discharge operation under bending and over 100 h of cycling. These metrics surpass most state‐of‐the‐art bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts. This work establishes partial sulfidation as a general strategy for engineering dual‐phase nonprecious metal electrocatalysts for practical flexible energy applications.

works.title: Pulse‐Width‐Dependent Laser‐Induced Nonequilibrium Microstructural Evolution of Pd Nanocubes for Ethanol Electrooxidation
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Laser irradiation enables a noncontact pathway for the nonequilibrium structural modification of nanomaterials. Here, the laser irradiation‐induced microstructural evolution of Pd nanocubes (Pd NCs) is investigated by combining theoretical simulations and experimental validation. Coupled finite element method‐molecular dynamics (FEM‐MD) simulations reveal the distinct nonequilibrium microstructural evolution pathways of Pd NCs under nanosecond (ns) and femtosecond (fs) laser irradiation. Although both processes involve rapid heating and cooling, ns laser irradiation follows a thermally extended melting‐annealing pathway that yields heterocrystalline structures, whereas fs laser irradiation induces rapid heating‐flash freezing pathway that produces amorphous structures. Additionally, a microstructural disorder descriptor ( w *) is introduced to quantitatively correlate laser‐induced microstructure with ethanol electrooxidation activity. The results reveal that ethanol electrooxidation activity initially increases and then decreases with increasing w * and exhibits a volcano‐type dependence on laser irradiance. Notably, the laser‐induced heterocrystalline Pd nanospheres (HC‐Pd NSs) achieve the highest mass activity of 3.98 A mg −1 . Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal the predominant role of Pd NC microstructure in modulating the electronic structure and intermediate adsorption. This work provides a mechanistic basis for pulse‐width‐dependent laser‐induced nonequilibrium microstructure engineering in nanomaterials and establishes a laser parameters‐microstructure‐activity framework for guiding the performance optimization of nanocatalysts.

works.title: Carrier‐Free Activatable Nanomodulators for Cuproptosis‐Augmented Photoimmunotherapy of Colorectal Cancer
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Photoimmunotherapy (PIT) has emerged as a promising modality for colorectal cancer (CRC) treatment, yet it often suffers from limited response rates and immune escape. We herein report a carrier‐free, tumor‐specific nanomodulator (IRP@Cu‐R) for near‐infrared second window (NIR‐II) fluorescence imaging‐guided cuproptosis‐augmented PIT of CRC. IRP@Cu‐R is prepared by co‐assembly of IRP@Cu, which is synthesized by linking a NIR‐II fluorophore (IR820) with a photosensitizer (PPa) through Cu 2+ ‐chelated DTPA, and a boronic ester‐masked immune adjuvant (R848‐PB) without additional nanocarrier. The drug loading contents for PPa and R848‐PB are as high as 21.1% and 17.8%, respectively. With Cu 2+ coordinated, both NIR‐II fluorescence and photodynamic activity are quenched via photoinduced electron transfer (PeT). Upon exposure to endogenous hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S), Cu 2+ is converted to CuS, thereby restoring both activities. The released Cu 2+ is reduced to Cu + by glutathione (GSH), depleting antioxidants and inducing cuproptosis via lipoylated protein aggregation. Together with PDT, this process enhances immunogenic cell death. Meanwhile, excess H 2 O 2 cleaves the boronic ester bond of R848‐PB to release R848. These processes promote dendritic cell maturation, thereby eliciting potent systemic antitumor immunity against primary, distant and metastatic tumors. Thus, this study provides a generalizable carrier‐free strategy for integrating activatable NIR‐II fluorescence imaging with cuproptosis‐augmented photoimmunotherapy.

works.title: Human Serum Albumin as a Smart Nanocarrier for [RuNO(CQ)(POA)Cl] Isomeric Complexes: Structural, Photodynamic, and Antitumor Activity Insights
works.abstract: Human serum albumin (HSA) is a natural and non-immunogenic nanocarrier with multifunctional binding pocket for various small bioactive molecules. Hereby, four [RuNO(CQ)(POA)X] (Ru 1-4) complexes with different configurations were synthesized, where CQ is 5-Cl-7-I-8-hydroxyquinoline, POA is 2-Pyrazinecarboxylic acid, and X is Cl or I. The -I group was transferred from the CQ ligand to the metal center Ru to form Ru-1 and 3 during the reaction process. The detailed binding modes and dynamic interactions of Ru 1-4 with HSA were investigated and clarified through analysis of the structures of the complex adducts. A subtle structural change in conformation and the substituted group leads to different recognition and binding modes with HSA for Ru 1-4. Both the complexes and their HSA complex adducts showed higher cytotoxicity against cancer cells, activating the mitochondrial-mediated endogenous pathway to induce apoptosis in HeLa cells and arresting the cell cycle at the S phase. The HSA complex adducts and photo irradiation slightly enhanced the antiproliferative activity against tumor cells. Notably, the complexes showed relatively low toxicity to developing zebrafish embryos. The studies offer insights into the interactions between metal complexes and HSA to design more effective protein-based drug delivery systems.

works.title: Cu‐N 4 Single‐Atom Nanozyme with Multi‐Enzyme Mimetic Activities Combined with In 2 O 3 /Bi 24 O 31 Br 10 Heterojunction: Toward Sensitive Triple‐Mode Detection and Photocatalytic Inactivation of Vibrio Alginolyticus
works.abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, a novel triple‐mode biosensor based on a Cu‐N 4 single‐atom nanozyme (Cu‐N 4 SAzyme) and an In 2 O 3 /Bi 24 O 31 Br 10 Z ‐Scheme heterojunction was constructed for the highly sensitive detection and photocatalytic inactivation of Vibrio alginolyticus ( V. alginolyticus ). The Cu‐N 4 SAzyme, possessing both ascorbate oxidase‐like and laccase‐like activities, was integrated with nucleic acid isothermal amplification technology. This integration enabled triple‐mode detection via photoelectrochemical (PEC), organic photoelectrochemical transistor biosensor (OPECT), and colorimetric (CL) methods, achieving a limit of detection (LOD, calculated) as low as 1.07 CFU/mL. An In 2 O 3 /Bi 24 O 31 Br 10 Z ‐Scheme heterojunction was fabricated as a photoactive gate electrode. Through UV‐vis diffuse reflectance spectrum ‐, Mott–Schottky, and electron spin resonance analyses, we conclude that the electron transfer mechanism is consistent with the proposed Z‐scheme mechanism, demonstrating that this structure exhibits highly efficient space charge separation and long carrier lifetime. Consequently, the photocurrent response was significantly enhanced, enabling highly sensitive triplex biosensing. Concurrently, the In 2 O 3 /Bi 24 O 31 Br 10 heterojunction was demonstrated to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) under light irradiation, enabling the inactivation of a high concentration of V. alginolyticus (approximately 10 7.24 CFU/mL) within 3 h. This platform provides an integrated new strategy for both pathogen detection and disinfection.

works.title: Polymorphic In Vitro Assembly of a Bacterial Microcompartment Shell Protein
works.abstract: Bacterial microcompartments (BMCs) are self-assembling protein nanocages involved in metabolic compartmentalization in bacteria. They consist of hexagonal and pentagonal protein subunits that tile the facets of polyhedral shells. BMCs can assemble a variety of morphologies, making them attractive platforms for engineering synthetic biomaterials and organizing catalysis. Here, a single 99-amino-acid hexameric shell protein from the BMC of Haliangium ochraceum is shown to self-assemble in vitro into a range of nanoscale and mesoscale architectures, including flat lattice sheets, nanorolls, single-walled nanotubes, and nanospheres. The assembly morphology can be controlled by modulating the ionic strength of the assembly buffer, which influences the anisotropic interactions between subunits. These structures represent model platforms for engineered synthetic nanoreactors and provide a framework for exploring the emergent physical, mechanical, and chemical properties of protein-based crystalline materials.

works.title: Plasma‐Driven Under‐Coordinated Metal Site Formation to Boost Elemental Mercury Adsorption Rate of Metal Sulfides
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Coal‐fired power plants are a major anthropogenic source of elemental mercury (Hg 0 ) emissions. Metal sulfide injection upstream of electrostatic precipitators offers an efficient and low‐cost route for Hg° capture, but its performance is constrained by slow adsorption kinetics under short gas‐solid contact times. Here we show that plasma generated within electrostatic precipitators can in situ engrave metal sulfides, creating under‐coordinated metal sites that accelerate Hg 0 uptake. Using ZnS as a model sorbent, plasma treatment increases the Hg 0 adsorption rate by 18‐fold relative to pristine ZnS. Mechanistic studies and theoretical calculations reveal that under‐coordinated Zn sites lower the energy barrier for Hg 0 oxidation to stabilization from 1.54 to 0.66 eV, thereby facilitating the rate‐limiting transition. This plasma‐engraving strategy is further generalizable to synthetic iron and copper sulfides and their natural mineral analogues. Our findings establish plasma engraving as a general strategy to overcome kinetic limitations in mercury capture.

works.title: Designed Peptide Coacervates for Extracellular Antibody Targeting
works.abstract: Therapeutic antibodies have transformed the treatment of cancer and immune-related diseases. However, improving their stability, protection from degradation, and efficient interaction with target cells remain major challenges. Peptide coacervates, formed by liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS), are emerging supramolecular assemblies that offer membraneless microenvironments for encapsulation and enrichment of polar macromolecules and thus are especially attractive for delivery applications. Here, we design minimalistic coacervates formed by oppositely charged peptides through LLPS as a functional biomaterial platform for efficient sequestration and extracellular targeting of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs). We use Rituximab (RIT), a human IgG1 mAb targeting CD20 on B cells, widely used in the treatment of B cell malignancies and autoimmune diseases, as a therapeutic mAb model. We show that the coacervates remain stable under physiologically relevant conditions, including serum-containing media and acidic pH, and that they can efficiently encapsulate RIT. Encapsulation within the coacervates enhances antibody-cell interactions and provides partial protection against enzymatic proteolysis, while coacervates maintain low cytotoxicity. Importantly, we demonstrate that the antibody biological activity is preserved by retaining complement-dependent cytotoxicity against CD20-expressing cells. Thus, our findings suggest that encapsulation within the peptide coacervates provides a promising strategy for improving stability, functionality, and extracellular delivery of therapeutic antibodies.

works.title: Cation‐Anion Co‐Adsorption With Facet‐Preferential Tendency for Stable Wide‐Temperature Zinc‐Ion Batteries
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) face critical challenges from dendrite growth, side reactions, and polyiodide shuttling at the zinc anode, particularly under extreme temperatures. This work presents a dual‐ion synergistic interfacial regulation strategy with Facet‐Preferential Tendency enabled by a trace ammonium iodide (NH 4 I) additive. Iodide ions (I − ), as soft bases, exhibit a facet‐preferential adsorption preference for Zn surfaces to guide uniform Zn 2+ deposition, while ammonium ions (NH 4 + ) are enriched at the Zn(101) facet and tip sites to provide electrostatic shielding and homogenize the electric field. Moreover, the adsorbed NH 4 + cations effectively capture free polyiodide anions via electrostatic interaction, suppressing their conversion into detrimental I 2 and mitigating the shuttle effect. This facet‐preferential complementary adsorption constructs a low‐polarization interphase that simultaneously suppresses hydrogen evolution, blocks water contact, and accelerates Zn 2+ transport. Consequently, the Zn//PANI(Polyaniline) full cell retains 90.05% capacity after a record 70 000 cycles at −30°C. Critically, practical Zn/I 2 pouch cells with a high‐loading cathode deliver a capacity retention of 85.53% after 900 cycles at 2 C under −30°C. This work breaks the low‐temperature performance bottleneck and provides a rational, practical design principle for long‐life aqueous batteries in extreme climates.

works.title: Colloidal Microdevices‐in‐Inks towards Ubiquitous Integration on Paper and Textiles
works.abstract: Colloidal devices represent an emerging interdisciplinary frontier, requiring advances in materials science, micro- and nanofabrication, and innovative design strategies. By benefiting from miniaturization, functional microdevices can be fabricated at the scale of pigment microparticles in inks, which are already massively deployed onto omnipresent paper and textile substrates. However, integrating microdevices onto these microfiber substrates remains elusive. Here, we investigate and demonstrate the fabrication, design, and transfer of colloidal microdevices-in-inks onto paper and textiles using contact and non-contact printing and writing methods. The transferred devices preserve their structural integrity and functionality, while exhibiting enhanced, tunable mechanical and optical properties at the nanoscale. This approach introduces new functionalities on fibrous substrates and enables innovative use of conventional writing and printing tools (i.e., ballpoint pens, fountain pens, paintbrushes, and inkjet printers) for scalable and accessible microdevice integration, opening the way to future transfer of chips and microrobotic components.

works.title: Adenosine-grafted nanocomposite hydrogel coordinates immunoregulatory and regenerative remodeling at the tendon-bone interface
works.abstract: Abstract Regeneration of the tendon–bone interface after rotator cuff repair is challenged by persistent inflammation, limited vascularization and incomplete matrix restoration. Prior studies highlighted adenosine as a candidate for local repair. We then analyzed a public fracture-callus single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset and observed immune-related changes associated with adenosine treatment. On this basis, we developed an adenosine-grafted nanocomposite hydrogel to support local tissue repair. Adenosine was grafted onto dendritic mesoporous bioactive glass through an α-ketoglutarate linker to form dMBG-K-A, which was incorporated into a gelatin methacrylate/hyaluronic acid methacrylate (GelMA/HAMA) hydrogel, yielding dMKA@GH. In vitro, dMBG-K-A reduced M1-associated markers under lipopolysaccharide stimulation and enhanced M2-associated markers in separate interleukin-4/interleukin-13-induced cultures. It also promoted osteogenic differentiation of human bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells and endothelial tube formation. In a rat rotator cuff repair model, dMKA@GH increased bone formation, collagen deposition and proteoglycan-rich, COL-II-positive matrix at the repair interface. Lower iNOS staining and higher VEGF staining were observed at 4 weeks. At 8 weeks, the dMKA@GH group achieved a maximum load of 23.550 ± 1.907 N, exceeding that of the other groups. These findings support adenosine-grafted nanocomposite hydrogels as a local material strategy for improving tendon–bone healing. Graphical Abstract

works.title: Plant-derived extracellular vesicles as natural nanobiotechnology platforms for therapeutic delivery and biomedical applications
works.abstract: Plant-derived extracellular vesicles (PDEVs) are nanoscale vesicles released by plant cells. PDEVs contain heterogeneous combinations of lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, and plant-derived metabolites, enabling interactions with mammalian cells, microorganisms, and other biological systems. Recent advances have expanded understanding of their biogenesis, molecular composition, isolation, characterization, and functional diversity, while also revealing considerable variation among plant sources and vesicle preparations. This review critically summarizes current knowledge of PDEV biology and preparation, including emerging evidence for distinct vesicle populations and advances in purification and physicochemical characterization. We further examine engineering strategies such as cargo loading, surface functionalization, membrane hybridization, and reconstruction using PDEV-derived lipids. Particular emphasis is placed on their reported pharmacological activities in inflammation, cancer, tissue regeneration, and other disease-related models, together with their application as carriers for small molecules, proteins, and nucleic acids. Emerging patent activity and registered clinical studies further illustrate growing translational interest in PDEV-based technologies. However, major challenges remain, including inconsistent nomenclature, lack of standardized isolation and quality-control procedures, cargo heterogeneity, incomplete mechanistic understanding, limited pharmacokinetic and biodistribution data, dose optimization, long-term safety, batch reproducibility, and large-scale manufacturing. Addressing these limitations through standardized, mechanism-driven, and translational research will be essential for advancing PDEVs from experimental bioactive vesicles toward reliable nanobiotechnology platforms for therapeutic delivery and biomedical applications.

works.title: Problem-driven engineering of porous silicon particles: from fundamental challenges to multifunctional biomedical platforms
works.abstract: Porous silicon nanoparticles (pSiNPs) occupy a unique position in the field of biomedical nanomaterials. Their degradable silicon framework, tunable porosity, intrinsic photoluminescence in suitably prepared materials, and diverse surface functionalization options make them attractive candidates for drug delivery, bioimaging, and therapeutic applications. However, these material attributes alone do not establish the performance or safety of individual formulations, which require evaluation in relation to their surface chemistry, coatings, payloads, and intended biological use. This review examines a decade of research by our groups addressing five interconnected engineering challenges: surface functionalization, cargo retention and release control, application-specific formulation design, biological safety evaluation, and particle production. We describe the development of novel surface chemistries, including thermal dehydrocoupling, heterocyclic silane functionalization, and microwave-induced Si–S bond formation, which expand the available toolkit for surface engineering. We then discuss inorganic silicate sealing and hybrid coatings as strategies for improving cargo retention and release control while introducing additional imaging or therapeutic functions. Selected imaging and disease-focused studies illustrate the adaptability of porous silicon-based formulations. We also discuss single-cell transcriptomic analysis in zebrafish as an approach to formulation-specific biological evaluation and describe engineering advances in gram-scale particle preparation. Chemical versatility and application are distinguished from biological generalizability: surface modification and coating strategies must balance cargo retention, release, and carrier degradation, while their biological effects require formulation-specific evaluation. We critically examine these trade-offs, the scope of available safety evidence, and the remaining requirements for long-term assessment and reproducible manufacturing. The narrative is organized not as a catalog of results but as a series of deliberate choices made in response to specific limitations, highlighting demonstrated capabilities, unresolved trade-offs, and the validation required to guide further biomedical development. In this review, five structural problems that hindered pSiNP translation are systematically resolved through a cumulative, problem-driven engineering strategy

works.title: From ROS scavenging to microenvironment remodeling: nanocatalytic strategies for wound healing and tissue regeneration
works.abstract: Nanocatalytic medicine has emerged as a promising strategy for the treatment of chronic wounds by enabling active modulation of the pathological wound microenvironment. Chronic non-healing wounds are characterised by persistent inflammation, microbial infection, oxidative stress, tissue hypoxia, and impaired vascularisation, which together create a hostile environment that prevents effective tissue regeneration. Although considerable progress has been made in the development of nanocatalysts for reactive oxygen species regulation and antibacterial therapy, many existing systems are primarily evaluated according to individual catalytic or therapeutic functions and do not adequately consider the dynamic interactions among redox status, cellular metabolism, and tissue repair. In this review, we discuss the transition from simple ROS scavenging toward comprehensive microenvironment remodeling through the concept of a catalytic landscape within the wound bed. Particular attention is given to the regulation of endogenous substrates, including H₂O₂, glucose, and O₂, and to the effects of catalytic activity, active-site properties, and cascade reactions on the wound microenvironment. We further examine how nanocatalytic regulation of redox and oxygen homeostasis influences mitochondrial function, macrophage phenotypes, endothelial angiogenic responses, and extracellular matrix remodelling. Recent advances in stimuli-responsive, spatiotemporally controlled, and self-regulating nanocatalytic systems are also summarised, with emphasis on their potential to coordinate antibacterial activity with subsequent tissue regeneration. In addition, we discuss the integration of nanocatalysts with hydrogels and microneedle-based delivery systems to improve spatial localization and therapeutic efficiency. Finally, key challenges associated with protein corona formation, catalytic behavior in vivo, safety evaluation, dose control, and large-scale manufacturing are discussed. This review highlights the importance of developing bio-interactive and dynamically regulated nanocatalytic systems and provides perspectives for their translation into next-generation wound therapeutics.

works.title: Engineered Lactococcus lactis enabling on-site melanin synthesis alleviates IBD-related anxiety and depression by regulating tryptophan metabolism
works.abstract: Abstract Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is often accompanied by anxiety and depression. Gut microbiota and their metabolites may play important roles in IBD-related anxiety and depression. Here, in order to relieve IBD-related anxiety- and depression-like behaviors, an engineered Lactococcus lactis ( L. lactis) NZ9000 TyrL-pMG36e, which can produce tyrosinase in the intestine, was constructed, thereby facilitating the biosynthesis of melanin as the final product. The engineered probiotic NZ9000 TyrL-pMG36e could significantly increase the abundance of SCFA-producing gut microbiota and anxiety- and depression-alleviating probiotics. Interestingly, propionic acid was identified as the key SCFA relieving dextran sulphate sodium (DSS) induced colitis and anxiety- and depression-like behaviors by inhibiting microglia activation via regulating tryptophan metabolism. We found that propionic acid could upregulate the expression of tryptophan metabolism-related genes in microglia, thereby activating the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) to enhance the expression of IL-22, and this pathway exerts anti-inflammatory effects via IL-22-mediated signaling to inhibit microglial activation. AhR knockout (AhR KO) mice were also used to further elucidate the critical role of AhR, which may serve as a bridge between the gut microbiota and the central nervous system, particularly in modulating microglial activation. This study uncovers the underlying mechanisms of the microbiota-gut-brain axis behind IBD-related anxiety and depression, and is expected to provide a new strategy for the clinical treatment of IBD-related anxiety and depression. works.title: Targeting hedgehog signaling with a smart microneedle system promotes tendon regeneration
