works.abstract: Achilles tendon homeostasis and repair rely on progenitor cells, but the role of Hedgehog/Glioma-Associated Oncogene Homolog 1(Hh/GLI1) signaling remains elusive. In response to inflammatory insults, Hh signaling is activated and Gli1-lineage cells undergo rapid expansion in the injured Achilles tendon. These GLI1 + cells constitute a distinct progenitor cell subset with substantial proliferative capacity. Functionally, while this pathway supports tendon homeostasis under normal conditions, ablation of GLI1 + cells compromises tissue repair and promotes heterotopic ossification (HO). Based on these findings, a novel smart-responsive hyaluronic acid-based microneedle (MN) was developed. It delivers purmorphamine (Pur; a smoothened agonist) encapsulated within a bilayer of tenocyte membrane and ROS-responsive Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (MN@TM-RRP-Pur). This design enhances the sustained penetration of the drug into dense tissue via the cell membrane coating, and enables drug release specifically at the inflammatory site via RRP degradation, thereby potentiating the stemness of progenitor cells and promoting regenerative repair. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrated that the degradation of MN@TM-RRP-Pur enables the stepwise release of Pur at the injury site, effectively inhibiting HO and promoting the restoration of Achilles tendon structure. These findings elucidate Hh signaling regulation of Achilles tendon progenitors and present a novel strategy to activate endogenous repair mechanisms.

works.title: Macrophage membrane-camouflaged diatomic nanozymes combined with FLASH radiotherapy reprogram tumor-associated macrophages to boost antitumor immunity
works.abstract: Despite the excellent normal tissue protection and immunomodulatory potency of ultra-high dose-rate FLASH radiotherapy (Flash-RT), CD47-mediated tumor immune escape severely restricts its clinical anti-tumor immune efficacy. To address this critical therapeutic bottleneck, we fabricated a novel macrophage membrane-biomimetic Cu/Ru dual-atom nanocatalyst (CRM) for synergistic Flash-RT tumor immunotherapy. Equipped with abundant macrophage membrane-derived SIRPα, intravenously injected CRM achieves long-term immune camouflage and accurate tumor accumulation, which efficiently blocks the CD47 “don’t eat me” immune checkpoint signal. The uniform Cu/Ru dual-atom active sites act as high-performance radiosensitizers to significantly amplify intracellular reactive oxygen species generation under Flash irradiation, triggering severe tumor cell apoptosis and reprogramming metabolic phenotypes of tumor-associated macrophages (TAM). This synergistic combinatorial strategy effectively reverses immunosuppressive M2 polarization of TAM, robustly enhances macrophage-mediated tumor phagocytosis, and activates durable systemic anti-tumor immune responses. In vitro and in vivo experimental results consistently confirm that CRM remarkably boosts the anti-tumor efficacy of Flash-RT, efficiently suppressing primary tumor growth and distant tumor metastasis. This study presents a novel and reliable dual-atom biomimetic nanocatalytic platform to optimize FLASH radiotherapy-based tumor immunotherapy for solid tumors.

works.title: Ultra-low-temperature seawater zinc–air batteries enabled by carbon nanochannel-confined high-entropy alloy catalysts
works.abstract: Abstract Seawater-based solid-state zinc–air batteries are attractive for extreme-environment applications because of their high energy density, intrinsic safety, low-temperature operability, and in situ resource utilization. However, sluggish cathodic oxygen redox kinetics at low temperatures and catalyst degradation in strongly alkaline seawater severely compromise their energy efficiency and cycling stability. We synthesized a noble-metal-free high-entropy alloy (HEA) nanoparticle catalyst with carbon nanochannel confinement by rapid Joule heating. The resulting catalyst couples this physical confinement with the distinctive electronic structure of the HEA. Molecular dynamics simulations show that this confinement increases the local probability of finding O2 and OH- near the catalyst surface, creating a favorable interfacial environment for oxygen redox reactions at low temperatures. Structural characterizations reveal that the confined carbon architecture limits direct exposure of the HEA to the alkaline chloride-containing electrolyte. The resulting seawater-mimetic hydrogel solid-state zinc–air battery, prepared with 8 M KOH containing 3.1 wt% NaCl, delivers a peak power density of 407.82 mW cm-2 and a specific capacity of 664.2 mAh gZn-1 at room temperature. It operates stably for over 800 cycles at −60 °C and 8 mA cm-2 while 1.4–3.1 wt% NaCl cells remain reversible at −60 °C; 7.0 wt% NaCl is a high-salinity stress condition that fails after 68 cycles. A solar-rechargeable battery powers a smartphone and an LED array at −60 °C, demonstrating reliable cryogenic operation and offering a practical route to salinity-tolerant low-temperature solid-state batteries.

works.title: Solid‐State Nanopores for High‐Accuracy Readout of Linear Biomolecules
works.abstract: Solid-state nanopores offer a robust and highly integrable platform for single-molecule analysis, with advantages over biological pores that include superior mechanical stability, tunable geometry, and compatibility with scalable device fabrication. High-precision readout of linear biomolecules is fundamental to DNA sequencing, diagnostic strategies, and protein or peptide sequencing. Here we review recent progress in improving the detection of linear biomolecules, including DNA, proteins, and peptides, with emphasis on the physical limits of readout, translocation control, and device optimization. We discuss the major factors that constrain precision, including rapid transport, stochastic dynamics, molecular folding, and device-dependent noise, and summarize engineering strategies that address these challenges through mechanical manipulation, gate-controlled translocation, and electric field coupled nanopores. We also highlight recent advances in ultrasmall nanopores for high-resolution molecular sensing and consider future opportunities for extending solid-state nanopores toward accurate and scalable linear-molecule analysis.

works.title: A Breathable Nanomesh–Textile Electrode Interface for Integrated Multimodal Monitoring
works.abstract: Long-term wearable electrophysiology requires electrodes that are skin-conformal, breathable, mechanically stable, and reliably connected to electronics. Existing dry electrodes address parts of this challenge, but the interface between soft electrodes and wearable electronics remains a major source of motion artifacts, open-circuit failure, and poor long-term usability. Here, we introduce a duo-electrode interface that separates the functions of skin contact and electronic interconnection. An electrospun nanomesh serves as a tattoo electrode that conforms intimately to the skin, while a compressible conductive taffeta-foam fabric electrode embedded in a garment provides stable electrical coupling to textile-routed electronics. This architecture preserves the advantages of skin-conformal electrodes while avoiding fragile connections to electronics. We integrate the interface into a bodysuit and eyemask platform for multimodal monitoring of ECG, EMG, EOG, and body position using a centralized electronics module. The system maintains reliable signal acquisition under body motion and muscle activation, with performance comparable to or better than that of commercial hydrogel electrodes. By bridging breathable electrodes with textile-based routing, the proposed duo-electrode strategy establishes a practical method for scalable, comfortable, and long-duration wearable bioelectronic monitoring. This approach may be broadly useful for remote healthcare, rehabilitation, sleep studies, human-machine interfaces, and personalized physiological sensing.

works.title: Quantitative Measurement of Li‐Ion Concentration in NCM811 Cathodes via Optimized Electrochemical Strain Microscopy
works.abstract: Inter-particle state-of-charge (SOC) heterogeneity governs electrochemical degradation in Ni-rich layered oxide cathodes, yet quantifying the underlying nanoscale lithium distribution remains inaccessible to bulk-averaging characterization techniques and impractical for destructive nanoscale probes. Here, a practical process for nanoscale Li-ion quantification in NCM811 cathodes is established by optimizing the measurement conditions of electrochemical strain microscopy (ESM). Through rational probe selection to suppress electrostatic artifacts and contact potential difference drift sensitivity combined with a markedly reduced acquisition time, a quantitative calibration framework directly correlating pixel-averaged ESM amplitude with ICP-MS-derived bulk Li concentration is constructed. Classification among three SOCs exceeds 90% accuracy with as few as four images per sample. This work establishes multi-particle ESM imaging as a statistically robust and non-destructive platform for nanoscale Li-ion quantification in NCM811 cathodes, with broad applicability across mixed ionic-electronic conductors in which local Vegard strain arises from ion redistribution.

works.title: Faceted Photocatalytic Microswimmers for Adaptive Navigation and Cargo Transport via Structured Illumination
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise navigation of photocatalytic microswimmers typically requires external fields, physical confinement, chemical gradients, or feedback control, limiting their operation in dynamically changing environments. Here, light‐programmable faceted BiVO 4 microswimmers are introduced, where structured illumination provides both the energy for propulsion and the spatial information required for navigation. While uniform illumination activates self‐propulsion without directional guidance, patterned illumination defines light–dark interfaces that the microswimmers autonomously follow through continuous reorientation. Fluorescence mapping, EPR spectroscopy, tracer‐particle experiments, facet‐distribution controls, and numerical simulations support a mechanism in which partial illumination creates asymmetric photocatalytic activity, generating local chemical gradients and associated flow fields around the particle. These local imbalances allow microswimmers to remain coupled to projected boundaries, adapt to static and dynamically reconfigured geometries, and follow independently programmed trajectories within the same field of view. The same strategy enables light‐controlled cargo capture, transport, and release along confined and serpentine pathways. Overall, this work establishes an all‐optical strategy to activate, direct, and reprogram photocatalytic microswimmer motion, enabling adaptive navigation and cargo transport along complex pathways.

works.title: Lysozyme-Modified Graphene/Silicon Carbide Heterostructure Fillers in a Cellulose/Polyvinyl Alcohol Matrix as a Multifunctional Composite for Thermal Management, Joule Heating, and Surface Adaptability
works.abstract: Abstract With the rapid advancement of electronic devices, flexible wearables, and battery packs, efficient thermal management has become an increasingly critical challenge. Herein, we report a high-performance composite for multifunctional thermal management, fabricated by incorporating heterostructure fillers of silicon carbide/lysozyme-modified graphene nanoplatelets (SiC@LmGNPs) into a cellulose nanofiber/polyvinyl alcohol (CNF/PVA) hybrid matrix. The optimized SiC@G80/CP20 composite (80 wt % SiC@LmGNP and 20 wt % CNF/PVA) exhibits an ultra-high in-plane thermal conductivity (TC) of 195.91 W·m−1·K−1, a high through-plane TC of 10.54 W·m−1·K−1, and a tensile strength of 25.61 MPa. Moreover, the composite exhibits a rapid Joule heating response (reaching 33.7 °C within 1.5 s) and favorable thermal stability. Additionally, the composite demonstrates excellent surface adaptability; its surface can be softened by ethanol−water mixture treatment, enabling tight conformal contact with target surfaces. This work provides valuable guidance for the design and development of multifunctional smart thermal management materials with integrated thermal, mechanical, electrical, and interfacial characteristics for next-generation electronic devices and energy storage systems.

works.title: Regulation of Fibroblast Spreading on Fused Silica Square Nanocone Arrays: Implications for Biomedical Applications
works.abstract: Abstract Developing and exploring fabrication techniques for nanostructured biomaterials that enable precise geometric control of the features for mediating cell−nanopattern interactions are essential for cutting-edge biomedical applications. Herein, we utilized a UV laser interference lithography (LIL) combined with an inductively coupled plasma (ICP) etching technique to fabricate 3D nanocones (NCs) with precisely controlled varying top geometries in square arrays on large-area fused silica substrates. The arrangement of NCs was designed via LIL, and the single parameter of the nanocone top diameter can be systematically modulated from 200 nm to 700 nm by ICP etching processing; thereby, the surface energy and wettability of the patterned surfaces were controlled accordingly. We then investigated the interactions of fibroblasts (L929) with these geometrical cues of NCs with changing adhesive area ratio (AAR) and flat substrates. Varying the AAR from 0.02 to 0.22 exerted pronounced impacts on the fibroblast morphology and directional alignment behavior of the fibroblasts. The cell circularity decreased from 0.76 to 0.35, and the aspect ratio increased from 1.66 to 4.11, the cell spreading area improved from 18.77% to 25.97%, and cell alignment shifts from a single axial orientation (0°) gradually toward a diagonal orientation (45°), finally forming dual orientations. We found that the topological nanocone-induced changes in cell morphology, spreading, and aspect ratio are predominantly governed by cytoskeletal remodeling, accompanied by adaptive nuclear morphological remodeling. The high-throughput and precise fabrication method proposed in this study, by enabling geometrically controlled tuning of the AAR, supports various morphogenetic trends in fibroblast cells, thus providing a viable platform for the design of future scaffolds.

works.title: Photovoltaic Modulation of MoS2 Transistors via Interfacial Photoelectron Injection in Pn-Si/MoS2/h-BN Heterostructures
works.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor transistors offer attractive optoelectronic functionality beyond the scaling limits of conventional silicon technology. However, conventional 2D phototransistors often suffer from limited photoresponse performance, high energy consumption, and unstable threshold voltage. To overcome these challenges, we demonstrate a photovoltaic modulated field-effect transistor based on a pn-Si/MoS2/h-BN heterostructure. Under visible illumination, photogenerated electrons accumulate near the pn-Si/MoS2 interface and are vertically injected into the adjacent MoS2 conduction channel. A current change from approximately 3.8 μA to 11.2 μA is observed when illumination is switched on during a gate-voltage sweep, corresponding to a switching-event current ratio of approximately 2.95. Concurrently, the device exhibits reversible current modulation during the recorded optical ON/OFF cycles. Wavelength-dependent measurements further elucidate a critical competition between injection-driven carrier enhancement and high-field suppression effects. First-principles calculations using monolayer MoS2/h-BN heterostructure models further show that electron doping increases the electrical conductivity of MoS2 by increasing the occupation of conduction-band states and improving carrier transport. These results demonstrate optical modulation in Si-supported MoS2 devices and motivate further investigation of the contributions from interfacial carrier transfer and photovoltaic gating.

works.title: Morphology-Tunable CeO2-Shelled Gold Nanospheres for Synergistic Photothermal and Dual Enzyme-Like Antibacterial Performance
works.abstract: Abstract Multifunctional nanomaterials are promising for effective antibacterial applications, yet single-component systems remain limited by insufficient catalytic activity and poor biocompatibility. Herein, core−shell Au@CeO2 nanocomposites with porous (Au@P−CeO2) and sheet-like (Au@S−CeO2) morphologies were constructed to achieve photothermal−catalytic synergistic antibacterial performance. The Au core enables efficient photothermal conversion, while the CeO2 shell provides dual enzyme-mimetic activitiesperoxidase-like for •OH generation and superoxide dismutase-like for •O2− scavenging. Au@S−CeO2 exhibits superior POD activity and completely eradicates Staphylococcus aureus (with 0.001 wt % H2O2) and E. coli (with 0.002 wt % H2O2) at only 3 μg mL−1 (based on Ce) in the dark; 660 nm laser irradiation further reduces the bactericidal threshold to 2 μg mL−1 via photothermal−catalytic synergy. Both nanocomposites maintain excellent hemocompatibility and cytocompatibility (cell viability >95%) at working doses. This work offers a facile strategy for integrating photothermal and dual enzyme-mimetic functions into a single nanoplatform for multifunctional antibacterial applications.

works.title: Laser Photoacoustic Spectroscopy for Nanoscale Chiroptical Sensing in Strongly Absorbing and Resonant Environments
works.abstract: Abstract Chiroptical detection at the nanoscale remains particularly challenging when the chiral response originates from a nanostructured object embedded in a strongly absorbing and optically dispersive environment. This limitation is especially relevant for plasmonic metasurfaces, where substrate absorption and resonant optical backgrounds can obscure the circular dichroism (CD) associated with the nanostructured layer. Here, we demonstrate that laser photoacoustic spectroscopy (PAS) enables the enhanced sensitivity to the chiroptical response of plasmonic elliptical nanohole arrays (ENHAs) supported by absorbing resonant Si3N4/Si substrates. The investigated structures consist of a 60 nm thick Au layer, nanopatterned by electron-beam lithography; three samples with different geometries provide a model platform for studying helicity-dependent absorption in nanoscale plasmonic systems. The chiroptical response is assessed by PAS, which combines polarization-resolved excitation with modulation-frequency control, to enhance sensitivity to the nanoscale surface layer. The PAS measurements reveal pronounced wavelength-dependent CD resonances, whereas the substrate remains achiral despite its strong optical absorption. Furthermore, the measured CD systematically increases with modulation frequency, suggesting that frequency-dependent thermal diffusion enhances the relative sensitivity to chiroptical responses originating from the nanoscale surface layer. Numerical simulations agree with the experimental results and confirm the plasmonic origin of the chiral response. These findings establish PAS as a powerful platform for resolving nanoscale chirality in complex resonant environments where conventional far-field optical measurements are limited by strong background absorption and optical dispersion.

works.title: Chiral Materials for the Recognition and Inhibition of Amyloid‐β Aggregation
works.abstract: Abnormal aggregation of amyloid-β (Aβ) peptides is a central pathological event in Alzheimer's disease (AD), closely associated with neurotoxicity and disease progression. The development of molecules or materials with high selectivity and affinity toward Aβ aggregates constitutes an essential component for the early diagnosis and intervention of AD. Aβ peptides, composed of homochiral amino acids, undergo intermolecular β-sheet assembly to form supramolecular chiral aggregates, providing a structural basis for chirality-sensitive recognition. Therefore, chiral materials have attracted significant attention in Aβ aggregates recognition and regulation. Previous reviews have examined different types of chiral materials for the inhibition of Aβ aggregation, including chiral small molecules, amino acids, peptides, and various chiral interfaces or nanomaterials. The present review organizes reported chiral materials according to three intervention strategies for modulating Aβ aggregation: conformation-locking, self-assembly-induced remodeling, and multifunctional intervention. We summarize representative materials in each category, along with the corresponding design principles and modulation performance toward Aβ aggregation. Current challenges and potential directions for the development of chiral therapeutics for AD are also discussed.

works.title: An Iron Disulfide‐Decorated Polymeric Carbon Nitride Integrated Photocatalytic Irrigation System Promotes Cartilage Repair via Transient H 2 O 2 ‐Mediated Immune Regulation
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Acute inflammation and necrosis in the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) hinder cartilage repair by disrupting immune–chondrocyte crosstalk and reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis. Photocatalytic production of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) offers a promising approach for reconstituting the local microenvironment by debriding and healing damaged tissue. However, achieving high catalytic activity and selectivity for efficient and controllable ROS regulation remains challenging. Herein, we developed an iron disulfide (FeS 2 )‐decorated polymeric carbon nitride (PCN‐FeS 2 ) composite as an efficient visible‐light–driven photocatalyst for controlled H 2 O 2 generation. The optimized PCN‐FeS 2 exhibited an H 2 O 2 production rate of 1657 µmol·L − 1 ·h − 1 , representing an 8.3‐fold enhancement over pristine PCN, owing to improved charge separation and efficient conversion of toxic superoxide radical (·O 2 − ) intermediates. This catalytic system was designed for transient intra‐articular lavage under acute inflammatory stress, providing controlled, light‐triggered H 2 O 2 generation to promote a reparative microenvironment while minimizing material retention. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in a rat model of lipopolysaccharide‐induced acute TMJ arthritis, in which PCN‐FeS 2 was administered through transient low‐pressure intermittent intra‐articular irrigation. Moreover, the oxidation signal contributed to the differentiation of IL10 + regulatory B cells (Bregs) to facilitate chondrocyte recovery. Overall, this study provides a translationally feasible strategy that integrates catalytic chemistry with endogenous immunocommunication for acute TMJ pathology.

works.title: Pagoda‐Inspired Microneedles for Multiphase Coverage Wound Healing
works.abstract: Microneedle patches are considered as an attractive technology for wound treatment. Current researches are devoted to enhancing the structure and functionality of microneedles to cover multiphase for wound healing. Here, we present a desired quaternized chitosan-coated pagoda-inspired microneedle (QPDMN) patch loaded with diverse drugs to treat wounds. The QPDMN tips are comprised of a bottom layer loading vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and a top layer containing antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), as well as with the outer surface coated with quaternized chitosan (QCS). When applied, QCS could firstly contact wounds and rapidly promote blood clotting. Subsequently, AMPs released from top needles could remarkably inhibit bacterium growth, while VEGF released from bottom tips effectively facilitate tissue regeneration. Animal experiments have further proved that the QPDMN system has rapid hemostasis, enhanced angiogenesis, anti-inflammation and collagen deposition performances, coordinating the different phases of wound healing. Thus, we believe that the pagoda-like microneedles could be an excellent multiphase-coverage therapeutic agent in clinic wound healing.

works.title: Synergistic Sulfur‐Atom Positioning and Acceptor Engineering Enable Preferential Type‐I Photodynamic Therapy
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Less oxygen‐independent Type‐I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated by photosensitizers offer distinct advantages for tumor photodynamic therapy (PDT). However, most conventional photosensitizers activate nonselective mixed ROS pathways, significantly hindering the advancement of PDT. In this study, we propose a synergistic molecular design strategy that integrates sulfur‐atom positioning and acceptor engineering to achieve preferential Type‐I ROS generation. We identified a novel near‐infrared Type‐I photosensitizer NS4 . Combined theoretical calculations and experimental characterizations demonstrate that sulfur substitution enhances the S 1 ‐T 1 intersystem crossing, while acceptor engineering promotes a pronounced twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT). This TICT effect lowers the energy of the S 1 state and stabilizes the T 1 state, thereby synergistically enabling the preferential production of Type‐I ROS. Both free NS4 derivative and NS‐NPs , self‐assembled from NS4 and F‐127, can generate substantial amounts of Type‐I ROS under 660 nm laser irradiation, effectively triggering tumor cell apoptosis. In vivo assessments confirm that a single dose of NS‐NPs significantly suppresses tumor growth with negligible systemic toxicity. This work establishes theoretical and structural guidelines for the rational design of high‐performance Type‐I photosensitizers and facilitates the further translation of PDT.

works.title: A Two‐Stage Strategy to Reprogram Cyanine Photosensitizers as Controllable‐Pyroptosis Inducers for Anticancer Phototherapy
works.abstract: Pyroptosis, a lytic and inflammatory form of programmed cell death, provides a promising strategy for antitumor immunotherapy. However, controllable modulation of pyroptosis using phototherapeutic agents remains challenging. In this study, we report a two-stage molecular reprogramming method to rationally design cyanine photosensitizers with tunable pyroptosis-inducing activity. We first reprogram IR808 into a novel photosensitizer T808, by integrating a tetraphenylethylene unit with IR808, which consequently enhances excited - state features related to intersystem crossing (ISC) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation capability, accompanied by inducing pyroptosis under irradiation. In the second process, T808 is conjugated with poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) chains of varying lengths (M.W. 550, 1000, and 2000 Da) to finely modulate the pyroptotic efficacy. The relationship of PEG chain length with pyroptosis-inducing activity is in the order of PT550 > T808 > PT1000 >> PT2000. Cellular and in vivo studies show that T808, PT550, and PT1000 treatments suppress tumor growth and induce pyroptosis with occurrence of immunogenic cell death (ICD). Even under a lower intratumoral injection dose (25 µM), T808 and PT550 therapies exhibit remarkable antitumor efficacy with measurable pyroptosis features. This work provides a new insight into reprogramming cyanine photosensitizers into pyroptosis-active molecules, and proposes possible structural association of PEGylated cyanines with the pyroptosis activity.

works.title: Artemisinin‐Loaded Core‐Shell Microspheres Modulate Histone Lactylation to Remodel the Microenvironment for Cartilage Protection in Rheumatoid Arthritis
works.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) involves persistent inflammation and metabolic dysregulation that jointly drive cartilage damage. Although lactate accumulates in arthritic joints, the role of lactate-induced histone lactylation in cartilage progenitor cell (CPC) dysfunction remains unclear. Here, we developed an injectable, tissue-adhesive core-shell microsphere (ART@PLGA@GH-A) for sustained intra-articular delivery of artemisinin (ART). CUT&Tag sequencing identified a pathological lactate-H4K16la-Ccnb2 axis in RA-derived CPCs, in which lactate accumulation enhanced H4K16la enrichment at the Ccnb2 promoter, promoting mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, and extracellular matrix degradation. ART@PLGA@GH-A suppressed H4K16la deposition at the Ccnb2 locus and more effectively inhibited CPC senescence and glycolytic lactate production than ART-loaded hydrogel microspheres (ART@GH). Mechanistically, ART@PLGA@GH-A promoted macrophage polarization from pro-inflammatory M1 toward anti-inflammatory M2, reduced intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, restored mitochondrial membrane potential and dynamics, enhanced chondrogenic markers (COL II, Aggrecan, and SOX9), and reduced matrix-degrading enzymes (MMP13 and ADAMTS5). In collagen-induced arthritis rats, a single intra-articular injection of ART@PLGA@GH-A reduced subchondral bone erosion and proteoglycan loss and improved hindlimb gait function, outperforming free ART and non-adhesive microspheres. Therefore, ART@PLGA@GH-A targets the lactate-dependent H4K16la-Ccnb2 axis and restores joint homeostasis, thereby achieving synergistic anti-inflammatory, anti-senescent, and chondroprotective effects and providing a clinically translatable local therapeutic strategy for RA.

works.title: Ultralow-Loss Femtosecond Laser Slicing of Lithium Niobate Enabled by Anisotropic Thermal Dissipation-Guided Vector Scanning
works.abstract: Abstract Lithium niobate (LiNbO3) crystals have been widely used in photonic and electronic devices owing to their outstanding intrinsic optoelectronic properties. However, fabricating hundreds-of-micrometer-thick LiNbO3 wafers remains dominated by diamond wire sawing, which causes substantial material loss. Although ultrafast laser processing offers a promising alternative, the intrinsic noncentrosymmetric lattice, spontaneous polarization, and anisotropic photothermal response of LiNbO3 severely hinder high-quality laser cutting. Here, a thermal dissipation-guided vector scanning technology is proposed to realize ultrafast laser slicing of LiNbO3 crystals for the first time. By tailoring the scanning direction according to the anisotropic thermal dissipation, we achieve crystal exfoliation with an ultrathin subsurface damage layer of 10 μm and an exceptionally high-quality separation surface. The results establish vector scanning technology as an innovative route for high-quality femtosecond laser processing and low-damage separation of anisotropic crystals.

works.title: Defect-Initiated Anisotropic Oxidation in Two-Dimensional GaSe
works.abstract: Abstract Oxidation governs the stability and functional conversion of two-dimensional semiconductors, yet its propagation through layered crystals remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the thickness-dependent oxidation of GaSe using optical spectroscopy, cross-sectional microscopy, and first-principles calculations. Experiments reveal concurrent top-down and edge-initiated oxidation, accompanied by Se redistribution and transient Ga2Se3 formation. Calculations identify Se vacancies as favorable sites for O2 adsorption and activation, which weaken neighboring Ga–Se bonds and promote oxygen incorporation. Molecular O2 faces a 4.03 eV barrier when penetrating a monolayer Ga2O3 model, compared with 0.54 eV along a GaSe van der Waals gap. This contrast supports interlayer diffusion as a plausible pathway for lateral oxidation, consistent with the pronounced thickness dependence and spatial anisotropy observed experimentally. Oxidation also yields a progression from p-type GaSe through ambipolar Ga2O3/GaSe heterostructures to n-type Ga2O3, whose devices retain stable characteristics after 300 °C air annealing.

works.title: Ultrathin SrTiO3 Capping Stabilizes the Surface Chemistry of Brownmillerite Ferrites during Reduction
works.abstract: Abstract Redox processes in oxides are central to materials synthesis and functionality, but their control is often hindered by surface instabilities. Using ambient-pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, we show that a nominally 1 nm-thick SrTiO3 (STO) cap markedly enhances the surface stability of La0.05Sr0.95FeO2.5-δ (LSFO) thin films during H2 reduction by suppressing the formation of a secondary metallic Fe0 phase. Kinetic analysis indicates that the STO cap reduces the effective Fe0 formation rates by more than 6-fold at both 250 and 350 °C. These findings highlight ultrathin capping layers as an effective strategy for stabilizing oxide surfaces during redox.

works.title: Photoinduced Carrier Doping of α-RuCl3 through Interlayer Charge Transfer
works.abstract: Abstract Controlling doping density in correlated quantum materials offers a route to tuning their electronic states, but chemical doping can introduce disorder and limits dynamic control. Here, we demonstrate optically tunable electron doping of the layered Mott insulator α-RuCl3 through photoinduced interlayer charge transfer in MoS2/α-RuCl3 heterostructures. Photoluminescence and transient absorption measurements support electron transfer to α-RuCl3, leaving holes in MoS2. The layer-separated carrier population persists for more than 100 ps with an estimated doping density tunable through the excitation fluence. Selective excitation of α-RuCl3 further reveals hole transfer to MoS2. Transient absorption microscopy yields an early time effective hole diffusion coefficient of approximately 100 cm2 s–1 in the heterostructure, supporting a predominantly unbound carrier population. These results establish photoinduced charge transfer as a means of dynamically controlling carrier doping in α-RuCl3, providing a route toward optical manipulation of correlated electronic states.

works.title: Emergent Giant Topological Hall Effect at the van der Waals Ferromagnet/Topological Insulator Interface
works.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnet-based heterostructures provide a vital platform for manipulating magnetic ground states and hosting complex spin textures. The topological Hall effect (THE) is a powerful tool for probing these textures in such systems. However, achieving a sizable THE in 2D vdW ferromagnets remains challenging due to the absence of broken inversion symmetry and sufficiently strong spin–orbit coupling (SOC). Here, we report an emergent giant topological Hall resistivity of 6.9 μΩ·cm at 10 K by interfacing the 2D ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) with the topological insulator BiSbTeSe2 (BSTS). Systematic temperature- and thickness-dependent studies suggest the origin of this pronounced signal to be the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI). Furthermore, temperature-field mapping reveals the coexistence of two distinct phases that we identify as having opposite topological charge. Our results establish these vdW ferromagnet/topological insulator heterostructures as a robust platform for enhanced interfacial THE, opening new avenues for high-efficiency topological spintronics.

works.title: Photoluminescence-Driven Quasi-BICs in Photonic Nanomembranes for Active Refractometric Sensing
works.abstract: Abstract Quasi-bound states in the continuum (quasi-BICs) offer a powerful platform for refractometric sensing by combining narrow resonances with strong electromagnetic confinement, promising high spectral resolution and large figures of merit (FOM). In practice, however, these advantages are often compromised by stringent angular alignment in passive transmission/reflection interrogation. Here, we demonstrate an active sensing platform that couples the defect-related photoluminescence (PL) of a freestanding silicon nitride nanomembrane to quasi-BIC modes. The substrate-free architecture suppresses radiation leakage and sustains tightly confined high-Q resonances, while emission-based readout bypasses stringent angular alignment. The resulting PL resonances exhibit line widths of 0.17 nm (Q ≈ 4000) in air and 0.26 nm in water. In aqueous sensing, the platform achieves a FOM of 250, substantially exceeding representative values reported for passive quasi-BIC sensors in the visible regime. This synergy translates the high-Q advantage of quasi-BICs into a practical active platform for high-performance refractometric and surface-binding sensing.

works.title: A probiotic-delivered AIEgen/natural medicine biohybrid system for prostate cancer therapy via HMGB2 targeting
Dual-crosslinked anisotropic alginate aerogels with Ca/Si–O synergistic networks for high-efficiency building energy management
A wound-reporting multiresponsive hydrogel with catalytic metal–polyphenol nanosheets and protease-responsive angiogenic depots for diabetic irradiated wound repair
works.abstract: Patients undergoing cancer treatment may have comorbidities such as diabetes, which compromise wound repair. Radiation-induced oxidative stress, inflammation, and microvascular dysfunction can aggravate hyperglycemia-associated oxidative injury, susceptibility to infection, and impaired angiogenesis, creating barriers to wound healing. However, biomaterial-based strategies addressing these multiple repair barriers remain limited. We developed a composite hydrogel based on phenylboronic-acid-grafted oxidized hyaluronic acid (OHA-PBA)/carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCS) and incorporating Cu–EGCG nanosheets, bromothymol blue (BTB), and deferoxamine-loaded gelatin microspheres (G@D). This system integrates semiquantitative visual pH indication with pH/ROS/MMP-9-responsive therapeutic release. Under combined stimulation with pH 5.0 and 5 mM H 2 O 2 , complete degradation occurred within 13.7 ± 1.90 h, while MMP-9-responsive deferoxamine (DFO) release reached 44.69 ± 1.38% at 120h in vitro . The optimized formulation containing 200 µg mL − 1 Cu–EGCG (HCC2B-G@D) reduced the proportion of DCFH-positive irradiated cells to 10.60 ± 1.15%, promoted an anti-inflammatory/M2-like macrophage phenotype, and decreased MRSA and E. coli counts by 4–5 log 10 units. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that its antibacterial activity involved cell-envelope disruption, oxidative damage, metabolic dysregulation, and virulence suppression. In vivo performance was evaluated in two complementary settings. In MRSA-infected wounds in Bama miniature pigs, HCC2B-G@D reduced the bacterial burden and promoted wound repair. In diabetic rats in which full-thickness wounds were created 2 days after local X-ray irradiation, HCC2B-G@D significantly accelerated wound closure and tissue regeneration under acute irradiation-impaired conditions. These effects were associated with reduced NF-κB-related inflammatory signaling, a molecular pattern consistent attenuated ferroptosis-associated changes and enhanced SLC7A11/GPX4-related antioxidant defense, and increased PI3K–AKT/HIF-1α/VEGF-related signaling. This study presents a multiresponsive smart-dressing strategy that integrates colorimetric pH monitoring, adaptive therapeutic delivery, and microenvironment regulation, with complementary efficacy demonstrated in MRSA-infected wounds and acute irradiation-impaired diabetic wounds.

works.title: Immunomodulatory copper-doped Houttuynia cordata derived carbon dots enable acute lung injury therapy via near infrared-amplified mitophagy
works.abstract: Abstract Acute lung injury (ALI) is an acute progressive hypoxic respiratory failure driven by various pathogenic factors. The current therapeutic strategies mainly focus on controlling the primary disease, and offering protective support but show limited efficacy in pulmonary repair. Herein, a novel type of novel carbon dot (CC@SS31) was fabricated by hydrothermal reaction of Houttuynia cordata followed by ultra-small copper loading and SS31 modification, which exhibited the various mimetic enzymatic activities. Combining with near infrared (NIR) irradiation, CC@SS31 + NIR had confirmed the enhanced functions of reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging, downregulation of inflammatory cytokines, upregulation of anti-inflammatory cytokines as well as promotion of tissue repair factors. In ALI rat models, it had demonstrated that CC@SS31 + NIR could be enriched in the lung, further to alleviate the ROS levels of lung, reduce lung inflammation, and promote the tissue repair with high biosafety. Furthermore, the amplified mitophagy was induced following CC@SS31 + NIR treatment, thereby effectively and precisely promoting the mitochondrial functions repair. Significantly, CC@SS31 + NIR also activated immunoregulation by inducing macrophages M2 polarization, and modulating T cells ratio, thus re-establishing pulmonary immune homeostasis. The work provided a mechanistic foundation for natural derived carbon dots as the multiple functions therapeutic strategies in inflammation related disease. Graphical abstract

works.title: Assembly of FA/PBA-functionalized albumin nanoparticles with hyaluronic acid-mitomycin C for integrated chemo-antiangiogenic therapy and macrophage reprogramming in colorectal cancer peritoneal metastasis
works.abstract: Colorectal cancer peritoneal metastasis (PM) is characterized by rapid progression, pathological angiogenesis, malignant ascites, and an M2 macrophage-dominated tumor microenvironment, which limit the efficacy of single-agent therapy. Herein, we constructed Reg@BFP-HM NPs by associating a hyaluronic acid-mitomycin C (HA-MMC, HM) with regorafenib-loaded folic acid/phenylboronic acid-modified bovine serum albumin nanoparticles (Reg@BFP NPs). Reg@BFP and HM were assembled into an integrated nanostructure through multiple interactions. As a targeted therapeutic nanoplatform, BFP-HM enables folate receptor/CD44-mediated tumor delivery and improves the dispersion of Reg and MMC. After intraperitoneal administration, Reg@BFP-HM NPs showed stronger antitumor efficacy than either component alone. HM exerts potent cytotoxicity to eliminate tumor cells, whereas Reg inhibits angiogenesis and tumor proliferation through suppression of the VEGFR2/ERK pathway. In addition, BFP activates the TLR4/NF-κB pathway to promote macrophage reprogramming toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype, which acts in synergy with Reg to suppress the formation of malignant ascites. In a CT26-luc PM mouse model, Reg@BFP-HM NPs inhibited peritoneal tumor growth, markedly reduced ascites volume, and prolonged survival without obvious systemic toxicity. These results highlight the potential of Reg@BFP-HM NPs as a chemo-antiangiogenic strategy for PM treatment.

works.title: Correction: Erythrocyte membrane with CLIPPKF as biomimetic nanodecoy traps merozoites and attaches to infected red blood cells to prevent Plasmodium infection
An All‐Natural Multifunctional Hydrogel Incorporating Carrier‐Free Self‐Assembled Microparticles for the Treatment of S. aureus ‐Infected Wounds
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Multifunctional wound dressings combining antibacterial activity and tissue regeneration are highly desirable for infected wound management. In this study, a multifunctional chitosan‐gelatin hydrogel incorporating carrier‐free self‐assembled anisaldehyde‐tannic acid‐Zn 2 + (AA‐TA‐Zn 2 + ) bioactive microparticles is developed. These microparticles are fabricated through non‐covalent self‐assembly and metal‐phenolic coordination without additional polymeric carriers or surfactants. Anisaldehyde (AA) serves as both an antibacterial agent and a hydrophobic structural building block, while tannic acid (TA) and Zn 2 + provide complementary antioxidant and coordination functions. Incorporation of these microparticles into the chitosan‐gelatin matrix enhances the structural integrity and multifunctionality of the resulting composite hydrogel through dynamic intermolecular interactions. The hydrogel exhibits excellent injectability, self‐healing capability, tissue adhesion, and sustained release with pH‐responsive behavior. In vitro experiments demonstrate the antibacterial, antioxidant, and anti‐inflammatory activities of the microparticles and composite hydrogel, including their ability to alleviate oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, as well as the hydrogel's effectiveness in disrupting established Staphylococcus aureus biofilms. In a murine model of S. aureus ‐infected wounds, the hydrogel significantly accelerates wound closure and enhances collagen deposition and tissue restoration. This study presents a promising strategy for integrating carrier‐free bioactive microparticles into a natural biopolymer hydrogel matrix, offering a multifunctional platform for infected wound management.

works.title: Shelf‐Stable Human‐Derived Granular Extracellular Matrix (gECM) Hydrogel Wafers as 2.5D Substrates for Microphysiological Modeling
works.abstract: Understanding disease pathology and evaluating emerging therapeutics require in vitro models that accurately recapitulate human tissue environments. However, existing microphysiological systems often compromise either biomimicry or ease-of-use, limiting widespread adoption and scalability. Here, we present lyophilized granular extracellular matrix (gECM) hydrogel wafers as shelf-stable, humanized 2.5D substrates that enable physiologically relevant modeling while simplifying integration into experimental workflows. Derived from decellularized human cartilage and bone, our gECM hydrogel wafers retain tissue-specific architecture while introducing microporosity and surface topography through lyophilization. These wafers maintain swelling behavior, structural integrity, and mechanical properties over three months of room-temperature storage, allowing pre-fabrication and on-demand use without loss of function. gECM hydrogel wafers support direct cell seeding without encapsulation and sustain viability and proliferation of human adipose-derived mesenchymal stromal cells over 21 days. Furthermore, wafers can be readily integrated into proof-of-concept on-chip fabrication with in situ hydration and transport of large biomolecules. Together, this platform bridges the gap between conventional 2D culture ease-of-use and 3D biomaterial biomimicry, providing a scalable, physiologically-relevant, and humanized in vitro model approach that shows potential for future high-throughput disease studies and therapeutic screening.

works.title: Plant-Derived Extracellular Nanovesicles as Engineered Nanomaterials for Antibacterial Therapy and Infected Wound Repair
works.abstract: Abstract Chronic infected wounds are hard to treat because three problems must be addressed simultaneously: infection, persistent inflammation, and stalled tissue repair. Conventional therapies rarely address all three. Plant-derived extracellular vesicles (PDEVs), nanoscale lipid-bilayer particles typically tens to a few hundred nanometres in diameter that are isolated from edible and medicinal plants, are an emerging class of biogenic nanomaterials reported to combine antibacterial, antioxidant, and pro-regenerative activities. Native PDEVs are reported to disrupt bacterial membranes, limit biofilm formation, and influence all four phases of wound healing, although the evidence that these effects arise from the vesicles themselves, rather than from co-isolated phytochemicals or added agents, remains uneven. Their properties can be tuned by cargo loading, surface functionalization, membrane hybridization, and stimuli-responsive design, strategies borrowed from synthetic nanomaterials. Here, we treat PDEVs as an engineered nanomaterial platform: we distinguish naturally secreted vesicles from tissue-derived nanovesicles and reconstituted lipid vesicles; relate size, curvature, and surface charge to antibacterial and regenerative functions; grade the evidence for each proposed antibacterial mechanism; and compare engineering strategies and wound studies in study-level tables. We argue that the absence of standardized isolation, characterization, and potency assays, together with limited chronic-wound-relevant evidence, is the principal barrier to clinical and technological translation, rather than the discovery of additional plant sources.

works.title: Sheath-Engineered Nanoscale Silicon Pillar Arrays with Sunflower-Like Radial Tilt Gradients for Angle-Selective Optical Sensing
works.abstract: Abstract Silicon nanopillar arrays enable versatile optical functionalities through geometric design, yet most fabrication methods produce vertical or uniformly tilted structures, limiting the spatial programmability of their nanoscale morphology. Here, we present a simple strategy for fabricating silicon nanopillar arrays with a sunflower-like radial tilt gradient using capacitively coupled plasma reactive ion etching (CCP-RIE). The fabricated silicon pillars have an average diameter of approximately 500 nm, a height of approximately 2 μm, and an array periodicity of 5 μm, forming an ordered nanostructured array with submicrometer lateral dimensions and micrometer-scale height. By introducing a metal base on the powered electrode, sheath distortion is induced, generating a radial electric-field component that continuously modulates ion incidence across the substrate. As a result, the nanopillars exhibit a centrosymmetric tilt distribution, evolving from near-vertical at the center to increasingly oblique toward the edges. Systematic experiments show that at the same outermost radial position of the silicon sample, the nanopillar tilt angle increases from approximately 8° to approximately 19° as the metal-base height increases from 2 to 8 mm, while the inner radius has a negligible influence on the spatial tilt-angle distribution. Increasing the sample size preserves the tilt angles at the center and edges but reduces the spatial gradient. Numerical simulations support the conclusion that the tilt originates from the coupling between sheath deformation and ion-trajectory deflection. The radially graded pillar orientations break the uniform geometrical symmetry of conventional vertical arrays and provide a spatially varying structural anisotropy that may be relevant to angle-dependent light−structure interactions. Such arrays could therefore be considered candidate nanostructures for angle-selective optical sensing, in which the incident angle or direction of light may be distinguished through spatial variations in optical response. Although the optical functionality remains to be experimentally validated, this work establishes a direct relationship between electrode geometry, plasma dynamics, and nanoscale morphology and provides a route to spatially programmable silicon pillar arrays for future angle-dependent optical studies and sensing-device development.

works.title: Tunable Palladium Nanopores for Broadband Optical Absorber Coatings
works.abstract: Abstract Nanoporous palladium (np-Pd) is of interest for broadband optical absorber coatings, photothermal conversion, and plasmon-assisted catalysis because it combines metallic conductivity, high surface area, and hydrogen uptake capability within a single material system. However, to achieve high optical absorptivity, other plasmonically active materials are often employed to attain the necessary optical absorption. Here we demonstrate a simple, scalable route to tunable np-Pd thin films formed by chemical dealloying of co-sputtered Pd−Cu alloys. Composition- and angle-resolved absorption reveal broadband absorptance exceeding 85% between 450 nm and 800 nm. Effective-medium modeling based on Maxwell−Garnett theory accurately links the measured porosity to an effective dielectric function, while finite-difference time-domain simulations suggest morphology-driven plasmonic hot spots at Pd ligaments and junctions, with maximum local near-field intensity enhancements, |E/E0|2, of order 102 for the idealized simulated surfaces within the visible-to-near-infrared spectral range. This composition-controlled dealloying route provides a scalable strategy for np-Pd broadband absorber coatings, with potential extensions to photothermal conversion, plasmon-assisted catalysis, and hydrogen-related surface processes.

works.title: Bifunctional MnCoP Electrocatalytic Nanospheres for Selective Electrooxidation of Benzyl Alcohol Coupled with Hydrogen Evolution
works.abstract: Abstract Replacing the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction with value-added organic electrooxidation offers an effective strategy to reduce the energy consumption of water electrolysis while simultaneously producing industrially important chemicals. This work reports a bimetallic MnCoP electrocatalyst for the hydrogen evolution reaction and benzyl alcohol oxidation reaction in alkaline media. The catalyst exhibits an HER Tafel slope of 117 mV dec−1 and enhanced anodic kinetics toward BAOR. For benzyl alcohol oxidation, MnCoP requires potentials of only 1.27 V vs RHE to deliver current densities of 10 mA cm−2, with a Tafel slope of 80 mV dec−1. At 1.425 V versus RHE, the catalyst shows ∼100% benzyl alcohol conversion and benzoic acid selectivity with a Faradaic efficiency of ∼99.4%. Time-dependent 1H NMR and HPLC analyses establish a sequential oxidation pathway in which benzyl alcohol is initially converted to benzaldehyde, followed by further oxidation to benzoic acid. The catalyst also maintains its performance up to 20 cycles and displays broad applicability toward other substituted aromatic alcohols. Finally, a MnCoP||MnCoP electrolyser was fabricated, which enables simultaneous benzyl alcohol oxidation and hydrogen evolution at a lower cell voltage (1.5 V vs RHE) than conventional water splitting. These results establish MnCoP as a versatile bifunctional electrocatalyst for integrating energy-efficient hydrogen production with value-added organic electrosynthesis.

works.title: Sulfur-Tolerant Nitroarene Hydrogenation over PtNi/TiO2 Catalysts via Coupled Heterolytic H2 Activation and Hydrogen Spillover
works.abstract: Abstract Sulfur poisoning is a critical bottleneck for noble-metal hydrogenation catalysts, severely hindering efficient production of high-value sulfur-containing fine chemicals like pharmaceutical intermediates. Conventional sulfur-tolerant strategies, electronic modulation to weaken sulfur adsorption and spatial confinement to isolate metal sites, both face an inherent activity−sulfur tolerance trade-off: electronic modification impairs H2 activation of metal sites, while spatial barriers reduce active site accessibility. Herein, we propose a hydrogen-mediated design strategy and fabricate a PtNi NPs/TiO2 catalyst with Ni-induced abundant surface oxygen vacancies, forming Ptδ+···OV···O2− interfacial motifs at the metal−support interface. The catalyst delivers 2.7-fold and 3.6-fold higher 4-nitroanisole hydrogenation activity than Pt1/TiO2 single-atom and Pt NPs/TiO2 references. Under thiophene poisoning, it shows only 14.8% deactivation with 48.9- and 11.9-fold activity margins; for sulfur-containing 4-nitrothioanisole, it achieves 78.8-fold and 4.6-fold higher activity with >99% target amine selectivity. DFT calculations and D2 isotope labeling among other experiments confirm that Ptδ+···OV···O2− interfacial motifs promote heterolytic H2 cleavage, generating reactive hydrogen for selective nitro group hydrogenation while reducing direct Pt site exposure to sulfur. Oxygen vacancies mediate hydrogen spillover to create extra surface sites, further shielding Pt centers. Their synergism breaks the inherent trade-off and establishes clear structure−performance correlations for rational sulfur-resistant catalyst design.

works.title: Extreme Light Confinement Mediated by the Transverse Kerker Effect
works.abstract: Abstract Dielectric nanoparticles can be engineered to scatter light predominantly in the transverse direction, perpendicular to the incident plane wave’s propagation direction, a phenomenon known as the transverse Kerker effect. Although complete cancellation of forward scattering from a single object is forbidden by the optical theorem, we show that a single photonic mode can provide an ideal transverse Kerker effect. When combining several nanoparticles to form a metasurface, the mode evolves into an accidental bound state in the continuum. This enables polarization-independent quasi bound states in the continuum whose quality factors are tunable without symmetry breaking. We experimentally demonstrate our concept in the visible, achieving the first polarization-independent bound state in the continuum without Brillouin-zone folding. These modes maintain large quality factors over a broader region of momentum space than conventional bound states in the continuum. Our results establish a platform for realizing ultranarrow resonances free of conventional design constraints.

works.title: Designing Strong and Broadband Nonreciprocal Thermal Radiation in Magnetic Topological Materials
works.abstract: Abstract Breaking reciprocity in thermal radiation opens opportunities for energy harvesting, sensing, and thermal management. Traditional nonreciprocal radiative semiconductor devices need an external magnetic field. In this work, we predict a series of magnetic topological materials for magnetic-field-free nonreciprocal thermal radiation in the infrared regime by combining first-principles calculations with Maxwell electrodynamics. We find strong and broadband nonreciprocity in magnetic Weyl semimetals (e.g., Co3Sn2S2), outperforming conventional semiconductor InAs. Furthermore, we propose material design recipes. Strong nonreciprocity requires a large anomalous Hall response relative to the optical loss, whereas the broadband response favors a large optical loss and small dielectric dispersion. Our work establishes a predictive material discovery framework and quantitative design rules for next-generation magnet-free nonreciprocal thermal devices.

works.title: Direct Selenization Growth and Electronic Properties of Ultrathin Fe(Te,Se) on a van der Waals Ferromagnet
works.abstract: Abstract Fe(Te,Se) is a prototypical iron-based superconductor and a promising platform for exploring topological superconductivity. However, growing high-quality ultrathin Fe(Te,Se) films on magnetic substrates remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate epitaxial growth of monolayer-to-trilayer Fe(Te,Se) on the van der Waals itinerant ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) via direct selenization of the substrate, without external Fe or Te deposition. Combined scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS), low-energy electron diffraction (LEED), scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), and energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) characterizations reveal large-area, atomically flat tetragonal films with well-defined rotational alignment to the hexagonal FGT lattice. Cross-sectional STEM-EDS confirms Se incorporation and interfacial elemental redistribution. Thickness-dependent spectroscopy reveals evolving electronic structures and progressive decoupling from the ferromagnetic substrate. Measurements across lateral monolayer–bilayer interfaces further uncover asymmetric band bending and charge redistribution driven by Fermi-level equilibration. These findings establish substrate-mediated selenization as a versatile route to ultrathin superconducting heterostructures and magnetic quantum platforms.

works.title: Continuous, Size-Based Purification of Virus-like Particles Using Electro-Viscoelastic Microfluidics
works.abstract: Abstract The modular assembly of protein nanoparticles has enabled the design of highly immunogenic and cross-protective viral vaccines. However, downstream translation is hampered by labor-intensive purification methods that lack the resolution needed to efficiently sort molecular assemblies. Here, we report an affinity tag-free nanoparticle sorting platform that exploits electro-viscoelastic microfluidic (EVM) migration for the high-fidelity, continuous-flow isolation of virus-like particle (VLP) assemblies. This migration mechanism can overcome Brownian fluctuations, which are typically dominant on the nanoscale, confining the target assemblies to central streamlines for selective collection. In a single pass, the system segregates 40 nm VLPs from 6 nm excess antigen monomers, increasing the VLP purity by 20.2%. A sacrificial electrode outlet directs undesired electrohydrodynamic effects to the waste, preserving the VLP-rich product stream. Our results offer an alternative downstream framework for the rapid purification and quality control of complex bionanomaterials, establishing a scalable pathway for precision nanomedicine processing.

works.title: Atomic-Scale Signatures of Structural Irreversibility during Oxygen Redox in Li-Rich Layered Oxide Cathodes
works.abstract: Abstract Li-rich layered oxides access high capacity through transition-metal and oxygen redox, but oxygen loss and structural reconstruction cause large first-cycle irreversibility. Here, we examine Li1.2Ni0.13Co0.13Mn0.54O2 at four states of the first charge–discharge cycle using atomic-resolution STEM, nanobeam electron diffraction with electron pair distribution function (NBED-ePDF) analysis, electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS), image simulations, and DFT. Up to 4.3 V, Li extraction is dominated by interlayer sites and the slab framework remains largely preserved. At 4.8 V, changes in Li/O contrast and O K-edge features coincide with a short ePDF correlation near 1.57 Å. Seeded DFT relaxations stabilize short O–O pairs near vacancies in the transition-metal slab. After discharge, incomplete spectroscopic recovery accompanies near-surface reconstruction and oxygen-related contrast changes consistent with oxygen depletion. Together, the results implicate Li depletion from the transition-metal slab in high-voltage oxygen rearrangement and suggest that controlling this site occupancy may improve oxygen-redox reversibility.

works.title: High-Q/V Plasmonic Metasurfaces Enable Ultrafast Probing of Long-Lived Carrier Relaxation in Potassium
works.abstract: Abstract Alkali metals are promising materials for low-loss plasmonics, because of their intrinsically weak optical damping and favorable free-electron response. However, their high chemical reactivity and weak optical absorption make their ultrafast carrier dynamics difficult to access conventionally. Here, we investigate the long-lived carrier relaxation in potassium using a mode-engineered concave metasurface as a resonantly enhanced optical readout. A strongly confined hybrid mode with a high quality-factor-to-mode-volume ratio (Q/V) greatly enhances the sensitivity to pump-induced dielectric perturbations. Transient-reflectance spectroscopy resolves two characteristic relaxation times of ∼0.5 ps and ∼8 ps due to the electronic redistribution and electron–phonon-mediated energy relaxation, respectively. Two-temperature-model analysis yields a record-low electron–phonon coupling factor, consistent with weak electron-to-lattice energy transfer in potassium. These results demonstrate high-Q/V mode engineering as an effective strategy for accessing weak nonequilibrium carrier dynamics in low-loss plasmonic materials and for exploring light–matter interactions in minimally dissipative plasmonic environments.

works.title: Electroelasticity-Regulated Vacancy Diffusion Enables Frequency-Adaptive Neuromorphic Perception and Control
works.abstract: Abstract Emulating frequency-dependent synaptic plasticity requires artificial devices capable of integrating temporal inputs and adapting their responses. Here, we demonstrate electroelasticity-regulated vacancy diffusion in MoSe2 memristors as a physical mechanism for frequency-adaptive synaptic dynamics. An applied electric field induces lattice deformation that lowers the vacancy diffusion barrier, whereas poststimulus electroelastic relaxation progressively restores the barrier, creating a dynamically evolving diffusion landscape. This coupled electroelastic–ionic process gives rise to intrinsic second-order memristive dynamics and enables frequency- and history-dependent plasticity, including pair- and triplet-spike-timing-dependent plasticity and Bienenstock–Cooper–Munro-type learning with a sliding modification threshold. Leveraging these dynamics, memristor-based spiking neural networks realize adaptive neuromorphic functions spanning composite color–direction perception and autonomous drone control. These results establish electroelastic regulation of vacancy diffusion as a materials-level mechanism for translating temporal input statistics into adaptive synaptic responses, providing a pathway toward neuromorphic systems with frequency-adaptive perception and control.

works.title: Chirality–Polarity-Regulated Magnetic Vortex Chains for Ternary Logic
works.abstract: Abstract Spin-based multivalued logic offers compelling advantages for next-generation computing. Thus far, only binary systems─exploiting domain walls, skyrmions, and vortices─have been realized. These schemes rely solely on the manipulation of the chirality or polarity of magnetic carriers, precluding the implementation of multivalued logic operations. Here, we demonstrate the implementation of ternary logic operations using a one-dimensional vortex chain, via the co-manipulation of both the chirality and polarity of magnetic vortices. We show that ternary AND logic functionality can be achieved via dipole-mediated chirality modulation and domain-wall-assisted polarity reversal in the vortex chain, with operation times on the nanosecond scale. Our work establishes a viable and scalable platform for multivalue magnetic logic, thereby paving the way for next-generation spintronic logic applications.

works.title: Oxygen Evolution along Grain Boundaries of LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 Particles as an Early Stage Degradation of High-Voltage All-Solid-State Batteries
works.abstract: Abstract Operating sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries (SSBs) at high voltages increases energy density but induces O2 release from cathode materials, degrading battery performance. To elucidate this early stage degradation, SSBs were fabricated using LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 (NCM523) particles with distinct grain-boundary (GB) densities: single-crystalline (SC) or polycrystalline (PC). Gas analysis of SSBs during charging up to 5.0 V (vs Li/Li+) reveals that the PC-cell produces 27 times more O2 than the SC-cell despite having identical total surface areas. STEM-EELS analysis reveals 2–5 nm thick rock-salt phase formation across particle surfaces and along GBs regardless of the crystallinity, indicating that O2 evolution in the PC-cell occurs mainly along GBs of NCM523 particles. Because surface coating on the PC substantially suppresses O2 evolution, oxygen-vacancy formation initiated at the particle surface propagates O2 release along the GBs. Consequently, suppressing surface oxygen-vacancy formation represents a critical strategy for improving the long-term stability of high-voltage SSBs.

works.title: Twinning by Controlled Cluster Coalescence: A Unified Pathway to Single‐Crystalline, Single‐Twinned, and Penta‐Twinned Gold Nanocrystals
works.abstract: The twin structure of metal nanocrystals is essential for engineering their electric conductance, mechanical stress, thermal stability, as well as morphology. Yet the formation pathway of twin planes in a nanocrystal during colloidal synthesis has not been fully established due to the lack of high-yield single-twinned (ST) structures that are thermally stabilized between the single crystalline (SC) and penta-twinned (PT) phases. Here we verify a cluster coalescence mechanism that unifies the high-yield synthesis of SC, ST, and PT gold nanocrystals in solution. ST gold seeds with a yield exceeding 85% can be directly produced by adjusting the cluster coalescence to an intermediate level through the surface potential, density, and size of the clusters. Molecular dynamics simulations and control experiments indicate that the ST seeds are enriched after the coalescence of 2-4 clusters with a size of about 2-5 nm. This general paradigm provides design guidelines for the synthesis of metal nanocrystals with desired twin defects.

works.title: Interfacial Engineering of Mixed Ionic‐Electronic Conductors for Moisture‐Enabled Electric Generation
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Powered by the abundance and ubiquitousness of atmospheric water, moisture‐enabled electric generators (MEGs) are emerging as a promising candidate for the next‐generation power source. Here, we develop a new type of MEG that exploits the interfacial potential arising from mixed ionic‐electronic conducting metal oxides with opposite semiconducting types. The interfacial potentials of (p‐type) NiO and (n‐type) TiO 2 were increased from 0.028 V to 1.2 V by doping NiO with 14% (atomic%) ferric ions (Fe 3+ ) and TiO 2 with 0.5% (atomic%) nitride ions (N 3− ). Similarly, upon increasing the atmospheric humidity level, the output current of the Fe‐NiO/N‐TiO 2 interface was boosted from 0.052 εA to 0.277 µA, attributed to the enhanced ionic charges formed on the surface of hygroscopic Fe‐doped NiO (Fe‐NiO). Upon replacing the poorly conducting nitrogen‐doped TiO 2 (N‐TiO 2 ) with mixed conducting partially reduced graphene oxide (Pr‐GO), a 5.7 times enhancement in the current value was achieved, albeit with a 2.4‐fold reduction in output potential. The optimized mixed‐conductor‐based MEG generated sufficient power to operate small electronic devices such as a calculator and a light‐emitting diode (LED), highlighting its practical applicability for sustainable energy harvesting from atmospheric moisture.

works.title: Ionic Liquid Regulated Wetting and Chemo‐Mechanical Stabilization of NCM811 Cathodes
works.abstract: (NCM811) cathodes due to non-selective interfacial adhesion, causing severe structural pulverization, interfacial debonding, and unstable cathode electrolyte interfacial (CEI) growth during cycling. Herein, we reveal the cation-dependent interfacial affinity of ionic liquids. An imidazolium-based ionic liquid (EMIM[TFSI]) preferentially wets and encapsulates NCM811 particles, forming a robust interfacial layer with superior elastic modulus (3.4 GPa vs. PVDF 0.49 GPa) and lower dissipation (0.15 vs. PVDF 0.27 keV), whereas pyrrolidinium- and piperidinium-based ILs predominantly plasticized the PVDF-rich phase. The conformal EMIM[TFSI] wetting buffers lattice strain efficiently, suppresses transition-metal dissolution, and induces the formation of thin, uniform, and robust CEI. Benefiting from the integrated chemo-mechanical stabilization, the EMIM[TFSI] modified NCM811 cathode delivers 83% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 1 C, and 0.1 Ah pouch cells achieve 84% retention at 0.5 C. This study establishes that ionic liquid binders offer a rational chemo-mechanical engineering strategy for high-performance NCM811 cathodes.

works.title: Quantum Dot‐Based Color Conversion Layers for Displays, Lighting, and Emerging Technologies
works.abstract: Quantum dot-based color conversion layers (QD-CCLs) have emerged as key spectral-engineering platforms for next-generation optoelectronic systems, enabling precise control of light emission through efficient photon conversion. Owing to their high photoluminescence quantum yield, narrow emission linewidth, and size-tunable bandgaps, quantum dots (QDs) offer significant advantages over conventional phosphors for lighting and display applications. Beyond material properties, QD-CCL performance is governed by the interplay between material photophysics, optical design, and structural architecture. This review provides a unified perspective on QD-CCLs by integrating advances across QD materials (Cd-based, perovskite, and heavy-metal-free systems), device architectures, and mechanically deformable platforms. Particular emphasis is placed on optical management strategies that control photon absorption, reabsorption, and light extraction, as well as structural approaches that enhance conversion efficiency and suppress excitation-light leakage. Emerging design considerations in flexible and stretchable systems are also discussed, highlighting the coupling between mechanical deformation and optical performance. Beyond conventional lighting and displays, QD-CCLs are further explored as functional photonic interfaces in applications such as visible light communication and human-machine interfaces. By bridging materials, optics, and device engineering, this review establishes a design framework for QD-CCLs and outlines future directions toward multifunctional photonic systems.

works.title: The Next‐Generation Layered Hydroxide Electrocatalysts Based on High‐Entropy Strategy: Synthesis, Characterization, and Electrochemical Applications
works.abstract: High-entropy layered hydroxides (HE-LHs) with five or more metal elements have drawn great attention because of their unique properties and scalable synthesis. Equipped with a tunable interlayer of two-dimensional infrastructure, considerable atomic diversity, and promising industrial applications. These HE-LHs have significantly higher mixed entropy and more complicated multiorbital hybrid effects than conventional hydroxides, which allows them to gain a customizable catalytic microenvironment, ideal conductivity, and thermodynamic stability. Although the high-entropy strategy has been widely discussed in alloy and oxide systems, its immense potential in layered hydroxides remains undervalued. This review provides a comprehensive summary of the latest progress of layered hydroxides modified with the high-entropy strategy, from the synthetic methods to electrochemical applications. The versatile synthetic strategies, including hydrothermal reaction, solvothermal reaction, co-precipitation, and electrodeposition methods, are summarized. Besides, a thorough discussion of characterization methods for analyzing the basic structure of HE-LHs is given and their electrochemical performance is assessed. Ultimately, this review briefly outlines the application of HE-LHs in fields of oxygen evolution reaction, hydrogen evolution reaction, organic-molecular oxidation reaction, and supercapacitors. This review provides a reliable reference for synthesizing and evaluating HE-LHs, thus highlighting the giant potential of HE-LHs and prompting the next generation of layered hydroxides.

works.title: Hierarchical Carbon Aerogel With Polarized Zr─O Interfaces Enables Dynamic Iodine Regulation in Aqueous Zn‐I 2 Batteries
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The shuttle effect of soluble polyiodides limits the cycling stability and rate capability of aqueous Zn‐I 2 batteries. Herein, a ZrO 2 ‐decorated cellulose‐derived carbon aerogel (ZCA) is developed by integrating hierarchical pore confinement with polarized Zr─O/carbon interfacial regulation. Spectroscopic analyses and density functional theory calculations reveal moderate O···I─I coupling with halogen‐bond‐like character for neutral I 2 at Zr‐adjacent oxygen sites, while reduced iodine species are stabilized through species‐dependent interfacial regulation within the polarized Zr─O‐containing environment. This structural‐interfacial synergy suppresses polyiodide diffusion while preserving reversible I − /I 3 − /I 2 conversion. Consequently, ZCA@I 2 delivers 187.2 mAh g −1 after 5000 cycles at 1 A g −1 and sustains 123.2 mAh g −1 after 50 000 cycles at 10 A g −1 , with a per‐cycle decay of only 0.000052%. At an iodine areal loading of 6.7 mg cm −2 , it retains 93.1% of its capacity after 6000 cycles at 1 A g −1 . These results provide a structure‐interface design strategy for durable, high‐rate, and high‐loading aqueous Zn‐I 2 batteries.

works.title: Coupling Plasma‐Synthesized N‐Doped Graphene With Ice Templated Porous Electrode for Enhanced Aluminum Battery Performance
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable aluminum batteries are promising for next‐generation energy storage owing to the low cost and abundance of aluminum. Graphene is an attractive cathode due to its high surface area and electrical conductivity, but its performance is limited by difficult production and sheet aggregation, which restrict electrolyte accessibility and ion transport. This study employs a plasma‐enabled synthesis approach to produce both pristine graphene and nitrogen‐doped graphene (N‐graphene), followed by an ice templating strategy to directly construct a three‐dimensional porous N‐graphene electrode. The effects of nitrogen doping and porous electrode architecture are systematically investigated by comparing dense and porous electrodes. Nitrogen‐doping increases the specific capacity by ∼50%, from 36.24 to 54.4 mAh/g at a current density of 0.1 A/g. Furthermore, introducing porous structure provides an additional ∼20% improvement, achieving a capacity of 65.5 mAh/g under the same conditions. This enhanced performance of porous electrode is attributed to its interconnected pores and partially aligned graphene sheets, which improve electrolyte accessibility and facilitate the adsorption and transport of AlCl 4 − anions. The robust porous structure of N‐graphene ensures excellent cycling stability, with no noticeable capacity decay over 5000 cycles. Coupling nitrogen doping with porous electrode architecture provides an effective strategy to enhance graphene‐based aluminum batteries.

works.title: Impact‐Tolerant Radiative Cooling Enabled by Bioinspired Multiscale Glass Composite Coatings
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Passive radiative cooling coatings are commonly designed for high reflectance under undamaged conditions, whereas protective surfaces must retain their optical function during impact. Reconciling mechanical and optical properties in a single material has been a challenge. The glass sponge ( Euplectella sp .) maintains damage tolerance with desirable optical properties by laminated nanocomposite designs. Inspiring from this hierarchical structure, a rapidly photocurable polyurethane acrylate/Glass (PUA/Glass) multilayer composite coating is developed to confine impact damage while preserving radiative cooling performance. Alternating compliant PUA interlayers deflect and arrest cracks, whereas hollow glass microspheres (HGMs) and TiO 2 /Al 2 O 3 nanoparticles in glass layers redistribute load across multiple scales. HGM crushing, shell fragmentation, and local particle‐matrix debonding dissipate energy yet retain or reconstruct air/glass/polymer interfaces; by contrast, connected macroscopic cracks disrupt the reflective layer. The coating combines solar reflectance above 92% with atmospheric‐window emittance above 95% and remains, on average, 10.42°C below ambient during daytime outdoor testing. After a 20 J impact, localized hierarchical pores preserve reflectance and local cooling, while repeated 1 J impacts reveal a transition from optically tolerable microscale damage to reflectance‐degrading macrocracks. These results provide a route toward impact‐tolerant radiative‐cooling surfaces for protective components.

works.title: Mechanism of Delayed Polarization Saturation Induced by B‐Site Zr Doping for Enhancing Energy Storage Performance in Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 TiO 3 ‐ Sr 0.7 Bi 0.2 TiO 3 Ceramics
works.abstract: ABSTRACT In this work, Zr 4+ ions are introduced into the B‐site of 0.67Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 TiO 3 ‐0.33Sr 0.7 Bi 0.2 TiO 3 relaxor ferroelectric ceramics, leading to a significant improvement in energy storage performance. On one hand, Zr 4+ doping suppresses grain growth, increasing the breakdown electric field from 250 to 470 kV cm −1 . On the other hand, it tailors the phase structure by reducing the fraction of the strong polar rhombohedral phase, refines polar nanoregions (PNRs) into discrete micro‐nano polar clusters with reduced size and weakened cooperative switching, and notably alters their morphology and distribution, thereby reducing the local polarization intensity.
