These micro‐nano polar clusters exhibit reduced switching cooperativity under an electric field, resulting in a marked delay of polarization saturation—the electric field required to achieve a comparable polarization value is increased. Finally, the recoverable energy storage density ( W rec ) and efficiency ( η ) of the 0.67Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 Ti 0.94 Zr 0.06 O 3 ‐0.33Sr 0.7 Bi 0.2 Ti 0.94 Zr 0.06 O 3 samples are significantly improved, reaching 7.2 J cm −3 and 88.1% under 470 kV cm −1 . It also exhibits stable performance from 30–160°C, with the fluctuation of W rec lower than 5%. Moreover, it possesses a high power density of 140 MW cm −3 and an ultrafast discharge time. The proposed “delayed polarization saturation” strategy offers a new route for designing high‐performance lead‐free dielectric energy storage ceramics.

works.title: Retraction Note: Restorative biodegradable two-layered hybrid microneedles for melanoma photothermal/chemo co-therapy and wound healing
Mechanistic study of Lip@ZIF-8(Mfn2/SMART1)-mediated ubiquitination regulation in restoring mitochondrial homeostasis and inhibiting cartilage endplate calcification
works.abstract: This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which SMAD ubiquitin regulatory factor 1 (Smurf1)-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of mitofusin 2 (Mfn2) lead to mitochondrial homeostasis imbalance and progressive cartilage endplate (CEP) calcification in intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), and to evaluate the therapeutic potential of the constructed pH-responsive PEGylated lipid-coated zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) nanoparticles co-delivering Mfn2 mRNA and Smurf1-targeting PROTAC (designated as SMART1) (Lip@ZIF-8(Mfn2/SMART1)) for reconstructing the Smurf1-Mfn2-AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-autophagy axis and suppressing CEP calcification. In this study, a rat IVDD model was first established via intervertebral disc puncture, and CEP tissues were collected from the Sham and IVDD groups for proteomic and metabolomic analyses. Differential analyses were performed in combination with Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment, metabolic pathway analysis, and the construction of an integrated proteomic-metabolomic network to delineate the global dysregulation of the Smurf1-Mfn2-AMPK-mitochondrial metabolic regulatory network. On this basis, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was conducted on CEP tissues from IVDD and Lip@ZIF-8(Mfn2/SMART1)-treated groups to assess the systemic remodeling effects of the treatment on CEP cellular states. For mechanistic investigations, primary CEP cells and 293T cells were isolated and cultured, and a β-glycerophosphate (β-GP)-induced osteogenic-like calcification model of CEP cells was established. Lentivirus-mediated Mfn2 overexpression, SMART1 treatment, and AMPK inhibitor intervention were applied to systematically evaluate the functional role of the Smurf1-Mfn2-AMPK-autophagy axis in calcification regulation. Co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), Glutathione S-transferase (GST) pull-down assays, and in vitro reconstituted ubiquitination reactions were further performed to validate the molecular mechanism underlying Smurf1-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of Mfn2. In functional experiments, alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and Alizarin Red staining, reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), Western blot (WB), JC-1 mitochondrial membrane potential assays, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and mCherry-GFP-LC3 dual-fluorescence tracing were comprehensively employed to assess mitochondrial homeostasis, autophagic flux, and osteogenic-like transdifferentiation. Subsequently, a Lip@ZIF-8(Mfn2/SMART1) was constructed, and its physicochemical properties were characterized. Cellular uptake, lysosomal colocalization, and CCK-8 assays were conducted to evaluate its biocompatibility and functional release efficiency. In vivo, the nanosystem was locally injected into intervertebral discs, and in vivo imaging system (IVIS), micro-computed tomography (micro-CT), histological staining, immunohistochemistry (IHC), and molecular analyses were integrated to systematically evaluate the in vivo retention and distribution characteristics of Lip@ZIF-8(Mfn2/SMART1), as well as its regulatory effects on CEP calcification, mitochondrial homeostasis, and the Smurf1-Mfn2-AMPK-autophagy axis. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic analyses revealed that Smurf1 was significantly upregulated, whereas Mfn2 was markedly downregulated in CEP tissues from IVDD, accompanied by impaired AMPK signaling and disrupted mitochondrial oxidative metabolism. Animal experiments demonstrated that, in a rat CEP calcification model, aberrant activation of Smurf1, suppression of Mfn2 and AMPK signaling, and blockade of autophagic flux occurred concurrently, leading to mitochondrial structural damage, enhanced osteogenic-like transdifferentiation, and aggravated pathological calcification. Mechanistic investigations confirmed that Smurf1 directly interacted with Mfn2 and functioned as its upstream E3 ubiquitin ligase, mediating Mfn2 ubiquitination and degradation. In vitro functional assays showed that combined Smurf1 inhibition and Mfn2 supplementation synergistically enhanced AMPK activity and restored autophagic flux and mitochondrial homeostasis. The constructed Lip@ZIF-8(Mfn2/SMART1) exhibited favorable physicochemical stability, acid-triggered release properties, and cellular compatibility, enabling efficient cellular uptake and lysosomal escape in CEP cells. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrated that Lip@ZIF-8(Mfn2/SMART1) simultaneously downregulated Smurf1, upregulated Mfn2, and activated the AMPK-autophagy axis, thereby markedly improving mitochondrial structure and function and suppressing osteogenic-like differentiation and calcification of the CEP. Lip@ZIF-8(Mfn2/SMART1) enabled the synergistic delivery of Mfn2 mRNA and SMART1 to reconstruct the Smurf1-Mfn2-AMPK-autophagy regulatory axis, restore mitochondrial function, and effectively inhibit CEP calcification, thereby providing a mechanistic basis and candidate nanotherapeutic strategy for future IVDD intervention.

works.title: Carrier-free self-assembled baicalein derivative nanoparticles: pH-responsive antibacterial agent for controlling plant diseases caused by Xanthomonas spp.
works.abstract: Plant bacterial diseases caused by Xanthomonas threaten global crop production and food security, whereas conventional bactericides exhibit poor stability and limited efficacy against biofilms. In this work, a series of baicalein derivatives (X1–X32) containing a tertiary amine-functionalized piperidine moiety are designed and synthesized. All compounds form carrier-free nanoscale assemblies in water and exhibit superior in vitro antibacterial activities against Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo), Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri (Xac), and Xanthomonas campestris pv. mangiferaeindicae (Xcm) compared to thiodiazole copper (TC). Among them, X28 self-assembles into uniform, nearly spherical nanoparticles in aqueous solution, initiated by hydrophobic effects and stabilized by van der Waals interactions and π–π stacking. X28 nanoparticles (NPs) display pH-responsive disassembly under weakly-acidic conditions in vitro. At 200 µg mL⁻¹, they show superior in vivo protective and curative efficacies (52.9%–78.4%) against the corresponding bacterial diseases compared to TC (21.7%–59.3%). Additionally, they exhibit favorable foliar wettability, photostability, and biosafety. Mechanistic studies demonstrate that X28 NPs significantly inhibit biofilm formation and partially eliminate mature biofilms, and reduce bacterial motility, colonization, and pathogenicity. These findings demonstrate that X28 NPs serve as a promising and eco-friendly agrochemical for the efficient and sustainable control of plant bacterial diseases. Rational molecular functionalization of natural baicalein with a pH-responsive piperidine moiety, combined with carrier-free self-assembly, constructs a multifunctional antibacterial system with favorable agricultural performance. X28 nanoparticles self-assemble driven by hydrophobic interactions, van der Waals forces and π–π stacking, undergo pH-responsive disassembly in acidic infection microenvironments, and exert multi-target antibacterial action against Xanthomonas spp. by suppressing biofilm formation, motility and pathogenicity. X28 nanoparticles exhibit superior in vivo control efficacy over commercial bactericide thiodiazole copper, along with excellent foliar wettability, photostability and biosafety, offering a feasible strategy for developing high-efficiency agrochemicals.

works.title: Functionalized carbon nanotube microphere-pullulan polysaccharide hydrogel for electric-photothermal immunomodulation and sequential repair of diabetic infected wounds
works.abstract: Chronic diabetic wounds display complex pathologies involving bacterial invasion, oxidative stress dysregulation, persistent inflammation, and impaired endogenous bioelectricity, which collectively amplify inflammatory cascades, suppress angiogenesis, and induce aberrant fibrosis. These events hinder tissue regeneration and trigger pathological scarring, which poses a critical clinical challenge. Conventional dressings with limited functionality and microenvironment adaptability cannot achieve synergistic interventions against multiple wound pathologies. Herein, we develop a multifunctional PI-CM@AP hydrogel with photothermal-triggered drug delivery and biomimetic conductivity. The hydrogel matrix was formed via aldehyde-hydroxyl acetal cross-linking of sodium periodate-oxidized pullulan, as spectroscopically verified, with uniformly incorporated astragalus polysaccharide-loaded carbon nanotube microspheres (CM@AP). The optimized hydrogel exhibited favorable injectability, self-healing capacity, and tissue adhesion. Pullulan enables conformal coverage of irregular wounds, while dispersed CM@AP imparts biomimetic conductivity. The engineered conductive microenvironment is hypothesized to couple with endogenous bioelectric signals, potentially facilitating directional cell migration and skin regeneration. Combining NIR photothermal sterilization, Zn 2+ antibacterial activity, and pH-responsive astragalus polysaccharide release, PI-CM@AP establishes a synergistic “photothermal-ion-drug” system to eliminate pathogens and mitigate infection-driven inflammatory deterioration. In vitro, the hydrogel scavenged excess ROS, which is associated with inhibited NF-κB inflammation and modulated Nrf2/HO-1 axis activity, thereby promoting M1-to-M2 macrophage polarization and remodeling an anti-inflammatory, antioxidative microenvironment. Its treatment is correlated with altered HIF-1α/VEGF signaling, which may facilitate endothelial migration and vascular reconstruction, whereas conductivity-associated regulatory mechanisms remain unvalidated. Rat diabetic infected wound models validated the favorable biosafety of PI-CM@AP. The hydrogel inhibits NF-κB cascades and TGF-β-induced Smad2/3 phosphorylation, alleviating pathological fibrosis and achieving high-quality scar-attenuated wound regeneration. Collectively, the integration of photothermal immunomodulation and biomimetic conductivity enables the hydrogel to mediate multi-target sequential repair of chronic diabetic wounds. This study offers a promising strategy for designing advanced wound-healing dressings. Schematic diagram demonstrating the therapeutic mechanism of CM@AP biomaterial against infected diabetic wounds. Constructed from zinc nitrate, AP and pullulan dialdehyde, the CM@AP system under near-infrared light can synergize with the endogenous electric field at the wound site. This integrated system achieves broad-spectrum antibacterial effect, orchestrates immunomodulation to drive M2 macrophage polarization, facilitates angiogenesis, and suppresses excessive scar formation, thereby comprehensively promoting the repair of refractory infected diabetic wounds.

works.title: Formulation‐Driven Design of Antimicrobial Hydrogel Wound Patches 3D‐Printed by Digital Light Processing: Mapping Polysaccharide and Nanoparticle Effects
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Wound dressings must balance antimicrobial efficacy with the printability limits imposed by nanoparticle‐mediated ultraviolet attenuation during digital light processing 3D printing. Here, we develop process–structure–property relationships for poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA)‐based hydrogel wound patches containing Ag/ZnO‐derived antimicrobial phases and polysaccharide/cellulose modifiers (cellulose nanofibrils, chitosan, or alginate). Beer–Lambert analysis shows that nanoparticle loading reduces optical penetration depth at 405 nm to 1.04‐1.28 mm, narrowing the usable curing margin so that radiant exposure exceeds the critical energy by only 4%–5%. Flory–Rehner analysis of swelling reveals formulation‐dependent crosslink density: alginate lowers effective crosslink density by 45% vs. neat PEGDA and increases mesh size from 0.42 to 0.60 nm. This network loosening drives 1.5× variation in water vapor transmission rate (WVTR; 346–518 g·m − 2 ·day − 1 ) and a 7× range in wettability (11.5°–81.1°). Two‐way factorial analysis identifies polysaccharide type as the dominant driver of swelling (87.5% of variance) and antimicrobial efficacy (>50%), while nanoparticle type controls contact angle (60.1%) and WVTR (76.9%). The Ag + chitosan formulation (S5) achieves 23–24 mm inhibition zones against Escherichia coli and Bacillus sp. via chitosan‐facilitated Ag + diffusion plus intrinsic contact‐killing. Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy confirms cumulative Ag + release (32.7 mg·L − 1 over 14 days), while Zn 2 + remains immobilized below detection.

works.title: Polycation-functionalized quantum dots enriched at thylakoid membrane domains enable in situ assembly of a semi-artificial photosynthetic system for broadband light harvesting and metabolic adaptation in synechocystis
works.abstract: Abstract Natural light-harvesting systems of photosynthetic microorganisms provide insufficient energy for photodriven biosynthesis because of inefficient solar-spectrum utilization. Constructing semi-artificial photosynthetic hybrid systems has become a promising strategy. However, mismatched spatial distribution and temporal dynamics of photogenerated electrons at the semiconductor-biointerface limit efficient coupling. We designed polycation-functionalized molybdenum disulfide quantum dots (th-BPQDs). In Synechocystis, th-BPQDs constructed intracellular, subcellular-scale semi-artificial photosynthetic hybrid systems, achieving broadband energy capture and intracellular metabolic adaptation. Their surface functionalization with the polycation PDDA and ultrasmall size facilitated transmembrane delivery and preferential enrichment in the thylakoid region, reducing charge-transfer resistance at the semiconductor-biological interface. Simultaneously, th-BPQDs possess a thylakoid-matched band structure and efficient photogenerated charge separation capabilities. th-BPQD-derived photoelectrons can couple to the endogenous photosynthetic electron transport chain in Synechocystis. Transcriptomic analysis revealed altered expression of genes involved in nitrogen metabolism and amino acid biosynthesis, alongside enhanced cell proliferation and glycogen accumulation, while downregulation of photosystem- and light-harvesting-related genes may reflect an adaptive transcriptional response. Photoelectrochemical measurements demonstrated significantly enhanced photocurrent generation and superior photoelectric conversion performance across visible and near-infrared regions. This work provides a general strategy for constructing efficient semi-artificial photosynthetic systems and rewiring microbial metabolic networks.

works.title: Dual-engine ferroptosis initiation via a hypoxia-responsive nanoplatform for colorectal cancer immunotherapy
works.abstract: Abstract Despite the promise of immunotherapy for colorectal cancer (CRC), efficacy is limited by an immunosuppressive microenvironment that resists single-modality interventions. Herein, we propose a dual‑engine ignition strategy for ferroptosis using a hypoxia‑responsive gadolinium‑coordination nanoplatform (PAD@CR) prepared via a one‑pot reaction among Gd³⁺, chlorin e6 (Ce6), retinoic acid (RA), and hypoxia‑sensitive PEG. This platform integrates two coordinated engines in a single system: Ce6 serves as the oxidative engine, generating ROS upon ultrasound activation, while RA acts as the brake‑release engine, inhibiting glycolysis to deplete NADPH and GSH, thereby dismantling the antioxidant defense. The convergence of these two orthogonal inputs overwhelms redox homeostasis and triggers immunogenic ferroptosis. The resulting DAMPs establish a positive feedback loop with α‑PD‑L1 therapy, promoting CD8⁺ T cell infiltration and long‑term immunological memory. Notably, IFN‑γ from activated T cells further suppresses GPX4, amplifying ferroptosis in a closed‑loop manner. In vivo, this dual‑engine ignition significantly inhibits tumor growth and extends survival without systemic toxicity. With scalable synthesis, integrated imaging‑therapy functions, and the ability to convert "cold" tumors into "hot" lesions, this nanoplatform offers a translatable strategy to overcome immunotherapy resistance in CRC.

works.title: Nanoporous Bimetallic Metal-Hydroxide Organic Frameworks for Urea-Assisted Natural Seawater Electrolysis
works.abstract: Abstract Metal-hydroxide organic frameworks (MHOFs), featuring a synergistic interplay between metal hydroxides and metal−organic frameworks, exhibit tremendous potential as next-generation electrocatalysts for water splitting. However, their underlying catalytic mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Herein, through a single hydrothermal method, the nanoporous NiCo-MHOF-6 was directly grown on nickel foam (NF). Doping Co into the Ni-MHOF framework changes the electronic configuration of the active metal centers, consequently promoting improved electrocatalytic performance. During the OER, NiCo-MHOF-6 requires a overpotential of only 356 mV to attain 500 mA cm−2, and retains 90.6% of its initial current over 220 h at a constant 1.55 V vs. RHE. In practical seawater electrolysis, the assembled electrolyzer exhibits energy-efficient performance, requiring only 1.57 V to deliver 200 mA cm−2 and sustaining stable operation for 210 h at 240 mA cm−2. Furthermore, when the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) takes the place of the anodic OER, only 1.30 V is needed to drive 10 mA cm−2, and the system runs continuously for 144 h. Operando Raman spectroscopy and X-ray absorption measurements show that in situ transformation into high-valent γ-NiOOH, which is key to its faster reaction kinetics. This work provides a viable pathway toward low-energy H2 generation via urea-assisted seawater electrolysis.

works.title: Construction of Carbon Dots@Alumina Materials with Long-Lived Room Temperature Phosphorescence for Digital Encryption
works.abstract: Abstract Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) carbon dots (CDs) materials have attracted considerable attention owing to their potential applications in digital encryption. However, achieving high-performance RTP CDs materials without introducing external emissive centers or complex substrates remains a significant challenge. Herein, CDs@Al2O3 materials were successfully prepared by a solid-state decomposition method with aluminum isopropoxide (AIP) as a single precursor. The double confinement of strong covalent bonds and a highly rigid structure is formed by calcination, which effectively suppresses the vibration of luminescent molecules and the non-radiative transition of triplet excitons and generates oxygen vacancies with suitable concentration (deeper traps) as effective trapping sites for triplet excitons. As a result, the CDs@Al2O3 material exhibits a long lifetime of 433.5 ms (more than 6 s to the naked eyes) and excellent stability. These composites show preliminary potential for applications in digital encryption. This work provides a simple strategy for the in situ construction of RTP CDs materials with a single precursor.

works.title: Insights into the Dynamics of In Situ Formed Active Cuδ+ Clusters in CuOx Electrocatalysts during the Nitrate Reduction Reaction
works.abstract: Abstract Hetero-structured Cu-based systems with positively charged active centers have emerged as a promising catalyst for the nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR). We systematically investigate the factors governing long-term NO3RR performance through comprehensive electrochemical analysis and post-catalytic characterization of CuO, Cu2O, and Cu catalysts. Among the studied systems, Cu2O exhibits superior performance, achieving a maximum ammonia yield rate of 945.75 μg h−1 mgcat−1 at −1.4 V (vs Ag/AgCl(sat.KCl)) with a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 62.69%, outperforming CuO and Cu under identical conditions. CuO and Cu2O demonstrate enhanced selectivity toward ammonia over nitrite across all potentials, whereas metallic Cu shows significantly higher nitrite formation (31% FE), nearly fourfold greater than that of the oxides. The higher NO3RR to ammonia performance of CuOx catalysts is attributed to the feasible in situ formation of polarized Cuδ+ species/clusters, supported by the insights gained through in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy and post-mortem analysis. This study elucidates the relationship between the dynamically formed Cuδ+ species/clusters and the retention of interfacial active surface area, which is sustained through the dissolution−redeposition dynamics of copper ions at the catalyst−electrolyte interface.

works.title: Metal−Organic Framework Nanosheet-Derived CuO for Efficient Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
works.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (NO3RR) offers a “two birds with one stone” strategy by simultaneously removing pollutants and producing value-added ammonia (NH3). However, its multiple electron- and proton-transfer steps require catalysts with both high activity and selectivity. Copper (Cu) is widely regarded as one of the most promising NO3RR electrocatalysts due to its low cost and relatively high activity, yet its ammonia yield rate is usually constrained by sluggish nitrite conversion kinetics. Herein, a series of Cu-based catalysts with distinct oxidation states and crystallinity were derived from Cu-based metal−organic framework nanosheets (Cu-MOF NSs) by adjusting the pyrolysis conditions, and their NO3RR performance in alkaline media was evaluated. The low-crystallinity copper oxide catalyst (CuO-1) achieved the highest NH3 yield rate of 11.5 mg cm−2 h−1 at −0.8 V vs reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), significantly outperforming the metallic Cu catalyst (Cu@NC), the highly crystalline CuO catalyst (CuO-2), and most previously reported catalysts. Mechanistic investigations suggest that CuO-1 undergoes partial reduction during the reaction to generate Cu0/Cu+ species, which may serve as key active species promoting ammonia production by enhancing active hydrogen generation. Finally, NH4Cl was recovered through acid absorption and rotary evaporation, demonstrating a practical route for converting NO3− pollutants into valuable NH3 products.

works.title: Heterophase-Interfaced Ultrasmall Pt−In Nanocatalysts: Multifunctional Catalysis in Fuel Cells
works.abstract: Abstract Aiming at the key issues of high cost, poor stability, and insufficient multifunctional catalytic performance of platinum-based electrocatalysts for fuel cells, a series of Pt−In nanocatalysts with triphasic heterointerfaces (face-centered cubic phase, ordered intermetallic phase, and amorphous phase) were prepared in one step via a liquid-phase reduction method in this work. The regulatory mechanisms of PDDA modification and the Pt−In atomic ratio on the catalyst structure were systematically investigated, and their catalytic performance in various electrocatalytic reactions of fuel cells was thoroughly characterized. The results demonstrated that PDDA not only realized the regulation of ultrasmall size and uniform dispersion of Pt−In nanoparticles but also played a pivotal role in the formation of triphasic heterointerfaces. The optimal atomic ratio of the triphasic PtIn0.701 nanocatalyst exhibited enhanced catalytic activity compared to the biphasic Pt−In catalyst and commercial Pt/C catalyst in methanol oxidation reaction, ethanol oxidation reaction, formic acid oxidation reaction, hydrogen oxidation reaction, and oxygen reduction reaction. The combination of theoretical and experimental studies confirmed that the geometric and electronic synergetic effects of the triphasic heterointerfaces were the core factors for the enhanced catalytic performance. This study lays a foundation for the development of low-cost and multifunctional electrocatalytic systems with promising potential for fuel cells.

works.title: Enzyme-Instructed Assembly of Hexapeptide Nanoantioxidants for Treatment of Radiation-Induced Skin Injury
works.abstract: Abstract Radiation-induced skin injury (RISI) remains a major clinical challenge in cancer radiotherapy due to uncontrolled oxidative stress and inflammation. Current clinical management of RISI relies on topical corticosteroids, which are associated with adverse effects such as skin atrophy and telangiectasias, highlighting the need for steroid-free alternatives. Herein, a hexapeptide (RRWWWY)-based nanoantioxidant is prepared via tyrosinase-instructed assembly for RISI treatment. Such nanoantioxidants effectively scavenge excess ROS, restore redox homeostasis, and suppress radiation-induced upregulation of pro-inflammatory (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α) and pro-apoptotic (p53, p21) genes. Western blotting analysis confirmed decreased γ-H2AX and restored Bcl-2 expression. In an RISI rat model, hexapeptide nanoantioxidant reduced lipid peroxidation, alleviated epidermal thickening and inflammatory infiltration, and preserved the dermal collagen network and hair follicles, with no obvious systemic toxicity observed under the experimental conditions. Such nanoantioxidants provide a promising strategy for protecting normal tissues during radiotherapy, and broaden the potential of bioactive peptides in managing oxidative stress-related disorders.

works.title: Mechanism of Polyacrylonitrile-Based Carbon Fiber Carbonization Optimization by Fullerene for High-Performance Carbon Fibers
works.abstract: Abstract Enhancement arising for polyacrylonitrile (PAN)-based carbon fibers from C60 fullerene, which possesses a unique zero-dimensional structure and similar nano-scale dimensions, remains rarely reported and merits investigation. In this study, C60@PAN precursor fibers were fabricated via wet spinning and subsequently subjected to stabilization and carbonization, yielding composite carbon fibers with superior properties that were compared against neat PAN-based carbon fibers by means of X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and other characterization techniques. Through multi-scale structural characterization, combined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and first-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations, mechanisms underlying C60-induced reinforcement in PAN-based carbon fibers were systematically explored. Experimental and characterization results revealed that incorporation of C60 did not impair spinnability of PAN; composite precursor fibers exhibited a uniform and continuous morphology without significant defects. During stabilization, C60 reduced activation energy of cyclization reactions, moderated exothermic behavior, and provided structural support via an induced crystallization effect. After carbonization, composite fibers exhibit a markedly improved carbon layer stacking order, graphitization degree, and a concurrent increase in char yield. MD and DFT further disclosed that C60 dispersed homogeneously in PAN at room temperature, facilitating uniform orientation of PAN chains; at elevated temperatures, gradual fragmentation and fusion of conjugated cage structures of C60 served as critical templates for enhancing carbon structural ordering. This study elucidates the promoting mechanism of C60 in a favorable microstructural arrangement of PAN precursor fibers and subsequent stabilization−carbonization processes, offering experimental evidence and theoretical guidance for structural optimization and performance enhancement of high-performance PAN-based carbon fibers. The high-performance carbon fibers fabricated via this strategy find applications in commercial aerospace and low-altitude aircraft sectors. Moreover, the variations in electrical properties induced by C60 incorporation also warrant further investigation in the fields of capacitors and batteries.

works.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Synergistic Supramolecular Recognition and Electroanalysis at a Nanoporous Permethoxy Terphen[3]arene−Macroporous Carbon Interface for Simultaneous Detection
works.abstract: Abstract The simultaneous determination of ascorbic acid (AA), dopamine (DA), and uric acid (UA) is of great significance in clinical diagnosis, yet remains challenging due to overlapping oxidation potentials. Herein, we report a robust nanoporous supramolecular sensing interface constructed by integrating permethoxy terphen[3]arene (PTP3) with macroporous carbon (MPC). This nanocomposite design synergizes the high conductivity and accessible surface area of the MPC scaffold with the specific host−guest recognition capability of the PTP3 macrocycle. The resulting PTP3-MPC/GCE sensor effectively resolves the voltammetric signal overlapping, enabling the simultaneous and sensitive quantification of AA, DA, and UA. The sensor exhibits wide linear ranges (10−4000 μM for AA; 0.1−400 μM for DA and UA) and low detection limits (2.30 μM for AA, 0.063 μM for DA, and 0.13 μM for UA). Furthermore, the practical utility of the sensor was validated through the accurate determination of these analytes in human urine samples with satisfactory recoveries. This work presents a promising nanoscale supramolecular strategy for developing high-performance biosensors for clinical point-of-care testing.

works.title: Issue Publication Information
Hot-Pressed SnS/rGO Electrodes for High-Power Asymmetric Supercapacitors
works.abstract: Abstract Herein, we present the rational engineering of SnS/reduced graphene oxide (rGO) composites to enhance pseudocapacitance through carrier concentration optimization. The orthorhombic pnma-based SnS showed transitions from p- to n-type transport with the addition of rGO. This leads to changes in the bandgap, Fermi levels, conductivity, and diffusion coefficient to achieve the desired properties. The SnS/rGO 5% composite illustrates a specific capacitance of 200 F/g at 1 A/g, three times higher than that of pure SnS owing to its extrinsic pseudocapacitive nature and diffusion-controlled kinetics. The half-cell demonstrates exceptional capacitance retention of 93% over 1200 cycles, attributed to the conducting framework provided by rGO. In a full-cell configuration, using SnS/rGO 5% as the anode and activated carbon as the cathode, an operational voltage of 1.2 V is obtained. This configuration delivers a specific capacitance of 100 F/g at 1 A/g and maintains a capacity retention of 88% at 40 A/g for 5000 cycles. The energy density is 20.081 Wh/kg, and the power density is 22,454 W/kg for the asymmetric SnS/rGO||activated carbon (AC) device. Furthermore, two identical full cells can power a red LED for 128 s, an orange LED for 83 s, and a green LED for 61 s, demonstrating their practical potential in energy storage applications.

works.title: Melanin-Mediated Growth of Ag Nanostructures for Ultrasensitive SERS of l -Dopa
works.abstract: Abstract Hybrid interfaces based on melanin films and electrochemically deposited silver nanoparticles (Mel@Ag) are presented as effective platforms for ultrasensitive surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS). Natural melanin extracted from sepia pigment was processed into homogeneous thin films on indium tin oxide (ITO) via a controlled dip-coating approach, providing a chemically stable and redox-active interface. The presence of the melanin layer promotes an anodic shift in the Ag+ reduction potential and enables controlled nucleation and growth of silver nanostructures. The resulting Mel@Ag systems exhibit enhanced plasmonic response and superior SERS performance, with optimal activity achieved at low scan rates. Experimental results combined with electromagnetic simulations indicate that nanoparticle dimers play a dominant role in generating effective hotspots, particularly under 638 nm excitation, where a larger near-field enhancement volume is observed. The analytical capability of the platform is demonstrated through the detection of l-Dopa down to 10−11 M. The melanin layer likely contributes not only to control the nanostructure growth but also to analyte preconcentration through π−π interactions, favoring molecular localization at plasmonic hotspots. Notably, the system retains measurable SERS activity in complex biological media, demonstrating the persistence of the SERS response despite increasing matrix complexity. These results highlight the potential of melanin-mediated hybrid architectures as versatile SERS platforms for sensing applications in biologically relevant environments.

works.title: Atomically resolved exciton emission from single defects in MoS2
works.abstract: Abstract Excitons, bound electron–hole pairs, govern the optical response of semiconductors and underpin technologies ranging from photovoltaics to quantum light sources. In nanoscale systems, the spatial extent of excitons approaches atomic dimensions, yet direct imaging of excitonic processes in real space has remained elusive. Two-dimensional semiconductors such as transition metal dichalcogenides provide a platform where reduced screening, high light extraction and atomically defined defect sites enable the exploration of exciton physics at atomic length scales. However, the microscopic origin of defect-related emission and its variability across samples have remained debated. Here we show that scanning tunnelling microscopy-induced luminescence reveals the atomic and optical fingerprints of individual defects in monolayer MoS 2 . Decoupling the material from its substrate using bilayer hexagonal boron nitride enables the detection of sharp excitonic emission and spatially localized defect emission, which we attribute to free-to-bound recombination ( e ,A 0 ), and map its distribution with subnanometre-resolved fluorescence imaging. We identify negatively charged carbon–hydrogen complexes as the defect species responsible for a ubiquitous defect emission band in MoS 2 . These results provide atomically resolved images of exciton emission in a solid-state material, linking atomic defect structure to its optical fingerprint and establishing a microscopic basis for deterministic quantum emitter engineering in two-dimensional materials.

works.title: Repurposed endogenous virus-like vesicles mediate dendritic cell long-range antigen presentation and T cell activation for enhanced cancer vaccination
Endogenous virus-like extracellular vesicles enhance the efficacy of cancer vaccines
Molecular and Nanoscale Control of Exciton Transfer in TADF-Sensitized Fluorescence
works.abstract: Abstract TADF-sensitized fluorescence (TSF), also known as hyperfluorescence, combines efficient triplet exciton harvesting with the narrowband emission of fluorescent emitters. Yet, its performance depends on the interplay between exciton conversion, energy transfer, and molecular organization across different length scales. Herein, we review recent progress in nanoscale exciton-transfer engineering for TSF, with emphasis on molecular excited-state dynamics, sensitizer-dopant spatial control, diversified energy-transfer pathways, and interlayer sensitization. These approaches regulate exciton conversion and lifetime, balance Förster and Dexter energy transfer, and control exciton distribution within emissive layers and across interfaces. We also discuss emerging directions including kinetic matching, spatial organization, and multiscale modeling for understanding the links between molecular structure, energy-transfer dynamics, and device performance. This Mini-Review provides profound insights into transforming random blend systems into controllable nanoscale exciton-transfer networks, paving the way for efficient narrowband TSF OLEDs.

works.title: Light-Induced Néel Vector Reversal in 2D van der Waals Antiferromagnets
works.abstract: Abstract Antiferromagnetic spintronics promises ultrafast device performance, yet the essential Néel vector reversal is hindered by its intrinsic immunity to external magnetic fields. Here, we propose a mechanism for deterministic Néel vector reversal in 2D van der Waals antiferromagnets enabled by ultrafast laser pulses. The core physics involves light-induced asymmetric interlayer demagnetization, which drives the antiferromagnet into a transient ferrimagnetic state with a finite net moment. This transient symmetry breaking allows the Néel vector to be controlled by an external magnetic field. We identify that the intrinsic structural and electronic asymmetries and spin–orbit-coupling mediated spin flips are essential for this process. Using first-principles calculations and real-time time-dependent density functional theory, we further demonstrate this mechanism in bilayer NiICl and YI2. Our work establishes a general strategy for the optical manipulation of 2D antiferromagnetic order.

works.title: Sequence-Switchable MOF-on-MOF Photonic Crystals for Broadband Visible Structural Color Modulation
works.abstract: Abstract Structural colors generated by photonic crystals (PCs) have attracted interest in optical sensing. However, the sensing behavior of porous PCs is commonly tailored through material composition, pore structure, or surface chemistry. Here, we show that the spatial configuration of sequence-switchable MOF-on-MOF Bragg stacks regulates molecular access and adsorption while preserving the constituent metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). The reflection wavelength is continuously tuned across the visible spectrum by controlling layer thickness and refractive-index contrast, producing blue-to-red structural colors with a peak reflectance of approximately 90%. Reversing the layer sequence generates distinct optical response amplitudes and kinetics toward volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Combined optical analysis and molecular dynamics simulations further show that the sensing responses depend not only on molecular uptake but also on spatial adsorption distribution and framework–guest interactions. These findings establish molecular transport pathway control through spatial configuration as an additional strategy for regulating the sensing behavior of porous photonic materials.

works.title: Three‐Dimensional Piezoelectric Fibrous Constructs for Muscle Regeneration
works.abstract: Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV), a biocompatible and biodegradable polymer with inherent piezoelectricity, holds promise for developing biomimetic scaffolds for tissue regeneration. Its ability to generate electrical charges in response to mechanical stimulation, mimicking the electromechanical environment in native tissues like muscle, makes it attractive. This study focuses on harnessing PHBV properties to engineer electrospun fibrous scaffolds for muscle regeneration. We investigated processing parameters, such as solvent combinations, polymer concentrations, and tip-to-collector distances on fiber morphology, porosity, and piezoelectric properties. We observed a 25-fold increase in the quasi-static piezoelectric coefficient (d33 from 0.117 to 2.9 pC/N) for scaffolds with controlled porosity. This piezoelectric activity was corroborated by dynamic Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) measurements, which identified an electromechanical coupling factor (kt) of 13.69%. This enhanced electromechanical response highlights their potential for stimulating cellular responses for tissue regeneration. The mechanical properties of these scaffolds demonstrated their ability to undergo strain up to 40%, within the optimal range for muscle tissue engineering and compatibility with muscle functionality. Cytocompatibility of PHBV scaffolds was confirmed, and preliminary studies suggest their potential to support myogenic differentiation. This research highlights PHBV-based biomimetic scaffolds potential for muscle regeneration and sets groundwork for developing advanced therapies addressing muscle injury and disease.

works.title: A Threefold Symmetric NDI‐Nanohoop With a Large Stokes Shift: A Red‐Emitting Dye for Inorganic Electroluminescence
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanohoops with radial π‐conjugation, such as cycloparaphenylenes (CPPs), exhibit intrinsically large Stokes shifts arising from excited‐state symmetry breaking. However, their integration into functional electroluminescent platforms has remained largely unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis of a threefold symmetric naphthalenediimide (NDI)‐embedded CPP analogue ( [3]CDPNDI ) and its application in inorganic powder electroluminescence (iEL) devices. [ 3 ]CDPNDI was obtained in only four steps with 63% overall yield. The incorporation of electron‐accepting NDI units extends the emission into the red region (λ em = 630 nm, Φ F = 37%, in CHCl 3 ) with a large Stokes shift of 136 nm (4370 cm −1 ), which is advantageous for suppressing self‐absorption. AC field‐driven iEL devices achieved reddish‐purple emission consistent with one‐step color conversion of ZnS emission. Notably, the nanohoop emitter was integrated into the device via a simple solution‐coating process by incorporating 1 wt% [3]CDPNDI into the ZnS‐based phosphor paste, and EL emission remained observable after the devices were formed into origami‐ and kirigami‐type architectures. This work demonstrates the integration of a red‐emissive NDI‐embedded nanohoop into a solution‐processable ZnS‐based iEL platform and its compatibility with mechanically reconfigurable device architectures.

works.title: Plasmonic Mediated Atomically Thin Aluminum Quasicrystal for Dopamine Sensing
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Dopamine levels are linked to neurological illnesses like Parkinson's and Alzheimer's. Thus, reliable and sensitive detection of dopamine is crucial for early diagnosis and surveillance of neurodegenerative diseases. Non‐noble‐metal‐based nanomaterials are ideal for light‐mediated sensing of organic molecules. Among these, two‐dimensional (2D) quasicrystal (QC) structures consisting of five elements ( Al 70 Co 10 Fe 5 Ni 10 Cu 5 (2D Al QC)) provide active sites due to their high surface‐to‐volume ratio, making them excellent for organic chemical sensing. Here, we propose a simple, label‐free, spatial self‐phase‐modulation (SSPM)‐based sensing method in liquid form. SSPM‐based time evolution of the diffraction pattern for varied mixing levels of a 1100 ppb dopamine solution shows a shift in the SPR‐activated 2D Al QC nanostructure solution. The 1100 ppb solution shows a different dN / dI value, indicating a change in sensitivity to the nonlinear refractive index and time constant. SSPM is used to demonstrate dopamine‐sensing methods and to perform qualitative and quantitative evaluations. The SSPM‐based sensing has been further compared with other optical sensing methods, such as Raman Spectroscopy, UV‐vis Spectroscopy, and FTIR Spectroscopy. The experimental observations are also explained using DFTB‐based simulations.The current SSPM method can be used for rapid, large‐scale medical diagnostics.

works.title: Efficient Hydrogen Peroxide Generation Modulated by Crystal‐Plane Engineering in Ti 2 O 3
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of stable and selective electrocatalysts for hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) synthesis via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) is critical for sustainable green chemistry. However, the performance of transition metal oxides (TMOs) is often severely limited by the thermodynamic tendency to expose crystal planes with sluggish kinetics. Herein, we present a doping‐mediated crystal‐plane‐engineering strategy to overcome these constraints, using Ti 2 O 3 as a model system. Guided by a d ‐orbital morphology descriptor, we identified specific crystal planes, including (012) and (113)/(104), as theoretically active sites. Experimentally, Ni doping acted as an effective crystal‐plane‐directing agent, successfully modulating surface energies to induce the synergistic exposure of these target planes. Consequently, the optimized Ni‐Ti 2 O 3 electrocatalyst delivered an H 2 O 2 selectivity (94.4%) and yield of 2.56 mol g cat −1 h −1 at 0.4 V vs. RHE. This work demonstrates the efficacy of orbital‐driven plane control, providing a generic paradigm for the rational design of high‐performance TMO electrocatalysts for advanced energy applications.

works.title: Unveiling the d‐Orbital Occupancy Driven Push‐Pull Effect on Pathway Selectivity in 1,2‐Dichloroethane Catalytic Combustion
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Unraveling the link between electronic structure and reaction pathway is key to regulating 1,2‐DCE catalytic combustion and reducing toxic byproducts. In this work, we dope the full series of 3d transition metals (Sc to Zn) into SBA‐15‐supported LaMnO3 perovskite and show that dopant d‐orbital occupancy determines the reaction pathway via a directionally polarized push‐pull configuration. Low‐occupancy dopants (Sc, Ti, V, Cr) withdraw electrons from Mn, forming electron‐rich sites that donate electrons to adsorbed 1,2‐DCE, moderately activating the C─H bond and driving the dehydrochlorination pathway to produce VC. In contrast, high‐occupancy dopants (Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn) push electrons toward Mn, generating electron‐deficient sites that strongly extract electrons from 1,2‐DCE, thereby promoting C─Cl bond cleavage and oxygen incorporation to yield ECH. Using S‐LMO‐V (T 90% = 199.7 °C) and S‐LMO‐Cu (T 90% = 224.8 °C) as representative catalysts, S‐LMO‐V exhibits higher activity, with a degradation pathway dominated by the less toxic VC, attributed to its moderate adsorption strength and the lower dechlorination barrier provided by electron‐rich V sites. Conversely, electron‐deficient Cu sites over‐stabilize the substrate and steer the reaction toward ECH. This work establishes the d‐orbital‐mediated push‐pull effect as a generalizable descriptor for pathway selectivity, guiding selective combustion of chlorinated VOCs and beyond.

works.title: Dimeric Acceptors Enable over 20% Efficiency Organic Solar Cells via Electron‐Deficiency Engineering of Quinoxaline Linkers
works.abstract: Dimeric acceptors attract intense interest in organic solar cells (OSCs) for their well-defined structures and solution processability, yet the electronic role of the linking unit, particularly in electron-deficient heteroarenes, remains largely unexplored. Here, we establish the quinoxaline skeleton as a versatile and tunable linking unit and accordingly have designed and synthesized three dimers, namely WD1, WD2, and WD4. By systematically changing the substituents with 4-methoxyphenyl, methyl, and 4-fluorophenyl groups on the quinoxaline-based linkers, their optoelectronic properties can be precisely adjusted. Among the three quinoxaline-based dimers, the most electron-deficient variant WD4, which bears a 6,7-difluoro-2,3-bis(4-fluorophenyl)quinoxaline linking unit, exhibits superior optoelectronic properties. Consequently, the devices with PM6:WD4 as the active layer obtained a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 17.95% with excellent stability, and the PM6:L8-BO:WD4 ternary devices deliver an impressive PCE of 20.15%. This work demonstrates that fine-tuning the electron delocalization of dimeric linking units represents a straightforward strategy to simultaneously boost efficiency and stability, offering a clear molecular design blueprint for next-generation oligomeric acceptors.

works.title: Self‐Activated Nitric Oxide Nanogenerators Induce Cuproptosis via Regulating the Endogenous Copper Metabolism for Anti‐PD‐L1 Blockade Therapy
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Low anti‐PD‐L1 therapy response is mainly caused by poor tumor immunogenicity and insufficient PD‐L1 expression. Cuproptosis, a newly identified copper (Cu)‐dependent cell death, can simultaneously enhance immunogenicity and upregulate PD‐L1, but whether nitric oxide (NO) initiates cuproptosis remains unclear. Herein, we reveal a “NO‐induced cuproptosis” strategy: nanomaterial‐generated NO induces cuproptosis via inhibiting copper chaperone (CCS) expression to trigger endogenous Cu + release. To optimize this mechanism, we design a non‐copper, self‐activated NO nanogenerator (AZORHP) composed of arginine (Arg)‐stabilized zinc peroxide (AZO) for generating NO via self‐supplied Arg and hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) reaction, siRNA for silencing the copper‐chelating protein (metallothionein 2A, MT2A), and hyaluronic acid‐polypeptides (HP) decorated with anti‐PD‐L1 peptide and matrix metalloproteinase‐2 (MMP‐2)‐cleavable linkers. AZORHP has been verified to integrate NO‐mediated CCS downregulation to release copper and simultaneously blocking copper chelation via MT2A silencing and copper efflux via ATPase copper transporting β (ATP7B) suppression caused by mitochondrial damage, thereby establishing a dual regulatory network of “copper release–copper retention” that amplifies cuproptosis. This amplified cuproptosis provokes immunogenicity and PD‐L1 upregulation, thereby enhancing the response rate of anti‐PD‐L1 immunotherapy together with MMP‐2‐responsive anti‐PD‐L1 peptide. Therefore, our findings provide a novel concept of NO‐induced cuproptosis via regulating endogenous copper metabolism for immunotherapy.

works.title: A‐Site Spin‐State Engineering in Antiperovskites for Enhanced Polysulfide Adsorption and Sulfur Redox Catalysis
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐sulfur batteries (LSBs) possess exceptionally high theoretical energy density and specific capacity, making them promising candidates for next‐generation energy storage systems. However, the sluggish adsorption and catalytic conversion kinetics of lithium polysulfides severely hinder their practical application. In this work, a functional separator modified with antiperovskite nitride (IZNC) was developed. The precise incorporation of In at the antiperovskite. A‐site regulation effectively modulated the spin state of Co active sites, inducing a low‐spin to high‐spin transition of Co ions and thereby enhancing their affinity for polysulfides. Furthermore, the antiperovskite transformed the conventional two‐dimensional Li 2 S deposition behavior into a mixed 2D/3D growth mode, Such altered deposition morphology facilitates Li 2 S nucleation‑growth kinetics and enhances the overall reaction reversibility of the sulfur cathode. Consequently, the assembled cell exhibited outstanding cycling stability, with an average capacity decay of only 0.06% per cycle over 600 cycles at 1 C. Moreover, even at a high sulfur loading of 4.3 mg cm −2 , an impressive areal capacity of 6.1 mAh cm −2 was achieved. This work provides valuable insights into the rational design of functional separators for high‐performance LSBs.

works.title: Barrier-informed inhaled nanomedicines: Integrating pulmonary mucosal biology with precision-targeted delivery strategies
Supramolecular mRNA-delivering hydrogel for inducing tertiary lymphoid structures and enhancing immunotherapy efficacy
works.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has improved cancer treatment outcomes, yet many solid tumors remain immunologically “cold” and resistant to therapy. Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are linked to enhanced survival and response rates, but germinal center-like TLSs are challenging to generate in subcutaneous tumors due to rapid clearance of soluble inductive signals. We engineered an injectable supramolecular hydrogel to co-deliver liposome-formulated mRNAs encoding CXCL13 and LIGHT, thereby stabilizing the complexes and extending intratumoral cytokine production. In murine B16.f10, CT26, and 4T1 subcutaneous tumor models, this strategy increased TLS density and maturation, suppressed tumor growth, and prolonged survival. Combination with PD-1 blockade yielded enhanced efficacy antitumor effects, achieving complete tumor regression in some cases. Our results support the development of a novel injectable hydrogel-encapsulated formulation in combination with liposomes for enhancing the efficacy of mRNA therapeutics against cancer.

works.title: Aptamer-functionalized GSTK1-derived Super-Mito-EV enable targeted mitochondrial restoration for intervertebral disc repair
works.abstract: The progression of intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) is accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction and ferroptosis in nucleus pulposus cells (NPCs), highlighting the need for further investigation into mitochondrial homeostasis-related mechanisms and targeted therapeutic strategies. We found that the mitochondrial protein GSTK1 is downregulated in degenerative NPCs, whereas its overexpression partially delays IDD progression in rats. Mechanistically, the GSTK1-ALDH1L2 axis exerts anti-ferroptotic effects by maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis, independently of the classical ACSL4 pathway. GSTK1 also promotes the formation of mitochondria-containing extracellular vesicles through CD38/IP3R/Ca 2+ -associated signaling. Based on these findings, we generated mitochondria-enriched extracellular vesicles derived from GSTK1-overexpressing NPCs (Super-Mito-EV), modified them with EY3 to enhance targeted mitochondrial transfer, and incorporated them into a thermosensitive hydrogel to construct an injectable sustained-release delivery system. In a rat IDD model, this strategy significantly delayed IDD and improved disc structure and molecular homeostasis. In summary, our findings reveal the role of GSTK1–ALDH1L2-mediated mitochondrial homeostasis in IDD-associated ferroptosis and propose a targeted therapeutic strategy based on Super-Mito-EV-mediated mitochondrial delivery.

works.title: Biodegradable neodymium metal-organic frameworks for persistent NIR-II fluorescence imaging-guided photodynamic therapy with glutathione exhaustion
works.abstract: Rare-earth-based near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence probes with narrow multi-peak emission, long luminescence lifetimes, and high photostability are highly desirable for bioimaging. Nevertheless, such probes remain largely underdeveloped due to poor biodegradability, sophisticated synthetic procedures, and complicated photophysical modulation. Herein, neodymium (Nd) was screened from the entire series of lanthanide-containing rare-earth elements, and we developed Nd-tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl) porphyrin (TCPP) metal-organic framework (MOF) nanoprobes. Interestingly, within this MOF assembly, the Nd-TCPP coordination creates a highly ordered rigid architecture, suppressing non-radiative transitions and dramatically boosting NIR-II emission peaking at 1060 nm. Benefiting from spatial confinement and close donor-acceptor proximity, the proposed resonant 4f-to-triplet energy transfer (f-TET) from excited Nd 3+ to TCPP is suggested to be efficiently triggered under 808 nm laser irradiation, activating photodynamic processes to generate singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ). The synthesized NTM was subsequently loaded with L-buthionine sulfoximine (BSO) followed by PEGylation to obtain NTMBP nanoprobes. Upon systemic administration, the nanoprobes efficiently accumulated at tumor sites and produced durable, bright NIR-II fluorescence under 808 nm laser excitation, enabling clear visualization of tumor boundaries for precise phototherapy guidance. Meanwhile, under irradiation with the same wavelength, the NTMBP nanoprobes could generate 1 O 2 for tumor photodynamic therapy (PDT). In addition, BSO could deplete intracellular glutathione (GSH) to weaken antioxidant defenses, amplifying oxidative stress, and inducing robust tumor cell death. Our nanoprobe with favorable biocompatibility and biodegradability exhibited outstanding capabilities for NIR-II fluorescence imaging-guided PDT, holding great promise for further precise cancer theranostics.

works.title: Correction: Amelioration of the rheumatoid arthritis microenvironment using celastrol-loaded silver-modified ceria nanoparticles for enhanced treatment
Ultrasound-activated piezoelectric hydrogel for local infection control and bone repair in osteomyelitis
works.abstract: Biofilm-associated infection and persistent inflammation make osteomyelitis difficult to eradicate while preserving the capacity for bone repair. Here, we developed an injectable gelatin hydrogel crosslinked by microbial transglutaminase and containing polarized barium titanate (BTO) nanoparticles (mTG-Gel/BTO). The material exhibited pressure-responsive electrical output. Pulsed ultrasound (US) exposure at device settings of 1.5 W cm⁻², 1 MHz, and 50% duty cycle produced time-dependent oxidative activity. The combined treatment reduced viable counts and biofilm-associated readouts for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Escherichia coli while maintaining RAW 264.7 macrophage viability under the tested conditions. In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated macrophages, mTG-Gel/BTO + US reduced intracellular oxidation-associated fluorescence, increased antioxidant-related transcripts, decreased CD86 expression and TNF-α secretion, and increased CD206 expression and IL-10 secretion. Separate endothelial and osteogenic assays showed enhanced cell migration, network formation, osteogenic differentiation, and matrix mineralization. In a rat tibial MRSA model, mTG-Gel/BTO + US reduced bacterial burden and infection-associated bone destruction and improved radiographic and histological indicators of repair. These findings support an ultrasound-responsive hydrogel strategy that combines local infection control with a cellular environment favorable for bone repair. The formulation integrates physically incorporated BTO with an enzymatically crosslinked gelatin matrix, offering a simple material design for conformal delivery into irregular defects. The injectable mTG-Gel/BTO hydrogel integrates an mTG-crosslinked gelatin network with physically incorporated BTO nanoparticles for local treatment of infected bone defects. Pulsed US activates BTO-associated piezoelectric responses, linking ROS generation to antibacterial and antibiofilm effects and VGCC-mediated Ca²⁺ signaling to macrophage immunomodulation. The resulting pro-regenerative microenvironment promotes angiogenic and osteogenic responses, ultimately supporting vascularized bone regeneration. US, ultrasound; mTG, microbial transglutaminase; BTO, barium titanate; ROS, reactive oxygen species; VGCCs, voltage-gated calcium channels

works.title: Correction: f-SPION-mediated magnetic stimulation induces reparative Schwann cell reprogramming via cytoskeletal dynamics - gated activation of Piezo1
Bioprinted Stiffness‑Tunable Pancreatic Microniches to Decode Early Tumor Initiation Mechanisms
works.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the deadliest human cancers, driven in 90% of cases by KRAS mutations and characterized by an intense desmoplastic reaction, early metastasis, and therapy resistance. The mechanisms driving PDAC initiation, however, remain poorly understood because early acinar transformation is difficult to model in a controlled microenvironment. Here, we introduce a microvalve-bioprinted 3D pancreatic cancer initiation niche that supports culture of primary acini from wild-type and Kras-mutant mice, up to 14 days, within gelatin-methacryloyl (GelMA) hydrogels. Our printing strategy enables tuning of hydrogel stiffness to cover the range reported for healthy murine pancreas and early stages of desmoplastic remodelling. In this system, wild-type acini retain a predominantly acinar phenotype, whereas intermediate GelMA conditions cooperate with pre-existing oncogenic Kras to promote acinar-to-ductal metaplasia and proliferative programs associated with early neoplastic reprogramming. Multimodal readouts revealed a stiffness-permissive window in which mechanical cues cooperated with oncogenic Kras to promote acinar transdifferenciation, proliferation and distinct stiffness-dependent secretory programs, including inflammatory and stromal-associated factors with previously reported relevance to PDAC biology. The deterministic droplet geometry supported reproducible, high-throughput, and longitudinal analysis under conditions inaccessible to conventional extrusion or laser‑assisted bioprinting, providing an experimental framework to study early Kras-driven acinar reprogramming.

works.title: A ROS‐Responsive Injectable Hydrogel Platform Reprograms the Diabetic Wound Microenvironment to Enable Exosome Therapy
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Diabetic wounds persist because excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) sustain chronic inflammation and disrupt the regenerative microenvironment, impairing the stability and function of bioactive therapeutic components, including stem cells and extracellular vesicles (EVs). Here, an injectable hyaluronic acid (HA) hydrogel integrates microenvironment modulation with regenerative cue delivery by co‐encapsulating ROS‐responsive cerium oxide nanozymes (CeO 2 NPs) and mesenchymal stem cell‐derived exosomes (EXOs). In this system, CeO 2 NPs act as antioxidant regulators that respond to oxidative stress, while EXOs provide regenerative signals for tissue repair. CeO 2 NPs are packaged within a thioketal‐linked PLGA‐PEG shell, enabling ROS‐triggered degradation and on‐demand activation, whereas the in situ crosslinked HA network serves as a localized matrix that protects components and synchronizes their sustained co‐release. Under high‐glucose conditions, the composite hydrogel reduces intracellular ROS, restores mitochondrial membrane potential, and enhances proliferation, migration, and angiogenic activity of endothelial cells and fibroblasts. In a diabetic mouse wound model, the hydrogel accelerates wound closure, accompanied by attenuated oxidative stress and inflammation, enhanced neovascularization and re‐epithelialization, organized collagen remodeling, and a shift of macrophages toward a pro‐regenerative M2 phenotype. This pathology‐responsive antioxidant–regenerative coupling strategy establishes a rational, modular platform for overcoming microenvironmental constraints in exosome‐based regenerative therapies.

works.title: A Biocatalytic Cascade‐Based Cu‐GMP Self‐Assembly Nanozyme for Accelerating Infected Diabetic Wound Healing
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanozymes with multi‐enzyme catalytic properties have emerged as promising multifunctional materials for biosensing and antimicrobial applications. Herein, a copper‐guanosine monophosphate (Cu‐GMP) nanozyme was synthesized via a simple one‐pot method. Its supramolecular network serves as a multifunctional carrier, enabling the encapsulation of functional guest biomolecules and retaining their inherent activity simultaneously. As a proof‐of‐concept, glucose oxidase (GOx) was incorporated to construct a glucose‐responsive cascade catalytic system (GOx@Cu‐GMP). In this system, GOx catalyzes glucose oxidation to produce hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) and gluconic acid. The latter creates a localized acidic microenvironment, which combined with in situ generated H 2 O 2 , effectively activates the peroxidase (POD)‐like activity of Cu‐GMP and further generates hydroxyl radicals (•OH). Leveraging this cascade reaction, GOx@Cu‐GMP was developed as a sensitive colorimetric platform for glucose detection. Furthermore, Cu‐GMP exhibits oxidase (OXD)‐, laccase (LAC)‐, and glutathione peroxidase (GPx)‐like activities, facilitating the generation of various reactive oxygen species. Benefiting from multi‑enzyme synergy, it achieves broad‑spectrum antibacterial performance. Moreover, GOx@Cu‐GMP can eliminate bacterial infections and accelerate wound healing in a diabetic mouse skin wound model. This work provides a multifunctional nanozyme‐based platform for glucose detection and diabetic wound antimicrobial therapy, offering new insights for the development of integrated biosensing and therapeutic materials.

works.title: A Mitochondrial Autophagy‐Synthesis Dynamic Equilibrium Liposome for the Repair of Energy Metabolism in Acute Kidney Injury
works.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a clinical syndrome primarily attributed to mitochondrial dysfunction, characterized by disrupted mitochondrial balance. Impaired biogenesis leads to insufficient energy supply, while defective autophagy results in the accumulation of damaged mitochondria-both of which exacerbate injury to renal tubular epithelial cells. In this study, we developed melatonin/pioglitazone liposomes (MP@Lip) for AKI therapy via restoration of mitochondrial dynamic balance. When melatonin and pioglitazone was jointly delivered to damaged renal tubules, they activated mitochondrial autophagy and biogenesis, thereby bidirectionally restoring mitochondrial network homeostasis. Mechanistically, AMPK/SIRT3/PGC-1α-related signaling may be involved in the mitochondrial protection of MP@Lip. Upon AMPK phosphorylation, SIRT1/SIRT3 deacetylase activity is upregulated, the ratio of LC3B-II/LC3B-I increases, p62/SQSTM1 decreases, and autophagy is enhanced. PGC-1α enhances transcriptional activity and promotes the expression of mitochondrial biogenic markers (TOM20). This complementary degradation-synthesis loop gradually restores mitochondrial dynamic balance. In vitro experiments confirmed that MP@Lip reduces ROS production and apoptosis while restoring mitochondrial membrane potential. In vivo studies demonstrated improvement in renal function indicators, alleviation of inflammatory responses and histopathological damage, and no systemic toxicity. This strategy shifts AKI treatment from symptomatic support to ameliorating mitochondrial dysfunction, providing a targeted, complementary and relatively safe approach that may be applicable to other mitochondrial functional-related diseases.

works.title: Inhibiting Lactylation‐Mediated Metabolic‐Epigenetic Reprogramming to Potentiate Tumor Photo‐Immunotherapy
works.abstract: Cancer immunotherapies face limitations in treating "cold" tumors due to immune suppression driven by metabolic dysregulation within the tumor microenvironment. Research has revealed that tumor cells produce excess lactate via hypoxia-induced glycolysis, promoting histone lactylation and establishing immunosuppression-associated metabolic-epigenetic reprogramming. Here, a near-infrared (NIR)-triggered nanoplatform (RgA-L-I/P/R) has been developed to fundamentally dismantle the immunosuppression via the metabolic-epigenetic axis. Upon NIR excitation, the platform released oxygen from perfluoropentane (PFP) ("oxygen unlocking chamber") in the tumor through dual targeting of AS1411 and Rg3 ("nano-warhead"), liberating the IR-1048 and the CRISPR/Cas9 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) ("NIR immune trigger" and "metabolic nanolock"). IR-1048 induced immunogenic cell death (ICD) to trigger dendritic cell maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration, while CRISPR/Cas9 RNP induced LDHA (lactate dehydrogenase A) gene knockdown that locked the lactate supply and reprogrammed metabolism and epigenetics. These changes reduced histone lactylation and IL-10 expression, promoting the conversion of tumor-associated macrophages to the M1 type and synergistically downregulating hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression upon oxygen release. This nanoplatform enables synergistic photothermal immunostimulation with CRISPR-mediated metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming. Rather than merely countering mild downstream immune regulation by ICD, it seeks to fundamentally eliminate the immunosuppression, offering novel therapeutic strategies through the metabolic-epigenetic pathway for poorly immunoresponsive tumors.

works.title: A reconfigurable self-rectifying dynamic memristor enabling integrated dendritic noise suppression and ReLU activation for target recognition
works.abstract: Abstract The growing demand for machine vision under noisy environments exposes a fundamental limitation of existing image-processing hardware, in which noise suppression and feature extraction are implemented as physically and functionally separated modules, leading to inefficient data transfer and constrained system-level optimization. Here, we report a reconfigurable rectifying dynamic memristor based on a NiOx/WOy heterojunction fabricated at room temperature, exhibiting a high rectification ratio of up to 105 without any post-treatment. More importantly, a single device is demonstrated, for the first time, to emulate both dendritic signal processing and ReLU-type neuronal activation through distinct operation modes. Under voltage-input operation, the device exhibits dendrite-like behaviors, including signal filtering and temporal integration, enabling effective suppression of background noise. Under current-input operation, its transfer characteristics closely resemble ReLU activation, playing a crucial role in edge detection. By intrinsically coupling noise suppression and feature extraction at the device level, this unified processing paradigm significantly improves image recognition performance under realistic noise conditions. When applied to image denoising and edge feature extraction on the SVHN dataset, the recognition accuracy of a convolutional neural network increase from 81.30% to 87.95%. This work establishes a materials-enabled device strategy for integrating information processing and computation within a single device, offering a promising pathway toward scalable and low-power neuromorphic vision systems.

works.title: Atomic Pd–Br interface for synergistic photocatalytic selective oxidation of alkyl aromatics
works.abstract: Abstract Photocatalysis offers a mild route to selective hydrocarbon oxidation and is an attractive alternative to harsh thermal oxidation. However, progress in developing efficient catalysts has been slow, largely because the active sites that govern activity and selectivity remain poorly understood. Here, we precisely construct Pd–Br4 sites on BiOBr nanosheets, creating an atomic Pd–Br interface that captures photogenerated carriers and promotes their separation and utilization. Once a Br atom has trapped a hole, it cooperates with the Pd site to activate the C(sp3)–H bond of toluene at the atomic interface. The resulting catalyst oxidizes toluene under ambient conditions witha reaction rate of ~3000 μmol g−1 h−1(14.9% conversion, >99% benzaldehyde selectivity) , a 48-fold enhancement over the pristine BiOBr supportand −15.4-fold higher than Pd nanoparticles on the same support, with a turnover frequency of 45 h..Under prolonged irradiation, benzoic acid is obtained with 96% selectivity at 98% conversion These findings demonstrate a rational design strategy for single-atom sites in which the atomic Pd–Br interface mediates synergistic C–H bond activation, providing a general route toward efficient heterogeneous photocatalysts.

works.title: All-optical modulator and switcher based on 2D MgB 2 nanosheets with strong nonlinear optical response
works.abstract: Abstract The Kerr nonlinearity in two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials is emerging as an appealing research topic owing to their prominent light processing, modulation, and manipulation abilities. In this contribution, 2D magnesium diboride (MgB2) nanosheets (NSs) are employed in nonlinear photonic devices based on the spatial self-phase modulation (SSPM) method. By exploiting the Kerr nonlinearity of 2D MgB2, an all-optical phase-modulated system is proposed to realize “ON” and “OFF” states for all-optical switching. Using the same system, an optical logic gate is further demonstrated, achieving the logical “OR” operation based on 2D MgB2 NSs dispersions. Moreover, a 2D MgB2/BN hybrid structure is fabricated. The results show that this hybrid structure enables unidirectional nonlinear excitation, leading to spatial asymmetric light propagation. This behavior is an important prerequisite for optical diode functionality and may also provide a useful foundation for the design of optical isolators. These initial investigations suggest that 2D MgB2 is a promising material for designing optical logic devices and represents a meaningful step toward all-optical information processing.

works.title: Bilayer Na‐MMT‐Intercalated Guar Gum Triboelectric Nanogenerator With Graphite‐Infused Electrodes for Machine Learning‐Assisted Neck Posture Monitoring
works.abstract: Prolonged screen use has fostered cervical musculoskeletal disorders, indicating the need for non-invasive, comfortable, low-power posture monitoring system. In this work, we developed a sustainable self-powered triboelectric nanogenerator consisting a biodegradable guar gum-based biopolymer for energy harvesting and neck posture monitoring. The device employing a bilayer architecture, comprises a guar gum-bentonite triboelectric film coated with a guar gum-graphite conductive electrode, eliminating the need for a metallic electrode. The addition of Na-bentonite filler improves the dielectric and surface charge properties, producing a stable electrical output. As a flexible patch, the G-TENG measures unique biomechanical voltage signals representing neck flexion and slouching posture. The analysis of these electrical signals with machine learning algorithms enables the precise classification of neck angle and sitting postures. This current study presents a strategy for green, self-powered electronics that bridge personalized digital healthcare with sustainable biopolymers to mitigate global e-waste.

works.title: CRISPR‐Cas Assays for Protein Detection: Strategies and Clinical Applications
works.abstract: Measurement of protein biomarkers with high accuracy is critical for disease diagnostics and prognostic monitoring. However, conventional analytical platforms for protein detection suffer from insufficient sensitivity for low-abundance targets and require time-consuming, multi-step workflows. The CRISPR-Cas system is emerging as a powerful tool for protein analysis, with advantages including high programmability, excellent sensitivity, and compatibility with diverse readouts. This review presents a systematic overview of recent advances in CRISPR-based protein assays. We first summarize the design principles of aptamer-, antibody-, and enzyme-mediated systems that convert protein recognition events into CRISPR-activatable nucleic acid signals. We next examine the signal amplification and readout strategies, such as direct CRISPR activation, enzyme-mediated nucleic acid amplification, and enzyme-free DNA nanotechnology, along with colorimetric, fluorescent, or electrochemical signal outputs. We also review applications of these assays in infectious diseases, cancer, and Alzheimer's disease. Finally, we discuss challenges and perspectives for next-generation CRISPR-based protein detection platforms in clinical translation.

works.title: Design and Navigation of Magnetic Micro/Nanorobotic Swarms in Complex Endovascular Networks: From Swarm Dynamics to Targeted Therapeutics
works.abstract: The human vascular network, with its intricate geometries and diverse flow regimes, represents a formidable frontier for microrobotic navigation. While isolated microrobots frequently reach their functional ceiling due to weak signal contrast, low payload capacity, and susceptibility to hydrodynamic drag, the emergence of programmable micro/nanorobotic swarms offers a strategy to overcome these limitations in vascular intervention. By harnessing collective intelligence and programmable behavior, these swarms enhance positional stability, detectability in hard-to-reach circulatory environments, and versatility across endovascular tasks. This review provides a critical synthesis of magnetic actuation as an effective strategy for governing these collectives, owing to its deep-tissue penetration and precise spatiotemporal control. An integrated design framework bridges fundamental physical principles and practical swarm-engineering strategies with their translational potential in endovascular medicine, emphasizing relationships among collective structure, swarm dynamics, and navigation. These collective structures facilitate amplified imaging signals, high local therapeutic payloads, and task-specific interventions, enabling robust navigation through tortuous vascular networks. By evaluating the transition from laboratory prototypes toward clinical applications, this work highlights the integrated advances required to overcome biosafety and scalability hurdles. Ultimately, programmable magnetic swarms emerge as a versatile platform with considerable potential for high-precision, minimally invasive endovascular medicine.

works.title: Jammed Emulsion Matrices as Transparent Porous Media for Studying Bacteria Under Confinement
works.abstract: Across diverse environments, bacteria inhabit structurally complex niches such as soil, tissues, sediment beds, and aquifers where they encounter confined, internally disordered, microporous 3D architectures that significantly alter their growth, motility and chemotaxis. While past efforts have interrogated bacteria in porous media using jammed packings of optically transparent hydrogels or refractive index-matched bead suspensions, these cannot capture key elements of their natural arenas. Critically, active fluid advection through a transport-confined granular matrix-a ubiquitous feature in environments such as aquifers and sediment beds-is yet to be effectively realized using existing experimental platforms. We bridge this gap by engineering an optically transparent, 3D transport-confined granular matrix using jammed packings of oil-in-water emulsion droplets where the refractive index of the oil matches that of bacterial nutrient broth. Using this platform, we interrogate bacterial growth and motility with single-cell resolution, as well as collective chemotaxis of bacterial cells inside the matrix. To demonstrate the flow-through capabilities, we deposit bacterial cells throughout the ensemble 3D matrix using a controlled flow system. Together, our work introduces a versatile and broadly adaptable experimental platform for investigating bacterial growth, motility, chemotaxis, and transport within an optically transparent, flow-through, transport-confined 3D granular medium.

works.title: Ultrahigh Thermal Conductive Graphite Films Derived From Poly(p‐Phenylene‐1,3,4‐Oxadiazole) Precursor Copolymerized With 2,6‐Naphthalenedicarboxylic Acid
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient thermal management materials are indispensable for next‐generation electronic devices with ever‐increasing power densities. However, the thermal conductivity of artificial graphite films remains far below the theoretical limit of graphene because abundant structural defects generated during carbonization and graphitization severely impede phonon transport.
