Herein, a pre‐fused aromatization strategy is proposed to regulate the microstructural evolution of graphite films by introducing 2,6‐naphthalenedicarboxylic acid (2,6‐NDA) into a poly(p‐phenylene‐1,3,4‐oxadiazole) (POD) precursor through copolymerization. The pyrolysis behavior of the copolymers was systematically investigated, revealing that the rigid fused naphthalene units promote the formation of enlarged conjugated aromatic domains during thermal decomposition, thereby facilitating the growth of highly ordered graphitic crystallites while suppressing defect generation during subsequent graphitization. Consequently, a graphite film with a thickness of 35 µm was successfully fabricated, exhibiting an ultrahigh in‐plane thermal conductivity of 1820 ± 20 W m − 1 K − 1 . Meanwhile, the incorporation of 2,6‐NDA significantly increased the carbon residue ratio owing to its superior thermal stability. This work demonstrates that molecular‐level pre‐fused aromatization effectively tailors the graphitization pathway and provides a scalable strategy for producing low‐defect, highly graphitized graphite films for advanced thermal management applications.

works.title: A High‐Speed Dielectric Approach to Track Domain Structure Evolution in Operating Ferroelectric Devices
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Ferroelectric switching is a fundamental process underpinning the functionality of modern electronic devices, yet the dynamic evolution of ferroelectric domain structures, especially in thin films, remains poorly understood. While established techniques such as piezoresponse force microscopy and transmission electron microscopy successfully image ferroelectric domains, they fail to capture global transient domain dynamics due to resolution limits and slow acquisition. In addition, performing in operando measurements on functional devices is highly impractical with these methods. This gap has hindered progress in understanding and controlling ferroelectric switching in thin films, which is critical for applications from nonvolatile memories to sensors. Here, we introduce a novel approach using amplitude‐modulated dielectric signals in the frequency domain to drastically reduce acquisition times to microseconds, instead of seconds. This method allows real‐time, nondestructive, and in operando tracking of domain wall density and mobility in ferroelectric devices, overcoming the limitations of existing techniques. By applying this approach to (Ba,Ca)TiO 3 thin films, we directly probe transient states in response to electric pulses, revealing previously inaccessible dynamics. This breakthrough opens new avenues for studying dynamic domain switching in thin films and promises to advance the design of ferroelectric materials for next‐generation electronic devices.

works.title: Photolithography Patternable and Mechanically Robust Silver Nanowire Films for High‐Resolution Flexible Light‐Emitting Devices
works.abstract: Flexible transparent conductive electrodes based on silver nanowires (Ag NWs) show strong potential for flexible electronic devices, yet high-resolution patterning remains a major challenge. Here, we present a composite electrode that integrates Ag NWs with a conductive photoresist (CPR), achieving both high electrical conductivity and high-resolution patterning in a unified structure. Silver nanoparticles and dispersants are incorporated into the photoresist at a designed ratio to form CPR, which maintains good dispersion and excellent photolithographic performance. In this composite, the bottom Ag NWs network provides efficient charge transport, while the top CPR layer forms a dense protective coating. The CPR/Ag NWs structure enables high-resolution electrode patterning with a minimum line width of 7 µm using only exposure and development, without requiring conventional etching processes. Meanwhile, the CPR layer reduces surface roughness, enhances adhesion to the substrate, and improves environmental stability and mechanical reliability, ensuring structural integrity during photolithography. With this structure, we fabricate flexible AC electroluminescent devices with a line width of 50 µm and further demonstrate its compatibility with LED integration. This strategy offers a high-performance, high-resolution, and patternable electrode platform for flexible displays and wearable electronics.

works.title: SiO2-Crosslinked Molecularly Imprinted Hybrid Nanostructures for Solid-Phase Extraction of Bisphenol A
works.abstract: Abstract Previously, a molecularly imprinted hybrid (MIH) was synthesized by imprinting bisphenol A (BPA) within SiO2-crosslinked poly(styrene-co-methyl methacrylate) nanoframeworks. In this work, its adsorption and solid-phase extraction (SPE) performance toward BPA in complex matrices was systematically investigated and compared with two commercial sorbents, C18 and SupelMIPBPA. MIH exhibited a high adsorption capacity of 49.5 mg/g with a large Langmuir coefficient (KL = 3.16 × 10−2 L/mg) and high BPA selectivity with factors of 1.53 and 35.4 relative to 2BPF and phenol, respectively. Moreover, it exhibited 12 and 1120 times higher specific adsorption ability than SupelMIPBPA and C18, respectively. The tailored binding sites embedded within the hydrophobic polymeric matrix and stabilized with rigid, hydrophilic SiO2 crosslinks contributed to stable adsorption over pH 2−9 and in the presence of humic acid up to 20 mg/L while enhancing BPA adsorption by 1.5-fold at NaCl concentrations up to 3000 mM. MIH maintained stable adsorption over 11 regeneration cycles across synthesis batches and retained its adsorption capacity after more than six months of storage. When applied to SPE, the optimized MIH-SPE method effectively enriched BPA while reducing matrix interference, achieving enrichment factors of 52.0−60.0. Coupled with HPLC-photodiode array detection, the method achieved matrix-specific MDLs of 1.3 ng/mL in DI water and 0.2−3.1 ng/mL in environmental waters. Recoveries of 88.8−118.7% and RSDs of 0.2−9.6% demonstrated satisfactory accuracy and precision across the tested water matrices. In contrast, C18- and SupelMIPBPA-based SPE exhibited inferior performance due to limited adsorption capacity or less efficient analyte elution.

works.title: Coordination-Assisted Synthesis of Nanoheterojunctions with Asymmetric Interfacial Oxygen Vacancies for Nonradical Persulfate Activation
works.abstract: Abstract Programming the location and coordination environment of oxygen vacancies in metal oxides remains a central synthetic challenge. Here, we report a coordination-assisted synthesis that converts an amorphous coordination polymer precursor, prepared by grinding cobalt and zinc nitrates with 2-methylimidazole in near-complete solid recovery, into oxide nanoparticles (∼10 nm) upon mild calcination. The Zn/Co ratio serves as a compositional switch that selects among pure Co3O4, Zn-doped Co3O4, and ZnO/Co3O4 nanoheterojunctions. The heterojunction interface stabilizes abundant asymmetric interfacial oxygen vacancies (formation energy 1.06 versus 3.27 eV for the doped lattice), which mediate nonradical peroxydisulfate activation through surface-complex formation and direct electron transfer, oxidatively polymerizing bisphenol A into insoluble deposits and achieving its complete removal within 9 min over a broad pH range. Compositional preorganization via amorphous coordination intermediates thus emerges as a general and scalable principle for interface and defect engineering in mixed-metal oxides.

works.title: Enhancement of Second-Harmonic Generation and Modulation of Excitonic Emission from Monolayer WS2 in Au Nanobipyramid Plasmonic Nanocavities
works.abstract: Abstract Plasmonic nanocavities provide an effective platform for enhancing nonlinear light−matter interactions in two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), with potential applications in compact on-chip nonlinear light sources. However, the simultaneous enhancement of nonlinear optical conversion and modulation of excitonic emission within a single hybrid structure remains insufficiently understood. Here, we report an Au nanobipyramid-on-mirror nanocavity integrated with monolayer WS2. The sharp nanobipyramid tips and nanoparticle−mirror plasmonic coupling strongly confine the fundamental field within the nanogap, producing an area-normalized second-harmonic generation (SHG) enhancement factor of up to ∼7522. Polarization-resolved measurements further reveal an anisotropic SHG response arising from the interplay between the intrinsic crystalline symmetry of monolayer WS2 and the polarization-sensitive field confinement of the nanocavity. More importantly, excitation-power-dependent measurements reveal a transition from trion-dominated to exciton-dominated emission. This spectral redistribution likely results from the combined effects of localized electromagnetic-field confinement, excitation-induced carrier-density variations, and local photothermal heating at the metal−semiconductor interface, which together modify exciton−trion interconversion and shift the emission balance toward neutral excitons. These combined nonlinear and excitonic responses make the Au NBP/WS2/Ag nanocavity particularly promising as a hybrid nanomaterial platform for compact on-chip frequency-doubling light sources with excitation-tunable excitonic output.

works.title: Electrochemical Reconstruction of Layered FeNi Metal−Organic Framework Nanostructures for Simulated Seawater and Alkaline Water Oxidation
works.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic water splitting for hydrogen production is an important approach to facilitate the transition toward a low-carbon energy system. Great efforts have been devoted to developing highly active and durable non-precious-metal catalysts. Herein, a layered iron-nickel bimetallic metal−organic framework (FeNi-MOF) with a nanoscale single-layer thickness of approximately 50 nm was fabricated via a room-temperature component regulation strategy. This nanoscale layered structure provides abundant surface active sites and efficient electron transport pathways. The as-prepared catalyst exhibits outstanding oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance, delivering an overpotential of only 242 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm−2, and possesses excellent corrosion resistance in simulated seawater electrolytes. Assembled with commercial Pt/C to construct a full water-splitting electrolyzer, the system achieves a current density of 10 mA cm−2 at a cell voltage of 1.56 V and maintains stable operation for 24 h. Mechanistic investigations verify that FeNi-MOF undergoes dynamic surface reconstruction during the OER process to form highly active FeNiOOH as the real catalytic active phase. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the electronic synergy between Fe and Ni sites optimizes the adsorption free energy of oxygen-containing intermediates, reducing the thermodynamic energy barrier of the rate-determining step from 1.52 eV to 1.39 eV and thus greatly enhancing the intrinsic catalytic activity. This work clarifies the reconstruction mechanism of MOF-based precatalysts and provides a promising strategy for designing high-efficiency non-precious metal electrocatalysts for freshwater and seawater electrolysis.

works.title: Platinum Drug-Assisted Responsive Nanoscale Metal Phenolic Networks with Self-Sufficient ROS Amplification for Synergistic Tumor Therapy
works.abstract: Abstract Monotherapy is severely limited by tumor adaptive evolution and intrinsic heterogeneity, making synergistic therapeutic strategies urgently necessary. Herein, we developed a platinum-drug-assisted, tumor microenvironment-responsive nanoscale metal-phenolic network (OXPT@FeMPN) with self-sufficient reactive oxygen species amplification for precision multimodal synergistic therapy. OXPT@FeMPN stably loads oxaliplatin via combined physical and chemical interactions, with a drug loading efficiency of 19.8%, and enables tumor microenvironment-responsive drug release. The released oxaliplatin promotes hydrogen peroxide production, which is subsequently catalyzed by the OXPT@FeMPN nanozyme into hydroxyl radicals, enabling self-sufficient reactive oxygen species amplification in tumors. OXPT@FeMPN also depletes intratumoral glutathione, thereby suppressing tumor antioxidant defense. These cascade catalytic reactions ultimately trigger chemodynamic therapy (CDT). Moreover, OXPT@FeMPN exhibits a high photothermal conversion efficiency (η = 37.5%) under near-infrared irradiation, generating localized hyperthermia for photothermal therapy (PTT) and further enhancing CDT efficiency. In vitro, OXPT@FeMPN plus near-infrared irradiation markedly depleted intracellular glutathione and generated abundant reactive oxygen species, ultimately inducing tumor cells apoptosis. In vivo, this therapeutic strategy achieved 87.8% tumor inhibition with favorable biocompatibility. Collectively, this study presents a multimodal nanoplatform integrating chemotherapy, CDT, and PTT, overcoming the limitations of monotherapy and showing promise for the management of advanced tumors.

works.title: Carbon Nanotube Network-Engineered Interfacial Charge Transport in ZnO/Perovskite Photodetectors for Wavelength-Dependent Signal Encoding
works.abstract: Abstract Perovskite/ZnO heterojunctions are promising for broadband photodetection, but limited charge extraction at metal contacts can prolong carrier residence and promote slow trap-mediated responses. Here, a nanoscale network of semiconducting single-walled carbon nanotubes (s-SWCNTs) was inserted at the Au/ZnO interface to provide an additional charge-extraction pathway. Relative to the control device, the modified device exhibited reduced persistent photoconductivity and more stable switching under 365 and 550 nm illumination. At a bias of 50 μV, the corresponding rise/decay times decreased to 78/66 ms at 365 nm and 83/63 ms at 550 nm, improving by more than one order of magnitude. Replicated Kelvin probe force microscopy and ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy measurements revealed architecture-associated electrostatic and surface electronic-structure shifts, supporting a proposed model of contact-mediated charge extraction. In separate spectral measurements at 10 V, the peak responsivity reached 10.06 A W−1 at 290 nm, with an external quantum efficiency of approximately 4.3 × 103%; responsivities at 365 and 550 nm were 6.44 and 6.15 A W−1, respectively. Measured current responses were subsequently used for proof-of-concept text encoding and offline exclusive-OR image mapping. These results demonstrate how a one-dimensional carbon nanotube network can regulate interfacial charge extraction and switching dynamics in hybrid broadband photodetectors.

works.title: First-Principles Study of ScM2 (M = C and N) Monolayers as High-Performance Anode Materials for Potassium-Ion Storage
works.abstract: Abstract The increasing demand for sustainable energy storage technologies has driven the exploration of alternatives to lithium-ion batteries, with potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) emerging as promising candidates owing to the natural abundance and favorable electrochemical properties of potassium. Two-dimensional (2D) scandium carbide (ScC2) and scandium nitride (ScN2) monolayers were systematically investigated as potential anode materials for PIBs through first-principles density functional theory calculations performed using the Vienna Ab Initio Simulation Package (VASP). The absence of imaginary phonon modes and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations confirm the dynamical and thermal stability of both monolayers, while electron localization function analysis reveals mixed ionic-metallic bonding in ScC2 and ionic-dominant charge transfer in ScN2, with both satisfying the Born mechanical stability criteria. Electronic band structure calculations using GGA-PBE and hybrid HSE06 functionals confirm an intrinsic metallic character in both materials, ensuring efficient electron transport during charge/discharge cycling. The most favorable K adsorption occurs at the Sc top site with adsorption energies of −0.86 eV and −1.32 eV for ScC2 and ScN2, respectively, with Bader charge analysis confirming a K+-like ionic character through charge transfers of 0.85e and 0.86e. The K-ion diffusion barriers calculated by the climbing image nudge elastic band method are 0.078 eV and 0.21 eV for ScC2 and ScN2, indicating ultralow barriers favorable for high-rate PIB performance. The theoretical storage capacities of 777.08 mAh g−1 and 734.57 mAh g−1 with average open circuit voltages (OCV) of 0.27 V and 0.46 V for ScC2 and ScN2, respectively, substantially exceed that of conventional graphite anodes. Small maximum lattice changes of 7.44% and 5.09% upon full K loading confirm mechanical resilience during cycling, while confirmed chemical stability against water adsorption establishes their suitability for ambient fabrication conditions, collectively identifying ScC2 and ScN2 as promising high-performance anode candidates for PIB applications.

works.title: Programmed Gut–Liver‐Targeted Oral Delivery of Peptide‐Probiotic Nano‐Microsystem for Metabolic Complications of Hyperglycemia and Hyperuricemia
authors: WANG Xiao-gang 1,  CHEN Yi-feng 2,  LU Bo 3,  WANG Yu-jie 1,  XU Wei-ya 4,  YANG Qiang 5,  ZHANG Xi-wei 6
works.abstract: Hyperglycemia and hyperuricemia are highly prevalent metabolic comorbidities characterized by systemic metabolic disturbances and complex multi-organ pathogenesis, urgently requiring synergistic multi-organ-targeted therapeutic strategies. Here, we present a programmed gut-liver-targeted oral peptide-probiotic nano-microsystem for metabolic complications of hyperglycemia and hyperuricemia treatment. The xanthine oxidase (XOD)-inhibitory peptide PPKNW (P1) was loaded in a layer-by-layer reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive nanoparticle (P1NPs), followed by engineering on the surface of probiotic Akkermansia muciniphila (Akk), resulting in a peptide-probiotic nano-microsystem (P1NPs@Akk). After oral administration, P1NPs@Akk remained stable during gastric passage. Upon reaching intestinal environment, CS and HA layers were progressively removed, exposing the P1-loaded polymersomes, which were transported across the intestinal epithelium via PAT-1-mediated transcytosis. In the liver, P1 was released in response to ROS-mediated disulfide bond cleavage to inhibit XOD and reduce uric acid synthesis. Meanwhile, Akk was delivered to and colonized in the intestine to regulate glucose metabolism. In a mouse model of combined hyperglycemia and hyperuricemia, P1NPs@Akk promoted hepatic accumulation of P1 and intestinal enrichment of Akk, resulting in significant reductions in blood glucose and uric acid levels. This work presents a programmed gut-liver-targeted oral platform that integrates peptide therapy and probiotic intervention for multi-organ regulation of metabolic disorders.

works.title: NIR‐Activated Ag 2 S Quantum Dots for Synergistic Immunomodulation and Precision Therapy of Refractory Osteomyelitis
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Staphylococcus aureus ( S. aureus ) is a predominant clinical pathogen responsible for a wide range of infections. By forming biofilms during infection, S. aureus evades conventional therapies, leading to persistent infections and treatment failure. To address this challenge, we employed silver sulfide quantum dots (Ag 2 S QDs) for near‐infrared (NIR) phototherapy. In vitro, the nanoagent achieved >99.99% killing of S. aureus within 10 minutes and reduced biofilm biomass by >58%. In a murine osteomyelitis model, a single NIR treatment reduced bacterial loads by 71.83% on implants and 59.18% in bone tissue, while also suppressing key inflammatory cytokines, with local macrophage polarization shifting from an M1‐dominant to an M2‐dominant phenotype. Histopathological and micro‐CT analyses indicated attenuated bone destruction. The nanoagent showed favorable biosafety, with no systemic toxicity in major organs and osteoblast viability >75% at therapeutic concentrations. Together, these results demonstrate a phototherapeutic strategy with combined antibacterial and anti‐biofilm effects, supporting its potential as an adjuvant approach for managing refractory osteomyelitis.

works.title: Fully dispersed site catalysts for the reverse water-gas shift reaction: recent advances and perspectives
works.abstract: Abstract The reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reaction enables the conversion of CO2 and renewable H2 into CO, providing an important way for the resource utilization of CO2. However, its practical application is still limited by the balance of catalytic activity, CO selectivity and high-temperature stability. As these catalytic properties are closely associated with the structure and coordination environment of the active sites, precisely regulating the active sites represents an effective strategy for improving RWGS performance. Fully dispersed site catalysts (FDSCs), including isolated atoms, or subnanometric clusters (<1 nm), offer unique opportunities for atomic-scale control over active-site structures and coordination environments. Therefore, this review summarizes recent advances in FDSCs for RWGS. Firstly, bottom-up construction and top-down redispersion strategies are summarized, highlighting the roles of metal nuclearity, support defects, and interfacial electronic structures in determining the formation and stability of fully dispersed sites. The applications of noble-metal (Pt, Pd, Rh, and Ru) and non-noble-metal (Fe, Co, Ni, and Cu) FDSCs in RWGS are then summarized, focusing on the effects of metal composition and site structure on CO2 activation, H2 dissociation, key intermediate conversion, and CO desorption, as well as the resulting catalytic performance. Finally, future research should integrate operando characterization, theoretical calculations, and artificial intelligence to unravel the dynamic structure–activity relationships of fully dispersed sites, thereby accelerating the rational design of efficient and stable RWGS catalysts.

works.title: Constructing chloride-repelling electrostatic barriers on Au@Rh-Al nanodendrites for highly efficient seawater electrolysis
works.abstract: Abstract Large-scale green hydrogen production via seawater electrolysis represents a pivotal pathway toward achieving carbon neutrality, while direct seawater splitting faces the dual challenges of chloride ion (Cl-) induced active site deactivation and sluggish alkaline water dissociation kinetics. Herein, a novel interface microenvironment modulation strategy is proposed by constructing lattice-strained RhAl hetero-dendritic interfaces on Au cores, in which the modulation of the electronic environment optimizes the d-band center of Rh active sites, providing a superior foundation for intrinsic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity. Comprehensive electrochemical analyses further demonstrate that the interfacial negative charge environment induced by Al sites under alkaline conditions helps regulate the ionic distribution at the catalytic interface and influences the migration of Cl- toward the catalyst surface and active sites, thereby mitigating Cl- interference with the active sites and improving the long-term stability of the catalyst in complex seawater environments. Consequently, the structural synergistic optimization of Au@Rh-Al not only facilitates the rapid replenishment and enrichment of interfacial *OH but also endows the catalyst with exceptional resistance to chlorine corrosion that enhance their intrinsic activity and corrosion resistance. This work provides valuable insights for the rational design and fabrication of highly active and corrosion-resistant electrocatalysts tailored for alkaline seawater electrolysis.

works.title: DNA Nanotechnology for Precision Sensing and Diagnostics at the Nanoscale
works.abstract: DNA nanotechnology provides a programmable framework for acquiring and processing biomolecular information with high precision. Structural DNA nanostructures enable nanoscale organization, molecular addressability and mechanical control, while dynamic DNA reaction networks support signal transduction and molecular computation. This review highlights recent advances in DNA nanotechnology for spatial, mechanical and single-molecule sensing, as well as emerging diagnostic applications based on molecular classifiers and DNA origami-enabled signal processing. Particular emphasis is placed on how nanoscale programmability can improve measurement resolution, enable parallel analysis of multiple molecular signals and facilitate the interpretation of biological information. These developments collectively highlight the potential of DNA nanotechnology for next-generation precision biosensing and diagnostic platforms.

works.title: Super‐Paraelectric Regulation of Energy Storage Performance in Sm 2 O 3 ‐Doped (Ba,Sr)TiO 3 Films via Nanostructure Engineering
works.abstract: ABSTRACT This work presents a strategy for enhancing the energy storage performance in BaTiO 3 ‐based nanocomposite films through a super‐paraelectric regulation approach enabled by Sm 2 O 3 doping. The proposed lead‐free (1‐ x )(Ba 0.8 Sr 0.2 )TiO 3 ‐ x Sm 2 O 3 (0.0 ≤ x ≤ 0.5) films contain only five elements, making them environmentally friendly and simple in composition. The incorporation of Sm 2 O 3 as an immiscible second phase within the (Ba 0.8 Sr 0.2 )TiO 3 matrix induces significant chemical and structural heterogeneity, inducing a transition from a conventional ferroelectric state to a super‐paraelectric state. In combination with an enhanced breakdown strength, this design results in an ultrahigh energy storage efficiency ( η ) exceeding 80%, along with a remarkable recoverable energy storage density ( U e ) of 50.6 and 59.2 J/cm 3 at Sm 2 O 3 contents of x = 0.4 and 0.5. Furthermore, the films with x = 0.4 and 0.5 exhibit superior frequency (20 Hz to 5 kHz) and thermal stability (25°C–160°C), highlighting exceptional operational reliability and robustness under varying conditions. This study demonstrates that the proposed super‐paraelectric regulation strategy provides a practical pathway for designing compositionally optimized and eco‐friendly energy storage materials.

works.title: Engineering ApoE‐Mimetic HDL‐Like Nanoparticles for Glioblastoma‐Targeted Theranostics
works.abstract: Glioblastoma theranostics remain limited by the tumor's blood-brain-barrier (BBB), infiltrative growth, and heterogenous, treatment-resistant cell populations. Here, we engineered self-assembled high-density lipoprotein (HDL)-like nanoparticles functionalized with an apolipoprotein E-mimetic peptide (ApoEm), designed to recapitulate and strengthen the multireceptor-mediated transport properties of native apolipoprotein E3 (ApoE3). Competition and receptor inhibition studies demonstrate coordinated uptake of ApoEm-HDL nanoparticle via low-density lipoprotein receptor, low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1, and scavenger receptor class-B type 1, which are expressed at BBB and upregulated in glioblastoma. Incorporation of porphyrin-lipid into the HDL-like scaffold yielded ApoEm porphyrin-lipoprotein nanoparticles (ApoEm-PLP) with a uniform, spherical morphology (∼30 nm). ApoEm-PLP increased porphyrin uptake relative to ApoE3-PLP across multiple glioblastoma cell lines (∼seven-fold in U87 cells, ∼four-fold in T98, and GL261-Luc cells) and induced ∼two-fold greater photodynamic therapy (PDT) efficacy in U87 cells. In an orthotopic U87 glioblastoma model, intravenous administration of ApoEm-PLP achieved ∼13-fold higher tumor porphyrin accumulation than normal brain, with homogeneous intratumoral distribution and pronounced peri-tumoral deposition. Transcranial PDT using ApoEm-PLP elicited widespread tumor damage. These findings establish ApoEm-HDL-like nanoparticles as a promising theranostic platform for uniform glioblastoma porphyrin delivery and effective phototherapy, with potential to address the infiltrative and heterogenous nature of glioblastoma.

works.title: Biophysics in Lipid Membranes: Advanced Experimental Platforms for Artificial Membrane Transport
works.abstract: Artificial membrane transport systems have attracted growing interest as simplified models of biological membranes in supramolecular chemistry, chemical biology, and medicine. A wide variety of membrane-active architectures have been realized, including artificial ion translocators, transmembrane signal transducers, cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs), and related systems for transport across biological membranes. These systems mediate ion translocation, molecule uptake, and signaling events across a lipid bilayer, holding significant potential for applications in medicine, sensors, materials, and artificial cells. In this review article, we provide a comprehensive overview of different techniques used to evaluate the transport properties of synthetic systems across lipid bilayer membranes. The current review aims to make a collection of various established fluorescence- and non-fluorescence-based assays. This review demonstrates how carefully conducted experiments and the combination of complementary methods can ensure data reliability and deepen our understanding of the interplay among transport efficiency, selectivity, and mechanism.

works.title: Accelerating Molecular Ferroelectrics: From Rapid Mapping to Scalable High‐Yield Synthesis
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular ferroelectrics (MFs) represent a transformative class of functional materials, which offer mechanical flexibility, low‐density architectures, and chemical tunability. However, their development is bottlenecked by empirical, “trial‐and‐error” crystallization methods that impede both structural determination and scalable synthetic routes. Here, we present an integrated flow‐assisted crystallization screening framework that could transform the discovery and processing of MFs from an empirical approach into a quantitative, data‐driven workflow. Using the molecular ferroelectric [Co( n ‐BuDABCO)Br 3 ] ( 1 ) as a robust MF reference, we demonstrate the rapid mapping of multidimensional crystallization space. We establish a scalable framework for the accelerated synthesis, to identify conditions that yield single‐crystal‐quality XRD material within minutes. This methodology is subsequently translated to continuous‐flow synthesis in ethanol, further intensified by the introduction of CO 2 as a sustainable anti‐solvent. Across the screened CO 2 /EtOH operating conditions, phase‐pure crystalline powders are recovered in consistently high yields up to 97%. While the high thermodynamic stability of 1 precludes the formation of new polymorphs for this system, this proof‐of‐concept highlights the viability of accessing crystallization regimes in non‐classical media, providing an adaptable strategy for the future screening and development of MFs and related multifunctional materials.

works.title: Dual-Interfacial Engineering of Charge-Transport Layers for Efficient Low-Current-Density Quantum Dot Light-Emitting Diodes
works.abstract: Abstract Quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs), employing nanoscale colloidal quantum dots as emissive materials, have emerged as strong contenders for next-generation lighting and display technologies owing to their advantages of simple fabrication, high brightness, and excellent color purity. However, conventional QLEDs suffer from severe nanoscale charge imbalance caused by excessive electron injection from the ZnMgO nanoparticle-based electron transport layer (ETL) relative to hole injection, which significantly limits both efficiency and operational lifetime. Moreover, excessive electrons can accumulate in the hole transport layer (HTL), inducing unwanted emission from the HTL and thereby reducing color purity. To address the charge imbalance, we introduced a molecular-scale self-assembled monolayer (2PACz) onto the hole injection layer (PEDOT: PSS), forming an interfacial dipole that improves contact with the HTL and reduces carrier leakage. The self-assembled monolayer also modulates the energy level alignment, reducing the hole injection barrier and enhancing hole transport capability. In addition, 18-Crown-6 was incorporated into the ZnMgO nanoparticle electron transport layer (ETL) to increase the electron injection barrier. Through this dual nanoscale interfacial engineering of both electron and hole transport layers, the red-emitting QLEDs achieved an external quantum efficiency (EQE) exceeding 20% at a low current density (10−2 mA/cm2), with a maximum EQE of 30.63% at 100 mA/cm2. Furthermore, the devices exhibited a T95 operational lifetime of 9289.8 h at 1000 cd/m2. This study provides a practical nanoscale interfacial engineering approach for fabricating low-power, high-performance red QLEDs with enhanced stability and longevity.

works.title: Correction to “Tuning Performance of Heterojunction Flexible Photodetectors by Energy Band Alignment Engineering”
authors: H. M. Noor ul Huda Khan Asghar

works.title: Three-dimensional imaging of individual carbon atoms
Rational design of lipid nanoparticles for brain delivery of RNA therapeutics
Mechano-immune reinforced exosomes from YAP-activated macrophages counteracting musculoskeletal trauma and age-related decline
works.abstract: Musculoskeletal repair is jointly constrained by impaired inflammation resolution, elevated oxidative stress, diminished regenerative capacity, and altered mechanical microenvironments. Here, we develop a cell-free reparative strategy based on exosomes derived from YAP-activated M2-like macrophages, integrated with reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive hydrogel delivery. Pharmacological activation of YAP under low-stiffness conditions partially recapitulates the reparative macrophage phenotype induced by matrix stiffening. Exosomes harvested from YAP-activated macrophages (Y-M2-EXO) exhibit stronger anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and pro-regenerative activities than conventional M2 macrophage-derived exosomes (M2-EXO), mitigating oxidative injury and lipid peroxidation-associated cellular damage in mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), preserving mitochondrial homeostasis, and enhancing MSC migration, proliferation, and osteogenic/tenogenic differentiation. MicroRNA sequencing and qRT-PCR validation reveal that YAP activation markedly reshapes the miRNA profile of Y-M2-EXO, enriching a candidate miRNA network associated with inflammatory stress, differentiation and regeneration, senescence homeostasis, and mechano-adaptation, which provides a molecular explanatory framework for the functional superiority of Y-M2-EXO over M2-EXO. To improve local retention and environmentally triggered release, Y-M2-EXO are encapsulated within an ROS-responsive hydrogel dynamically crosslinked by hyaluronic acid-aminophenylboronic acid (HA-APBA) and poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA). In rat models of Achilles tendon rupture and tibial fracture, hydrogel-delivered Y-M2-EXO ameliorate the injured microenvironment, promote structural tissue reconstruction and biomechanical recovery, and maintain robust reparative performance under conditions of restricted mechanical input. In naturally aged mice, Y-M2-EXO reduce the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-related inflammatory burden and alleviate bone and muscle degeneration; when combined with aerobic exercise, selected tissue reconstruction and motor function parameters are further improved. Collectively, this study supports donor-cell YAP preprogramming to optimize exosome bioactivity, coupled with ROS-responsive local delivery, as a translationally promising cell-free regulatory strategy for musculoskeletal repair.

works.title: Osteoarthritis‐Microenvironment‐Triggered Phase Alteration of Injectable Conductive Hydrogel for Attenuating Cartilage Degradation
works.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is associated with excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, which contributes substantially to chondrocyte dysfunction, oxidative stress, and cartilage degradation. Although stimuli-responsive hydrogels have emerged as promising platforms for OA therapy, conventional hydrogel-based systems exhibit limited sensitivity and require external detection equipment, highlighting the need for a simple, sensitive, and directly observable monitoring system. To address these challenges, we developed a ROS-triggered, in situ-forming gel-sol transition of a polydopamine (PDA)-loaded, diselenide-crosslinked polymer dot (PD) injectable hydrogel (HGC-PDA@PD or OA gel) as a monitorable theranostic for OA therapy at physiological temperature (37°C). The monitorable OA microenvironment-responsive hydrogel relied on interactions between the high ROS levels in OA cartilage and the OA gel, which triggered diselenide bond cleavage and the release of PDA from PD, causing a unique gel-sol transition of the OA gel. Owing to PDA release after diselenide breakage, the fluorescence and electroconductivity of the OA gel changed, which could serve as additional signals during OA detection. In vitro studies demonstrated the sensitive gel-sol transition of OA gel towards OA-induced immature articular chondrocytes (IL-1β/siSOD1/siCatalase-transfected iMACs). Furthermore, the OA gel showed a distinct gel-sol transition in cartilage of an in vivo OA mouse model compared with that in control mice. The lower transcription levels of cartilage matrix-degrading enzymes (ADAMTS4, ADAMTS5, MMP-3, and MMP-13) observed after OA gel injection confirmed that the OA gel could scavenge ROS and attenuate cartilage damage, revealing its potential application for dual-function OA diagnosis and rehabilitation.

works.title: Core‐Shell Microneedles for Sequential Delivery of Antibacterial, Antioxidant, and Anti‐Inflammatory Agents in Infected Wound Healing
works.abstract: Infected wounds are dynamic pathological processes that progress through acute, chronic, and repair phases, each with distinct therapeutic requirements. Conventional treatments, which release all drugs simultaneously, often fail to meet these stage-specific needs. In this study, we develop a multifunctional core-shell microneedle (MN) system capable of sequential delivery of different therapeutics to address the requirements of various healing stages. During the acute phase, the shell composed of gelatin-hydroxyphenylalanine (Gtn-HPA) hydrogel rapidly releases bacitracin (Bac), thereby inhibiting bacterial proliferation. During the chronic phase, MMP9-responsive peptide nanoparticles (INM-1@EDA) within the MN core undergo enzymatic cleavage, releasing the edaravone (EDA) and indomethacin (INM) moieties to exert antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, respectively. During the repair phase, the residual gelatin at the site supports keratinocyte proliferation and migration, promoting skin tissue regeneration. In a mouse wound model with Staphylococcus aureus infection, core-shell MN treatment achieves nearly complete wound closure in 12 days (96.7 ± 1.3%) with markedly reduced bacterial burden and decreased inflammatory cytokine levels. This MN system achieves sequential release of antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant therapeutics based on wound microenvironments, offering new strategies for efficacious treatment of infected wounds.

works.title: Breaking the Vicious Cycle for Diabetic Wound Healing: A Dynamic‐Static Dual‐Mode Nanofiber Platform for NETs Degradation, Inflammation Resolution, and Scar Prevention
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Chronic diabetic wounds are trapped in a self‐perpetuating vicious cycle—persistent infection, oxidative stress, and NET‐driven inflammation—that severely impairs healing. Here, we engineer a piezoelectric nanofiber membrane (DMTP) that breaks this cycle via a dynamic‐static dual‐mode strategy. DMTP integrates a Mn‐Ti bimetallic MOF with sustained DNase I release, enabling four coordinated functions: (i) piezodynamic ROS generation for on‐demand antibacterial action; (ii) an electric field to guide fibroblast migration; (iii) sustained DNase I release to degrade pathological NETs; and (iv) intrinsic POD/SOD enzyme‐mimetic activity for continuous ROS scavenging. Mechanistically, we show that NETs drive fibroblast differentiation into α‐SMA + myofibroblasts, a key fibrotic driver, and DMTP effectively suppresses this pro‐fibrotic process. In diabetic mice, DMTP achieves 94.32% wound closure with orderly collagen deposition and modulated inflammation (TNF‐α↓, TGF‐β↑). In a rabbit ear hypertrophic scar model, DMTP significantly reduces scar formation by inhibiting α‐SMA expression. This work offers a transformative strategy to achieve diabetic wound healing with diminished scarring by directly dismantling the infection–oxidative stress–NETs–fibrosis axis.

works.title: Microwave‐Responsive AIE Nanocomposite Induces Immunogenic Senescence for Imaging‐Guided Therapy and Bone Repair in Osteosarcoma
works.abstract: Osteosarcoma remains challenging due to incomplete tumor resection, local recurrence, and limited immunostimulatory efficacy of current microwave (MW)-based therapies. Here, we develop a multifunctional theranostic nanoplatform, GPC3@TTBC, by conjugating an osteosarcoma-targeting anti-GPC3 peptide onto aggregation-induced emission (AIE) nanoparticles. GPC3@TTBC enables selective tumor accumulation and high-contrast near-infrared fluorescence imaging, allowing precise tumor margin delineation and superior tumor-to-background resolution compared with clinically used dyes, including effective visualization in patient-derived xenograft models. Upon MW irradiation, lysosome-localized GPC3@TTBC generates robust nonthermal reactive oxygen species (ROS) through enhanced charge separation and electron transfer, resulting in substantial tumor cell apoptosis while simultaneously inducing a prominent immunogenic senescence-associated phenotype and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) response. Importantly, MW + GPC3@TTBC suppressed tumor cell migration and invasion in vitro and reduced pulmonary metastatic lesions in vivo. Meanwhile, the SASP promoted dendritic cell maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocyte activation, thereby enhancing antitumor immune responses and remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment. Beyond tumor eradication, GPC3@TTBC facilitates osteogenic microenvironment reconstruction and bone regeneration after tumor clearance, while exhibiting favorable biosafety. Collectively, GPC3@TTBC integrates targeted fluorescence-guided imaging, MW-enhanced ROS generation, immunogenic senescence induction, and bone regeneration, providing a comprehensive theranostic strategy for precise osteosarcoma treatment.

works.title: Hypoxia‐Guided Magnetic Catheter for Localization and Minimally Invasive Intervention in Early‐Stage Lung Cancer
works.abstract: To enable the precise localization and minimally invasive treatment of early-stage pulmonary lesions, we developed a magnetic catheter system integrating magnetic navigation, hypoxia fluorescence imaging, and multifunctional minimally invasive intervention. The distal end of the system incorporates multiple permanent magnets, a miniature camera equipped with an optical filter, multiple fiber-optic channels, and a flexibly switchable multifunctional working channel. Under a 40 mT magnetic field applied perpendicular to the initial catheter axis, the catheter incorporating 2.0 mm-diameter magnets achieved a bending angle of 39.63° ± 2.47° and successfully navigated to multiple designated branches in the bronchial phantom. A proof-of-concept model was established using A549 lung cancer spheroids labeled with hypoxia-responsive fluorescent probes, enabling fluorescence-guided localization of simulated hypoxic lesions. In the bronchial phantom, the system successfully identified simulated hypoxic lesions and subsequently performed biopsy sampling, simulated drug delivery, and localized laser irradiation. The system was further evaluated in porcine lungs to demonstrate its navigation and localized intervention capabilities. This magnetic catheter system provides a new technological strategy for the precise localization and in situ treatment of early-stage lung cancer.

works.title: Dual-function hollow CoP/Ni 2 P polyhedra for electrocatalytic NO-to-ammonia conversion and rechargeable Zn-NO batteries
works.abstract: Abstract The electrocatalytic reduction of nitric oxide (NO) to ammonia (NH3) offers a sustainable, low-temperature alternative to the energy and carbon-intensive Haber-Bosch process, simultaneously facilitating green NH3 synthesis and environmental remediation under ambient conditions. This study reports the development of a metal-organic framework (MOF)-derived, hierarchically engineered hollow polyhedral CoP/Ni2P bimetallic phosphide catalyst with high activity toward the nitric oxide reduction reaction (NORR) in both neutral and acidic media. Importantly, the catalytic activity is significantly improved in acidic conditions with an NH3 yield of 68.28 μmol∙cm-2∙h-1 and Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 65.4% at −1.05 V vs reversible hydrogen electrode (vs. RHE). The acid-enhanced performance highlights the important role of proton concentration in the NO hydrogenation steps. In addition, the CoP/Ni2P-based gas diffusion cathode in a Zn-NO battery system serves as a concentration-universal energy conversion platform that achieves high open circuit potentials of 1.56 V (neutral) and 2.00 V (acidic) with peak power densities of 2.39 mW∙cm-2 and 3.34 mW∙cm-2, respectively. Through density functional theory calculations, it is revealed that the built-in electric field-induced optimization of the d-band center at the CoP/Ni2P heterogeneous interface is determined by charge rearrangement towards Fermi level alignment. The width and shape of the d-band are correlated with the position of its center, which in turn tunes the adsorption free energies of key reaction intermediates. This study demonstrates the viability of integrating environmental pollutant remediation with sustainable ammonia production and concurrent power generation within a unified electrochemical cell and establishes MOF-derived bimetallic phosphides as a novel class of efficient NORR electrocatalysts.

works.title: Revealing the Atomic‐Scale Structure of the Copper–Sulfuric Acid Interface
works.abstract: Corrosion originates from atomistic reactions occurring at dynamic solid-liquid interfaces; however, direct experimental observation of these reactions has remained elusive due to the inability to preserve transient interfacial states during characterization. To refine corrosion models, advanced techniques capable of analyzing corrosion interfaces at the atomic scale are essential. Recent advancements in cryogenic-atom probe tomography (cryo-APT) enabled 3D nanoscale analysis of frozen liquid-metal interfaces. However, challenges remain in sample preparation for cryo-APT on metals undergoing corrosion. This study introduces a microcorrosion cell fabricated using localized electrodeposition in liquid (LEL), enabling atomic-scale capture of liquid-metal reactions by integrating picoliter-scale electrolytes encapsulated within sealed metallic microvessels, subsequently analyzed using cryo-APT. This approach enables 3D, nanoscale mapping of corrosion reactions with simultaneous spatial, chemical, and temporal resolution. As a model system, copper exposed to aerated dilute sulphuric acid reveals temperature- and time-dependent interfacial evolution, including nanoscale clustering of copper-sulphate species, enhanced ion pairing at elevated temperature, and the emergence of transient carbon-based interfacial complexes inaccessible to conventional characterization methods. Beyond copper corrosion, the presented microcorrosion cell architecture establishes a strategy for interrogating confined electrochemical and degradation processes across a wide range of material-liquid systems, using a combination of microfabrication and cryo-APT.

works.title: Controllable Template Assisted In Situ Perovskite Growth for Display Application
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide perovskites are compelling emitters for next‐generation optoelectronics, yet their translation into flexible display architectures remains limited by interfacial optical losses, non‐radiative recombination, and poor operational durability. Here we report a one‐step, template‐assisted in situ crystallization strategy that integrates CsPbX 3 (X = Cl, Br, I) directly within a porous polyethylene terephthalate (PET) membrane. A bifunctional diamine ligand molecularly bridges the perovskite and polymer, directing crystallization, promoting uniform pore filling and eliminating interfacial air gaps. This chemically defined interface suppresses non‐radiative losses, increases light outcoupling from ∼13% to 36%, and yields a film‐state photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 62%. The resulting perovskite‐integrated porous PET membrane retains ∼82% of its initial photoluminescence after 150 days under ambient conditions and exhibits a projected T 50 of ∼10 000 h, establishing benchmark stability among in situ synthesized perovskite/polymer display‐class systems. It further preserves >90% emission under repeated bending and enables inkjet‐printed full‐color RGB pixel arrays with 70% NTSC gamut. Using a highly porous PET membrane (0.5 µm pore diameter), a luminance of 1050 nits are achieved, confirming that brightness scales with pore density and is substrate limited. These results establish active encapsulation as a practical route to stable, efficient and mechanically compliant perovskite display platforms.

works.title: Phase Engineering of MoS 2 for High‐Performance Anion Exchange Membrane Water and Glucose Electrolyzer
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Water electrolysis for green hydrogen production is hindered by the high energy consumption of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Replacing OER with the glucose oxidation reaction (GOR) using a phase‐engineered MoS 2 ‐based electrocatalyst offers a promising route to lower the overall cell voltage while simultaneously valorizing biomass. Herein, Fe and P co‐doping induces a 2H‐to‐1T phase transition in MoS 2 , generating abundant sulfur vacancies and metallic conductivity. At high glucose coverage, electron transfer shifts from Fe to Mo sites, enabling selective GOR over OER. The Fe, P‐MoS 2 catalyst delivers ultralow overpotentials of 98 mV for HER and 260 mV for OER, along with a low operating voltage of 1.30 V (vs. RHE) for GOR at 10 mA cm −2 . In a full anion‐exchange membrane glucose electrolyzer (AEMGE), the Fe, P‐MoS 2 ||Fe, P‐MoS 2 configuration achieves cell voltages of 1.74 and 2.00 V at 0.5 and 1.0 A cm −2 , respectively, substantially lower than the corresponding water electrolyzer (2.16 and 2.56 V), with excellent stability over 50 h. DFT calculations reveal that Fe/P co‐doping synergistically enhances charge carrier mobility and optimizes adsorption energies for glucose activation and intermediate conversion. This work highlights efficient hydrogen production alongside biomass upgrading with reduced energy consumption.

works.title: Interfacial Oxygen Vacancies as Electron Trapping Centers and Kinetic Mediators of Interfacial Charge Transfer in Bi2O3/BiOBr Heterojunctions: In Situ Spectroscopic Evidence and Enhanced Photocatalysis
works.abstract: Abstract The controversial charge transfer mechanism in Bi2O3/BiOBr heterojunctions and the lack of direct in situ evidence for the role of interfacial oxygen vacancies remain critical challenges. An in situ HBr acid etching strategy was employed to construct Bi2O3/BiOBr heterostructures, in which BiOBr nanosheets grew vertically on the porous Bi2O3 nanocubes. This topological transformation generated abundant interfacial oxygen vacancies through the synergistic effects of the lattice mismatch and the nanoscale Kirkendall effect. Band structure analysis, in situ XPS, and EPR spectroscopy provided direct evidence that interfacial oxygen vacancies serve as electron-trapping centers. Under illumination, the photogenerated electrons from both Bi2O3 and BiOBr migrate to and accumulate at the interfacial oxygen vacancy sites, as directly evidenced by the reversible redshifts of Bi 4f, O 1s, and Br 3d peaks and the decreased intensity of the defect-related O 1s component. The trapped electrons reduce adsorbed O2 to •O2−, which is the dominant active species for both Cr(VI) reduction and tetracycline degradation. The optimized heterojunction (S3) exhibited a Cr (VI) (100 mg/L) reduction rate constant of 0.179 min−1 (8.5 times that of pure Bi2O3) and completely degraded tetracycline (TC, 50 mg/L) within 20 min. Free-radical trapping experiments revealed a distinctive kinetic fingerprint: hole scavengers significantly inhibited Cr(VI) reduction but barely affected TC degradation, which is consistent with the electron-trapping mechanism where holes are not the dominant active species for TC degradation. This work provides direct in situ spectroscopic evidence that interfacial oxygen vacancies act as electron traps and kinetic mediators of interfacial charge transfer, establishing a defect-engineering foundation for the rational design of high-efficiency heterojunction photocatalysts.

works.title: Shape Memory PVA-Tannic Acid/CuO Nanocomposites for Microneedle Patches with Antibiofouling and Antioxidant Properties
works.abstract: Abstract Shape memory materials capable of responding near physiological temperature are highly desirable for minimally invasive biomedical applications. However, achieving simultaneous mechanical robustness and biological functionality remains challenging. In this study, we developed a multifunctional CuO nanomaterial-reinforced poly(vinyl alcohol)-tannic acid (PVA-TA/CuO) nanocomposite as a temperature-responsive shape memory platform. PVA-functionalized CuO nanostructures with an average diameter of 200− 300 nm and lengths ranging from 0.5 to 1 μm were reinforced into a PVA-TA matrix through dynamic hydrogen bonding and Cu2+-polyphenol coordination interactions. The resulting composite exhibited improved structural stability, an enhanced tensile strength of 9.31 MPa, and a superior thermal stability compared with the PVA-TA composite. Notably, PVA-TA/CuO showed a rapid shape recovery at 40 °C, with dynamic mechanical analysis revealing a temperature-dependent relaxation transition at approximately 38 °C, supporting its near-physiological-temperature shape recovery. The PVA-TA/CuO composite also demonstrated significant antioxidant activity, excellent cytocompatibility, and pronounced antibiofouling behavior, achieving up to 83% and 75% biofilm inhibition against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, respectively. Furthermore, PVA-TA/CuO was successfully fabricated into a mechanically robust microneedle patch with sufficient insertion capability. Overall, our results highlight that nanoscale CuO reinforcement is an effective strategy for engineering mechanically robust, temperature-responsive shape memory materials with multifunctional properties for advanced biomedical applications.

works.title: Energy-Transducing Scintillating Nanoparticles for Combined Proton Beam Therapy and Photodynamic Therapy
works.abstract: Abstract Deep-seated tumors in complex anatomical regions pose significant challenges for conventional photodynamic therapy (PDT) due to limited light penetration. While proton beam therapy (PBT) offers superior spatial precision via the Bragg peak, its biological effectiveness is comparable to X-ray therapy, necessitating potent radiosensitizers to overcome radioresistant tumors. Herein, we report the design of NaLuF4:Ce,Tb@NaYF4 scintillating nanoparticles (ScNPs) as a robust platform for an integrated PBT-PDT. By leveraging the high-atomic-number element lutetium (Lu), these ScNPs facilitate enhanced radiation deposition and serve as efficient energy transducers with multimodal responsiveness to ultraviolet (UV), X-ray, and clinical proton beams. Upon proton irradiation, the ScNPs exhibit proton-induced luminescence to activate the photosensitizer Rose Bengal (RB), enabling deep-tissue reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and bypassing the penetration constraints of external light sources. Furthermore, the persistent luminescence lifetime is flexibly tailored by modulating the Ce3+ doping concentration, ensuring controllable therapeutic action. In vitro and in vivo studies confirm that this synergistic approach significantly intensifies tumor DNA double-strand breaks and triggers a robust apoptotic cascade, far surpassing the efficacy of PBT or PDT monotherapies. This study marks the novel development of proton-beam-induced luminescent ScNPs for combined PBT-PDT, establishing a high-precision methodological framework that optimizes spatiotemporal control for next-generation oncological interventions.

works.title: Recent Advances in Layered Double Hydroxides and Their Derivatives for Electrochemical CO2 Reduction Reaction
works.abstract: Abstract The rising global energy demand and continued overuse of fossil fuels have significantly increased CO2 emissions, leading to severe environmental pollution. As a result, we urgently need sustainable alternatives to fossil fuels. The electrocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) has gained considerable attention for its ability to transform CO2 into value-added carbon-based products. However, the CO2RR is kinetically slow, so developing highly efficient electrocatalytic materials is essential to improve performance. Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) have emerged as promising CO2RR electrocatalysts because of their layered structure, tunable composition, interlayer anion-exchangeability, abundant active sites, high surface area, and adjustable microscale morphologies. This review presents the reaction mechanisms and pathways by which CO2RR transforms into carbon-containing materials. It categorizes LDHs used as electrocatalysts, including transition metal-based LDHs (Ni, Cu, and Zn), other non-transition metal-based LDHs, and LDH-derived other materials, and summarizes their major carbonaceous products, electrochemical onset potential, Faradaic efficiency, and current density. The review aims to provide insights into strategies for enhancing the electrocatalytic performance of LDHs and their derivatives. Finally, this study discusses current challenges, recent developments, and prospective directions for the rational design of LDH-based catalysts for effective CO2RR.

works.title: Construction of a Thermoresponsive and Controllably Shrinkable Dual-Network Hydrogel Incorporating Copper-Doped Prussian Blue Nanozymes with In Vitro Antibacterial and Antioxidant Activities
works.abstract: Abstract Infection-associated wounds are typically characterized by elevated bacterial burden, oxidative stress imbalance, and highly heterogeneous microenvironments, whereas conventional hydrogels remain limited in achieving rapid in situ gelation, stimuli-responsive deformation, and on-demand release of functional components. To address these challenges, this work presents a thermoresponsive, controllably shrinkable, copper-doped Prussian blue nanozyme-based dual-network hydrogel (SGCP@CuPB). In situ polymerized PNIPAM constitutes a thermosensitive covalent first network that enables rapid initial gelation and heat-triggered shrinkage, while an SA/GDL/CaCO3-based ionically crosslinked second network is subsequently established to progressively consolidate the network architecture and reinforce mechanical strength. Embedded CuPB nanozymes confer near-infrared (NIR) photothermal conversion, multi-enzyme-mimicking activity, and reactive oxygen species (ROS)-regulating capability. SGCP@CuPB-1 gels within 2 min, and its gelation time can be tuned from 2 to 10 min by adjusting the APS/TEMED dosage. Upon 808 nm NIR irradiation, SGCP@CuPB-1 undergoes controllable shrinkage, thereby promoting the outward migration and responsive release of CuPB. Cu doping modulates the local electronic environment of PB, enhancing its NIR absorption, photothermal conversion, and catalytic activity, which enables SGCP@CuPB to achieve a photothermal conversion efficiency of 37.0% while exhibiting SOD-like, CAT-like, and POD-like multi-enzyme-mimicking activities along with enhanced ROS-scavenging capacity. Upon NIR irradiation, SGCP@CuPB achieves antibacterial rates of 96.3%, 92.5%, and 86.8% against Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, respectively. Collectively, SGCP@CuPB integrates sequential dual-network construction, thermoresponsive and NIR-enhanced shrinkage, NIR-enhanced CuPB release, ROS regulation, and in vitro antibacterial function, providing a responsive hydrogel design for infection-associated wound microenvironments.

works.title: Lignocellulose Nanofibers-Induced In-Situ Self-Assembly of Copper Nanoclusters for pH-Adaptive Fluorescent Composite Films Integrating UV Shielding with Humidity-Responsive and Preservation Functions
works.abstract: Abstract Lignocellulose nanofibers (LCNFs) possess unique interfacial properties, yet their ability to direct the ordered assembly of metal nanoclusters remains underexplored. Inspired by biological reinforcement, this study proposes an in-situ self-assembly strategy for copper nanoclusters (CuNCs) induced by LCNFs. Through Cu2+ coordination cross-linking, polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)-LCNFs hydrogen bonding, and glutathione ionizable groups, the high-performance composite film was constructed. It exhibits a tensile strength of 15.04 MPa (1.8 times that of the pure LCNFs films) and an approximately six-fold enhancement in fluorescence emission intensity (from 2.1% to 12.4%) relative to the pure LCNFs films. It achieves UV shielding (blocking >99% for UV-B/C) and humidity-responsive conductivity (398 μS/m at 90% RH). Its fluorescence is pH-adaptive, reversibly switching from orange-yellow to deep blue. Strawberry tests confirmed freshness retention after 48 h of UV irradiation. By fusing these multifunctional properties, this work provides design insights for sustainable, durable polymer materials with enhanced resistance to photo-oxidative degradation.

works.title: Correction to “Engineered Metallic MoWS2 Nanodots for Photoacoustic Imaging-Guided Photothermal Cancer Theranostics”
Site-Directed Functionalization of MXene/GO with Cysteine for Dual-Metal Ion Detection: A Plug-and-Play Paper Electrodes
works.abstract: Abstract Mercury and cadmium contamination pose serious environmental and public-health risks, requiring rapid and selective detection at trace levels. In this work, a site-directed functionalization strategy is developed using a cysteine-modified MXene-graphene oxide composite (MX-GO-C) for dual metal-ion sensing. The intrinsic chemical asymmetry of cysteine enables controlled orientation of active sites: coordination of the amine (−NH) group with MXene leaves the thiol (−SH) group available for selective Hg2+ binding, while anchoring through the thiol group on graphene oxide exposes the amine site for Cd2+ recognition. This deliberate molecular arrangement allows metal-specific interactions within a single sensing platform. The successful functionalization and selective metal binding were confirmed by FT-IR, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM). Electrochemical studies using cyclic voltammetry (CV) and differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) reveal excellent sensitivity and selectivity toward Hg2+ and Cd2+, with well-resolved oxidation signals. For practical applicability, a plug-and-play paper-based microfluidic analytical device (μPAD) was fabricated using the MX-GO-C composite, enabling rapid, low-cost, and portable on-site detection. Both glassy carbon electrode and μPAD platforms achieve nanomolar-level detection limits, highlighting the robustness and versatility of the sensing system for environmental monitoring applications.

works.title: Rapid Synthesis of Fibrous Phosphorus for Ammonia Sensing at Room Temperature
works.abstract: Abstract Ammonia (NH3) is a representative reducing toxic gas whose rapid, low-concentration detection is important in constant-temperature, constant-humidity environments such as semiconductor cleanrooms, yet existing NH3 sensors often suffer from high operating temperatures or slow response/recovery kinetics. Fibrous phosphorus (FP), a layered allotrope of elemental phosphorus with a parallel tubular structure, is an appealing sensing candidate, but its efficient preparation and gas-sensing potential remain underexplored. Here, we report an iodine-assisted chemical vapor transport method that enables gram-scale synthesis of FP within 5 h with a yield exceeding 99%, without the need for precise temperature-gradient control. The key is the iodine-mediated cleavage of P4 cages and the directed assembly of active phosphorus fragments into tubular FP. Taking advantage of the weak interlayer van der Waals interactions, high-quality FP nanoribbons (FP-NRs) with an average width of ∼50 nm, an average length of ∼6 μm, and aspect ratios exceeding 150 for ∼60% of the ribbons are obtained by 60 min of ice-bath exfoliation. The FP-NRs sensor exhibits a high response of 826% toward 100 ppm NH3 at room temperature, with response/recovery times of 31/7 s under the 90% criterion, and remains responsive at 2 ppm NH3 (response 69.8%). When all tested gases are compared at the same concentration, the response to NH3 is significantly higher than that to the interfering gases. Combined DFT calculations and in situ FTIR/Raman measurements reveal that NH3 adsorption on FP is dominated by physical adsorption (adsorption energy −0.26 eV; Bader charge transfer ∼0.02 e), which accounts for the high sensitivity, selectivity, and fast recovery. This work provides a scalable route to FP nanoribbons and demonstrates their potential for practical room-temperature NH3 sensing.

works.title: M1 Macrophage-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Enable Efficient Cytosolic Delivery of siRNA to Suppress Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma
works.abstract: Abstract Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) remains a clinically challenging malignancy with limited targeted therapies. We previously reported Sugen kinase 495 (Sgk495) overexpression in LUSC and its pro-tumorigenic functions. However, efficient cytosolic delivery of Sgk495 siRNA to LUSC cells remains a major obstacle. Here, we engineered biomimetic nanoscale extracellular vesicles (EVs, ∼130 nm) derived from M1-polarized macrophages and loaded them with Sgk495 siRNA (M1 EV/siSgk495) as a targeted nanomedicine for LUSC therapy. Compared with M0 EVs and conventional liposomal nanocarriers, M1 EVs exhibited superior siRNA stability. Mechanistically, M1 EV/siSgk495 downregulated Sgk495, disrupted its interaction with E3 ligase COP1, reduced K48-linked polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of IFNGR1, and thereby upregulated IFNGR1 protein. Collectively, this M1 macrophage-derived EV nanoplatform inhibits LUSC via IFNGR1 stabilization, representing a promising biomimetic nanotherapeutic strategy for cytosolic RNAi-based treatment of LUSC.

works.title: Orchestrating a metabolic blockade and immune reprogramming in refractory TNBC via calcium-based nanomodulator
Aptamer-functionalized exosomal delivery of species-matched Anti-PD-1 antibodies modulates the tumor immune microenvironment during cirrhosis-to-HCC malignant transformation
works.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) often arises from hepatic cirrhosis, yet interventions that block this malignant transition are lacking. This study developed an aptamer-functionalized exosomal nanoplatform carrying an anti-PD-1 antibody to enable targeted immunomodulation. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of HCC specimens revealed reduced CD8 + T cell infiltration alongside elevated PD-1 expression in CD8 + T cells. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic profiling highlighted suppression of CD8 + T cell-related proteins, upregulation of proteasome 20 S subunit alpha 1 (PSMA1), and enrichment of altered metabolites within lipid metabolic pathways, indicating immune-metabolic dysregulation during cirrhosis-to-HCC progression. The engineered exosomal platform was evaluated in a 3D co-culture system containing HCC cells, cirrhotic hepatocytes, and CD8 + T cells, where it enhanced T cell-associated cytotoxic readouts and reduced fibrosis-related changes. In a mouse model of cirrhosis-associated malignant transformation, the platform showed preferential lesion-associated fluorescence, improved measured liver injury and lesion-burden endpoints, and enhanced CD8 + T cell effector readouts. These findings support exosome/aptamer-assisted anti-PD-1 delivery as a preclinical strategy for immune modulation during cirrhosis-associated malignant transformation, while further validation in human immune-cell systems or humanized models remains necessary.

works.title: A Biomimetic Microneedle Platform Using Neutrophil Membrane for Synergistic Antibacterial Therapy of MRSA Infection
works.abstract: Persistent bacterial infection has become life-threatening challenge worldwide. Bacterial biofilm formation, causing induced antimicrobial resistance and suppressive immune microenvironment, is one of the critical pathways leading chronic and persistent infection. Herein, an integrated microneedle patch harboring neutrophil membrane and antibiotics is designed to elicit therapeutic in-situ immunization for the management of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection. When applied on the infected skin, microneedles can physically penetrate the biofilm barrier, helping the diffusion of antibiotics to kill the bacteria deep in the biofilm. After breaking the integrated structure of biofilm, neutrophil membrane tightly binds to the bacterial debris to enhance the phagocytosis of antigen-presenting cells followed by the robust activation of T helper cells. Naïve B cells then differentiate to plasma cells or memory B cells to produce specific antibodies, thereby efficiently managing infection and preventing relapse. Overall, our study highlights the capability of eliciting therapeutic in-situ immunization mediated by the integrated biomimetic microneedle, providing an attractive perspective for the treatment of persistent bacterial infection.

works.title: Nanobody‐Modified Outer Membrane Vesicles Attenuate Alzheimer's Disease‐Like Neurodegeneration by Modulating Mitophagy‐Associated Phenotypes and cGAS‐STING‐Related Inflammatory Signaling
works.abstract: This study examined anti-transferrin receptor (TfR) nanobody-functionalized bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) as an engineered platform for improving Alzheimer's disease (AD)-like neuronal injury. Escherichia coli-derived OMVs were characterized for morphology, size distribution, surface charge, protein features, nanobody loading, residual endotoxin levels, endotoxin-associated inflammatory responses, and repeated-exposure immune-safety readouts, and were evaluated in neuronal-related cells and APP/PS1 mice. Engineered OMVs showed receptor-associated uptake and preferential brain-delivery signals, increased HT-22 cell viability, reduced apoptosis, and elevated mitophagy-associated markers including LC3-II, PINK1, and Parkin. OMV treatment also reduced cytosolic mtDNA abundance, DNA/cGAS colocalization, phosphorylation of STING/TBK1/IRF3, and inflammatory-marker expression. PINK1 or Parkin knockdown partially weakened OMV-associated mitochondrial and inflammatory readouts, whereas pharmacological autophagy modulation supported a contribution of autophagy-related processes without establishing selective PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy in vivo. In APP/PS1 mice, OMV administration improved Morris water maze and rotarod performance and alleviated neuroinflammatory and histological injury-related changes. Overall, anti-TfR nanobody-modified OMVs were associated with enhanced receptor-related delivery, mitophagy-linked phenotypes, reduced cytosolic mtDNA/cGAS-STING-related inflammatory signaling, and improved AD-like outcomes, supporting further delivery-system optimization and mechanistic validation.

works.title: Biocompatible Conjugated Electrospinning Nanofibrous Membrane With Self‐Powered Piezoelectric Capacity for Accelerated Wound Healing
works.abstract: Extensive research has demonstrated that electrical stimulation (ES) accelerates wound healing by promoting cellular proliferation and migration. However, the delivery of continuous and noninvasive ES to the wound site remains a major challenge. Conventional ES devices generally depend on external power supplies and often suffer from limited biocompatibility. To address these limitations, we developed an innovative wound healing strategy that integrates ES with biocompatible materials. Specifically, a self-powered nanofibrous membrane (PGPM) was fabricated via conjugated electrospinning by combining the piezoelectric polymer poly(vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene) (PVDF-TrFE) and MXene with polycaprolactone (PCL) and gelatin, two polymers with excellent biocompatibility. The resulting PGPM has inherent piezoelectric properties allowing the generation of localized electrical signals in response to mechanical stimuli, for example, skin tension, compression or ultrasound. These electrical signals significantly promote the growth and migration of wound healing-related cells, as well as the deposition of type I/III collagen fibers, α-SMA expression, and VEGF production in vivo. Together, such an approach has offered a self-powered and biocompatible platform on which wound healing can be accelerated using endogenous ES.

works.title: Small‐Pore Chitosan Microcarriers Support Surface‐Adherent Growth of Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell–Derived Neural Stem Cells and Improve Intranasal Therapy of Murine Anosmia
works.abstract: Intranasal delivery of neural stem cells offers a non-invasive strategy for central nervous system repair, yet its efficacy is limited by rapid mucociliary clearance and poor cellular retention. Although chitosan-based carriers have been explored, the architectural principles governing neural stem cell behavior in the intranasal microenvironment remain poorly defined. We compared chitosan microcarriers (CSMs) with three pore architectures (mean surface pore sizes 4.7 ± 1.7, 15.9 ± 3.2, and 20.5 ± 0.7 µm), fabricated via freezing-controlled phase separation, using induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neural stem cells (iPSC-NSCs). Cellular responses did not vary linearly with pore size: the smallest-pore formulation, CSM-196, supported surface-adhesion-dominant growth, whereas both larger-pore formulations supported infiltration-dominant growth. CSM-196 was also associated with increased proliferative activity, spontaneous neuronal differentiation, and elevated neurotrophic factor secretion without exogenous induction factors. In a methimazole-induced anosmia model, the CSM-196-iPSC-NSC formulation produced greater improvements in olfactory behavioral recovery, olfactory epithelial thickness, neuronal marker expression, and epithelial proliferation than cell-only delivery administered by the same route and schedule. This chitosan-based platform provides a surface-adhesion-oriented cell-delivery strategy that warrants further evaluation for intranasal neural regenerative therapy.

works.title: Modulation of the electronic structure of a single-atom Ni catalyst for sensitive and simultaneous detection of dopamine and hydroquinone
works.abstract: Abstract Simultaneous electrochemical detection of dopamine (DA) and hydroquinone (HQ) is clinically significant but challenging because overlapping redox signals obscure detection on conventional sensing materials. Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer promising adsorption and electron-transfer capabilities; however, limited synthetic control, poor cycling durability, and inevitable signal interference in complex multi-analyte matrices hamper their application. Herein, we report a nickel single-atom catalyst embedded in nitrogen-doped carbon (Ni SA/NC) with a unique electronic structure that enables simultaneous detection of DA and HQ. Benefiting from the unique Ni–N4 moieties, the oxidation peaks for DA and HQ are well resolved, enabling simultaneous quantification. Notably, the Ni SA/NC achieves ultra-low detection limits (0.0018 μM for DA and 0.0017 μM for HQ), wide segmented linear response windows, and high anti-interference selectivity toward typical coexisting contaminants. Additionally, the Ni SA/NC exhibits outstanding measurement reproducibility, as evidenced by ultra-low relative standard deviations, alongside favorable storage stability. DFT calculations reveal that the Ni–N4 configuration modulates the Ni d-band center to afford moderate *OH adsorption strength, thereby lowering the electro-oxidation barriers. Overall, this work establishes a rational design paradigm for SAC-based electrochemical sensing materials, offering potential for practical implementations in early disease diagnosis.

works.title: Ligand-programmed interfacial nucleation enables uniform ferrite-gold core-shell nanostructures
works.abstract: Abstract Precise control of heterogeneous nucleation at inorganic interfaces is essential for constructing uniform multicomponent nanostructures but remains challenging because nucleation is highly sensitive to local surface chemistry. Here, we demonstrate a ligand-programmed interfacial nucleation strategy for controlling ferrite-gold growth through regulation of surface citrate coverage. Using gold magnetic nanoparticles (GMNPs) composed of Fe3O4 and Au as a model system, we show that surface-bound citrate modulates gold precursor adsorption and the heterogeneous nucleation landscape, enabling interlayer-free aqueous synthesis of highly uniform nanostructures with tunable sizes. Notably, citrate transforms iterative gold deposition from a heterogeneity-amplifying process into a self-homogenizing process by suppressing secondary nucleation and excessive growth of pre-existing particles while promoting utilization of residual ferrite nanoparticles. Surface citrate quantification and density functional theory calculations reveal that increasing citrate coverage strengthens interfacial Au-O electronic coupling, charge redistribution, and gold precursor adsorption, providing a molecular basis for the observed growth behavior. The strategy is further validated in Co0.5Fe2.5O4@Au and Mn0.5Fe2.5O4@Au systems. The resulting GMNPs enable a 10-fold sensitivity enhancement over conventional AuNPs-based lateral flow immunoassays following magnetic enrichment. These findings establish surface ligand coverage as a molecular parameter for programming heterogeneous growth at ferrite-gold interfaces.

works.title: Scalable p-type Te 1-x Se x thin-film transistors and low-power complementary logic gates
works.abstract: Abstract Despite the promise of Te as a p-type channel material, realizing Te-based thin-film transistors (TFTs) with low off-state current and high on/off ratio is challenging due to its small bandgap and high background carrier density. Se-alloying offers a potential solution to mitigate these limitations, yet the device performance has remained suboptimal. In this work, through the synergy of stoichiometric control and thickness engineering, we achieve an optimal trade-off between charge transport and switching characteristics in Te1-xSex TFTs.
