The resulting devices exhibit an average field-effect mobility of 16.8 cm2 V-1 s-1, Ion/Ioff ratio of 1.3×105 and an ultralow off-state current of 10 pA μm-1. The fabrication process is fully compatible with established low-temperature TFT technologies, enabling high-yield production of transistor arrays with favorable electrical uniformity. Notably, the devices demonstrate exceptional environmental stability, retaining critical performance metrics after six months of storage without encapsulation. Complementary logic gates (NOT, NAND, and NOR) are fabricated by integrating p-Te0.63Se0.37 and n-IGZO TFTs. The inverter achieves a high voltage gain of 28, a noise margin of 92.3%, and a low static power consumption of 420 pW at 3 V supply voltage. This study highlights the potential of Te1-xSex as a scalable p-type channel material, advancing the development of TFT-based logic circuits.

works.title: Bias Polarity Switching (BiPS): A Transient Method for Probing Interfacial Carrier Dynamics
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfaces and contacts critically influence the performance and stability of semiconductor devices, yet direct experimental access to charge accumulation and release processes near biased interfaces remains limited. Here, we introduce the Bias Polarity Switching (BiPS) technique as a transient method for probing carrier dynamics in the sub‐/micrometer‐scale near‐interface region under realistic operating conditions. We show that BiPS enables distinction between free‐ and trapped‐carrier contributions to the transient response, allowing extraction of carrier mobility, characteristic trapping and detrapping times, and an effective interfacial extraction rate. Applied to representative single‐crystal semiconductor systems with different contact configurations, including melt‐grown CsPbBr 3 (Cr/Cr) and solution‐grown MAPbBr 3 (Cr, SnO 2 /Cr), BiPS reveals interfacial barriers that drive carrier accumulation and defect filling. CsPbBr 3 exhibits long‐lived space charge densities in the order of ∼3 × 10 11 cm −3 . Analysis of the BiPS transients yields trapping times of 1–100 µs, detrapping times of 20 µs–3 ms, and activation energies of 280–450 meV for interfacial defect states. Finally, a proof‐of‐feasibility experiment on CdZnTe demonstrates the feasibility of extending BiPS beyond perovskite materials.

works.title: Potential‐Regulated Phosphate Intercalation in Defective Nickel Hydroxyphosphate for Efficient Oxygen Evolution
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling the transformation and structural incorporation of phosphorus‐containing species is critical for regulating the structure and catalytic performance of nickel‐based oxygen‐evolution catalysts, yet how catalyst‐growth conditions direct phosphorus species evolution and structural incorporation remains unclear. Herein, a potential‐directed in‐situ electrodeposition strategy is developed to regulate the evolution and incorporation behavior of phosphorus‐containing species, enabling the construction of phosphate‐intercalated nickel hydroxyphosphate on nickel foam (NF). Using hypophosphite as the phosphorus precursor, the deposition potential guides phosphorus‐containing species toward either Ni–P formation or phosphate intercalation into the α ‐Ni(OH) 2 framework through modulation of the local interfacial environment. The resulting phosphate‐intercalated nickel hydroxyphosphate (Ni 2 (PO 4 )(OH)/NF) preserves the hydroxide framework while inducing lattice expansion, local structural distortion, defect‐rich transport channels, and P–O–Ni coordination interactions. These structural and electronic features facilitate the formation and stabilization of high‐valence Ni oxyhydroxide active species during oxygen evolution. As a result, Ni 2 (PO 4 )(OH)/NF delivers an overpotential of 197 mV at 10 mA cm −2 in 1 M KOH and sustains stable electrolysis for over 1200 h. This work establishes a potential‐regulated strategy for coupling interfacial alkalization with phosphorus species transformation and phosphate intercalation, providing mechanistic guidance for constructing oxyanion‐intercalated electrocatalysts for efficient oxygen evolution.

works.title: Construction of Near‐Infrared Organic Long‐Afterglow Materials via Efficient Cascaded Förster Resonance Energy Transfer
works.abstract: energy level promote nonradiative decay. Constructing efficient organic room temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials that emit near-infrared afterglow remains challenging. Thus, we doped (9-phenyl-carbazol-2-yl)-boric acid into the polyvinyl alcohol to obtain a phosphorescence film with excellent photophysical performance. Then this film was used as the donor for resonance energy transfer and the near-infrared dye Nile Blue was selected as the energy acceptor. To address the lack of spectral overlap between the donor emission and the acceptor absorption, fluorescein and rhodamine B were introduced as mediators, thereby constructing a four-component co-doped cascade resonance energy transfer system. Through highly efficient cascade triplet-singlet and singlet-singlet Förster resonance energy transfer, this film achieved a near-infrared ultra-long afterglow emission at 695 nm and a lifetime of 562 ms. Remarkably, the total cascade energy transfer efficiency reached 66.01% and the total photoluminescence quantum yield was 28.72%. Furthermore, based on the multicolor and time-dependent performance of this luminescent material, a six-layer anti-counterfeiting and encryption system was designed. Finally, the extended experimental results demonstrated the promising prospects for achieving near-infrared luminescence in cascaded systems.

works.title: Hydrogels in Airway Devices and Tracheal Repair: Clinical Requirements, Patient‐Specific Manufacturing, and Translational Testing
works.abstract: Airway stents can rapidly restore ventilation in central airway obstruction, but complications after placement remain common. Migration, mucus retention, infection, granulation, fracture, and difficult removal often reflect a mismatch between the device and the airway environment. This review examines how hydrogels may contribute to airway devices and tracheal repair, with emphasis on clinically relevant design and testing criteria. Hydrogels provide a water-rich interface and allow control of mechanics, degradation, and local delivery. Softness alone, however, cannot maintain airway patency. A useful hydrogel-enabled device must keep the lumen open during breathing and coughing without excessive wall pressure, while also preserving mucus transport. The review covers hydrogel classes and manufacturing routes relevant to patient-specific devices. 4D shape programming is considered an early concept rather than a proven airway-stent strategy. Direct evidence for intraluminal stents still comes mainly from printed degradable elastomers, whereas most hydrogel studies concern tracheal repair or surface biology. Rabbit studies are informative but remain limited by small cohorts and short follow-up. A structural frame with a hydrogel surface therefore appears to be the most realistic near-term route. Translation will require testing of the final sterilized device under cyclic loading and airway-like conditions.

works.title: Regulating Interfacial Potential Fields and Molecular Solubility via Amide‐Linked Graphene‐Quinone Heterostructures for Ultrastable and Fast‐Kinetic Supercapacitors
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Tetraamino‐p‐benzoquinone (TABQ) is a highly promising supercapacitor electrode due to its high theoretical capacity, yet its practical application is severely hindered by significant solubility in electrolytes and sluggish charge transfer kinetics. Herein, an interfacial potential field engineering strategy is developed to overcome these bottlenecks by constructing amide‐linked graphene‐quinone heterostructures. Through the covalent anchoring of TABQ onto graphene via amide linkages (–CO–NH–), the dissolution in the electrolyte of TABQ is effectively suppressed, ensuring cycling durability. Simultaneously, the integration of a highly conductive graphene network combined with the optimized interfacial potential field significantly boosts the overall electrical conductivity and accelerates interfacial H + transport kinetics. Experimental results and theoretical analysis demonstrate that this synergistic modulation endows TABQ with an impressive specific capacity of 367 F g −1 at 1 A g −1 and a capacity retention of 93.2% after ultra‐long 50 000 cycles at 30 A g −1 . Impressively, the assembled asymmetric supercapacitor delivers a high energy density of 24.22 Wh kg −1 at a power density of 700 W kg −1 and retention of 92.1% after 50 000 cycles. This work provides a molecular‐level paradigm for designing high‐performance organic electrodes by concurrently regulating solubility and interfacial electronics for advanced aqueous energy storage.

works.title: Freeform Nanopatterning of Hydrogel Surfaces
works.abstract: Hydrogels are a promising material for biomedical applications due to their tunable properties and biocompatibility. The ability to structure hydrogel surfaces with high precision leads to greater control over interactions at the hydrogel interface, which in turn impacts many applications, such as implant integration, drug delivery, and cancer modeling. However, freeform patterning of hydrogel surfaces at the nanometer scale and the characterization of their topography with atomic force microscopy have not yet been achieved. Here, we demonstrate a reliable process for nanopatterning hydrogel surfaces by combining thermal scanning-probe lithography and replica molding to create grayscale surface topographies with features as small as 138 nm on the hydrogel interface. During our fabrication process, the hydrogels are dehydrated, introducing shrinkage of the original patterns. We explore hydrogel shrinkage as a route for pattern miniaturization and investigate the shrinkage behavior. We determine a lateral shrinkage factor between 1.4 and 2.2, and a vertical shrinkage factor between 2.5 and 37.0, and demonstrate that the shrinkage can be varied by changing the water-to-monomer ratio in the hydrogel precursor. Furthermore, we show that the shrunken, dehydrated hydrogel patterns can be exploited as templates for metal deposition.

works.title: Ternary DES Electrolyte Integrates High‐Value Utilization of Spent Zn‐Mn Batteries for Opening up ZnO‐Based Wide Temperature Zn‐Ion Batteries
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Unlocking the recycling and application of spent zinc‐manganese dry batteries (SZMBs) can effectively unleash the potential of urban resources. A zinc‑ion electrolyte strategy is proposed herein, which directly employs recycled ZnO from SZMBs within a ternary deep eutectic solvent (DES) of choline chloride (ChCl), urea, and ethylene glycol (EG). Regulating EG amount renders the ZnO‐based electrolyte suitable for a wide temperature range. Spectroscopic and dynamics simulations reveal that EG weakens the energy barrier for Zn 2+ reduction, achieving reversible Zn 2+ /Zn 0 redox. Simultaneously, the DES adsorbed on the Zn anode induces a solid electrolyte interphase film for guiding preferential zinc deposition along the Zn(100) plane. The ZnO‐based electrolyte enables the Zn||Zn symmetric cell to operate steadily for over 4100 h at 25°C, over 200 h at 60°C, and over 1400 h at –10°C. The Zn||PANI full cell delivers a specific capacity of 220 mA h g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 and maintains a capacity retention of 93.98% after 175 cycles at 0.5 A g −1 . This integrated design concept not only provides a practical value‐added approach for the utilization of zinc from SZMBs, but also offers a feasible strategy for the development of new high‐performance, wide‐temperature zinc‐ion battery electrolytes.

works.title: Unveiling the Failure Mechanisms of High‐Voltage 18650‐Type O3‐Layered Oxide//Hard Carbon Sodium‐Ion Full Cells
works.abstract: ABSTRACT High‐voltage O3‐type layered oxide//hard carbon full cells offer a promising route toward high‐energy‐density sodium‐ion batteries, yet their high‐voltage degradation mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Here, Ah‐level 18650 cylindrical full cells were cycled under different cut‐off voltages to elucidate the underlying failure mechanisms through non‐destructive and post‐mortem analyses. Increasing the cut‐off voltage from 4.05 to 4.20 V raises the energy density from 117.5 to 144.0 Wh kg −1 , but accelerates degradation, with direct‐current internal resistance growth increasing from 181% to 387% and capacity retention after 300 cycles decreasing from 96.4% to 68.3%. Impedance analysis reveals that charge‐transfer resistance gradually becomes dominant during high‐voltage cycling. Post‐mortem analysis reveals cathode interphase thickening and heterogeneous inorganic‐rich interphase growth, accompanied by an organic‐rich anode interphase, and increased accumulation of sodium‐containing deposits. Aging‐model decoupling demonstrates that capacity fading is primarily governed by active‐material loss and electrode capacity mismatch rather than sodium inventory loss. Notably, eliminating the constant‐voltage step in the 4.15‐CC protocol shortens the high‐voltage dwell time, reduces the resistance growth from 369% to 153%, and improves capacity retention from 85.0% to 93.9%. These findings provide full‐cell insight into high‐voltage degradation and highlight charging‐protocol optimization as an effective strategy to balance high energy density and long cycle life.

HSA-coated intrinsically radiolabeled [177Lu]Lu₂O₃ nanoparticles for injectable nanoscale brachytherapy: Preclinical validation and first-in-human imaging
Physiochemical and biological evaluation of curcumin-derived carbon dots conjugated with chenodeoxycholic acid in streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice
Interplays Between Therapeutic Radiopharmaceuticals and Tumor Microenvironment
works.abstract: Radiopharmaceuticals have progressed from diagnostic agents toward theranostic. With the accelerating development of therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals, radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) is being increasingly implemented in clinical practice in oncology. However, current therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals often contribute to tumor stabilization rather than complete remission. A major determinant of this limited clinical response is the tumor microenvironment (TME), which critically influences the delivery, penetration, and retention of radiopharmaceuticals. Meanwhile, the radiopharmaceuticals can modulate multiple components of the TME, thereby contributing to antitumor effects. These interactions provide opportunities for advancing radiopharmaceuticals to enhance RPT efficacy. In this review, the bidirectional relationship between therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals and TME in solid malignancies is comprehensively discussed. First, common therapeutic strategies that modulate TME are outlined. The impact of the TME on radiopharmaceutical efficacies and how radiopharmaceuticals reshape the TME are then highlighted. In addition to elucidating the bidirectional interplay between RPT and the TME, we examine two fundamental clinical barriers that constrain RPT efficacy: dosimetric limitations and systemic immune collateral damage. Finally, critical challenges and potential strategies to enhance next-generation therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals in solid malignancies are inspected.

works.title: Biodegradable Monometallic Manganese Nanoparticles for Multimodal Tumor Therapy
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Synergistic therapeutic nanoplatforms are of considerable interest in tumor therapy, but their translational potential is often limited by complex multicomponent designs and unknown in vivo degradation behavior. Herein, we show a degradable, single‐component manganese nanoparticles (Mn NPs) using liquid‐phase exfoliation of commercial bulk manganese powder for cancer therapy. In the acidic tumor environment, Mn NPs react with H + to generate Mn 2+ and H 2 and raise the local pH. The released Mn 2+ drives Fenton‐like reactions to produce ROS, while H 2 causes mitochondrial damage, which together lead to tumor cell death. In addition, Mn 2+ activates cGAS‐STING signaling and initiates antitumor immunity. Moreover, Mn NPs inhibit tumor growth in CT26, 4T1, and B16F10 mouse models and show better effects than Mn 2+ alone. Transcriptomic analysis further reveals activation of multiple immune‐related signaling pathways following Mn NP treatment. In a bilateral tumor model, unilateral injection of Mn NPs triggers a systemic antitumor immune response, leading to effective inhibition of distant, untreated tumor growth. Collectively, this study identifies Mn NPs as a simple, biodegradable, single‐component nanoplatform that offers a promising new route for multimodal tumor therapy.

works.title: Rutin‐Coated Ultrasmall Gadolinium Oxide Nanoparticles with High T1 Relaxivity for MRI of Blood Vessels and Glucose Transporter‐Overexpressing Malignant Tumors
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The straightforward one‐step wet‐chemical approach represents a promising strategy for the preparation of ultrasmall gadolinium oxide nanoparticles (GdONs) featuring high T 1 relaxivity and excellent aqueous dispersion stability. However, achieving specificity for conventional GdONs still requires multi‐step modifications with targeting molecules, introducing uncertainty into their application prospects. Herein, rutin (Ru)‐coated ultrasmall GdONs (Gd@Ru) possessing both high T 1 relaxivity and glucose transporter (GLUT)‐overexpressing tumor‐targeted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) capability were successfully prepared via a one‐step wet‐chemical method. Among all the as‐prepared Gd@Ru, Gd@Ru‐5 with the lowest Gd content (∼3.8 wt% Gd, as determined by EDS) exhibits the smallest crystalline size (∼ 1.8 nm) and hydrodynamic diameter (∼ 4.0 nm), achieving the highest T 1 relaxivity (40.4 mM − 1 s − 1 at 1.5 T) along with exceptional stability. Moreover, Gd@Ru‐5 showed satisfactory biosafety and excellent magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) performance in SD rats and New Zealand rabbits, as well as effective targeted imaging of GLUT‐overexpressing 4T1 breast tumors. Overall, we present a facile one‐step wet‐chemical strategy for fabricating ultrasmall GdONs that integrate high T 1 relaxivity, excellent MRA performance, and tumor‐targeted MRI capability.

works.title: Stiff Extracellular Matrix Rejuvenates Aged Mesenchymal Stem Cells via PI3K‐AKT Signaling
works.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are widely used to modulate immune responses and promote tissue regeneration, but cellular senescence significantly impairs their therapeutic potential. MSCs undergo senescence characterized by an enlarged morphology, reduced proliferative capacity, and altered expression of genes related to the cytoskeleton. This study revealed that the mechanical microenvironment critically regulates MSC aging. Culturing senescent MSCs on high-stiffness extracellular matrix (ECM) hydrogels reverses key aspects of the senescent phenotype, including the restoration of normal morphology, improved cytoskeletal integrity, and enhanced proliferation. This mechanical rescue is accompanied by genetic reprogramming and activation of the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway. The inhibition of PI3K-Akt with LY294002 abolished these rejuvenating effects. These findings demonstrate that the mechanical microenvironment can reprogram senescent MSCs through PI3K-AKT-mediated mechanotransduction, offering a novel strategy to restore stem cell function in aging and regenerative medicine.

works.title: Microfluidic Nano‐Assembly of Red‐Blood‐Cell (RBC) Lipids and Components for Engineering Extracellular Vesicles (Adv. Healthcare Mater. 41/2026)
works.abstract: Red Blood Cell Lipids The cover illustrates the microfluidic production of engineered red blood cell extracellular vesicle (eRBCEVs) from RBC lipids. The central vesicle encapsulates adeno-associated virus (AAV), highlighting efficient viral loading and immune-evasive delivery. The fluorescent cellular background represents successful eGFP-AAV9 transduction of HEK293T cells despite the presence of neutralizing AAV9 antibodies. More details can be found in the Research Article by Eduardo Reátegui, and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adhm.202504351).

works.title: A Non‐Cryogenic Dugout‐Structured Microneedle Patch for Co‐Delivery of Irisin and Fibroblasts in Diabetic Wound Repair (Adv. Healthcare Mater. 41/2026)
works.abstract: Cell-Delivery Microneedles A dugout-structured microneedle patch carries live fibroblasts together with irisin. A portable vacuum pump draws the cell-laden alginate into three internal microchannels within minutes, so no freezing or cryoprotectants are needed. Pressed onto a diabetic wound, the patch releases both payloads beneath the surface, lowering TNF-α, raising fibronectin and TGF-β1, and closing wounds faster than topical treatment. More details can be found in the Research Article by Shu-Hung Huang, Hung-Wei Yang, and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adhm.71598).

works.title: Issue Information: Adv. Healthcare Mater. 41/2026
Salt-regulated interfacial desolvation suppresses Co-intercalation of strongly coordinating ether-based electrolytes for fast-charging lithium-ion batteries
works.abstract: Abstract Ether-based electrolytes are highly attractive for fast-charging lithium-ion batteries due to their low viscosity and rapid Li+ transport kinetics, yet their practical application with graphite anodes is severely hampered by solvent co-intercalation. Herein, we propose a salt-regulated ether electrolyte with a conventional concentration of 1 M, employing lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate (LiDFOB) as the sole lithium salt in a 1,2-dimethoxyethane/fluoroethylene carbonate (DME/FEC, 95/5, v/v) solvent mixture to simultaneously regulate the Li+ solvation structure and interfacial chemistry. Theoretical calculations and experimental characterizations demonstrate that DFOB− competitively coordinates Li+, thereby reducing the contribution of DME to the primary solvation sheath. Meanwhile, early interfacial reactions of LiDFOB facilitate the formation of a compact B-containing solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on graphite, which progressively enriches in LiF during lithiation and thus suppresses solvent co-intercalation. Electrolyte-exchange experiments further verify that the preformed SEI retains its protective capability even in co-intercalation-prone electrolytes. The designed electrolyte exhibits a high ionic conductivity of 10.37 mS cm−1 and superior interfacial stability. Graphite half-cells deliver a reversible capacity of approximately 325 mAh g−1 at 5 C, while high-loading Gr||NCM811 full cells retain 80.2% of their stabilized capacity after 300 cycles at 4 C with a 4.4 V upper cutoff. This work offers new mechanistic insights into solvent co-intercalation and establishes a practical salt-regulation strategy for long-life fast-charging lithium-ion batteries.

works.title: Interfacial Electronic Coupling and Surface Reconstruction in Co(OH) 2 @NiFe‐btz for Durable Alkaline Oxygen Evolution
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Coupling metal hydroxides with coordination frameworks offers a route to active and durable oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrodes. A binder‐free Co(OH) 2 @NiFe‐btz heterostructure, where btz is 1,4‐bis(4H‐1,2,4‐triazol‐4‐yl)benzene, is constructed on nickel foam through solvothermal growth followed by electrodeposition. Microscopy reveals close contact between Co(OH) 2 nanosheets and the framework. Ultraviolet and x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicate interfacial charge redistribution consistent with the work‐function difference, while electron paramagnetic resonance detects paramagnetic states. In 1.0 M KOH, the electrode delivers 10 mA cm −2 at an overpotential of 219 mV, exhibits a Tafel slope of 57.1 mV dec −1 , and operates at 100 mA cm −2 for 1000 h. Operando Raman spectroscopy reveals potential‐dependent formation of a cobalt/nickel oxyhydroxide‐like surface phase. Isotope‐labeling mass spectrometry and infrared spectroscopy of the target electrode, considered alongside electrochemical probes, are consistent with possible lattice‐oxygen participation, without establishing its fraction of the oxygen‐evolution flux. Density functional theory calculations on idealized precursor structures show that interfacial coupling and an imposed oxygen vacancy modify metal d and O 2p states and reduce the largest uphill free‐energy step in a candidate lattice‐oxygen pathway. Together, these results connect framework‐hydroxide coupling with enhanced electrode performance and the evolution of its catalytic surface.

works.title: Ambient Pressure Drying of Aerogels for Structure Preservation and Multifunctional Applications
works.abstract: Ambient-pressure drying (APD) is attractive for scalable aerogel manufacturing because it avoids the pressure vessels used in supercritical drying and the low-temperature vacuum equipment required for freeze-drying. Its principal limitation is the liquid-gas meniscus generated during evaporation, which couples solvent surface tension, wetting, pore size, drying rate, and skeleton strength to shrinkage and cracking. This review establishes a process-structure-property framework for APD-derived aerogels. After defining the scope of APD and distinguishing it from the broader category of subcritical drying, we quantitatively analyze capillary pressure using the Young-Laplace relationship and discuss the absence of a universal critical contact angle or pore size. Physical, chemical, and hybrid crosslinking are compared in terms of synergistic reinforcement and possible competition caused by densification, brittleness, or blocked mass transport. The structural outcomes of APD are benchmarked against supercritical and freeze-drying, with emphasis on density, porosity, specific surface area, shrinkage, and mechanical integrity. Application sections then connect pore architecture and interfacial chemistry to thermal insulation, adsorption, energy storage, electromagnetic shielding, acoustics, and biomedical functions. Finally, environmental fate, solvent safety, reporting standards, and continuous manufacturing are identified as priorities for translating APD aerogels from laboratory demonstrations to reproducible products.

works.title: Issue Information

works.abstract: Front Cover The ultrafast laser synthesis technique, using femtosecond laser pulses, enhances zeolite synthesis by providing high-precision control over energy delivery and reaction kinetics. This technique accelerates synthesis of high-quality zeolite crystals with enhanced functionality. In article number e70929, Sezin Galioglu and co-workers investigate LTA zeolites with multiple aspects, including structural properties, crystal formation zone, defect generation, and CO2 adsorption behaviour.

In article number e70929, Sezin Galioglu and co-workers investigate LTA zeolites with multiple aspects, including structural properties, crystal formation zone, defect generation, and CO2 adsorption behaviour.

works.title: Scalable Room‐Temperature Terahertz Graphene Cameras (Small Methods 21/2026)
works.abstract: Inside Front Cover Graphene-based terahertz cameras enable scalable, room-temperature, non-destructive imaging. Using photo-thermoelectric detection, broadband antennas, tunable responsivity, and optimized readout circuitry, they achieve nanowatt-scale sensitivity, responsivity up to 36 V/W, and high pixel uniformity, reducing calibration complexity for large-format arrays. More in article number e70657, Miriam S. Vitiello and co-workers.

works.title: How We Simulate Nanopores (Small Methods 21/2026)
works.abstract: Back Cover Despite the dramatic transformation of nanopore sensing from a what-if research to a platform for big omics sequencing, the method remains subject to interpretative limitations. All-atom simulations have become the preferred method for relating the chemical structure of the biomolecules to their nanopore signals. In article number e70904, Aleksei Aksimentiev and co-workers review the latest computational approaches for accurate modelling of nanopore sensing outcomes.

works.title: Targeting oxidative stress-senescence crosstalk via mitochondrial homeostasis remodeling using metal-polyphenol antioxidants for osteoarthritis relief
Periodic table-guided design of metal-based theranostics for precision oncology
Matrix-confined Zn/Cu bimetallic MOFs couple bacterial adhesion resistance with osteoimmunomodulation for infected bone regeneration
Transformable peptide-drug conjugate nanoparticle for bladder cancer therapy
works.abstract: Bladder cancer (BC) remains a significant health concern, necessitating the development of innovative therapeutic approaches. Herein, a novel strategy is developed utilizing BC cell surface receptor-mediated, transformable peptide nanoparticles, where the prodrug leucine-doxorubicin (Leu-DOX) and the PLZ4 ligand are linked by a β-sheet-forming peptide sequence, KLVFF, to enhance drug delivery efficacy while minimizing toxicity. These transformable peptides self-assemble into nanoparticles with high specificity for BC tissues through the specific recognition of αvβ3 integrin via PLZ4. Upon binding to αvβ3 integrin, the nanoparticles undergo a transformation process facilitated by ligand-receptor interaction, forming nanofibrils on the cancer cell surface, followed by gradual uptake by the cancer cells. In response to matrix metallopeptidase 9 (MMP-9) overexpressed in the tumor microenvironment, the conjugate is cleaved to release the Leu-DOX prodrug, which is subsequently converted into active doxorubicin inside the tumor cells, leading to effective tumor cell elimination. These findings suggest substantial implications for the development of targeted therapies for BC.

works.title: A Metal‐Free Nitroxide Radical Nanoliposome for MRI‐Guided Therapy of Ulcerative Colitis
works.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) remains challenging to diagnose and treat because of the limited sensitivity of current imaging techniques, the safety concerns associated with metal-based magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast agents, and the insufficient efficacy of conventional anti-inflammatory therapies. Here, we report a metal-free theranostic nanoliposome (A@Clip) that integrates nitroxide radical-containing phospholipids (TEMPO-lipids) and 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) into a biocompatible liposomal platform for MRI-guided therapy of UC. The liposomal architecture enhances the T1 MRI performance of TEMPO radicals while enabling efficient reactive oxygen species scavenging and anti-inflammatory drug delivery. A@Clip exhibits excellent biocompatibility, promotes cellular uptake, and effectively suppresses oxidative stress and inflammatory responses in vitro. In a murine colitis model, A@Clip enables sensitive visualization of inflamed colon tissue and markedly alleviates disease progression, intestinal injury, inflammatory responses, and gut microbiota dysbiosis without detectable systemic toxicity. This work establishes a metal-free nanotheranostic strategy for integrating non-invasive MRI with anti-inflammatory therapy and provides a versatile platform for the precision management of inflammatory diseases.

works.title: Engineered tumor-derived blebs as integrated antigen repositories for enhanced CD4+ and CD8+ T cell immunity
Conjugated covalent organic frameworks with covalently integrated sulfur as cathodes for lithium–sulfur batteries
pH-responsive HA/chitosan nanoplatform delivering deer antler polypeptide to induce DNA damage and checkpoint imbalance for TNBC therapy
works.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) lacks effective targeted therapeutic options and often relies on stress-adaptation pathways for survival. Deer antler peptides (DAP) is a complex mixture of peptides and proteins with potential bioactivity, but its therapeutic application is limited by delivery inefficiency. In this study, we characterized DAP, investigated its antitumor effects in TNBC, and developed a pH-responsive hyaluronic acid/chitosan nanodelivery system (CS-HA-DAP) to improve its biological performance. Proteomic analysis identified 79 proteins and 122 peptides in DAP; DAP consisted mainly of low- to medium-molecular-weight proteins and peptides and dose-dependently inhibited the viability of 4T1 cells, with half-maximal inhibitory concentrations of 1.62 mg/mL, and also impaired migration and invasion of 4T1 cells, with relatively lower toxicity toward normal MCF-10 A cells. Transcriptomic and molecular analyses showed that DAP induced persistent DNA damage-associated stress, time-dependent γ-H2AX accumulation, incomplete sustained CHK1 activation, and dysregulation of cell-cycle regulators, together with pyroptosis- and ferroptosis-related changes, which were rescuable by Fer-1 and VX-765. CETSA showed that GDQGPVGR physically bound TOP2A and CHK1, and docking together with inhibitor-combination assays supported the involvement of TOP2A- and CHK1-related processes; furthermore, DAP exhibited synergy with etoposide and MK-8776. To improve delivery, we constructed CS-HA-DAP nanoparticles by coupling DAP to hyaluronic acid via EDC and NHS conjugation followed by ionic gelation with chitosan and tripolyphosphate. The optimized nanoparticles, which showed spherical morphology and measured 158.2 nm with a zeta potential of +28.7 mV, achieved a high encapsulation efficiency of 89.2% and a drug loading capacity of 57.2%. They also showed marked pH-responsive release, with substantially higher cumulative release at pH 5.0 than at pH 7.4, reaching 89.18% at pH 5.0 versus 23.43% at pH 7.4 over 48 h. CS-HA-DAP enhanced the inhibitory effects of free DAP on 4T1 cell viability, migration, and invasion while maintaining relatively low toxicity toward MCF-10 A cells. In orthotopic 4T1 tumor-bearing mice, orally administered CS-HA-DAP showed tumor-associated fluorescence signals in tumors, suppressed tumor growth more effectively than free DAP, achieving a tumor growth inhibition (TGI) rate of 85.74% versus 53.57%, and exhibited acceptable preliminary biosafety. DAP is a bioactive peptide mixture with antitumor activity associated with sustained genomic stress and checkpoint imbalance in TNBC, and CS-HA-DAP represents an effective nanodelivery strategy that enhances its therapeutic efficacy, with improved tumor accumulation and acceptable preliminary safety. This work provides a nanobiotechnology-based approach for improving the antitumor potential of complex natural peptide mixtures and offers a promising lead for further translational development.

works.title: Correction: Attenuation of osteoarthritis progression via locoregional delivery of Klotho-expressing plasmid DNA and Tanshinon IIA through a stem cell-homing hydrogel
Core–shell structural calcium-deposited manganese-copper oxide that induces immunogenic cell death and STING activation for augmented metalloimmunotherapy of triple-negative breast cancer
works.abstract: Metal ions mediated tumor immunotherapy showed considerable potential in clinical application, but the efficacy of single metal ion elicited immune response was relatively low. Herein, we developed a PDGFB cyclopeptide modified core–shell structural calcium-deposited manganese-copper oxide (CMC) for enhanced metalloimmunotherapy of triple-negative breast cancer. Due to the overexpression of PDGFR-β receptors, PCMC selectively recognised 4T1 cells, efficiently entering the tumor cells and triggering the release of substantial amounts of Cu, Mn, and Ca ions. These Cu ions catalysed Fenton-like reactions, rapidly increasing intracellular ROS levels, thereby inducing cuproptosis in tumor cells and promoting calreticulin exposure and HMGB1 release with confirmed ICD. Additionally, Mn ions activated the cGAS-STING signalling pathway, enhancing dendritic cell (DC) maturation, promoting cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) infiltration, and boosting the anti-tumor immune response. Ca ions disrupted intracellular calcium homeostasis, synergistically enhancing ROS production and potentiating cGAS-STING activation, further amplifying the anti-tumor immunotherapy. In vitro and organoid assays confirmed that PCMC-mediated ROS production effectively induced tumor cuproptosis and calreticulin exposure and HMGB1 release. In vivo, PCMC markedly promoted DC maturation, increased CTL infiltration, and facilitated NK cell recruitment, leading to significant inhibition of tumor growth, recurrence, and metastasis. This study presents a novel and practical strategy for developing polymetallic-based anti-tumor immunotherapies.

works.title: Correction: Delivery of an ERK inhibitor using bioactive lipid nanoparticles reduces angiogenesis and prevents oral squamous cell carcinoma development
Current Advances in Biomaterials for Glioblastoma Immunotherapy
works.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) constitutes the most prevalent malignant neoplasm within the central nervous system, representing 12%–15% of intracranial malignant neoplasms. GBM is characterized by molecular heterogeneity and therapeutic resistance, which significantly impair survival prognosis of patients. The current standard treatment regimen involves surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy. Nevertheless, the invasive growth pattern of GBM renders current therapeutic approaches only capable of achieving alleviation of local symptoms and tumor volume reduction, thus impeding the complete eradication of malignant cells and curative efficacy. Biomaterial-enhanced immunotherapy has shown promise as a therapeutic approach owing to its notable therapeutic response rate and favorable safety profile. This therapy effectively impedes tumor progression by precisely modulating the cellular and molecular network of the tumor microenvironment (TME). This review examines the potential mechanisms involved in GBM therapy, with a specific focus on biomaterial-enhanced tumor immunity. Moreover, the review also summarizes immune cell phenotype reprogramming, reversed remodeling of the TME, and the efficacy of synergistic immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) to elicit endogenous antitumor immune responses. Consequently, this in-depth elucidation of synergistic mechanisms between biomaterials and immunotherapy will provide a scientific foundation for the development of a novel generation of immunotherapy regimens for patients with GBM.

works.title: Magnetoactive Hydrogels to Probe Curvature‐Directed Endothelial Cell Mechanosensing
works.abstract: The vascular system exhibits complex, nonplanar geometries that become further distorted during pathological remodeling, including arterial tortuosity and aneurysms. Although hemodynamic shear stress is a well-established regulator of vascular function, the direct effects of curvature as an intrinsic geometric cue remain poorly defined. This is largely because existing in vitro models are static and fail to capture the dynamic changes that accompany disease progression. To address this gap, we used a magnetoactive hydrogel platform that enables real-time, on-demand curvature of endothelial monolayers to reproduce clinically established tortuosity metrics. Using this system, we found that elevated curvature increased nuclear localization of Yes-associated protein (YAP), with the strongest response in convex relative to concave regions of highly tortuous endothelial monolayers. This mechanosensitive response was accompanied by reduced VE-Cadherin junctional thickness and increased membrane localization of endothelial nitric oxide synthase. These findings identify local curvature, independent of shear stress, as a regulator of endothelial cell mechanosensing and function, and establish a dynamic hydrogel platform for isolating geometric regulation from shear stress inputs in vascular mechanobiology.

works.title: TiCoCr‐Based Multi‐Principal Element Alloys for Biomedical Applications
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Next‐generation biomedical implants require materials with excellent wear resistance, corrosion resistance, and biocompatibility. This study developed two novel multi‐principal element alloys (MPEAs) based on the TiCoCr composition (equiatomic and non‐equiatomic) with ultra‐high hardness, excellent wear resistance, corrosion stability, and biocompatibility. The as‐cast microstructures revealed a multiphase combination of Ti‐rich hexagonal closed packing (HCP), C 14 Laves, and face‐centered cubic (FCC) phases. Upon heat treatment, equiatomic (Ti 33 Co 33 Cr 33 ) MPEA developed two major body‐centered (BCC) phases and a minor HCP phase, whereas heat treatment of non‐equiatomic (Ti 50 Co 25 Cr 25 ) MPEA revealed one BCC and C 14 Laves phase. The hardness of both MPEAs was slightly reduced after heat treatment. Wear and corrosion tests conducted in Hanks' balanced salt solution (HBSS) at 37°C on heat‐treated MPEAs demonstrated improved tribological and corrosion behavior, with reduced wear and a lower coefficient of friction (COF). Electrochemical analysis indicated superior corrosion resistance, particularly for Ti 33 Co 33 Cr 33 MPEA. With respect to biocompatibility, both MPEAs demonstrated excellent cell adhesion and proliferation properties. Cell viability improved significantly, increasing from the control (100%) to ∼105% and 115% after 3 and 5 days, respectively. The combined results highlight the strong potential of these MPEAs for biomedical applications, offering a unique balance of high “density‐normalized” hardness, excellent corrosion resistance, and biological compatibility for future implant solutions.

works.title: Measuring Blood Plasma Glutamine Levels Using a Nanopore‐Based Sensor
works.abstract: Measuring blood glutamine (GLN) levels is valuable for managing urea cycle disorders. Currently, patients visit the hospital to have their GLN levels checked using analytical techniques that, despite being highly accurate and reliable, lead to long waiting times and delay clinical decisions. A point-of-care device would enable patients to monitor GLN levels at home, allowing for greater control over the condition. Here, we made use of a highly sensitive GLN biosensor system based on dodecameric Cytolysin A variant AS (ClyA-AS) nanopore coupled with the GLN-specific protein, the substrate-binding domain 2 (SBD2). Measurements are performed on a single ClyA-AS nanopore embedded into an artificial lipid bilayer, where the application of a small voltage generates ionic currents that report on the binding and unbinding of GLN (added in the trans side of ClyA-AS) to SBD2 (added in cis). We demonstrate that the ClyA-AS and SBD2 biosensor pair can quantify GLN levels in patients' blood plasma. To facilitate the use of this sensor in clinical and point-of-care settings, we also developed a dedicated algorithm that accelerates signal processing and data analysis. Together, these advances represent a significant step toward a point-of-care device for GLN monitoring, both at the hospital and home-care levels.

works.title: Mesoporous Silica Nanoplatforms: From Controllable Synthesis to Versatile Biomedical Applications
works.abstract: The increasing global burden of severe diseases, such as cancers, cardiovascular and neurodegenerative disorders, highlights the urgent need for advanced diagnostic and therapeutic agents. Although techniques like computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography (PET), and chemotherapy show promise, their effectiveness is frequently constrained by the inherent drawbacks of conventional agents, such as poor solubility, low stability, and lack of targeting ability, as well as physiological barriers like the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which limit bioavailability and induce systemic toxicity. Mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) have emerged as promising platforms to overcome these challenges, offering high surface area, tunable pore size, and facile surface functionalization for efficient cargo loading. Therefore, in this work, the recent advances in the synthesis, structural control, and functional design of MSNs-based composites are systematically reviewed, with a focus on their biomedical applications in diagnosis (e.g., fluorescence imaging (FLI)/MRI/PET), therapy (e.g., chemo-, dynamic, thermal, and gas therapy), and tissue engineering. Key strategies for performance optimization and structure-property relationships are discussed in depth. Finally, we delineate prevailing challenges and future directions for the clinical translation of MSNs-based nanomaterials, providing an integrated perspective to guide their rational design and biomedical implementation.

works.title: Ni-induced interfacial engineering enables recycled aluminum hydride for high-efficiency electrochemical hydrogen storage
works.abstract: Abstract Aluminum-based hydrides are attractive hydrogen carriers because of high gravimetric hydrogen capacity and relatively moderate working temperature. However, poor reversibility significantly increases the difficulty of application of aluminum hydride materials. Electrochemical hydrogen storage represents an attractive alternative for hydride synthesis and recycling which would be integrated with green electricity. In this work, a Ni-induced interfacial activation strategy has been explored by coupling Al derived from spent AlH3 with carbonyl Ni to construct an Al*/Ni composite anode for electrochemical aluminum-hydride synthesis in a LiAlH4/THF system. The optimized Al*/Ni=7:3 anode delivers a high current density of 0.123 A cm−2, which is 2.7 times that of pristine Al*, and retains 80% of its initial current after 3 h of electrolysis, compared with 31% for the Al* anode. The AlH3 formation rate reaches 5.56 mmol h-1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 77.62%, representing a 2.84-fold increase in formation rate compared with the Al* anode. The results of XPS analysis and DFT calculations are consistent with Ni-induced interfacial electronic redistribution and the formation of a polarized Al*/Ni interfacial environment, which lowers the calculated AlH4- activation barrier and stabilizes the AlH3*+H* final state, thereby promoting Al-H conversion and suppressing anode passivation. This work systematically introduces Ni-induced interfacial electronic modulation as an effective strategy for the electrochemical synthesis of aluminum-based hydrides using Al derived from spent AlH3, providing a pathway toward a closed-loop aluminum-based hydride hydrogen-storage system.

works.title: One-dimensional proton conductor catalyst layers for high-performance proton exchange membrane fuel cells
works.abstract: Abstract The practical performance of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) is critically hampered by the disordered distribution of ionomers within the catalyst layer, which causes severe sulfonate‑induced poisoning of Pt active sites, discontinuous proton conduction, and restricted oxygen transport to catalytic centers. However, addressing these interrelated limitations simultaneously remains a formidable challenge, as most existing strategies tackle only one aspect at the expense of others. In this study, we report a catalyst layer architecture based on a one-dimensional proton conductor (1D Proton Conductor) that addresses the coupled limitations of random ionomer distribution, Pt site poisoning, and inefficient transport in PEMFCs. This design encapsulates ionomers uniformly on carbon nanotubes to create linear and continuous proton pathways, while spatially separating sulfonate groups from Pt surfaces and preserving open pore structures. The 1D Proton Conductor reduces sulfonate coverage on Pt from 31.7% to 14.9%, and decreases proton conduction and oxygen transport resistances by 34% and 40%, respectively. As a result, the mass activity of Pt doubles and the cell achieves a peak power density of 0.73 W cm-2 under 30% relative humidity, twice that of conventional electrodes. This work demonstrates that simultaneous regulation of ionomer distribution, surface chemistry, and transport properties offers a viable route to high-performance PEMFCs, particularly under low-humidity conditions. This study provides a feasible strategy for designing high-performance catalyst layer for PEMFCs.

works.title: Discerning and exploiting two-dimensional polymorphism using nanomechanical resonators
works.abstract: Abstract Various structural phases in two-dimensional (2D) crystal polytypes provide distinct material properties including electronic band structure, conductivity, optical properties, ferromagnetic and ferroelectric properties. However, the impact of phase on mechanical properties remains largely unexplored. Here, we quantitatively resolve the Young’s modulus of MoSe2 polytypes with different structural phases by leveraging the dynamic response of MoSe2 nanomechanical resonators. Through experimentally elucidating resonant behavior of MoSe2 drumheads with varying diameters and thicknesses, and developing theoretical models linking resonance behavior to phase-dependent mechanical properties, we determine the Young’s modulus for 2H (131 ± 10 GPa), 3R (77 ± 8 GPa), and 2H-3R mixed-phase (95 ± 5 GPa) MoSe2. We further show that structural phase can modulate the Young’s modulus by up to ~70%, which is effective for tuning device frequency and nonlinearity. Our findings establish phase as a powerful degree of freedom for tailoring mechanical properties of 2D polytypes and for exploiting polymorphism in designing strain-engineered multifunctional nanoelectromechanical devices.

works.title: Complex Refractive Index Determination Via Microspectroscopy Through Magnifying Optics: Challenges and Opportunities
works.abstract: ABSTRACT For the design and optimization of optoelectronic devices, accurate knowledge of the complex refractive indices of the constituent materials is essential. Herein, we present a fast and nondestructive approach for the extraction of the refractive indices from reflectance and transmittance spectra of samples with lateral dimensions down to the micrometer scale. Microspectroscopy, combining an optical microscope and a spectrometer, enables the assessment of the optical response of multilayer stacks using high‐magnification optics with correspondingly large numerical apertures. Employing a numerical formalism explicitly accounting for the influence of the numerical aperture allows for wavelength‐by‐wavelength retrieval of the refractive index with subsequent refinement by dispersion modeling. We demonstrate the applicability of the proposed method for large‐area, homogeneous, optically incoherent samples such as transparent glasses and absorbing 4H‐SiC, for a thin film on a glass substrate, and for mechanically exfoliated flakes of highly oriented pyrolytic graphite and , as representatives of uniaxial and biaxial optical anisotropy. The proposed approach provides a cost‐effective proof of concept for retrieving optical constants of microscale samples under arbitrary numerical apertures. The case of graphite highlights the limitation for discerning the out‐of‐plane optical constants due to reduced sensitivity. Finally, we discuss paths to probe out‐of‐plane anisotropy.

works.title: Engineering Antigen Density on M13 Bacteriophage for Personalized Nanovaccine
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanovaccines have been engineered to co‐deliver antigens and adjuvants for robust immune responses. While extensive studies have examined the effect of nanovaccine size, shape, surface charge, and targeting on vaccine efficacy, the impact of antigen density remains underexplored. Here, we systematically optimize the anti‐tumor CD8 + T cell response by modulating the antigen density on an M13 phage‐based nanovaccine. By fine‐tuning the antigen ratio from ∼6.0% to ∼70.4% on the phage capsid, the anti‐tumor CD8 + T cell response was enhanced. Further investigation demonstrated that the antigen density affected not only antigen presentation efficacy but also dendritic cell uptake. Applying this strategy to a neoantigen in the MC‐38 colorectal cancer model, we achieved up to a ∼7‐fold increase in the neoantigen‐specific CD8 + T cell frequency, resulting in significant tumor suppression. These findings underscore the critical role of antigen density in nanovaccine design and establish M13 bacteriophage as a universal platform for personalized cancer vaccine applications.

works.title: Peri‐Infarct Cortical Network Remapping During Stroke Recovery via a Soft Liquid Metal Neural Interface
works.abstract: Stroke causes substantial reorganization of neural activity and connectivity in the peri-infarct cortex during functional recovery. Tracking these changes at high resolution, however, remains difficult. Mechanical mismatch of conventional rigid neural probes is exacerbated in the fragile peri-infarct region, destabilizing the tissue-electrode interface and limiting long-term recording. Here, we present a fully soft, liquid metal-based multichannel neural interface that enables stable electrophysiological recording in freely moving mice. Using this platform, we performed longitudinal recordings before and after ischemic stroke, enabling within-animal comparisons. We applied complementary analyses of population-level latent dynamics and functional connectivity, capturing network-level coordination and pairwise interactions. Both analyses revealed acute suppression followed by partial recovery without restoration of the pre-stroke state. Instead, neural networks reorganized into a distinct and reproducible functional configuration. These findings establish soft liquid metal neural interfaces combined with population-level analysis as a useful approach for resolving neural reorganization during stroke recovery.

works.title: Issue Information
works.abstract: Carbon black actively modulates the microenvironment, influences catalyst reconstruction, and optimizes mass transfer, fundamentally transitioning from an inert conductive additive to a versatile functional material in electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction.

works.title: Tailoring pore microenvironments in scalable classic COFs boosts solar H 2 O 2 production and antibiotic remediation
works.abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising for solar-driven chemical synthesis and environmental remediation, yet their practical application is constrained by the trade-off between structural sophistication and synthetic scalability. In this work, we develop a pore microenvironment engineering strategy on classic COF skeletons to boost photocatalytic performance without relying on intricate monomer design. Two isostructural hexagonal COFs (TTA-DMA and TTA-DHA) are synthesized via a facile, cost-effective autoclave solvothermal route using commercially available linkers, achieving gram-scale yield while preserving high crystallinity and uniform pore channels. Combined advanced transient spectroscopies and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that hydroxyl functionalization on pore walls rationally modulates localized electronic states, extending light harvesting, suppressing radiative charge recombination, accelerating charge separation, and lowering the O2 activation energy barrier. The optimized TTA-DHA delivers an exceptional solar H2O2 production rate of 14,562 mmol g−1 h−1 with an apparent quantum yield of 9.1% at 400 nm. The in situ generated H2O2 further drives a concurrent advanced oxidation cascade, achieving 85%-97% degradation of five representative recalcitrant antibiotics within 1 h under visible light. This work bridges scalable material fabrication with efficient solar energy conversion, providing a practical blueprint for functionalizing classic porous frameworks toward multipurpose applications.

works.title: Ternary Ag-Te-S colloidal quantum dots for shortwave infrared photodetectors
works.abstract: Abstract Ecofriendly silver telluride (Ag2Te) colloidal quantum dots (QDs) are promising for shortwave infrared (SWIR) photodetectors. However, the performances of the devices–especially beyond 1.5 μm–remain constrained photoelectric conversion efficiency due to inefficient charge extraction. Here, we develop a ternary Ag-Te-S QDs via sulfur (S) pre-injection strategy. The incorporation of S atoms in Ag2Te crystal lattice suppresses the particle fusion, improves structural uniformity, and prolongs the exciton dynamics. By integrating the ternary Ag-Te-S QDs into SWIR photodiodes, the devices achieve a state-of-the-art external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 26% beyond 1.5 mm under 0 V bias at room temperature. We finally demonstrate SWIR fluorescence imaging by using the Ag-Te-S QD photodiodes. This work establishes a practical polynary alloy design to overcome charge-extraction bottlenecks in colloidal QD photoactive layers for eco-friendly high-performance SWIR photodetection.

works.title: Machine Learning‐Assisted Discovery of Unconventional Molybdenum Nitride Nano‐Facets as Hydrogen Evolution Electrocatalysts
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Transition‐metal nitrides (TMNs) are promising electrocatalysts owing to their unique electronic structures and surface properties. Yet, the formation of metastable phases during particle growth is unavoidable in the traditional synthesis of TMNs. These metastable phases cannot be holistically depicted by conventional phase diagrams. Here, we use density functional theory (DFT) calculations in conjunction with thermodynamic analysis to establish particle‐size‐dependent phase diagrams for Mo nitrides (Mo x N y ), including both metastable and thermodynamically stable phases. To accelerate the identification of energetically favourable high‐Miller‐index facets of Mo nitrides, we complement our DFT approach with a machine learning (ML) model trained on computed results for low‐Miller‐index facets. Furthermore, we compute hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) free energy diagrams using DFT for both low‐ and high‐Miller‐index facets, uncovering that several previously underexplored high‐Miller‐index facets of Mo nitrides are not only stable but also catalytically active for HER. Our study elucidates the correlation between nanoparticle dimension and phase stability, predicts unconventional facets of Mo nitrides that serve as good catalysts in HER, and ultimately presents a computationally guided strategy to efficiently navigate the material discovery landscape and further discover robust and efficient catalysts for green energy conversion schemes.

works.title: Ultra‐Efficient Memristive Voltage‐Resistance Logic Framework With Integrated Readout Strategy Based on Hafnium Zirconium Oxide
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of logic operations and data storage is regarded as a promising strategy for enabling edge computing, a key requirement for real‐time, data‐intensive scientific and industrial applications. Achieving edge‐capable computing, however, requires exceptional spatiotemporal efficiency, and many previously proposed logic schemes still face substantial limitations. Here, we introduce a memristive voltage–resistance (V–R) logic strategy that infers output resistance states without additional incurring area or latency penalties. The approach relies on integrated readout of the discharge behavior into programming of a two‐terminal capacitor‐type memristor. Implemented in an HfO 2 ‐based ferroelectric tunnel junction (FTJ) device with multiple resistive states, this strategy enables a half adder to be computed using a single device in a single step, and a 1‐bit full adder using only three FTJs in three steps—achieving previously unattainable spatiotemporal cost for execution of standard benchmarking tasks. Our work provides a pathway to edge computing by maximizing the spatiotemporal efficiency achievable with memristor‐based logic‐in‐memory.

works.title: Donor Geometry Engineering for Regulating Spatial Charge Distribution in Heptazine‐Based D‐A Porous Organic Polymers Toward Efficient Photocatalysis
works.abstract: Regulating the spatial charge distribution in donor-acceptor (D-A) porous organic polymers (POPs) to suppress charge recombination remains a formidable challenge in the field of photocatalysis. Herein, donor geometry engineering as a design method is proposed to address this issue. Three novel heptazine-based donor-acceptor porous organic polymers (D-A POPs) with varied fusion patterns and connection sites of the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) donors have been constructed. DFT calculations reveal that the linear 2,7-bis(4-aminophenyl)pyrene donor in Py-2,7-Cy confines holes exclusively to the pyrene core and electrons dominantly to the heptazine acceptor, minimizing the wavefunction overlap, whereas hole delocalization to peripheral phenyl rings in Phe-2,7-Cy and Py-1,6-Cy leads to more significant overlap. Such geometry-dependent spatial separation of the photogenerated carriers in Py-2,7-Cy directly translates into a reduced exciton binding energy, suppressed charge recombination, and extended exciton lifetimes. Consequently, Py-2,7-Cy achieves 95% conversion of methyl phenyl sulfide dramatically outperforming Phe-2,7-Cy (12%) and Py-1,6-Cy (25%) under the same conditions, and exhibits excellent recyclability and broad substrate scope. This work establishes that donor geometry engineering is a powerful method to tune the charge dynamics in D-A POPs.

works.title: Precise Sputter Control by Tailored Waveform Biasing for Selective Ablation in Future 2D Electronics Manufacturing
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control of ion energy in plasma processes is pivotal for the selective, damage‐free etching that future two‐dimensional (2D) electronics demand. Conventional equipment technology with RF sinusoidal waveform biasing is unable to generate the monoenergetic ion energy distribution function (IEDF) required for the selective sputtering of materials that exhibit only marginal differences in threshold ion energy for sputtering. Applying a low‐frequency tailored pulse‐wave‐shaped bias voltage waveform to the substrate electrode of a commercial 200 mm inductively coupled plasma (ICP) plasma reactor results in an IEDF with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of just 10 eV even at higher ion energies. These narrow IEDFs are used within this study to determine the sputtering thresholds of molybdenum disulfide () and selected dielectrics: , , and , with the aim of enabling the efficient selective physical etching of dielectric materials relative to 2D materials, and vice versa. Armed with this knowledge, the dielectric environment and layer structure can be designed specifically to the application at hand, ensuring the highest possible selectivity in the patterning process. Additionally, a tailored waveform bias allows layers of varying quality to be plasma cleaned below the sputtering threshold energy.

works.title: Mixed-sized TiO₂ particles are more potent than mono-sized counterparts in promoting colitis-associated colorectal cancer
Injectable and reactive oxygen species-responsive nanogel–microgel hybrid bio-lubricants for osteoarthritis therapy by immunometabolic reprogramming
works.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common degenerative joint disorder involving irreversible cartilage damage, subchondral bone dysfunction, and chronic synovitis. Current intra-articular therapies suffer from short-lived effects and inadequate control of macrophage-mediated inflammation. To address this limitation, we develop an injectable, ROS-responsive nanogel–microgel hybrid bio-lubricant for OA treatment via immunometabolic reprogramming. Skatole-loaded mesoporous silica nanoparticles were crosslinked with polyvinyl alcohol to form ROS-responsive nanogels (Ska@NGs), which were subsequently encapsulated into HAMA/CSMA microgels using microfluidics as Ska@N-MGs. The physicochemical, rheological, lubricating, ROS-responsive, and biological properties of the system were evaluated in vitro, followed by therapeutic assessment in an ACLT + MMT-induced rat OA model. Ska@N-MGs exhibited favorable lubricating and ROS-regulating properties, with a friction coefficient of approximately 0.007. Skatole attenuated inflammatory responses in LPS-stimulated macrophages, while Ska@NGs treatment in the macrophage–chondrocyte co-culture system was accompanied by improved cartilage matrix-related markers. In a rat OA model, intra-articular injection of Ska@N-MGs reduced synovial inflammation and alleviated OA progression. This hybrid system integrates lubrication, stimuli-responsive drug delivery, and immunometabolic modulation, providing a promising platform for OA therapy.

works.title: Catechol-based antioxidant nanoplatform alleviates chondrocyte senescence and osteoarthritis via ATM/ATR-PINK1-mediated mitophagy
works.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease associated with cellular senescence and mitochondrial dysfunction. Although epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) and D-methionine (D-Met) exhibit antioxidant and anti-senescent activities, poor bioavailability and rapid intra-articular clearance limit their therapeutic potential. Here, we developed an EGCG-based antioxidant nanoparticle, ED@F127 nanoparticles (NPs), by conjugating EGCG with D-Met through a green Mannich reaction, followed by encapsulation in Pluronic F127. The resulting NPs exhibited a uniform size of approximately 80 nm, high drug-loading efficiency, and favorable biocompatibility. Using basic calcium phosphate (BCP) crystals as an OA-relevant pathological stimulus, we showed that ED@F127 NPs attenuated BCP-induced chondrocyte senescence. ED@F127 NPs also increased ATM/ATR abundance and PINK1/PARKIN-associated mitophagy markers. These changes were accompanied by reduced reactive oxygen species accumulation and improved mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP-associated signals. In vivo , intra-articular administration of ED@F127 NPs alleviated cartilage degeneration, abnormal subchondral bone remodeling, and osteophyte formation in a BCP crystal-induced rat OA model. Together, these findings support ED@F127 NPs as a promising nanotherapeutic strategy for attenuating oxidative stress and cellular senescence in OA.

works.title: Bacterial missile with ultrasound-triggered prodrug release for targeted pancreatic cancer therapy
works.abstract: Pancreatic cancer poses a severe clinical challenge owing to its deep-seated site, inefficient drug delivery, poor tumor penetration, and systemic toxicity of conventional chemotherapy. Herein, we fabricated an ultrasound-responsive “bacterial missile” via in situ atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP) on attenuated Salmonella VNP20009. Thioketal-linked 5-fluorouracil (5-Fu) prodrugs were densely grafted onto bacteria to form a protective polymer shell, enabling high drug loading, reducing off-target toxicity, and shielding surface antigens to alleviate excessive immunogenicity. Manganese carbonate (MnCO 3 ) nanoparticles were further assembled onto the engineered bacteria to construct VNP@P5-Fu@Mn. Under ultrasound irradiation, reactive oxygen species cleave thioketal bonds for on-demand 5-Fu release, while released Mn 2+ activates the cGAS–STING pathway. The living bacterial chassis actively penetrates dense tumor stroma and targets deep lesions. In vitro and in vivo studies confirm that this system induces robust immunogenic cell death, promotes dendritic cell maturation, enhances CD8 + T-cell infiltration, and effectively inhibits orthotopic pancreatic tumor growth with minimal systemic toxicity. This work integrates bacterial targeting, ultrasound-controlled prodrug activation, and cGAS–STING-mediated immunotherapy, offering a programmable and translatable living therapeutic platform for precise treatment of deep-seated solid tumors. We developed an ultrasound-responsive “bacterial missile” by grafting chemotherapy prodrugs onto attenuated Salmonella via ATRP. This system leverages bacterial tumor targeting for deep accumulation and uses ultrasound for precise drug release at the tumor site, enhancing efficacy while minimizing off-target damage to normal tissues. This strategy offers a promising approach for precise deep-tumor therapy.

works.title: Correction: High-throughput synthesis and optimization of ionizable lipids through A3 coupling for efficient mRNA delivery
Dynamic conductivity model-correlated membrane kinetics with cell viability, permeability, and nanoparticle delivery efficiency
Bletilla striata polysaccharide‑zinc complex ameliorates ulcerative colitis by modulating endoplasmic reticulum stress-associated autophagy and apoptosis
MXene@C/SiO 2 composite films with layered heterostructures for high-temperature infrared stealth, electromagnetic interference shielding, and fire safety
works.abstract: Abstract Flexible materials integrating infrared stealth, electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding, thermal management, and fire safety are highly desirable for aerospace and high-temperature electronics. Here, layered MXene@C/SiO2 composite films (MCSx) with tunable structural units were constructed by combining low-thermal-conductivity C/SiO2 nanofiber layers with highly conductive MXene layers. This heterogeneous architecture endows the films with pronounced anisotropic thermal transport and an ultralow through-plane thermal conductivity of 0.030 W m−1 K−1. Benefiting from the low emissivity of MXene and efficient thermal insulation, the films achieve infrared stealth over 50–500 °C and reduce the apparent surface temperature by 365.7 °C at a heat source temperature of 500 °C. The continuous MXene network enables rapid Joule heating from 29.5 to 149.6 °C at 0.5–3.0 V with an electrothermal conversion efficiency exceeding 99%. The conductive layers and heterogeneous interfaces jointly achieve an X-band EMI shielding effectiveness of 71.6 dB. The films also exhibit excellent flame retardancy, thermal insulation, and fire resistance while maintaining EMI shielding performance after flame exposure. This work provides a heterostructure engineering strategy for developing multifunctional protective materials under thermally demanding conditions.

works.title: Enzymatically Active Liposomal Nanobots for the Penetration of Intercellular and Intracellular Barriers
works.abstract: Delivery systems for nanomedicine are critical, however, they are restricted by intercellular and intracellular barriers including lysosomal sequestration after cellular uptake, that impede penetration from the tissue to the subcellular level. Here, we report a liposomal nanobot with enzymatic propulsion and drug-payload capabilities that exhibits tumor microenvironment responsiveness and active penetration, enabling intracellular transport and active lysosomal escape. This nanobot arises from phase-separated vesicles of liposome and bacterial outer membrane vesicles that possess doxorubicin-encapsulation capability and are asymmetrically functionalized with glucose oxidase to form a Janus catalytic interface for self-diffusiophoresis in the presence of glucose. Under mildly acidic conditions, these nanobots display enhanced motility and chemotactic migration toward acidic regions, leveraging pH gradients in the tumor microenvironment to infiltrate tumor spheroids. Once internalized, the nanobots are rapidly captured by lysosomes and subsequently escape, as a plausible chemo-mechanical mechanism involving catalytic membrane perturbation and active motion. Then nanobot-associated signals redistribute toward ER- and Golgi-associated compartments and persist across successive recipient cells, supporting intercellular relay transport. The encapsulated drug is released within tumor cells, enabling enhanced antitumor efficacy. This nanobot thus demonstrates an active drug delivery system capable of traversing cellular barriers, providing a strategy for precision tumor therapy.

works.title: Highly stable hydrophobic dietary polyphenols enhance brain delivery and neuroprotection: Tunable crystallization properties in interfacial assembly
Nanomaterials reinforced probiotic delivery: From systematic design to health applications
Biodegradable polymer-enabled ROS-responsive nanogels for controlled drug release and boosted cancer treatment
works.abstract: Biodegradable nanogels (NGs) have emerged as promising platforms for controlled drug delivery free of long-term biosafety concerns. Reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive nanomaterials have garnered increasing attention as smart drug delivery systems exploiting the aberrant redox environment of tumors for precise and efficient therapy. We developed biodegradable, biocompatible, and crosslinkable polymer-based ROS-responsive NGs to enable controlled drug release and enhanced cancer treatment outcomes. Three different ROS-responsive drug linkers, featuring thioether and ester groups separated by varied lengths of carbon chains, were exploited to attach paclitaxel (PTX) molecules to the NG scaffold. The PTX-NGs were fabricated through a mild polymer-crosslinking process, yielding spherical nanoparticles with an average diameter of ~60 nm, which facilitated cellular internalization and tumor penetration. Leveraging the elevated intracellular ROS levels of cancer cells to trigger the release of PTX, PTX-NGs exhibited efficient tumor inhibition while minimizing systemic toxicities. Notably, the anticancer therapeutic efficiencies of different NGs were determined by the ROS-responsive drug linkers, specifically the length of carbon chains between the thioether and ester groups. In addition, the PTX-NGs were well tolerated by mice during long-term administration, exhibiting desired biocompatibility. Overall, this work highlights the advantages of biodegradable ROS-responsive polymeric NGs serving as an advanced drug delivery platform for boosted cancer treatment.

works.title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Silver Icosahedrons for SERS Sensing Applications
works.abstract: Ag icosahedrons, characterized by the size-dependent distribution of strain fields, has garnered increasing interests across disciplines from crystallography to materials science. However, the metastability arising from such intrinsic strain greatly restricts the available synthetic routes. Here, we present a facile aqueous-phase electrodeposition technique for the robust synthesis of Ag icosahedrons. By decreasing the Ag reduction rate, we achieve enhanced control over the electrodeposition kinetics, as quantitatively evidenced by the apparent activation energy. The pronounced kinetic stability allows for the synthesis of particles up to 5 µm in size within 10 min (Pretreatment time: 48 h). Through systematic variation of applied potentials, currents, and electrolyte compositions, we enable the design of Ag icosahedrons with tunable hierarchical structures. These structured particles can be effectively employed as surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) substrates for pesticide detection. This work establishes a stable and pure model system that facilitates the straightforward synthesis of metastable structures.

works.title: Fast and Selective Photochemical Doping of Spiro‐OMeTAD
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Oxidizing a redox‐active molecule rapidly and selectively to a targeted oxidation state, without residual dopant ions, is a central challenge in molecular doping. Spiro‐OMeTAD exemplifies it: the standard LiTFSI/O 2 protocol is slow (>12 h), leaves hygroscopic Li + aggregates in the film, and yields an uncontrolled +1/+2/+3 mixture. Here we report a biphasic photochemical doping platform, the crown ether/acid‐assisted doping system (CEADS), in which a chlorobenzene solution of spiro‐OMeTAD/LiTFSI is layered above an aqueous phase of concentrated HCl and 12‐crown‐4 (12C4) and irradiated with broadband UV. Doping completes in 60 s, yielding a > 10 4 ‐fold conductivity enhancement (σ = 1.18 × 10 −2 S cm −1 , ≈60‐fold over LiTFSI/O 2 ) and removing >98% of Li + from the organic phase. Three sequentially optimized parameters control the spiro‐OMeTAD oxidation manifold: high H + quenches over‐oxidation, Cl − provides secondary kinetic modulation at intermediate acid, and 4 equiv 12C4 enforces charge‐balanced phase transfer. Temperature‐dependent conductivity yields an Arrhenius activation energy E a = 0.19 eV ( R 2 = 0.99) over 193–298 K, consistent with reduced Li‐related deep traps. CEADS produces lithium‐free, cleanly +1/+2‐oxidized hole‐transport films on a minute timescale.

works.title: Compositional variation insights into nanoprecipitation through Asymmetric flow field-flow fractionation (AF4): Impact of lipid composition and surfactant placement on particle formation
works.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are attractive drug delivery platforms, yet a fundamental limitation of conventional batch characterizations is their inability to resolve compositional heterogeneity across polydisperse particle size distributions under nanoprecipitation. Here, the impact of two key formulation parameters, surfactant placement and solid/liquid lipid composition, are systematically investigated on particle formation, with particular emphasis on the size distribution and partitioning of physical encapsulation within nanoparticles. The model system, LNPs incorporating a Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) donor-acceptor fluorophore pair (FLNPs), are used to probe nanoscale payload distribution. Integration of batch characterization (dynamic light scattering (DLS), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and photophysical analysis), flow-induced dispersion analysis (FIDA) with asymmetrical flow field-flow fractionation (AF4) coupled to multi-angle light scattering (MALS), DLS, UV–vis and fluorescence detection, reveal that surfactant placement is the dominant parameter: when dissolved in the organic phase, the surfactant produces smaller particles with varied shapes and single-donor FLNPs, whereas when the surfactant is dissolved in the aqueous phase it results in larger, more spherical and co-localization particles. The addition of liquid lipid shifts size distributions towards greater size uniformity. These findings link nanoprecipitation parameters to size distribution and component localization, highlight the power of AF4 in resolving heterogeneity, and provide design principles for controlling LNPs size and payload distribution.

works.title: Redox‑active selenium-doped graphene quantum dots boost baicalein-mediated breast cancer therapy via synergistic ferroptosis and tumor immune remodeling
Chylomicron-biomimetic nanoparticles enable efficient intestinal lymphatic transport for oral delivery of therapeutic proteins
works.abstract: Oral delivery of therapeutic proteins remains a major challenge due to poor gastrointestinal stability and limited transport across the intestinal epithelium. Intestinal lymphatic transport (ILT), a physiological pathway responsible for lipid absorption via chylomicron (CM) assembly, offers a promising route to overcome these barriers, yet its efficient exploitation for macromolecular delivery remains elusive. Here, we report chylomicron-biomimetic nanoparticles (CMB-NPs) designed to engage endogenous CM assembly and transport pathways, thereby facilitating ILT-mediated transcytosis. The nanoparticles exhibit high lipoprotein affinity and strong association with CMs. Mechanistic studies reveal endoplasmic reticulum/Golgi-associated trafficking, ApoB-48-associated processing, and transport into mesenteric lymphatics in vivo, collectively supporting their engagement with endogenous CM-associated transport pathways.
