As a result, the system achieves an absolute oral bioavailability of 26.7% for the model protein Klotho, markedly enhancing systemic exposure and promoting preferential accumulation in fibrotic kidneys. In murine models of renal fibrosis, oral administration of Klotho-loaded CMB-NPs significantly alleviated disease progression and produced robust anti-fibrotic effects by restoring renal function and suppressing fibrotic signaling. Collectively, this work establishes engagement with endogenous CM-associated transport pathways as an effective strategy for oral protein delivery and provides a generalizable framework for exploiting ILT in nanomedicine.

works.title: Deep-learning-predicted sinomenine ameliorates metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease by delaying cellular senescence via NES
works.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common metabolic liver disorder worldwide, and its burden is growing as populations age and obesity rates rise. Current therapies only partially correct metabolic disturbances and fail to reverse hepatocyte senescence or restore functional capacity. Here, we built a deep-learning efficacy prediction system (DLEPS) powered by L1000 transcriptomic data to screen bioactive compounds and identified the natural alkaloid sinomenine (Sino) as a potent MASLD modulator. Mechanistically, Sino suppresses the transcriptional activity of NF-κB and thereby downregulates NES expression. NES emerged as an important intermediate mediator linking NF-κB signaling to hepatocyte senescence. Reduced NES expression was associated with lower Smad3 phosphorylation and reduced P53/P21 pathway activation, delays cellular senescence, inhibits the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), and restores normal mitochondrial structure and metabolic function. To enhance hepatic delivery, we further engineered galactose-lipid-membrane-coated Sino nanoparticles (Gal-SiNPs), which enhanced hepatic accumulation and retained therapeutic activity at a relatively lower administered dose. Collectively, deep-learning-guided discovery of Sino reshapes hepatocyte function via the NES -senescence pathway, and its nano-targeted formulation shows promising therapeutic potential for MASLD therapy and merits further translational exploration.

works.title: Glycan-targeted gold nanorod nanoplatform for photothermal immunotherapy of pancreatic cancer
works.abstract: Despite the clinical successes of adaptive immune checkpoint blockade, sialic acid-mediated interactions associated with the Siglec-10/CD24 “don’t eat me” pathway can contribute to impaired macrophage-mediated clearance in pancreatic cancer. Here, we report a dual-targeting gold nanorod platform (Man-AuNR-SNA) designed to combine glycan-mediated targeting with photothermal therapy. The nanoplatform targets CD206-expressing M2-like macrophages via mannose and recognizes sialylated pancreatic cancer cells via SNA lectin. Dual functionalization enhanced macrophage–cancer cell interactions compared with single-target controls, supporting complementary contributions of mannose- and SNA-mediated targeting. NIR-triggered photothermal treatment induced apoptotic cancer cell death and, in a PANC-1 xenograft model, achieved 70.9% tumor growth inhibition, comparable to that observed with gemcitabine. Treatment was also associated with an increased CD86/CD206 ratio and changes in macrophage-associated gene expression consistent with a more pro-inflammatory phenotype. These findings support the integration of glycan-mediated macrophage–cancer cell targeting with photothermal therapy as a potential strategy for pancreatic cancer treatment.

works.title: Layer-parity-defined surface polarization in Nb 3 Cl 8 for excitonic modulation at van der Waals interfaces
works.abstract: Abstract The intrinsic symmetry breaking in the breathing kagome lattice of layered Nb3Cl8 provides a unique mechanism for realizing electrically polar surfaces. In each monolayer, the trimerization of Nb atoms breaks inversion and mirror symmetries, generating an out-of-plane electric dipole. The AB-stacked α phase arranges adjacent layer dipoles antiferroelectrically, leaving the uncompensated surface polarization determined by layer parity. Here, using atomic force microscopy operated in Kelvin probe force microscopy mode, we map the layer-dependent surface electrostatic potential in exfoliated Nb3Cl8 flakes and resolve a pronounced odd-even oscillation consistent with alternating surface-polarization states. Beyond this parity-locked layer polarization, we further identify intralayer polar domains separated by domain walls that do not coincide with a local thickness step, in which the local out-of-plane polarization reverses independently of layer parity, consistent with a local reconstruction of the breathing kagome network. By interfacing monolayer MoSe2 with Nb3Cl8, we demonstrate that these surface-polarization textures effectively modulate adjacent excitonic emission through domain-dependent interfacial band alignment and charge transfer. Our findings establish Nb3Cl8 as an intrinsic layer-polarized van der Waals platform and show that layer parity provides a powerful structural degree of freedom for programming excitonic and optoelectronic responses at van der Waals interfaces.

works.title: Issue Information
Hydrocolloid-integrated organic optoelectronic patch for wearable wound phototheranostics
works.abstract: Abstract In this study, we developed a flexible wearable phototheranostic patch integrating a red organic light-emitting diode (OLED) and an organic photodiode (OPD) with a hydrocolloid dressing. The platform enables photobiomodulation (PBM) using a 630 nm red OLED together with photoplethysmographic (PPG) sensing through an adjacent OPD. The hydrocolloid provides low elastic modulus and high conformability while maintaining mechanical and optical stability under repeated bending. To coordinate optical therapy and sensing, the OLED was operated using pulse-width modulation (PWM) at 50 Hz with a 30 % duty cycle. PPG measurements showed that PWM maintained clear signal acquisition at reduced time-averaged irradiance, with SNR generally increasing as the PWM ON-state irradiance increased. Among the tested PWM conditions, PWM-16.67 exhibited the strongest overall cell-proliferative response and the highest SNR, while delivering approximately the same radiant exposure as the DC reference. Notably, PWM-10 also achieved a cell-proliferative response comparable to the DC reference while reducing radiant exposure by 40 %, indicating its potential as a lower-exposure operating condition. Thermal measurements further showed that PWM reduced heat accumulation relative to continuous DC operation at matched peak irradiance, although this thermal advantage was partially diminished as the higher ON-state current required for increased PWM irradiance introduced additional thermal load. These results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating optical therapy and physiological sensing within a single conformable hydrocolloid-based OLED–OPD platform and provide a basis for further development of wearable wound phototheranostic systems.

works.title: Neutrophil-excluding nanoparticles abrogate biomechanical and immunological barriers to sensitize radioimmunotherapy
works.abstract: Abstract Desmoplastic tumors are highly resistant to treatment, largely due to their dense fibrotic stroma. Paradoxically, radiotherapy (RT) exacerbates this challenge by triggering a pro-fibrotic and immunosuppressive cascade. Here, we identify an RT-induced neutrophil-fibroblast-macrophage hierarchy as a key driver of this therapeutic resistance. To circumvent this barrier, we developed a nano-modulator, termed NanoNex, to precisely intervene in this cellular crosstalk. By transcriptionally inhibiting post-RT neutrophil recruitment via SMAD3 suppression, NanoNex effectively abrogates neutrophil-dependent stromal deposition and alleviates biomechanical tension. Crucially, this remodeling of the tumor microenvironment restores macrophage plasticity and unlocks their responsiveness to immune adjuvants, enabling potent M1 polarization. In refractory murine models of pancreatic and breast cancer, NanoNex markedly potentiated radioimmunotherapy, eliciting robust tumor regression. Furthermore, NanoNex induced systemic anti-tumor immune memory in the pancreatic cancer model. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that this nano-enabled neutrophil exclusion strategy serves as a transformative platform to normalize the biomechanical and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, converting RT-induced stromal barriers into a permissive landscape for effective radioimmunotherapy.

works.title: Phase engineering of Mo x C regulates electronic structure and interfacial hydrogen-bond networks over Ru sites for pH-universal hydrogen evolution
works.abstract: Abstract Metallic ruthenium (Ru) represents a promising Pt alternative for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, achieving efficient HER, particularly under pH-universal conditions, remains challenging due to sluggish interfacial water dissociation kinetics. Herein, we report a phase engineering strategy that utilizes well-defined cubic and hexagonal molybdenum carbide (α–MoC/β–Mo2C) supports to regulate Ru–MoxC metal–support interactions and interfacial microenvironments. The Ru–MoC exhibits superior performance to Ru–Mo2C across a wide pH range. Notably, the Ru–MoC requires an overpotential of 12 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in alkaline media, outperforming most previously reported catalysts. Moreover, no activity loss occurs during 80 h of reaction, demonstrating the good durability of the Ru–MoC. Detailed characterizations reveal that the electron-rich Ru centers in Ru–MoC induce stronger interfacial polarization. The enhanced polarization enables effective reorganization of interfacial hydrogen-bond networks into a beneficial dynamic and weakly hydrogen-bonded state for water dissociation in alkaline medium. This work provides new insights into the regulation of interfacial catalytic microenvironments, offering a promising strategy for the design of advanced nanocatalysts.

works.title: 3D-printed flexible piezoelectric scaffolds restore load-bearing function of regenerated bone
works.abstract: Abstract Flexible piezoelectric scaffolds can conform to irregular bone defects and deliver wireless electrical stimulation, yet whether their mechanical and electrical functions persist throughout the months-long course of bone remodeling, as well as whether the regenerated bone ultimately recovers load-bearing function, remains unresolved. Here, we report PUA/BTO/β-TCP elastomer–ceramic piezoelectric scaffolds fabricated by digital light processing (DLP) into a triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) architecture. Calcination of BTO increased its ferroelectric tetragonal phase content and enhanced the piezoelectric coefficient d33 of the composites by up to 44.3%. The scaffolds combined full elastic recovery after 50% compression with durable mechanoelectrical performance: after 28 days of immersion in simulated body fluid, their quasi-static and cyclic mechanical properties remained essentially unchanged, and d33 remained above its initial value. Under ultrasound excitation, the scaffolds significantly enhanced osteoblast proliferation and osteogenic differentiation in vitro and accelerated femoral defect repair in rats, with the bone volume fraction reaching approximately 70% at 8 weeks, versus below 13% for controls. Critically, biomechanical testing at 8 weeks post-implantation showed that the repaired femur withstood a fracture limit load approximately 9.1% higher than that of intact native bone, survived cyclic compression at 70% of the limit load without detectable cracking, and exhibited crack arrest at the scaffold–bone interface, which was direct evidence of stable mechanical integration. We term the concurrent retention of mechanical resilience and piezoelectric output during remodeling, together with stable scaffold–bone mechanical integration, mechanoelectrical adaptation, and propose it as a design principle that shifts bone-scaffold development from short-term osteoinductivity toward sustained in vivo functionality.

works.title: Visible-spectrum-spanning halide-composition-graded CsPbX 3 perovskite films toward integrated spectral detection
works.abstract: Abstract Monolithically integrated spectral detection requires functional materials that can directly convert spectral information into spatially distinguishable optical and photoelectrical responses. Here, we report halide-composition-graded CsPbX3 perovskite films fabricated by a dual-source vapor-phase anion-exchange strategy. Spatially regulated chloride and iodide exchange in CsPbBr3 films produces a continuous transition from chloride-rich through bromide-rich to iodide-rich regions across a centimeter-scale substrate, enabling broadband optical tunability over the visible spectrum. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, UV–vis absorption, and micro-area photoluminescence confirm the continuous compositional evolution and corresponding bandgap modulation. To quantitatively resolve the local optical response, micro-scale spectroscopic ellipsometry is combined with a physics-informed residual network, enabling high-throughput inversion of spatially resolved optical constants and dielectric-function phase diagrams. The extracted optical parameters further reveal continuous exciton-energy evolution and composition-dependent shallow band-tail states. Incorporating these experimentally determined optical profiles into numerical PIN photodetector simulations demonstrates wavelength-dependent carrier-generation redistribution and intrinsic self-filtering behavior. A simulated 20-channel photocurrent transmission matrix is then used to evaluate proof-of-concept computational reconstruction of smooth, continuous polychromatic spectra within the calibrated optical-power range. This work establishes visible-spectrum-spanning halide-gradient CsPbX3 films as a promising material platform for compact, filter-free computational spectral sensing.

works.title: Recent advances in the use of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) as delivery vectors for mRNA
works.abstract: Abstract Therapeutic mRNA has demonstrated great promise in infectious disease vaccines, cancer immunotherapy, and protein replacement therapies. However, its clinical translation is hampered by intrinsic limitations, including rapid degradation, poor membrane permeability, extremely low endosomal escape, lack of tissue specificity, and potential immunogenicity. Naked mRNA alone is insufficient to overcome these challenges, which has driven the emergence of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) as the leading clinical-grade delivery platform. LNPs employ a four-component system: ionizable lipids for encapsulation and pH-responsive fusion; helper phospholipids and cholesterol for structural integrity and membrane fluidity; and PEGylated lipids for colloidal stability and prolonged circulation. This review systematically addresses LNP composition, structure–activity relationships, and the interplay with extrinsic factors—including administration routes, targeting ligands, immunostimulant co-delivery, and organ tropism (liver, spleen, lungs, lymph nodes)—that collectively govern mRNA biodistribution and therapeutic efficacy. Nonetheless, several major bottlenecks persist, such as unclear endosomal escape mechanisms, PEG-related immune interference, obstacles to extrahepatic delivery, manufacturing complexities, and challenges in AI-driven lipid design. Future progress will rely on integrating rational design, high-throughput screening, and engineering innovations to develop precision delivery systems that are safe, efficient, and amenable to repeated administration—thereby fully unlocking the clinical potential of mRNA-based therapies.

works.title: Universal surface-coordinated assembly of metal oxide/sub-1 nm nanowire composite aerogels
works.abstract: Abstract Sub-1 nm nanowires (SNWs) have attracted significant attention as novel building blocks in the aerogel field because of their unique structures; however, their single chemical composition and limited assembly strategies restrict the development and application of sub-1 nm nanowire aerogels (SNWAs). Herein, we report a controlled assembly strategy for SNWs that utilizes the coordination between metal oxide precursors and hydroxyl ligands on the SNW surface, as well as the hydrolysis-condensation reactions of the precursors themselves, to achieve the compositing of metal oxides with SNWs, thereby endowing the resulting SNWAs with multifunctionality. This approach successfully yields twelve types of metal oxide/sub-1 nm nanowire composite aerogels (MOx-SNWAs) with low density (as low as 14 mg cm−3) and high specific surface area (up to 299 m2 g−1). Further studies revealed that WO3 composite sub-1nm nanowire aerogel (WO3-SNWAs) simultaneously exhibited excellent transparency, photochromism, thermal insulation, and photocatalytic performance, demonstrating broad application prospects.

works.title: Ultrathin and efficient wearable EMI shields with integrated self-powered sensing and information coding
works.abstract: Abstract Developing ultrathin and robust high-performance electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials with multifunctional integration for wearable electronics is imperative yet remains challenging. Here, we report a bioinspired versatile and wearable MXene/cellulose nanofiber-silver nanowire (MXene/CNF-AgNW) composite film with superior mechanical strength, high-efficiency EMI shielding and integrated self-powered sensing capabilities. The film achieves superior mechanical robustness with a high tensile strength reaching 315 MPa through a multiscale reinforcement strategy that combines hybrid sandwich and nacre-like structures. The sandwiched AgNWs with MXene/CNF-based shells impart the composite film with high electrical conductivity and excellent EMI shielding effectiveness (EMI SE) reaching 62 dB for a tiny thickness of 23 μm, corresponding to an outstanding specific EMI SE (SSE/t) of 16550 dB·cm2·g-1, together with remarkable electrothermal conversion capability. Furthermore, the flexible and antibacterial film can also serve as wearable electronic skin with self-powered sensing for human activity monitoring and information coding. Notably, by integrating a machine learning algorithm, the system can enable intelligent handwriting recognition with an accuracy of 100%, establishing an advanced communication interface. This work provides a facile multiscale engineering strategy for constructing multifunctional composite films that seamlessly integrate protection, perception, and communication functionalities for next-generation smart wearable electronic applications.

works.title: Mechanism-guided nano and advanced biomaterials for intrauterine adhesions: from pathological microenvironment modulation to functional endometrial regeneration
works.abstract: Abstract Intrauterine adhesions arise from failed endometrial repair, in which wound apposition, maladaptive immune–stromal signaling, oxidative injury, fibrotic remodeling and loss of regenerative niches impair reproductive function. This critical narrative review organizes nano and advanced biomaterials around six overlapping biological repair requirements and examines how material structure influences interfacial behavior, mechanics, transport and local exposure. Study-level comparisons distinguish treatment timing, component controls, measured release or residence, and reproductive outcomes. Spatially asymmetric interfaces, stimulus-responsive networks and sequential delivery are evaluated as different design principles; differential release alone does not establish repair-stage matching. Nanoscale structure is also distinguished from evidence that a particular nanoscale feature causes therapeutic benefit. Human evidence is most developed for relatively simple barriers and selected cell–scaffold strategies, whereas catalytic, EV-containing and responsive systems remain predominantly preclinical. We propose minimum sufficient material complexity as a comparison principle: each added component should address a defined unmet function and demonstrate an increment over an indication-relevant simpler approach. Functional recovery requires coordinated hormonal, epithelial, stromal and vascular behavior, with pregnancy outcomes interpreted alongside product fate and reproductive safety.

works.title: Solution-processable conjugated polymer films via fluorination-induced noncovalent conformational locks for efficient photocatalytic U(VI) removal
works.abstract: Abstract The practical application of donor-acceptor(D-A) conjugated polymers for photocatalytic U(VI) extraction is limited, fused-ring planar backbones that enable efficient charge transport yet resist film processing and soluble backbones that allow film fabrication yet suffer from poor planarity and photocatalytic activity. Here, we demonstrate that a single fluorination method locked the backbone into a near-planar conformation via F···S simple noncovalent interactions, while simultaneously conferring enough solubility for direct casting of recyclable polymer films. The optimized Film-PFBT, tested in a lab-scale continuous-flow photoreactor, achieves 95% U(VI) removal within 4 hours with a rate constant 1.74 times that of its non-fluorinated control, and retains >60% efficiency even in genuine uranium mining wastewater. This work offers a conjugated polymer photocatalyst design featuring enhanced processability and reusability for potential application in uranium-contaminated water remediation.

works.title: Magnetic-field-induced micro-potential promotes charge separation in S-vacancy-rich ZIS/MoS 2 /Mo heterostructure for efficient photocatalytic H 2 evolution
works.abstract: Abstract Enhancing charge separation in the absence of external bias remains a central challenge in photocatalytic hydrogen evolution. Herein, a sulfur-vacancy-rich ZIS/MoS2/Mo heterostructure is constructed, in which a magnetic-field-induced micro-potential is harnessed to regulate charge dynamics and enable efficient H2 evolution. Under a rotating magnetic field, metallic Mo component generates a motional electromotive force, thereby establishing a wireless internal electric field that spatially directs the migration of photogenerated electrons and holes in opposite directions. Owing to the synergistic interplay among sulfur vacancies, heterointerface engineering, and the magnetically induced micro-potential, the optimized ZISv/MoS2-x/Mo catalyst delivers a hydrogen evolution rate of 5.19 mmol·g−1·h−1, which is 10.4-fold higher than that of pristine ZIS and represents an approximately 50% enhancement relative to the non-magnetic-field condition. Meanwhile, an apparent quantum yield of 20.98% is achieved at 380 nm. Systematic experimental characterizations, together with COMSOL simulations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, demonstrate that the induced micro-potential significantly accelerates charge carriers separation and directional transport, while sulfur vacancies act as active electron-trapping centers that further promote charge utilization efficiency. This work establishes a magnetically engineered wireless electric-field strategy for rationally manipulating charge dynamics and boosting photocatalytic performance.

works.title: Hybrid bio-synthetic polymer gel electrolytes: Synergistic design and advanced applications for zinc-ion batteries
works.abstract: Abstract Zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) hold great promise for large-scale energy storage and wearable electronics owing to their high safety, raw material abundance, and environmental friendliness. However, conventional liquid electrolytes suffer from water decomposition, evaporation, and leakage, while zinc dendrites, anode corrosion, and hydrogen/oxygen evolution reactions further compromise battery stability. Polymer gel electrolytes mitigate these issues by forming hydrogen bonds with free water, yet gels based on a single biopolymer gel (BPG) or a single synthetic polymer gel (SPG) electrolytes show clear performance trade-offs, where BPGs offer biocompatibility and good interfacial regulation but lack mechanical strength and high ionic conductivity, whereas SPGs provide strong mechanical properties but poor biocompatibility and weak electrode modulation. This review examines emerging hybrid bio-synthetic gel (HB-SG) electrolytes that combine the strengths of both polymer systems, covering their design principles, four main structural types, key synergistic mechanisms, and fabrication methods. Their performance in ion transport, mechanical resilience, self-healing, temperature tolerance, and resistance to parasitic reactions is discussed alongside practical applications across flexible, extreme-environment, and harsh-condition ZIBs. Current challenges, unclear synergistic mechanisms, limited room-temperature ionic conductivity, storage instability, and industrial scalability barriers are identified, along with future directions including multiscale structural design, theoretical simulation, green manufacturing, intelligent functionalization, and biomedical applications.

works.title: Electrochemically choreographed relay reconstruction into an adaptive NiOOH-CoOOH active interface for industrial water oxidation
works.abstract: Abstract Dynamic regulation and precise construction of reaction interfaces under operating conditions offer an effective route to optimize water-oxidation catalysis and develop advanced water-electrolysis catalysts. Here, we report a potential-gated relay reconstruction strategy using NiO/CoP nanohybrid as a model pre-catalyst, enabling the in situ formation of an active interface adapted to high-current-density alkaline water oxidation. Strong interfacial charge coupling between NiO and CoP enhances the structural flexibility of the pre-catalyst and establishes hierarchical oxidation characteristics for the two components. This fosters the preferential restructuring of CoP into CoOOH at low potentials, followed by the relay reconstruction of adjacent NiO into NiOOH, ultimately yielding a stably coupled service-state NiOOH-CoOOH active interface. Of importance, the reconstruction-derived interface establishes a Co–O–Ni electronic-coupling channel that cooperatively regulates the adsorption configurations and reaction energetics of key oxygenated intermediates, enhancing the activity. The reconstructed electrode requires an overpotential of 207 mV at 10 mA cm−2, while the assembled alkaline electrolyser operates at 1.818 V at 1,000 mA cm−2 and remains stable for over 260 h. Such precise construction of nanointerfaces through programming reconstruction of catalytic materials during operational service in this work provides a paradigm for further dynamic design or optimization of earth-abundant and efficient electrocatalysts.

Enhanced electron transfer by confinement effect coupled with nitrogen-rich sites of carbon nanorings for peroxydisulfate activation
works.abstract: Abstract Carbon materials with unique structures and properties exhibit significant potential as metal-free catalysts for peroxydisulfate (PDS) activation, promoting the efficient degradation of refractory organic pollutants. Herein, a template-confined pyrolysis strategy is proposed to construct hollow nitrogen-rich carbon nanorings (N-CNRs, N 13.15 at.%). The N-CNRs (0.06 g L−1) with porous architecture activate PDS efficiently for the complete degradation of phenol (20 mg L−1) within 18 min at room temperature, achieving a kinetic constant of 0.29 min−1 that is 10 and 29 times higher than those of N-doped carbon nanosheets and carbon spheres, respectively. Comprehensive characterization combined with mechanistic analysis and theoretical calculations reveals that the large specific surface area (985.8 m2 g−1) ensures abundant accessible nitrogen active sites, while the unique annular cavity structure facilitates reactant delivery to adjacent confined nanochannels. Serving as confined reaction domains, the nanochannels of N-CNRs enhance PDS adsorption at graphitic N sites and promote the formation of the metastable PDS* intermediate, thereby accelerating the interfacial electron transfer process. This work opens a new avenue for the rational design and fabrication of carbon materials with high nitrogen doping and engineered nanostructure for wastewater treatment.

works.title: Boosting triboelectric nanogenerators via hierarchical textures: insights from coupled adhesion contact and electrical modeling
works.abstract: Abstract Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are an emerging nanotechnology for distributed energy harvesting, where introducing hierarchical micro/nanotextures onto contact interfaces effectively enhances electrical output. However, existing theoretical models lack the capability to guide the design of hierarchical textures, particularly overlooking the gap-dependent variation of surface charge density, which is a key factor governing the electrical output. Here, a comprehensive numerical model coupling adhesive contact mechanics with electrical performance is established for hierarchical textured TENGs, with the gap-dependent charge density explicitly incorporated. The effects of texture hierarchy and micro/nano texture sizes are quantitatively analyzed based on numerical algorithms such as bi-conjugate stabilized (Bi-CGSTAB) method and fast Fourier transform (FFT) technique. It is shown that the present model achieves significantly improved agreement with experimental measurements compared with the conventional constant-charge-density assumption. Under a large indentation depth, hierarchical textures yield an open-circuit voltage of up to 295.7 V, representing an enhancement of 7.97% over single-scale textures, while reducing the pull-off force by 84.6% to effectively prevent separation failure and the consequent voltage degradation. At a small indentation depth, hierarchical textures offer an optimal trade-off between high output and low adhesion. Notably, nanotexture size exerts a dominant regulatory influence on output performance, with larger nanotexture sizes significantly boosting the open-circuit voltage, whereas microtexture size shows a weaker effect. These quantitative insights provide theoretical references for texture design and performance optimization of high-output hierarchical textured TENGs.

works.title: Rethinking performance metrics for emerging photodetectors
works.abstract: Abstract Low-dimensional materials offer tunable bandgaps, versatile device architectures, and compatibility with silicon platforms, enabling sensitive photodetectors for imaging and sensing. However, their distinct optoelectronic properties and operating mechanisms compared with conventional crystalline photodiodes complicate reliable extraction and comparison of standard performance metrics. These issues are particularly pronounced in gain-based and nonlinear photodetectors, where responsivity, noise, and detectivity are strongly coupled to operating conditions and measurement protocols. Here, we address these challenges from a metrology perspective. Using heterojunction-gated field-effect transistors (HGFETs) as a representative evaluation platform, we examine deviations in conventional characterization approaches from physically consistent parameter extraction. HGFETs are treated as a generalized model system capturing key complexities of emerging photodetectors, including optoelectronic gain, nonlinear transfer characteristics, and 1/f noise–dominated behavior. Within this framework, we identify systematic errors in the evaluation of responsivity, noise, temporal response, and specific detectivity. We further develop a cross-validated methodology enabled by the intrinsically decoupled HGFET architecture, mitigating coupling between optical excitation, electrical transport, and signal amplification, and thereby enables consistent parameter extraction across various configurations. Finally, we derive physically grounded expressions for detectivity and fundamental sensitivity limits set by background radiation and signal fluctuation. This work provides a general metrology framework for nonlinear and gain-based photodetectors, with applicability beyond the HGFET platform.

works.title: From delivery to function: Imaging-defined PK-to-PD mapping in activatable nanomedicine
Electrochemically driven vanadium-mediated phase-interface reconstruction for efficient and durable seawater oxidation
works.abstract: Abstract Efficient seawater oxidation requires rapid active-phase formation together with selective interfacial hydroxide/chloride ion (OH-/Cl-) regulation. Here, we report a cyclic-voltammetry activation strategy to electrochemically drive V-mediated phase-interface reconstruction in V-doped NiFe layered double hydroxide (V-NiFe LDH (EC)) for efficient and durable seawater oxidation. The V-NiFe LDH (EC) requires only 291 and 322 mV to reach 0.5 and 1.0 A cm-2 in alkaline seawater and remains stable for up to 3900 h, markedly surpassing NiFe LDH and the majority of previously reported seawater oxidation electrocatalysts. Spectroscopic analyses and DFT calculations reveal that, during activation, lattice V is oxidized and redistributed into surface-bound vanadate species, creating V-deficient and structurally labile Ni-O coordination that facilitates oxyhydroxide formation and accelerates OER kinetics. Meanwhile, the oxygen-rich vanadate interface strengthens interfacial hydrogen bonding, promoting OH- accessibility and suppressing Cl- adsorption and corrosion. This work establishes electrochemical dopant redistribution as a strategy to couple catalytic activation with interfacial ion selectivity for durable seawater electrolysis.

Model-dependent transport limitations shape the in vitro evaluation of platinum-based nanotherapeutics
works.abstract: Platinum-based chemotherapeutics remain central in oncology but are limited by systemic toxicity and poor tumor selectivity. Here, we investigate hydroxyapatite nanoparticles (HA NPs) as carriers for Pt(II) complexes, and compare the activity of free and NP-conjugated formulations across 2D cultures, static 3D tumor models, and flow-conditioned 3D systems using identical formulations, doses, and biological endpoints. Static 3D models impose diffusion-driven constraints that limit NP penetration, promote peripheral accumulation, and attenuate the apparent efficacy of NP-conjugated formulations. In contrast, quantitative spatial fluorescence profiling show that dynamic flow conditions partially alleviate these limitations, enhancing distal NP distribution and therapeutic activity. Notably, these transport-dependent effects influence the relative performance of free and nano-formulated drugs across models. Overall, our findings demonstrate that transport limitations in static systems can distort nanomedicine evaluation, highlighting the importance of incorporating flow-controlled conditions in preclinical screening.

works.title: Cobalt doping-induced spin polarization and in-situ Bi 0 decoration of Bi 2 MoO 6 synergistically boosting photocatalytic CO 2 -to-CO conversion
works.abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic CO2 reduction utilizing solar energy to convert CO2 into value-added fuels and chemicals is regarded as a promising strategy for alleviating energy crises and achieving carbon cycling. However, this process remains limited by rapid recombination of photogenerated carriers and sluggish CO2 activation kinetics. In this work, Bi2MoO6 (BMO)-based photocatalysts with Co doping and in-situ formation of Bi0 nanocrystals were developed through a facile one-step solvothermal method. X-ray absorption spectroscopy analysis reveals that Co species are atomically dispersed within the BMO lattice in a CoO4 coordination configuration. The weak crystal-field environment of CoO4 preserves unpaired 3d electrons and induces spin-polarized electronic states, thereby decreasing the photocarrier recombination. Meanwhile, the Co doping leads to in-situ formation of Bi0 nanocystals on the catalyst surface, which promotes photocarrier transfer between Bi0 and Co-BMO and facilitates the photocarrier separation. The Co doping increases the CO2 adsorption energy on the Bi active sites and decreases the energy barrier for the formation of the key *COOH intermediate. Moreover, the Co doping generates extra Co and Bi0 active sites for CO2 photoreduction reactions. The cascade synergistic mechanism significantly boosts the photocatalytic CO2-to-CO conversion, where the optimal Co2-BMO sample delivers a CO production rate of 158.47 μmol g−1 h−1 that is 3.8 times higher than that of pristine BMO. This work provides an intriguing strategy for designing efficient solar-driven CO2 conversion photocatalysts from the perspectives of electronic spin manipulation and interfacial charge transfer.

works.title: Ag-glued Au/C catalyst layer for durable CO 2 -to-CO electrolysis at industrial current density
works.abstract: Abstract Durable CO2-to-CO electrolysis at industrial current density remains a key bottleneck in low-temperature systems, especially in zero-gap electrolyzers, where prolonged high-rate operation drives impedance growth and destabilizes the catalyst-layer reaction environment. Here, we report an Ag-glued Au/C catalyst layer, in which large Ag nanoparticles are physically embedded in a nano-Au/C matrix. In a 10 cm × 10 cm zero-gap electrolyzer at 800 mA cm-2, Ag-glued Au/C (7:3) operated continuously for 200 h and degraded substantially more slowly than nano-Au/C, with cell-voltage and CO Faradaic-efficiency (FECO) decay rates of 1.3 mV h-1 and 0.12% h-1, respectively, and slower impedance growth. In flow cell tests, it reached 92.9% FECO at 139 mA cm-2. Neither AuAg alloying nor nanoscale Au/C-Ag/C mixing replicated this durability at the same composition, pointing to a catalyst-layer-organization effect that slows impedance growth under sustained operation. Within the configurations examined here, these results indicate that catalyst-layer organization, beyond composition, offers a practical design lever for durable CO2-to-CO electrolysis under industrially relevant zero-gap operation.

works.title: Engineering exosome-based delivery of IL-37 to enhance cytokine stability and antitumor activity in vitro and in vivo
Single-component dual-interface optimization for enhancing the performance and bias-stressing stability of conjugated polymer field-effect transistors
works.abstract: Abstract The performance of organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) is significantly influenced by the interfaces of organic semiconductor/electrodes and organic semiconductor/dielectric. In this work, an acceptor molecule (PTCDI-Me) modification layer was introduced to the bottom-gate bottom-contact configuration FETs of the conjugated polymer (PffBT4T-2OD), which not only passivated the electron trap states at the SiO2 dielectric, but also reduced the depletion area width at the interface of PffBT4T-2OD/electrodes by the holes generated through the weak charge transfer from PffBT4T-2OD to PTCDI-Me, thus achieving the one-stone two-birds effect. Consequently, the threshold voltage (Vth), subthreshold swing, and bias-stressing stability were improved evidently. For instance, after modification, Vth is positively shifted to -1.8 V from -13 V before modification; Vth shows only 1 V movement after bias-stressed 25 minutes by the gate potential of -50 V, while it moves negatively around 10.8 V without the PTCDI-Me modification layer. The results suggest the promising applications of conjugated components in the efficient modification of OFET interfaces and the development of high-performance OFETs with good bias-stressing stability.

works.title: Multi-component ultra-high-temperature boride ceramic whiskers with enhanced electromagnetic wave absorption
works.abstract: Abstract Boride ceramics have emerged as promising candidates for electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorption due to their thermal stability and conductivity. However, their intrinsically high conductivity often causes impedance mismatch with free space. Herein, multi-component boride whiskers were prepared. Benefiting from compositional design, the (Hf2/5Zr2/5Ti1/5)B2 whiskers exhibit effective EMW absorption performance at room temperature, achieving a minimum reflection loss of -60.88 dB at a matching thickness of 2.55 mm. This results from regulating the Ti content, which introduces lattice distortion and charge inhomogeneities, establishing abundant relaxation-type dipole centers to enhance polarization loss. Simultaneously, the interconnected whisker network facilitates carrier transport, boosting conductive loss. Crucially, after heat treatment at 1500 °C, the whiskers preserve structural integrity, and the (Hf1/3Zr1/3Ti1/3)B2 exhibits improved performance, achieving an ultra-wide effective absorption bandwidth of 8.64 GHz at a thickness of only 2.50 mm. This improvement stems from promoted electron transport and optimized impedance matching. This work provides a strategy for developing ultra-wideband and thermally stable EMW absorbers in extreme environments.

works.title: Repulsive biexciton interactions in near-infrared Ag 2 Se quantum dots
works.abstract: Abstract While biexciton interactions are pivotal for high-performance optoelectronics, their energetic nature in near-infrared silver chalcogenide colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) remains unclear. Herein, broadband femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy is utilized to map the dynamic Coulomb interactions across ground, asymmetric, and hot biexcitonic states in Ag2Se CQDs. Spectral analyses and theoretical models confirm that all three species exhibit unusually repulsive interactions governed by negative binding energies. Ground and asymmetric biexcitons display repulsive energies of ~3.5 meV and ~5.2 meV, respectively, whereas the hot biexciton interaction approaches nearly zero. This repulsive energy divergence originates from the uneven spatial localization of electron-hole wavefunctions and the differing probability distributions of hot/cold excitons. This work provides a crucial mechanistic foundation for deploying Ag2Se CQDs in multiexciton-driven optoelectronics, such as low-threshold lasers and high-efficiency hot-carrier photovoltaics.

works.title: A biodegradable hyaluronic acid hydrogel orchestrates cascaded H 2 S/Ca 2+ -amplified sonodynamic immunotherapy for osteosarcoma via remodeling the tumor microenvironment
works.abstract: Abstract Immunogenic cell death (ICD) activates antitumor immunity by releasing damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), which promote dendritic cell maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration. Sonodynamic therapy (SDT) offers deep tissue penetration for inducing ICD, but its efficacy is constrained by the hypoxic and glutathione (GSH)-rich tumor microenvironment. Herein, a biodegradable hyaluronic acid-based hydrogel (C-S-AH) was developed for cascaded H2S/Ca2+-amplified sonodynamic immunotherapy of osteosarcoma. The AH hydrogel co-encapsulates H2S/Ca2+-releasing C@MSHD nanoparticles and oxygen-vacancy-rich SnO2-x-FA sonosensitizers. Released H2S inhibits mitochondrial respiration by blocking cytochrome c oxidase, reducing oxygen consumption to relieve hypoxia while depleting GSH to amplify oxidative stress. Ca2+ overload further disrupts mitochondrial function and synergizes with SDT-generated ROS. This cascade induces robust ICD, promotes DC maturation and CD8+ T cell infiltration, and converts “cold” tumors into “hot” ones. In OS-bearing mouse models, this strategy significantly suppresses tumor growth and elicits long-term immune memory that effectively resists tumor rechallenge. This work provides a mechanistically validated strategy, supported by systematic controls and rescue experiments, for SDT-immunotherapy in immunotherapy-resistant solid tumors.

works.title: Adhesive HNDH@LUT hydrogel promotes spinal cord repair by suppressing dsDNA–STING signaling and autophagy-associated ferroptosis-related injury
works.abstract: Abstract Background: Spinal cord injury (SCI) remains difficult to treat because the lesion is mechanically fragile, fluid-rich, and biologically hostile, while cerebrospinal fluid-mediated diffusion limits local retention of soluble neuroprotective agents. Luteolin (LUT) has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, but insufficient lesion-site exposure restricts its application. We developed an adhesive hyaluronic acid-based hydrogel, HNDH@LUT, for sustained local LUT delivery and in situ SCI repair.Methods: HNDH@LUT was prepared from HA-NCSN and HA-DA precursors and characterized by structural, morphological, rheological, adhesion, swelling, degradation, and drug-release analyses. Its protective effects were evaluated in hemin- and H2O2-induced HT22 oxidative injury models and a mouse spinal cord transection model using biochemical assays, immunofluorescence, western blotting, RNA sequencing, behavioral testing, and histological analyses.Results: HNDH@LUT formed a porous, adhesive, shear-thinning hydrogel with low swelling, progressive degradation, and sustained LUT release. LUT reduced ROS accumulation and lipid peroxidation, preserved Nissl bodies, restored SOD and GSH homeostasis, and normalized SLC7A11, GPX4, P62, and LC3-I/LC3-II expression. It also reduced cytosolic dsDNA accumulation, inhibited STING oligomerization, and suppressed STING–TBK1–IRF3 phosphorylation. In vivo, HNDH@LUT improved locomotor recovery, preserved neurons, myelin, and axons, reduced fibrotic scarring and lesion-associated tissue discontinuity, and promoted axon-, myelin-, and synapse-related transcriptional programs while suppressing inflammatory responses. Systemic histology and serum biochemical indices revealed no detectable toxicity during the 28-day observation period.Conclusion: HNDH@LUT enhances local LUT retention, supports neural tissue preservation, and promotes SCI repair in the fluid-rich injured spinal cord by attenuating oxidative stress, dsDNA–STING activation, and autophagy-associated ferroptosis-related injury.

works.title: Raman spectra of van der Waals layered MoSi 2 N 4 and WSi 2 N 4
works.abstract: Abstract Raman spectroscopy, as a rapid, nondestructive and powerful technique, has been widely used to study two-dimensional (2D) materials. The emerging 2D van der Waals layered MSi2N4 (M = Mo or W) semiconductors show remarkable electrical, optical, thermal, and mechanical properties. However, their Raman signatures and defect-related features remain poorly understood. Here, we use first-principles calculations and Raman spectroscopy to investigate the Raman spectra of MSi2N4. The first-order phonon modes are unambiguously assigned, while most of the second‑order Raman peaks are preliminarily identified. Furthermore, we observe an anomalous Davydov splitting in multilayer samples, suggesting a distinctive interlayer vibrational coupling. By controllably introducing defects into MSi2N4, defect-activated Raman features are identified, providing a practical nondestructive approach for crystal quality assessment. This work offers foundational insights into the Raman spectra of MoSi2N4 and WSi2N4, enabling rapid and nondestructive structural characterization and facilitating their controlled synthesis.

works.title: Potential clinical significance of soluble and extracellular vesicle-bound HER2 in breast cancer
A universal NTA chelation-derived strategy to develop triple-functional core@shell magnetic carbon nanorods for microwave absorption, antibacterial, and anticorrosion applications
works.abstract: Abstract Simultaneous achievement of high-performance microwave absorption, antibacterial activity, and corrosion resistance remains a key challenge for multifunctional materials in real-world application scenarios. Herein, one-dimensional core@shell FeCo@carbon nanorods (CNRs), FeCoNi@CNRs, and FeCoNiMn@CNRs consisting of magnetic alloy nanoparticles as core confined in the shell of CNRs are fabricated through a nitrilotriacetic acid chelation (NTAC)-assisted hydrothermal route, phenolic-resin coating, and carbonization treatment. The increased annealing temperature promotes graphitization of carbon shell, yielding the improved impedance matching and dielectric/magnetic synergy. The optimized FeCoNi@CNRs deliver a minimum reflection loss of -52.57 dB and an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 5.60 GHz. Successive Ni and Mn incorporation further enhances complex permittivity, attenuation constant, and impedance matching. The acquired FeCoNiMn@CNRs display an EAB of 6.40 GHz, a radar cross-section reduction up to 39.59 dB·m2, a bacteriostatic rate approaching 100% against E. coli, and the highest corrosion potential with the lowest corrosion current density in simulated seawater. The functionally complementary core@shell design with magnetic alloy core for loss/ROS generation and graphitic carbon shell for interfacial polarization/barrier protection establishes a facile and universal NTAC-derived strategy for advanced wave-absorbing materials with integrated antibacterial and environmental durability.

Opinion: Ligand identity ambiguity in LNP-induced metastasis promotion via TLR9-MyD88/cGAS-STING-dependent NETosis – Endogenous mtDNA or exogenous bacterial PAMPs?
works.abstract: Wang and colleagues recently reported that lipid nanoparticle (LNP) administration promotes experimental pulmonary tumor metastasis through TLR9-MyD88- and cGASSTING-mediated neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, invoking mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) released from necrotic muscle cells as the activating ligand. This Opinion challenges a fundamental assumption underlying that interpretation: because TLR9 recognizes unmethylated CpG dinucleotides shared equally by mtDNA and bacterial DNA, and cGAS detects double-stranded DNA in a sequence-independent manner, the genetic rescue experiments are equally consistent with bacterial nucleic acid or lipopolysaccharide (LPS) contamination of the LNP preparations. Standard endotoxin detection methods, including the Limulus amebocyte lysate assay, are demonstrably unreliable in lipid matrices, where LPS lipid A inserts stably into hydrophobic domains and evades detection. Total lipid A quantification by EndoQuant (acid hydrolysis/HPLC-MS/MS), 16S rDNA analysis, polymyxin B pretreatment, and amplicon sequencing are required to resolve ligand identity. Until these controls are applied, the mtDNA hypothesis and a manufacturing contamination hypothesis remain equally supported by the available data — a distinction with profoundly different regulatory and clinical implications for LNP-based therapeutics.

works.title: Neighboring Rh nanoclusters promote the activity and stability of Rh single-atom catalyst for the hydroformylation of sterically hindered diisobutylene
works.abstract: Abstract Developing efficient and leaching-resistant heterogeneous Rh catalysts for the hydroformylation of sterically hindered olefins remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a ligand-free heterogeneous Rh catalyst (Rh/N-AC-T), featuring a proximal dual-active-site architecture, in which Rh single atoms and nanoclusters are co-anchored on nitrogen-doped carbon (Rh/N-AC-T). The optimized Rh/N-AC-650 catalyst exhibits outstanding catalytic performance in the hydroformylation of diisobutylene (DIB), delivering high catalytic activity, excellent structural stability, and negligible Rh leaching during continuous-flow operation for over 200 h. Comprehensive spectroscopic characterizations combined with density functional theory calculations suggest that the intimate coupling between adjacent Rh single atoms and nanoclusters modulates the Rh electronic structure and the adsorption balance of H2, DIB, and CO. The dual-site interface facilitates H2 activation and lower the relative energy barrier for the rate-determining CO-insertion step, accounting for the enhanced hydroformylation performance. Meanwhile, pyridinic N species within the carbon framework benefit for the stronger interactions between Rh species and support, thereby helping suppress Rh aggregation and leaching under harsh reaction conditions. This work establishes proximal Rh single atom-nanocluster dual sites as an effective design strategy for constructing high-performance, ligand-free heterogeneous catalysts for challenging carbonylation reactions.
